title: Energy intake and appetite are suppressed by glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) in obese men.
journal: International journal of obesity and related metabolic disorders : journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity
population: Obese male subjects with BMI 45.5 +/- 2.3 kg/m2
intervention: Intravenous infusion of GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) at 0.75 pmol x kg(-1) min(-1) for eight hours
comparison: Intravenous saline infusion
outcomes_primary: Ad libitum energy intake at lunch and dinner
outcomes_secondary: Appetite sensations using visual analogue scales (VAS); blood glucose, insulin, C-peptide, GLP-1, and peptide YY concentrations; gastric emptying using paracetamol absorption technique
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=8). Primary outcome not explicitly designated; assumed based on study objective. Cross-over design specified.

title: Continuous subcutaneous infusion of glucagon-like peptide 1 lowers plasma glucose and reduces appetite in type 2 diabetic patients.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes
intervention: Glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) continuous subcutaneous infusion at 2.4 pmol/kg/min for 48 hours
comparison: Saline subcutaneous infusion for 48 hours
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes assessed included: appetite (hunger, prospective food intake, satiety, fullness) during fixed energy intake, plasma glucose (fasting and 24-hour mean), insulin, C-peptide, glucagon, postprandial lipidemia (triglycerides, free fatty acids), blood pressure, heart rate, basal metabolic rate, and side effects. Crossover design with randomized order. Small sample size (n=6).

title: Inhibition of sham feeding-stimulated human gastric acid secretion by glucagon-like peptide-2.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
population: Healthy volunteers
intervention: GLP-2 infused intravenously at a rate of 0.8 pmol/kg x min during sham feeding
comparison: Saline infusion during sham feeding
outcomes_primary: Gastric acid secretion
outcomes_secondary: Gastric volume, osmolarity, plasma concentrations of GLP-2, GLP-1, gastrin, cholecystokinin, and secretin
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=8). Crossover design with each volunteer studied twice on separate days. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; determined based on study objective. Duration of infusion not explicitly stated.

title: Effect of glucagon-like peptide 1(7-36)amide in insulin-treated patients with diabetes mellitus secondary to chronic pancreatitis.
population: Patients with diabetes mellitus secondary to chronic pancreatitis treated with insulin (9 patients) or sulfonylurea (1 patient); normal subjects included as controls
intervention: Glucagon-like peptide 1(7-36)amide (GLP-1) administered intravenously at doses of 0.4 or 1.2 pmol/min/kg body weight for 4 hours
comparison: Saline infusion
extraction_notes: Small study (n=10 patients, n=5 normal subjects). Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly designated in abstract. Outcomes measured included blood glucose, plasma C-peptide, and plasma glucagon, but these were not categorized as primary or secondary.

title: Effect of glucagon on carbohydrate-mediated secretion of glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) and glucagon-like peptide-1 (7-36 amide) (GLP-1).
population: Healthy men, aged approximately 23-24 years, with body mass index approximately 24 kg/m2
intervention: Intravenous infusion of glucagon combined with 100 g oral carbohydrate load containing 1.5 g paracetamol
comparison: Intravenous infusion of saline combined with 100 g oral carbohydrate load containing 1.5 g paracetamol
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucose concentrations, plasma GIP concentrations, plasma GLP-1 concentrations, plasma insulin concentrations, plasma paracetamol concentrations (as marker of gastric emptying), measured before and after carbohydrate load for 6 hours
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=6). Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes. Crossover design implied but not explicitly stated. Glucagon dose, infusion rate, and duration not specified in abstract.

title: Effects of intraduodenal glucose and fructose on antropyloric motility and appetite in healthy humans.
journal: American journal of physiology. Regulatory, integrative and comparative physiology
population: Healthy volunteers
intervention: Intraduodenal infusion of 25% fructose, 2 ml/min for 90 min
comparison: Intraduodenal infusion of 25% glucose, 2 ml/min for 90 min; Intraduodenal infusion of 0.9% saline, 2 ml/min for 90 min
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes measured included: antropyloric pressures (antral waves, isolated pyloric pressure waves, basal pyloric pressure), blood glucose, plasma insulin, gastric inhibitory peptide (GIP), glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), and food intake at buffet meal. Sample size n=10.

title: The effect of glucagon-like peptide-1 on energy expenditure and substrate metabolism in humans.
journal: International journal of obesity and related metabolic disorders : journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity
population: Healthy, normal weight men (body mass index 20.3-25.7 kg/m2), aged 20-31 years
intervention: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) infusion, 50 pmol/kg x h, started simultaneously with initiation of test meals
comparison: Saline infusion (placebo)
outcomes_primary: Diet-induced thermogenesis (DIT), energy expenditure, substrate oxidation (carbohydrate, fat, protein oxidation)
outcomes_secondary: Desire to eat specific types of food assessed by visual analogue scales, palatability of test meals, plasma hormone and substrate concentrations
extraction_notes: Cross-over study design with 20 subjects. Duration of infusion not explicitly stated beyond 4 hours of post-meal measurement. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly designated in abstract.

title: Influence of acarbose on post-prandial insulin requirements in patients with Type 1 diabetes.
population: Patients with Type 1 diabetes (T1DM)
intervention: Acarbose 100 mg administered with a standardised meal
comparison: Placebo administered with a standardised meal
outcomes_primary: Insulin requirement for maintenance of normoglycaemia over a 3-hour period following a standardised meal, assessed using a closed-loop insulin infusion system (artificial pancreas, Biostator)
outcomes_secondary: Post-prandial triglyceride levels; glucagon levels; gastrointestinal peptide levels (including gastric inhibitory polypeptide AUC, Cmax, and tmax); gastric emptying; oxidative glucose metabolism; blood glucose control
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=10). Double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomised cross-over study design with 10±3 days washout between periods. Blood glucose was normalised before each meal test.

title: Short-term treatment with GLP-1 increases pulsatile insulin secretion in Type II diabetes with no effect on orderliness.
population: Type II (non-insulin-dependent) diabetes mellitus patients (n = 8)
intervention: GLP-1 infusion at 1.2 pmol/l x kg(-1) x min(-1) with plasma glucose clamped at initial concentration by variable glucose infusion
comparison: Saline infusion (randomised cross-over design, studied on 2 separate days)
outcomes_primary: Pulsatile insulin secretion measured by secretory burst mass and secretory burst amplitude; basal insulin secretion; fraction of insulin delivered in pulses
outcomes_secondary: Regularity of secretion measured by spectral analysis (normalised spectral power), autocorrelation analysis (autocorrelation coefficient), and approximate entropy statistic; serum insulin concentrations
extraction_notes: Short-term treatment duration not explicitly defined. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; classification based on study aims. Cross-over design with basal conditions and two treatment days.

title: No effect of glucagon-like peptide-1 on short-term satiety and energy intake in man.
population: Non-obese male subjects (n=10)
intervention: GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) infusion at 1.2 pmol/kg per min for 1 hour, administered at 18:00 hours
comparison: Saline infusion (control)
outcomes_primary: Gastric emptying of a 400 ml water load; energy intake from ad libitum buffet meal
outcomes_secondary: Self-assessment of hunger and satiety using behavioural self-rating scales; circulating GLP-1 concentrations; circulating insulin levels; glucose levels
extraction_notes: Randomized single-blind within-subject crossover design. Primary outcomes not explicitly designated; inferred from study objectives. Water load administered at 20 min after starting infusion; buffet meal provided at 40 min.

title: Diet-induced change in fatty acid composition of plasma triacylglycerols is not associated with change in glucagon-like peptide 1 or insulin sensitivity in people with type 2 diabetes.
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
population: Overweight people with type 2 diabetes
intervention: High-MUFA diet (20.3% of total energy from monounsaturated fatty acids) for 24 days
comparison: High-PUFA diet (13.4% of total energy from polyunsaturated fatty acids) for 24 days
outcomes_primary: Insulin sensitivity measured by the short-insulin-tolerance test
outcomes_secondary: Plasma triacylglycerol linoleic-oleic acid ratio (L:O); phospholipid L:O; ratio of total to HDL cholesterol; fasting and postprandial incremental area under the curve for glucose, insulin, triacylglycerol, nonesterified fatty acids, and glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1)
extraction_notes: Sample size is 9 participants. Randomized double-blind crossover design with isoenergetic diets. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; insulin sensitivity inferred as primary based on study objective.

title: Circulating levels of incretin hormones and amylin in the fasting state and after oral glucose in GH-deficient patients before and after GH replacement: a placebo-controlled study.
population: 24 GH-deficient adults
intervention: GH replacement therapy: daily evening injections of 2 IU GH/m² for 4 months
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_secondary: Plasma concentrations of glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) in fasting state and after OGTT; plasma concentrations of glucose-dependent insulin-releasing peptide (GIP) in fasting state and after OGTT; total amylin concentrations in fasting state and after OGTT; non-glycosylated amylin concentrations in fasting state and after OGTT; plasma glucose concentrations in fasting state and after OGTT; plasma insulin concentrations in fasting state and after OGTT; ratio between amylin and insulin
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; all outcomes listed as secondary. GH dose unit appears as 'IU GH/m' which may be truncated (likely 'IU GH/m²'). Study design is double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel study.

title: Glucagon-like peptide 1 increases secretory burst mass of pulsatile insulin secretion in patients with type 2 diabetes and impaired glucose tolerance.
population: Type 2 diabetic patients and subjects with impaired glucose tolerance (IGT); Type 2 diabetic patients: age 64±9 years, BMI 28.9±7.2 kg/m2, HbA1c 7.7±1.3%; IGT subjects: age 63±10 years, BMI 31.7±6.4 kg/m2, HbA1c 5.7±0.4%; Healthy volunteers for comparison: age 62±7 years, BMI 27.7±4.8 kg/m2, HbA1c 5.4±0.5%
intervention: Exogenous GLP-1 administered intravenously at 1.2 pmol/kg/min, started at 10:00 PM the evening before study, continued administration during fasting state
comparison: Placebo (crossover design for type 2 diabetic patients and IGT subjects); Healthy volunteers studied only with placebo for comparison
outcomes_primary: Pulsatile insulin secretion parameters including secretory burst mass, amplitude, and burst frequency characterized by deconvolution analysis, autocorrelation analysis, spectral analysis, and approximate entropy
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucose concentrations; Period (lag time) between subsequent maxima of insulin concentrations
extraction_notes: Small sample sizes (8 per group). Healthy volunteers were not given GLP-1, only serving as placebo comparison group. Study appears to be crossover design for type 2 diabetic and IGT groups.

title: Effect of metformin on glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) and leptin levels in obese nondiabetic subjects.
population: Obese nondiabetic male patients
intervention: Metformin 2,550 mg/day for 14 days
comparison: Untreated obese control subjects
outcomes_primary: GLP-1(7-36)amide/(7-37) levels before and after oral glucose load during euglycemic hyperinsulinemic clamp
outcomes_secondary: Leptin levels before and after oral glucose load; GLP-1(7-36)amide degradation in human plasma and buffer solution containing dipeptidyl peptidase IV (DPP-IV)
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=10 per group). Study assessed outcomes on days 0 and 15. In vitro experiments on GLP-1 degradation were also included.

title: Additive glucose-lowering effects of glucagon-like peptide-1 and metformin in type 2 diabetes.
population: Type 2 diabetic patients
intervention: Combination therapy with GLP-1 (continuous subcutaneous infusion of 2.4 pmol x kg(-1) x min(-1)) and metformin (1,500 mg daily orally) for 48 h
comparison: Metformin monotherapy (1,500 mg daily orally) for 48 h; GLP-1 monotherapy (continuous subcutaneous infusion of 2.4 pmol x kg(-1) x min(-1)) for 48 h; No treatment
outcomes_primary: Fasting plasma glucose; 24-h mean plasma glucose
outcomes_secondary: Plasma insulin levels; C-peptide levels; Glucagon levels; Appetite scores
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=7). Semiblinded randomized crossover design. Fixed energy intake during study period. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly specified in abstract.

title: The effect of physiological levels of glucagon-like peptide-1 on appetite, gastric emptying, energy and substrate metabolism in obesity.
journal: International journal of obesity and related metabolic disorders : journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity
population: Obese men
intervention: GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) infusion at physiological dose
comparison: Saline infusion (placebo)
outcomes_primary: Appetite sensations (hunger, prospective food consumption assessed by visual analogue scales), energy intake (ad libitum energy intake at lunch), gastric emptying (measured using paracetamol as marker)
outcomes_secondary: Resting metabolic rate (RMR), substrate oxidations (carbohydrate oxidation), plasma hormone profiles (GLP-1, GLP-2, GIP, insulin, glucagon), plasma substrate profiles (glucose, lactate, NEFA, TAG), thirst, comfort, palatability of test meals
extraction_notes: Study design: placebo-controlled, randomized, single-blinded, cross-over. Sample size n=18. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; categorization based on stated study objectives.

title: Antidiabetogenic action of glucagon-like peptide-1 related to administration relative to meal intake in subjects with type 2 diabetes.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes treated with oral sulphonylureas
intervention: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) 17 nmol administered as 3-hour stepwise intravenous infusion at three different timings relative to a standard meal (550 kCal): (A) at onset of meal, (B) 30 minutes after start of meal, or (C) 60 minutes after start of meal
comparison: Placebo (control meal)
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes measured included postprandial glycaemia, postprandial insulin levels, postprandial glucagon levels, and gastric emptying (determined by paracetamol test). Crossover design with random assignment to treatment sequence. Small sample size (n=8).

title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 infusion must be maintained for 24 h/day to obtain acceptable glycemia in type 2 diabetic patients who are poorly controlled on sulphonylurea treatment.
population: Type 2 diabetic patients who were poorly controlled on sulfonylurea treatment, hospitalized
intervention: GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) continuous infusion at 4 ng/kg/min or 8 ng/kg/min for either 16 or 24 hours per day for 7 days
comparison: Placebo infusion for either 16 or 24 hours per day for 7 days
outcomes_primary: Change in average plasma glucose (area under the curve for day 7 minus AUC for day 0 divided by 24 h)
outcomes_secondary: 24-hour profiles of glucose, glucagon, and insulin; nocturnal and fasting plasma glucose levels; adverse events; clinical chemistry and hematology
extraction_notes: Single-center study with 40 patients. The study had a 2x2 factorial design with GLP-1 doses (4 or 8 ng/kg/min) and infusion duration (16 or 24 h/day). Primary outcome not explicitly labeled but glucose AUC change appears to be the main efficacy measure.

title: Inhibition of gastric emptying by acarbose is correlated with GLP-1 response and accompanied by CCK release.
journal: American journal of physiology. Gastrointestinal and liver physiology
population: Healthy subjects
intervention: Acarbose 100 mg (alpha-glucosidase and pancreatic alpha-amylase inhibitor)
comparison: Without acarbose (crossover design, random order, at least 1 week apart)
outcomes_primary: Gastric emptying of solid meals (measured by scintigraphy)
outcomes_secondary: Plasma responses of gut hormones including insulin, glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), CCK, glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), and peptide YY (PYY)
extraction_notes: Study tested meals of varying nutrient composition: carbohydrate-free meal, mixed meal, and carbohydrate-free meal given 2 hours after sucrose ingestion. Sample size not specified in abstract. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; outcomes inferred from study description.

title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (7-37) augments insulin-mediated glucose uptake in elderly patients with diabetes.
journal: The journals of gerontology. Series A, Biological sciences and medical sciences
population: Elderly patients with type 2 diabetes, age approximately 76 years, body mass index approximately 28 kg/m2
intervention: Primed-continuous infusion of GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1 [7-37]) at a final rate of 1.5 pmol/kg/min administered from 30 to 180 minutes during euglycemic insulin clamp (insulin infusion rate 40 mU/m2/min)
comparison: Euglycemic insulin clamp with glucose and insulin infusion alone (no GLP-1)
outcomes_primary: Glucose disposal rate (Rd) measured using tritiated glucose methodology during 120-180 minute period
outcomes_secondary: Glucose production rate (Ra), insulin values, glucose values
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=8). Crossover design with each subject undergoing both studies in random order. Two subjects excluded from secondary analysis due to substantial insulin responses to GLP-1.

title: Bedtime administration of NN2211, a long-acting GLP-1 derivative, substantially reduces fasting and postprandial glycemia in type 2 diabetes.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes
intervention: NN2211 (long-acting GLP-1 derivative), single subcutaneous injection, 10 microg/kg, administered at 2300 h (bedtime)
comparison: Placebo (double-blind, crossover design)
outcomes_primary: Fasting plasma glucose, postprandial glucose (meal-related AUC), insulin secretory rates (ISR), plasma glucagon levels
outcomes_secondary: Gastric emptying (assessed by 3-ortho-methylglucose AUC), high frequency regularity of insulin release during glucose pulse entrainment, pharmacokinetic profile (T1/2, Tmax), gastrointestinal side effects
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=11). Crossover design used. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; classification based on emphasis in reporting.

title: Postprandial glucose, insulin, and incretin responses to grain products in healthy subjects.
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
population: Healthy men and women with normal glucose tolerance
intervention: Whole-kernel rye bread, whole-meal rye bread containing oat beta-glucan concentrate, dark durum wheat pasta; each product providing 50 g available carbohydrate, served with breakfast; paracetamol added to breads as gastric emptying marker
comparison: Wheat bread made from white wheat flour providing 50 g available carbohydrate
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished. Outcomes measured include plasma glucose, glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1), serum insulin, and paracetamol concentrations at fasting and 8 postprandial timepoints over 3 hours. Study design is a crossover with random order, except beta-glucan rye bread served at last visit. Sample size: 10 men and 10 women (n=20).

title: Effects of glucagon-like peptide-1(7-36)amide on motility and sensation of the proximal stomach in humans.
population: Healthy male volunteers
intervention: Synthetic glucagon-like peptide-1(7-36)amide (GLP-1) intravenous infusion at 0.3 pmol/kg/min (low dose) or 0.9 pmol/kg/min (high dose)
comparison: Saline infusion
outcomes_primary: Fundus tone and volume waves measured by barostat; gastric compliance derived from isobaric distension
outcomes_secondary: Perception of gastric distension (sensation score); pressure at half maximum bag volume; total volume displaced by volume wave events
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=11). Crossover design with separate days in random order. Duration of infusion periods specified as 60 minutes each for basal and peptide periods. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract.

title: Effect of GLP-1 on gastric volume, emptying, maximum volume ingested, and postprandial symptoms in humans.
journal: American journal of physiology. Gastrointestinal and liver physiology
population: Healthy human volunteers
intervention: Intravenous GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1)
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Gastric volume measured using 99mTc-single photon emission computed tomography imaging; gastric emptying of a nutrient liquid meal (Ensure) measured using scintigraphy
outcomes_secondary: Maximum tolerated volume (MTV) of Ensure; postprandial symptoms 30 minutes after MTV; vagal cholinergic function assessed by human pancreatic polypeptide (HPP) response to the Ensure meal
extraction_notes: Dose, frequency, and duration of GLP-1 administration not specified in abstract. Sample size not reported. Whether primary/secondary outcome distinction is as designated by study authors is unclear; classification based on order of mention in abstract.

title: Impaired beta-cell function, incretin effect, and glucagon suppression in patients with type 1 diabetes who have normal fasting glucose.
population: Subjects with type 1 diabetes manifested by glucose >11.1 mmol/l 120 min after an oral glucose load but with normal fasting glucose levels, compared to age-matched nondiabetic control subjects
intervention: Not applicable - observational metabolic characterization study
comparison: Age-matched nondiabetic control subjects
outcomes_primary: Parameters of islet hormone secretion including first-phase insulin response, insulin secretory response to intravenous arginine at euglycemia, slope of glucose potentiation of insulin response to arginine, maximum insulin response to arginine
outcomes_secondary: Incretin effect, plasma levels of GLP-1 and GIP, glucagon suppression after oral and intravenous glucose administration, glucose effectiveness, insulin sensitivity
extraction_notes: This is an observational/comparative physiology study rather than an interventional clinical trial. No therapeutic intervention was administered. Sample sizes not specified in abstract.

title: The pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, safety and tolerability of NN2211, a new long-acting GLP-1 derivative, in healthy men.
population: Healthy male subjects
intervention: NN2211 (fatty acid derivative of GLP-1) administered subcutaneously at dose levels of 1.25, 5.0, 7.5, 10.0, or 12.5 microg/kg, given on day 1 and days 5-11 (daily dose for seven days)
comparison: Placebo (ratio 2:1 active to placebo at each dose level)
outcomes_primary: Pharmacokinetics (84-hour profile including half-life, AUC, Cmax, accumulation index); pharmacodynamics (24-hour glucose and insulin profiles)
outcomes_secondary: Safety and tolerability including adverse events, vital signs, ECG parameters, physical examination, safety laboratory parameters, diuresis, packed cell volume
extraction_notes: This is a phase I dose escalation study in healthy volunteers, not patients with diabetes. Six subjects allocated at each of five dose levels. Study design is double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled.

title: Acute ingestion of a meal rich in n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids results in rapid gastric emptying in humans.
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
population: Healthy women aged 50-62 years
intervention: 40 g oil rich in n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids consumed as part of a mixed meal, with 100 mg [1-(13)C]octanoic acid added
comparison: 40 g oil rich in saturated fatty acids; 40 g oil rich in monounsaturated fatty acids; 40 g oil rich in n-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids (each as part of a mixed meal with 100 mg [1-(13)C]octanoic acid added)
outcomes_primary: Gastric emptying assessed by labeled octanoic acid breath test (recovery of 13C in breath)
outcomes_secondary: Gastrointestinal hormone concentrations (cholecystokinin, glucagon-like peptide 1); plasma lipid concentrations
extraction_notes: Single-blind randomized crossover design with 4 separate study visits. Primary outcome not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in abstract.

title: Pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, safety, and tolerability of a single-dose of NN2211, a long-acting glucagon-like peptide 1 derivative, in healthy male subjects.
population: Healthy male subjects
intervention: NN2211 (long-acting glucagon-like peptide 1 derivative), single subcutaneous dose at eight escalating dose levels (1.25, 2.5, 5.0, 10.0, 12.5, 15.0, 17.5, and 20.0 microg/kg)
comparison: Placebo (3:1 active:placebo randomization)
outcomes_primary: Safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of NN2211 (including half-life, time to maximal plasma concentration)
outcomes_secondary: Pharmacodynamics of NN2211: 48-h pharmacokinetic profiles, 24-h glucose profiles, 24-h insulin profiles, 24-h glucagon profiles, intravenous glucose tolerance test (IVGTT) parameters including insulin secretion, glucagon levels, glucose levels, and glucose disappearance constant
extraction_notes: Phase 1 study in healthy volunteers, not patients with diabetes. Sample size per dose level stated (8 subjects with 3:1 randomization) but total N not explicitly stated.

title: Plasma glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) responses to duodenal fat and glucose infusions in lean and obese men.
population: Healthy lean men (BMI 19.1-24.6 kg/m²) and obese men (BMI 31.3-40.8 kg/m²), young adults
intervention: Intraduodenal infusion of glucose at 2.86 kcal/min for 120 minutes; Intraduodenal infusion of fat at 2.86 kcal/min for 120 minutes
comparison: Lean versus obese subjects; glucose infusion versus fat infusion
outcomes_primary: Plasma GLP-1 levels measured at baseline and every 20 minutes during infusion
extraction_notes: This is a physiological study comparing GLP-1 responses rather than a therapeutic intervention trial. Sample size is small (n=7 per group). The study uses a crossover design with each subject receiving both nutrient infusions on separate days.

title: The effects of miglitol on glucagon-like peptide-1 secretion and appetite sensations in obese type 2 diabetics.
population: Obese type 2 diabetic women
intervention: Miglitol 100 mg orally three times a day for 2 days (six doses total)
comparison: Placebo three times a day for 2 days
outcomes_primary: Plasma GLP-1 levels in response to mixed meal; plasma GIP levels; plasma insulin levels; plasma glucose levels measured periodically during 3 hours after eating a 720 kcal breakfast
outcomes_secondary: Appetite ratings using visual analogue scales (VAS) assessing hunger and satiety hourly before breakfast and for 6 hours after until lunch; food consumption measured by number of tuna sandwiches eaten at lunch
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=8). Crossover design with double-blind randomization implied but washout period not specified.

title: High-fat diet effects on gut motility, hormone, and appetite responses to duodenal lipid in healthy men.
journal: American journal of physiology. Gastrointestinal and liver physiology
population: Healthy men
intervention: 14-day high-fat diet followed by 90-min duodenal lipid infusion (6.3 kJ/min)
comparison: 14-day low-fat diet followed by 90-min duodenal lipid infusion (6.3 kJ/min)
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished. Outcomes measured included: appetite (hunger), antropyloroduodenal pressures (pyloric tonic and phasic pressures, pressure-wave sequences), plasma CCK levels, plasma glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) levels, and food intake. Randomized crossover design with n=12.

title: The effects of fiber enrichment of pasta and fat content on gastric emptying, GLP-1, glucose, and insulin responses to a meal.
population: Ten subjects (no further eligibility criteria specified)
intervention: Pasta with psyllium enrichment (1.7 g psyllium) served with tomato sauce; pasta served with tomato sauce containing fat (30 g sunflower oil and 3 g sodium propionate, 520 kcal per meal)
comparison: Control pasta without psyllium enrichment served with tomato sauce without fat (240 kcal per meal); two-by-two factorial design comparing psyllium vs no psyllium and fat vs no fat
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified as primary
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly specified as secondary; outcomes measured included: gastric emptying (paracetamol absorption test), incremental area under the curve (IAUC) for GLP-1, IAUC for insulin, IAUC for glucose, visual analog scales for feelings of hunger, pleasantness and nausea, buffet meal consumption
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the abstract. All four meals contained 50 g of available carbohydrate. Study design was single blind randomized crossover. Blood samples collected for 240 minutes post-meal.

title: Casein and whey exert different effects on plasma amino acid profiles, gastrointestinal hormone secretion and appetite.
population: Healthy adults (specific eligibility criteria not stated in abstract)
intervention: 1700 kJ liquid preload containing 48 g whey protein
comparison: Equivalent 1700 kJ liquid preload containing 48 g casein protein
outcomes_primary: Energy intake from ad libitum buffet meal (Study 1); Postprandial plasma amino acid concentrations (Study 2)
outcomes_secondary: Subjective ratings of hunger and fullness; Plasma cholecystokinin (CCK); Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1); Glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP); Gastric emptying (plasma paracetamol profiles)
extraction_notes: Two separate studies reported within one publication. Population eligibility criteria not explicitly defined in abstract. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction inferred from study design description.

title: Differential effects of saturated and monounsaturated fats on postprandial lipemia and glucagon-like peptide 1 responses in patients with type 2 diabetes.
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
population: Twelve overweight patients with type 2 diabetes
intervention: Control meal (energy-free soup with 50 g carbohydrate) plus 100 g butter; Control meal plus 80 g olive oil
comparison: Energy-free soup with 50 g carbohydrate (control meal)
outcomes_secondary: Postprandial responses (8 h) of glucose, insulin, fatty acids, triacylglycerol (measured in total plasma, chylomicron-rich fraction, and chylomicron-poor fraction), gastric inhibitory polypeptide, GLP-1, HDL-cholesterol concentrations
extraction_notes: Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in the abstract. Study uses randomized crossover design with 3 meal conditions.

title: Effect of glucagon-like peptide 1 (7-36 amide) on insulin-mediated glucose uptake in patients with type 1 diabetes.
population: Patients with type 1 diabetes; 6 women and 5 men
intervention: GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide 1, 7-36 amide) at 1.5 pmol/kg/min administered during hyperinsulinemic-euglycemic clamp (480 pmol/m2/min)
comparison: Hyperinsulinemic-euglycemic clamp alone (without GLP-1), paired randomized crossover design
outcomes_primary: Insulin-mediated glucose uptake
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucose levels; plasma insulin levels; plasma C-peptide levels; plasma total GLP-1 levels; plasma glucagon levels; hepatic glucose production
extraction_notes: Paired randomized crossover design with each subject serving as their own control. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; glucose uptake assumed primary based on study objective. Sample size relatively small (n=11).

title: No effect of physiological concentrations of glucagon-like peptide-2 on appetite and energy intake in normal weight subjects.
journal: International journal of obesity and related metabolic disorders : journal of the International Association for the Study of Obesity
population: Healthy, normal weight young subjects; 18 total (8 women, 10 men)
intervention: GLP-2 infusion at rate of 25 pmol/kg body weight for 4.5 hours
comparison: Placebo infusion
outcomes_primary: Appetite sensations measured by visual analogue scales every 30 min; ad libitum energy intake at test meal
outcomes_secondary: Palatability of test meals; glucose concentrations; GLP-1 concentrations; insulin concentrations; GIP concentrations; glucagon concentrations; GLP-2 concentrations
extraction_notes: Crossover design with randomised, blinded, placebo-controlled methodology. Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in abstract.

title: Effects of fat digestion on appetite, APD motility, and gut hormones in response to duodenal fat infusion in humans.
journal: American journal of physiology. Gastrointestinal and liver physiology
population: Healthy, young, lean men
intervention: Duodenal infusion of a triglyceride emulsion (2.8 kcal/min) for 120 minutes with 120 mg tetrahydrolipstatin (lipase inhibitor)

title: Dose-dependent satiating effect of whey relative to casein or soy.

title: The effect of exogenous glucagon-like peptide-1 on the glycaemic response to small intestinal nutrient in the critically ill: a randomised double-blind placebo-controlled cross over study.

title: Pharmacology and tolerability of a single dose of exenatide in adolescent patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus being treated with metformin: a randomized, placebo-controlled, single-blind, dose-escalation, crossover study.

title: Acute effects of casein on postprandial lipemia and incretin responses in type 2 diabetic subjects.

title: Effect of rimonabant and metformin on glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucagon-like peptide-1 in obese women with polycystic ovary syndrome.
population: Obese women with polycystic ovary syndrome
intervention: Rimonabant
comparison: Metformin
outcomes_primary: Glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) levels; Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) levels
extraction_notes: Abstract text not available; extraction based solely on title information. Dose, route, frequency, and duration of interventions not specified. Primary vs secondary outcome classification not confirmed. Study design unclear from title alone.

title: Adding liraglutide to oral antidiabetic drug monotherapy: efficacy and weight benefits.

title: Liraglutide once a day versus exenatide twice a day for type 2 diabetes: a 26-week randomised, parallel-group, multinational, open-label trial (LEAD-6).

outcomes_primary: Change in glycosylated haemoglobin (HbA1c)
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of patients achieving HbA1c less than 7%; fasting plasma glucose; postprandial glucose control; weight loss; tolerability; nausea; minor hypoglycaemia; major hypoglycaemic episodes
extraction_notes: Open-label study design; patients stratified by previous oral antidiabetic therapy; multinational trial (15 countries)

title: Efficacy of a continuous GLP-1 infusion compared with a structured insulin infusion protocol to reach normoglycemia in nonfasted type 2 diabetic patients: a clinical pilot trial.
population: Type 2 diabetic patients with self-measured fasting glucose levels >150 mg/dl; clinically stable; treated with oral antidiabetic drugs; excluded: New York Heart Association class III or IV heart failure, uncontrolled hypertension, impaired kidney function (creatinine >3 mg/dl), or acute infection

outcomes_primary: Time to reach plasma glucose level below 115 mg/dl
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucose after 2 hours; plasma glucose after 4 hours; maximum glycemia; number of hypoglycemic episodes
extraction_notes: Prospective open randomized crossover trial with 7±3 days washout between periods; small pilot study (n=8); standardized meal challenge design

title: Effects of the phases of the menstrual cycle on gastric emptying, glycemia, plasma GLP-1 and insulin, and energy intake in healthy lean women.
journal: American journal of physiology. Gastrointestinal and liver physiology
population: Healthy, lean women with regular menstrual cycles
intervention: Assessment during follicular phase (days 6-12 of menstrual cycle) following consumption of a 300-ml glucose drink (0.17 g/ml)
comparison: Assessment during luteal phase (days 18-24 of menstrual cycle) following consumption of the same glucose drink; repeat assessment during follicular phase for reproducibility
outcomes_primary: Gastric emptying, blood glucose, plasma GLP-1 concentrations, plasma insulin concentrations, plasma CCK concentrations, hunger ratings, energy intake at buffet meal
extraction_notes: This is a within-subjects observational study comparing menstrual cycle phases rather than a randomized controlled trial. Nine participants were studied on three occasions. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract.

title: Improved treatment satisfaction and weight-related quality of life with exenatide once weekly or twice daily.
journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
population: Adults with Type 2 diabetes managed with diet and exercise and/or oral glucose-lowering medications
intervention: Exenatide once weekly (2 mg QW) subcutaneous injection
comparison: Exenatide twice daily (10 μg BID) subcutaneous injection
outcomes_primary: Change in glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) at 30 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Diabetes Treatment Satisfaction Questionnaire—status (DTSQ-s) total score and individual items; Impact of Weight on Quality of Life—Lite (IWQOL-Lite) total score and domain scores (physical function, self-esteem, sexual life, public distress, work); fasting plasma glucose; weight; adverse events
extraction_notes: Open-label study design. Primary endpoint was HbA1c at 30 weeks; PRO measures (DTSQ-s, IWQOL-Lite) appear to be secondary outcomes. After week 30, subjects on BID were switched to QW for weeks 30-52, allowing assessment of switching effects but no true parallel comparison beyond 30 weeks.

title: Potential of albiglutide, a long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist, in type 2 diabetes: a randomized controlled trial exploring weekly, biweekly, and monthly dosing.
population: Men and women of non-childbearing potential aged 18-75 years with type 2 diabetes diagnosed ≥3 months before screening, drug naïve (diet and exercise) or treated with metformin monotherapy stable for >3 months, BMI ≥20 and ≤40 kg/m2, A1C ≥7 and ≤10% at screening. Exclusion criteria included any oral antidiabetic monotherapy (except metformin) ≤3 months prior to screening or insulin <1 month prior to screening, pancreatitis within 5 years, significant cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, renal, or hepatobiliary diseases, fasting serum triglycerides ≥800 mg/dl at screening
intervention: Subcutaneous albiglutide administered over 16 weeks in multiple dose regimens: weekly (4 mg, 15 mg, or 30 mg), biweekly/every 2 weeks (15 mg, 30 mg, or 50 mg), or monthly (50 mg or 100 mg), administered in physician's office
comparison: Double-blind placebo (matched to albiglutide arms); open-label exenatide 5 μg twice daily for 4 weeks followed by 10 μg twice daily for 12 weeks (in metformin-treated subjects only)
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline A1C at week 16 versus placebo across different doses within each schedule (weekly, biweekly, and monthly)
outcomes_secondary: Fasting plasma glucose, fasting fructosamine, C-peptide, glucagon, insulin, lipid profiles, β-cell function (HOMA), body weight, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, proportion of subjects achieving A1C <7.0%, safety and tolerability (adverse events, nausea, vomiting, hypoglycemia, injection site reactions), immunogenicity (anti-albiglutide antibodies), pharmacokinetics
extraction_notes: Phase II dose-finding study with multiple albiglutide dose arms. Exenatide arm was open-label and restricted to metformin-treated subjects only, with no formal statistical comparisons conducted against albiglutide. Study included 11-week washout period following 16-week treatment phase.

title: Food form and portion size affect postprandial appetite sensations and hormonal responses in healthy, nonobese, older adults.
population: Healthy, non-obese older adults aged ≥65 years with BMI between 20-29 kg/m2; not dieting with no weight change >2 kg in past 6 months; non-smoking; non-diabetic; clinically normal blood profiles including normal liver and kidney function, normal complete blood count, fasting blood glucose <110 mg/dL; maintained free-living, sedentary lifestyle
intervention: Beverage form test meal (meal-replacement shake) matched for energy content and macronutrient composition, provided at either 12.5% or 25% of estimated daily energy need, consumed within 15 minutes along with 88.7 mL water
comparison: Solid form test meal (meal-replacement nutrition bar) matched for energy content and macronutrient composition, provided at either 12.5% or 25% of estimated daily energy need; also comparison between 12.5% portion size group (n=18) versus 25% portion size group (n=25)
outcomes_primary: Appetite sensations (hunger, fullness, desire to eat) measured using 13-point numerical rating scale over 4 hours postprandially, analyzed as area under the curve
outcomes_secondary: Hormonal responses including plasma glucose, insulin, total ghrelin, cholecystokinin (CCK), and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) concentrations measured over 4 hours postprandially, analyzed as area under the curve
extraction_notes: Semi-randomized partial crossover design with food form as within-subject factor and portion size as between-subject factor. Primary versus secondary outcomes not explicitly designated in the abstract; classification based on study aims stated in introduction. Different subjects consumed different portion sizes, limiting direct comparison between portion size groups.

title: Four-month treatment with GLP-2 significantly increases hip BMD: a randomized, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging study in postmenopausal women with low BMD.
population: Postmenopausal women with low BMD
intervention: GLP-2 (glucagon-like peptide-2) administered as nightly subcutaneous injection at three dose levels: 0.4 mg, 1.6 mg, and 3.2 mg for four months
comparison: Saline control injection (placebo)
outcomes_primary: Bone mineral density (BMD) at total hip
outcomes_secondary: Biochemical markers of bone turnover (s-CTX for bone resorption, serum osteocalcin for bone formation); safety and tolerability; tachyphylaxis; antibodies against GLP-2
extraction_notes: Primary vs secondary outcome designation not explicitly stated in abstract; outcome hierarchy inferred from study emphasis. Route of administration (subcutaneous injection) implied but not explicitly stated.

title: Improvement in glucose metabolism after bariatric surgery: comparison of laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy: a prospective randomized trial.
population: Patients undergoing bariatric surgery, mostly nondiabetic
intervention: Laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (LRYGB)
comparison: Laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG)
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished. Outcomes measured include fasting and meal-stimulated insulin, glucose, glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), PYY, and ghrelin concentrations; body weight; body mass index; excess BMI loss. Specific eligibility criteria beyond surgical candidacy not provided. Sample size: 13 patients randomized to LRYGB, 14 to LSG. Follow-up timepoints: 1 week and 3 months after surgery.

title: Exenatide versus insulin glargine: a cost-effectiveness evaluation in patients with Type 2 diabetes in Switzerland.
journal: International journal of clinical pharmacology and therapeutics
population: Individuals with Type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled with combination oral agents in the Swiss setting
intervention: Exenatide as add-on treatment to oral therapy
comparison: Insulin glargine as add-on treatment to oral therapy
outcomes_primary: Long-term clinical outcomes (diabetes-related complications, life expectancy), quality-adjusted life expectancy (QALYs), direct medical costs, incremental cost-effectiveness ratio
extraction_notes: This is a cost-effectiveness modeling study using data derived from a 26-week randomized clinical trial. Treatment effects modeled include changes in HbA1c, BMI, systolic blood pressure, and serum lipid levels. Time horizon was 35 years. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished; all outcomes listed as primary.

title: Differential effect of PYY1-36 and PYY3-36 on gastric emptying in man.
population: Eight healthy adults

comparison: Intravenous infusion of saline with a radio-labelled omelette
outcomes_primary: Gastric emptying measured by scintigraphy (half-emptying time, retention at 120 min)
outcomes_secondary: Appetite ratings measured by visual analogue scale (VAS), plasma concentrations of insulin, glucose, GLP-1, and PYY
extraction_notes: Single-blinded, randomized crossover design with each participant studied at separate occasions. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; categorization based on study aim. Small sample size (n=8).

title: Adaptation of colonic fermentation and glucagon-like peptide-1 secretion with increased wheat fibre intake for 1 year in hyperinsulinaemic human subjects.
population: Hyperinsulinaemic human subjects with fasting plasma insulin ≥40 pmol/l
intervention: High-wheat fibre cereal providing 24 g fibre/d daily for 1 year
comparison: Low-fibre cereal daily for 1 year
outcomes_primary: Time-course of effects on plasma acetate, butyrate and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) concentrations over 1 year, measured during 8 h metabolic profiles performed every 3 months
outcomes_secondary: Body weight
extraction_notes: Study described as randomized by computer. Sample size: 20 assigned per group with 6 dropouts each, 14 included per group for analysis.

title: Liraglutide vs insulin glargine and placebo in combination with metformin and sulfonylurea therapy in type 2 diabetes mellitus (LEAD-5 met+SU): a randomised controlled trial.
population: Adults aged 18-80 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus treated with oral glucose-lowering drugs for at least 3 months, HbA1c 7.5-10% if on monotherapy or 7-10% if on combination therapy, BMI ≤45 kg/m2. intervention: Liraglutide 1.8 mg subcutaneous injection once daily (dose escalation starting at 0.6 mg with weekly increments of 0.6 mg over 2 weeks), in combination with metformin 1 g twice daily (2 g/day) and glimepiride 4 mg once daily, for 26 weeks
comparison: 1) Liraglutide placebo (blinded) subcutaneous injection once daily in combination with metformin 1 g twice daily and glimepiride 4 mg once daily; 2) Open-label insulin glargine 100 IU/ml subcutaneous injection once daily (self-titrated based on fasting blood glucose targeting ≤5.5 mmol/l) in combination with metformin 1 g twice daily and glimepiride 4 mg once daily. Randomisation ratio 2:1:2 (liraglutide:placebo:insulin glargine)
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline after 26 weeks of treatment
outcomes_secondary: Change in bodyweight; change in waist circumference; change in fasting plasma glucose; eight-point plasma glucose profiles; beta cell function (proinsulin to C-peptide ratio); change in blood pressure; proportion of participants achieving HbA1c targets (ADA target <7%, AACE target ≤6.5%); hypoglycaemic episodes (major, minor, symptoms only); adverse events; liraglutide antibodies; calcitonin levels
extraction_notes: Open-label design for insulin glargine arm. Non-inferiority margin for liraglutide vs insulin glargine was set at 0.4% for HbA1c. Insulin glargine was patient-titrated according to AT-LANTUS algorithm.

title: Safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of exenatide once weekly in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes.
population: Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes suboptimally controlled by diet and exercise alone or combined with biguanide, sulfonylurea, thiazolidinedione, or combinations of these agents
intervention: Exenatide once weekly (QW) 0.8 mg or 2.0 mg subcutaneous injection for 10 weeks
comparison: Placebo once weekly subcutaneous injection
outcomes_primary: Safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics of exenatide once weekly
outcomes_secondary: Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), fasting plasma glucose (FPG), 2-hour postprandial plasma glucose excursions, adverse events, injection site reactions, hypoglycemia
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; outcomes listed based on study objectives stated. Randomization ratio was 1:1:1 to three groups.

title: A high-fat vs. a moderate-fat meal in obese boys: nutrient balance, appetite, and gastrointestinal hormone changes.

extraction_notes: Crossover design implied but not explicitly stated. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly specified in abstract; categorization based on order of presentation.

title: Orally administered glucagon-like peptide-1 affects glucose homeostasis following an oral glucose tolerance test in healthy male subjects.

Control group not explicitly defined. Study design appears to be pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic study.

title: Absence of QTc prolongation in a thorough QT study with subcutaneous liraglutide, a once-daily human GLP-1 analog for treatment of type 2 diabetes.

extraction_notes: Crossover study design with 4 treatment periods. Sample size explicitly stated as 51 participants. Duration of ECG recording specified as periodic over 24 hours at end of placebo and highest dosing periods.

title: Gut microbiota fermentation of prebiotics increases satietogenic and incretin gut peptide production with consequences for appetite sensation and glucose response after a meal.

extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=10). Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; classification based on study objectives. Specific prebiotic type not named in abstract.

title: Effects of exenatide alone and in combination with daclizumab on beta-cell function in long-standing type 1 diabetes.
population: Adults aged 18-60 years with long-standing type 1 diabetes (duration ≥5 years), C-peptide ≥0.3 ng/ml at baseline or after arginine stimulation, positive antibodies (GAD65, ICA-512) and/or typical history of type 1 diabetes, BMI 20-30 kg/m2. extraction_notes: Prospective randomized open-label crossover trial. Sample size was 20 enrolled, but 4 discontinued before randomization, leaving 16 randomized and 14 completing exenatide analysis. title: Teduglutide, a novel mucosally active analog of glucagon-like peptide-2 (GLP-2) for the treatment of moderate to severe Crohn's disease.

title: Role of fat hydrolysis in regulating glucagon-like Peptide-1 secretion.

outcomes_secondary: CCK release, plasma CCK concentrations

title: Improvement in peripheral glucose uptake after gastric bypass surgery is observed only after substantial weight loss has occurred and correlates with the magnitude of weight lost.

population: Morbidly obese nondiabetic patients aged 21-65 years meeting NIH criteria for bariatric surgery with BMI >40 or >35 kg/m2 with high-risk comorbidities, documented BMI >35 kg/m2 for more than 5 years, documented repeated failure of nonsurgical supervised weight loss programs. title: The effect of exenatide on lisinopril pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics in patients with hypertension.

title: Effects of meal size and composition on incretin, alpha-cell, and beta-cell responses.

title: Effects of liraglutide in the treatment of obesity: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study.

extraction_notes: Secondary outcomes not explicitly labeled as such but mentioned in findings. Open-label orlistat comparator (not blinded). 84-week open-label extension mentioned but not detailed in abstract.

title: Safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of albiglutide, a long-acting GLP-1-receptor agonist, in Japanese subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

title: A simulation of the comparative long-term effectiveness of liraglutide and glimepiride monotherapies in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

extraction_notes: This is a modeling/simulation study using the CORE Diabetes Model, not a primary clinical trial. Primary and secondary outcomes were not explicitly distinguished. The study projected long-term outcomes based on short-term trial data from LEAD-3.

title: Eating slowly increases the postprandial response of the anorexigenic gut hormones, peptide YY and glucagon-like peptide-1.

title: Endogenous glucagon-like peptide-1 slows gastric emptying in healthy subjects, attenuating postprandial glycemia.

population: Healthy fasted subjects

title: The effect of glucagon-like peptide-2 on arterial blood flow and cardiac parameters.

comparison: Isotonic saline subcutaneous injection (placebo)

extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=10 total, with 5 in placebo group). Single-blinded study design. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly designated in abstract.

title: Adding liraglutide to oral antidiabetic drug therapy: onset of treatment effects over time.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes from three phase 3 trials; prior treatment with metformin (LEAD-2), glimepiride (LEAD-1), or metformin plus rosiglitazone (LEAD-4) during run-in and titration period
intervention: Liraglutide 1.2 mg or 1.8 mg once-daily in combination with oral antidiabetic drugs (metformin, glimepiride, or metformin plus rosiglitazone)
comparison: Active comparator and/or placebo (specific comparators not detailed in abstract)
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c
outcomes_secondary: Fasting plasma glucose (FPG), body weight, systolic blood pressure (SBP), safety profile including nausea
extraction_notes: Pooled analysis of three phase 3 trials (LEAD-1, LEAD-2, LEAD-4); 0.6 mg liraglutide dose excluded from this analysis; specific active comparators not named in abstract; primary vs secondary outcome designation inferred from presentation order

title: Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic properties of taspoglutide, a once-weekly, human GLP-1 analogue, after single-dose administration in patients with Type 2 diabetes.
journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
population: Patients with Type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled with metformin (≤2 g/day)
intervention: Taspoglutide, single subcutaneous injection at 1 mg, 8 mg, or 30 mg doses
comparison: Placebo (single subcutaneous injection)
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes measured included: pharmacokinetic properties (plasma concentrations), pharmacodynamic properties (24-h blood glucose AUC, 5-h postprandial glucose AUC), safety and tolerability (adverse events). Study used sequential cohort design with 12 patients per taspoglutide dose cohort and 4 patients receiving placebo per cohort.

title: Exenatide compared with long-acting insulin to achieve glycaemic control with minimal weight gain in patients with type 2 diabetes: results of the Helping Evaluate Exenatide in patients with diabetes compared with Long-Acting insulin (HEELA) study.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes, body mass index >27 kg/m², inadequate glycaemic control (HbA1c 7.5–10.0%) despite treatment with stable doses of two or three oral antidiabetes drugs (metformin, sulphonylurea, and/or thiazolidinedione) for at least 3 months, and at least one cardiovascular risk factor (previous cardiovascular event, peripheral vascular disease, LDL >3.0 mmol/l, HDL <1.0 mmol/l for men or <1.3 mmol/l for women, triglyceride >1.7 mmol/l, systolic BP >130 mmHg, diastolic BP >80 mmHg, or increased waist circumference). comparison: Insulin glargine initiated at 10 IU/day subcutaneously once daily at bedtime, titrated weekly to target fasting plasma glucose ≤5.6 mmol/l, as add-on to existing oral antidiabetes drugs, for 26 weeks
outcomes_primary: Proportion of patients achieving composite endpoint of HbA1c ≤7.4% and weight gain ≤1 kg at 26 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Change in HbA1c from baseline; change in body weight from baseline; change in waist circumference; change in fasting serum glucose; proportion achieving fasting serum glucose ≤5.6 mmol/l; fasting serum lipid profile (total cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, triglycerides, LDL cholesterol); systolic and diastolic blood pressure; treatment-emergent adverse events; hypoglycaemic episodes (overall, nocturnal, severe); discontinuation rates
extraction_notes: Post hoc analysis with composite endpoint HbA1c ≤7.0% with weight gain ≤1 kg also performed. Open-label study design.

title: Weight loss with liraglutide, a once-daily human glucagon-like peptide-1 analogue for type 2 diabetes treatment as monotherapy or added to metformin, is primarily as a result of a reduction in fat tissue.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes, aged 18-80 years, body mass index ≤40 kg/m² (LEAD-2) or ≤45 kg/m² (LEAD-3), HbA1c 7.0-11.0%
intervention: Liraglutide 1.8, 1.2, or 0.6 mg/day once daily; LEAD-2: combined with metformin 1.5-2 g/day for 26 weeks; LEAD-3: liraglutide 1.8 or 1.2 mg/day monotherapy for 52 weeks
comparison: LEAD-2: placebo/metformin, glimepiride 4 mg/day/metformin; LEAD-3: glimepiride 8 mg/day
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified
outcomes_secondary: Total lean body tissue, fat tissue, fat percentage (LEAD-2 and LEAD-3); adipose tissue area (visceral and subcutaneous), hepatic steatosis assessed by liver-to-spleen attenuation ratio (LEAD-2 only)
extraction_notes: Primary outcome not explicitly designated. Two separate trials reported together (LEAD-2 and LEAD-3). Body composition outcomes listed but not clearly distinguished as primary vs secondary in the abstract.

title: Regulation of energy balance during long-term physical inactivity induced by bed rest with and without exercise training.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
population: Sixteen lean women
intervention: Combined aerobic/resistive exercise training concomitantly to 60-day bed rest
comparison: Control group subjected to strict 60-day bed rest without exercise training
outcomes_secondary: Body composition, spontaneous energy intake, hunger, total energy expenditure, fasting gut hormones
extraction_notes: Primary outcome not explicitly specified. This appears to be a physiological study using bed rest as a model for physical inactivity rather than a traditional clinical trial. Sample size is small (n=8 per group). Study design described as two groups but not explicitly stated as randomized.

title: Cardiovascular and metabolic effects of 48-h glucagon-like peptide-1 infusion in compensated chronic patients with heart failure.
journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
population: Patients without diabetes with compensated congestive heart failure due to ischemic heart disease, ejection fraction approximately 30%, New York Heart Association class II and III
intervention: GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) infusion at 0.7 pmol/kg/min for 48 hours
comparison: Placebo infusion for 48 hours
outcomes_primary: Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF)
outcomes_secondary: Diastolic function, tissue Doppler regional myocardial function, exercise testing, noninvasive cardiac output, brain natriuretic peptide (BNP), blood pressure, heart rate, metabolic parameters (insulin, glucose levels), body weight, hypoglycemic events
extraction_notes: Crossover design with randomized, double-blind methodology. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; LVEF appears to be the main cardiac outcome of interest based on study objectives.

title: Actions of prolonged ghrelin infusion on gastrointestinal transit and glucose homeostasis in humans.
population: Healthy male volunteers
intervention: Intravenous ghrelin infusion at 15 pmol kg(-1) min(-1) for 360 min (6 hours)
comparison: Intravenous saline infusion for 360 min
outcomes_primary: Gastric emptying rate, gastric half-emptying time
outcomes_secondary: Orocecal transit, colonic transit, postprandial plasma concentrations of glucose, insulin, glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), and peptide YY, insulinogenic index, in vitro gastrointestinal muscle contractility
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=12). Study described as evaluating effects but primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract; classification based on study aims and methods description.

title: Appetite suppression through smelling of dark chocolate correlates with changes in ghrelin in young women.
population: Female residents, BMI between 18 and 25 kg/m², young women
intervention: Smelling dark chocolate (85% cocoa) or melt-and-swallow 30 g chocolate (85% cocoa, 12.5 g sugar per 100g product)
comparison: Control group (no eating or smelling)
outcomes_primary: Appetite measured by visual analogue scale (VAS), correlation between appetite and gastrointestinal hormone levels (ghrelin, insulin, GLP-1, CCK)
outcomes_secondary: Glucose levels
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=12 total, n=6 per group in second session). Study design appears to be crossover for eating session and randomized parallel for smelling/control session. Duration of chocolate smelling not specified. Age range not explicitly stated beyond 'young women'.

title: Effects of exenatide plus rosiglitazone on beta-cell function and insulin sensitivity in subjects with type 2 diabetes on metformin.
population: Adults aged 18-75 years with type 2 diabetes, BMI 25-40 kg/m2, stable body weight for at least 6 months prior to screening, A1C 6.8-10.0%, stable dose of metformin for at least 6 weeks prior to screening, no treatment with any other antidiabetic medication, absence of islet cell autoantibodies
intervention: Exenatide 5 μg subcutaneous injection twice daily for first month then 10 μg twice daily thereafter, plus rosiglitazone 2 mg twice daily for first month then 4 mg twice daily thereafter, added to continued metformin regimen, for 20 weeks
comparison: Exenatide alone (5 μg twice daily for first month then 10 μg twice daily thereafter) plus continued metformin; Rosiglitazone alone (2 mg twice daily for first month then 4 mg twice daily thereafter) plus continued metformin
outcomes_primary: Glucose-potentiated arginine-stimulated incremental insulin area under the curve (ASI-iAUC) during hyperglycemic clamp test
outcomes_secondary: Glucose area under the curve from 15 to 180 min during meal challenge; A1C; fasting plasma glucose; fasting insulin; body weight; lipid parameters (total cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, triglycerides); 1st and 2nd phase insulin secretion; M value (insulin-stimulated glucose disposal during euglycemic clamp); disposition index; Matsuda whole-body insulin sensitivity index; insulinogenic index; adverse events including nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, pedal edema, hypoglycemia
extraction_notes: Open-label study design. A subset of 73 participants underwent clamp procedures while 137 total participants were randomized. Metformin dose not specified.

title: Effect of exenatide on heart rate and blood pressure in subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized pilot study.
population: Adults aged 18 to 75 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus on stable metformin (for 30 days) and/or thiazolidinedione (for 120 days), body mass index >25 and <40 kg/m2, hemoglobin A1c between 6.5 and 9.5%, stable body weight (≤10% variation for 3 months), stable antihypertensive regimens for at least 6 weeks. Exclusions: history of clinically significant cardiac disease or cardiac disease within one year, clinically significant arrhythmia, resting heart rate <60 or >100 beats/minute, repeated systolic BP >160 mm Hg or diastolic BP >100 mm Hg, current treatment with beta blockers
intervention: Subcutaneous exenatide 5 μg BID for 4 weeks followed by 10 μg BID for 8 weeks (total 12 weeks), administered within 60 minutes before morning and evening meals
comparison: Subcutaneous placebo BID for 12 weeks, administered within 60 minutes before morning and evening meals
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline in mean 24-hour heart rate at Week 12
outcomes_secondary: Hourly heart rate; change from baseline in 24-hour, daytime, and nighttime heart rate; change from baseline in 24-hour, daytime, and nighttime systolic blood pressure and diastolic blood pressure; rate pressure product; mean arterial pressure; hemoglobin A1c; body weight
extraction_notes: Per-protocol population used for primary analysis; intent-to-treat population used for secondary analyses. Study conducted at 5 centers in Canada and the Netherlands.

title: The fermentable fibre inulin increases postprandial serum short-chain fatty acids and reduces free-fatty acids and ghrelin in healthy subjects.
journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
population: Overnight fasted healthy subjects
intervention: 400 mL drink containing 56 g high-fructose corn syrup plus 24 g inulin
comparison: 400 mL drink containing 80 g high-fructose corn syrup (80HFCS); 400 mL drink containing 56 g high-fructose corn syrup (56HFCS)
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes measured included postprandial glucose, insulin, serum short-chain fatty acids (acetate, propionate, butyrate), free-fatty acids, and gut hormones (glucagon-like peptide-1, ghrelin). Study used randomized, single-blind, crossover design with n=12 subjects studied for 6 hours after test drink consumption, with standard lunch served at 4 hours.

title: A psyllium fiber-enriched meal strongly attenuates postprandial gastrointestinal peptide release in healthy young adults.
population: Healthy, nonobese young adult volunteers
intervention: Fiber-enriched meals with psyllium: (1) Low protein (2.6 g) and high soluble fiber (psyllium, 23.0 g); (2) High protein (18.4 g) and high fiber (23.0 g)

outcomes_primary: Postprandial serum insulin and plasma glucose, ghrelin, glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1), and peptide YY (PYY) concentrations measured for 2 hours following meals
outcomes_secondary: Hunger and satiety ratings
extraction_notes: Single-blind, randomized, cross-over study with 16 participants. All test meals were isoenergetic. Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in abstract.

title: Exenatide versus glibenclamide in patients with diabetes.

comparison: Glibenclamide 2.5 mg three times a day titrated to 5 mg three times a day
outcomes_primary: Body weight, glycemic control, beta-cell function, insulin resistance, inflammatory state
outcomes_secondary: Body mass index (BMI), glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), fasting plasma glucose (FPG), postprandial plasma glucose (PPG), fasting plasma insulin (FPI), homeostasis model assessment insulin resistance (HOMA-IR) index, homeostasis model assessment beta-cell function (HOMA-beta) index, plasma proinsulin (PPr), PPr/FPI ratio, resistin, retinol binding protein-4 (RBP-4), high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (Hs-CRP)
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; all measured outcomes listed under secondary with main stated objectives under primary

title: Addition of metformin to exogenous glucagon-like peptide-1 results in increased serum glucagon-like peptide-1 concentrations and greater glucose lowering in type 2 diabetes mellitus.
population: Subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus (n=10)
intervention: Metformin 1 g orally plus GLP-1 1.5 nmol/kg body weight subcutaneously (Metformin + GLP-1)
comparison: Metformin 1 g orally plus subcutaneous saline injection (Metformin alone); GLP-1 1.5 nmol/kg body weight subcutaneously plus placebo tablet (GLP-1 alone)
outcomes_primary: Plasma glucose response (AUC 0-180 minutes); serum insulin response (AUC); plasma DPP-4 activity (AUC); plasma active GLP-1 concentrations (AUC)
extraction_notes: Randomized crossover design study. Glucose was raised to 15 mmol/L by rapid intravenous infusion at 15 minutes post-treatment. Responses assessed over 3 hours. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Baseline characteristics reported (age 68.7 years, BMI 29.6 kg/m², HbA1c 7.0%) appear to be descriptive rather than inclusion criteria.

title: Do the actions of glucagon-like peptide-1 on gastric emptying, appetite, and food intake involve release of amylin in humans?
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
population: C-peptide and amylin-negative patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) and matched healthy controls
intervention: Near-physiological infusions of GLP-1, human amylin, or pramlintide for 270 min during and after a fixed meal, with glucose clamped between 6 and 9 mM
comparison: Saline infusion (placebo)
outcomes_primary: Gastric emptying measured using paracetamol
outcomes_secondary: Appetite measured using visual analog scales; food intake during subsequent ad libitum meal at 240 min; postprandial glucagon responses
extraction_notes: Study design is placebo-controlled, randomized, single-blinded, crossover. Sample sizes: 11 T1DM patients and 12 healthy controls. Multiple active interventions compared (GLP-1, amylin, pramlintide) but primary/secondary outcome designation not explicitly stated in abstract.

title: Efficacy and safety of the once-daily human GLP-1 analogue, liraglutide, vs glibenclamide monotherapy in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes.
population: Japanese subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus, inadequately controlled with diet therapy or oral antidiabetic drug monotherapy
intervention: Liraglutide, maximum planned dose 0.9 mg, once daily, subcutaneous (human GLP-1 analogue), for 24 weeks
comparison: Glibenclamide, maximum planned dose 2.5 mg/day, administered once or twice daily, before or after meals
outcomes_primary: HbA1c at 24 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Fasting plasma glucose, body weight change, hypoglycaemic episodes (minor and major), adverse events including gastrointestinal adverse events
extraction_notes: Primary outcome not explicitly labeled but HbA1c appears to be the primary efficacy endpoint based on non-inferiority/superiority design. Route of administration for liraglutide not explicitly stated but implied as subcutaneous injection.

title: Improvement of postprandial endothelial function after a single dose of exenatide in individuals with impaired glucose tolerance and recent-onset type 2 diabetes.
population: Adults aged 35-70 years with impaired glucose tolerance (IGT) or recent-onset (<3 years) diet-controlled type 2 diabetes (A1C <7.5%) and fasting triglycerides 1.6-5.6 mmol/l
intervention: Single subcutaneous injection of exenatide 10 μg administered in the lower right abdominal quadrant, given just before a standardized high-fat meal (600 kcal/m2; 45% fat [60% saturated], 40% carbohydrates, 15% protein)
comparison: Single subcutaneous injection of normal saline (placebo) administered in the lower right abdominal quadrant, given just before the same standardized high-fat meal
outcomes_primary: Postprandial endothelial function measured by reactive-hyperemia peripheral arterial tonometry (PAT) index at 210 min after meal ingestion
outcomes_secondary: Postprandial concentrations of glucose, insulin, and triglycerides measured at 120 and 240 min after meal ingestion
extraction_notes: Crossover design with 1-3 weeks washout between periods. Primary outcome not explicitly labeled as such but PAT index appears to be the main endpoint based on study objectives.

title: DURATION-1: exenatide once weekly produces sustained glycemic control and weight loss over 52 weeks.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes; 295 patients initially randomized, 258 patients entered the 22-week open-ended assessment phase
intervention: Exenatide once weekly (exenatide QW) 2 mg subcutaneous injection weekly for up to 52 weeks
comparison: Exenatide twice daily (exenatide BID) 5 μg subcutaneous injection for first 28 days then increased to 10 μg BID for remainder of initial 30-week period; patients switching from exenatide BID to exenatide QW after 30 weeks
outcomes_primary: A1C change from baseline; fasting plasma glucose (FPG)
outcomes_secondary: Body weight; blood pressure (systolic and diastolic); fasting lipid concentrations (total cholesterol, triglycerides); proportion of patients achieving A1C <7.0% and ≤6.5%; safety and tolerability including treatment-emergent adverse events, nausea, injection-site reactions, hypoglycemia incidence, antibodies to exenatide
extraction_notes: Open-label trial design; inclusion and exclusion criteria referenced as previously reported but not detailed in this text; primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in protocol description

title: Effects of exogenous glucagon-like peptide-1 on gastric emptying and glucose absorption in the critically ill: relationship to glycemia.
population: Mechanically ventilated critically ill patients in the intensive care unit, without known diabetes
intervention: Intravenous glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) at 1.2 pmol/kg/min, infused from -30 to 330 minutes, with administration of 100 mL liquid nutrient (1 kcal/mL) containing 100 microg 13C-octanoic acid and 3 grams 3-O-methyl-glucose at time 0
comparison: Placebo infusion (same timing and nutrient administration protocol)
outcomes_primary: Gastric emptying (measured by gastric emptying coefficient calculated from exhaled 13CO2), glucose absorption (measured by serum 3-O-methyl-glucose concentrations), glycemia (blood glucose response to meal)
outcomes_secondary: Plasma insulin concentrations, insulin/glucose ratio, plasma glucagon concentrations
extraction_notes: Crossover design with patients studied on consecutive days. Sample size n=25. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; classification based on study objectives stated.

title: Switching to once-daily liraglutide from twice-daily exenatide further improves glycemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes using oral agents.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled (A1C 7–11%) with maximally tolerated stable doses of metformin, sulfonylurea, or both for ≥3 months
intervention: Switching from 10 μg twice-daily exenatide to 1.8 mg once-daily liraglutide (with weekly dose escalation: 0.6 mg once daily for 1 week, then 1.2 mg for 1 week, then 1.8 mg maintenance dose) for 14-week extension period
comparison: Continuation of 1.8 mg once-daily liraglutide (patients originally randomized to liraglutide in 26-week LEAD-6 trial)
outcomes_primary: Change in A1C from week 26 to week 40
outcomes_secondary: Change in fasting plasma glucose (FPG); change in body weight; change in systolic blood pressure (SBP); change in homeostasis model of β-cell function (HOMA-B); proportion of patients reaching A1C targets; postprandial glucose; diastolic blood pressure; fasting insulin; fasting C-peptide; proinsulin-to-insulin ratio; homeostasis model assessment–insulin resistance (HOMA-IR); adverse events; hypoglycemia (major and minor); nausea; diarrhea; vomiting; calcitonin levels
extraction_notes: This is a 14-week nonrandomized extension of the 26-week LEAD-6 randomized trial. Treatment groups were not compared statistically; only within-group changes were analyzed. Primary outcome not explicitly designated but A1C appears to be the main efficacy endpoint based on presentation.

title: Effects of exenatide and lifestyle modification on body weight and glucose tolerance in obese subjects with and without pre-diabetes.
population: Obese adult subjects with BMI ≥30 kg/m2, with normal glucose tolerance (NGT), impaired glucose tolerance (IGT), or impaired fasting glucose (IFG). IGT defined as fasting glucose <7 mmol/l and 2-h postprandial glucose ≥7.8 and <11.1 mmol/l. IFG defined as fasting glucose 6.1–6.9 mmol/l and 2-h postprandial glucose <7.8 mmol/l. intervention: Exenatide 10 μg subcutaneous injection (with a 4-week 5 μg dose-initiation period) administered before morning and evening meals for 24 weeks, combined with structured program of diet and physical activity (lifestyle intervention)
comparison: Placebo administered before morning and evening meals for 24 weeks, combined with structured program of diet and physical activity (lifestyle intervention)
outcomes_primary: Change in body weight from baseline
outcomes_secondary: Change in glucose concentrations, change in lipid concentrations, change in A1C, change in blood pressure, change in physical activity, change in food intake, normalization of glucose tolerance in subjects with IGT or IFG, proportion achieving ≥5% body weight reduction
extraction_notes: Route of administration for exenatide not explicitly stated in abstract but implied subcutaneous based on standard exenatide administration. 1-week single-blind placebo lead-in period preceded randomization. Follow-up visit conducted 4 weeks after study completion.

title: The role of adjunctive exenatide therapy in pediatric type 1 diabetes.
population: Adolescents aged 13-22 years with type 1 diabetes (antibody positive) for ≥1 year, using multiple daily injections or insulin pump, BMI <90th percentile for age, hemoglobin >12 g/dl, hemoglobin A1C <8.5%, with minimal or no endogenous C-peptide response to meals. Exclusion: pregnant/lactating females, concomitant medications affecting blood glucose concentrations
