outcomes_primary: Glucose stimulated insulin release, incretin hormones (GLP-1, GIP), oxidative stress markers, cell adhesion molecules measured during oral glucose load
outcomes_secondary: Glucose (fasting, 2-h, AUC), insulin, C-peptide, total antioxidant status, F2-isoprostane, interleukin-6, ICAM-1, E-selectin; areas under the curve at 45, 60, and 120 minutes
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; all outcomes listed under Methods. Study design is randomized clinical trial but blinding not specified.

title: Safety, tolerability and sustained weight loss over 2 years with the once-daily human GLP-1 analog, liraglutide.
population: Adults aged 18–65 years with stable weight, body mass index 30–40 kg/m², fasting plasma glucose <7 mmol/L (126 mg/dL), without type 1 or 2 diabetes mellitus, drug-induced obesity, use of weight-lowering pharmacotherapy or participation in weight-control study within preceding 3 months, surgical obesity treatment, or major medical conditions
intervention: Once-daily subcutaneous liraglutide at doses of 1.2 mg, 1.8 mg, 2.4 mg, or 3.0 mg, administered by evening injection in abdomen or thigh, starting at 0.6 mg/day with weekly dose escalation over 4 weeks, plus diet (500 kcal deficit/day, approximately 30% energy from fat, 20% protein, 50% carbohydrates) and exercise counseling. Safety assessments: adverse events, standard laboratory tests, serum liraglutide antibodies, serum calcitonin
extraction_notes: 20-week trial data previously published; this report focuses on 1-year and 2-year results. Complex study design with sponsor unblinded at 20 weeks and all participants/investigators unblinded at 1 year. Placebo comparison only available for first year. Non-uniform timing of dose switch from 2.4 mg to 3.0 mg during year 2 due to variable ethics committee approval timing

title: Effects of exenatide on measures of β-cell function after 3 years in metformin-treated patients with type 2 diabetes.
population: Metformin-treated patients with type 2 diabetes, age 30-75 years, HbA1c 6.5-9.5%, BMI 25-40 kg/m2, metformin treatment at stable dose for at least 2 months, no other blood glucose-lowering agents within 3 months prior to screening
intervention: Exenatide initiated at 5 µg twice daily injected 15 min before breakfast and dinner for 4 weeks, then increased to 10 µg twice daily, titrated to maximum 20 µg three times daily or maximum tolerated dose based on HbA1c levels, for 3 years (168 weeks), in addition to ongoing metformin treatment

outcomes_primary: β-cell function measured as first-phase glucose-stimulated C-peptide secretion adjusted for M value (disposition index)
outcomes_secondary: HbA1c, fasting plasma glucose, body weight, insulin sensitivity (M value measured by euglycemic hyperinsulinemic clamp), second-phase C-peptide secretion, arginine-stimulated C-peptide secretion, adverse events including gastrointestinal symptoms and hypoglycemia
extraction_notes: Extension study of original 1-year trial; 69 patients originally randomized, 46 entered extension phase, 36 completed 3-year treatment period (EXE n=16, GLAR n=20). Clamp measurements performed after 4-week off-drug periods.

title: Exenatide reduces reperfusion injury in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction.
population: Patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) and Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) flow 0/1 treated with primary percutaneous coronary intervention (pPCI)
intervention: Exenatide administered intravenously, commenced 15 minutes before intervention and maintained for 6 hours after the procedure
comparison: Placebo (saline) administered intravenously with same timing
outcomes_primary: Salvage index calculated from myocardial area at risk (AAR) measured in the acute phase and final infarct size measured 90 ± 21 days after pPCI by cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR)
outcomes_secondary: Infarct size in relation to AAR; absolute infarct size; left ventricular function; 30-day clinical events; adverse effects
extraction_notes: Exenatide dose not specified in abstract

title: Postprandial glucose, insulin and glucagon-like peptide 1 responses to sucrose ingested with berries in healthy subjects.

outcomes_primary: Postprandial glucose concentrations (capillary and venous plasma), serum insulin concentrations, glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) response
outcomes_secondary: Maximum increases of capillary and venous glucose and insulin concentrations, glycaemic profile
extraction_notes: Study design: randomised, single-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study. Measurements taken at baseline and at 15, 30, 45, 60, 90 and 120 min after meal consumption. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; classification based on emphasis in text.

title: Intraduodenal administration of intact pea protein effectively reduces food intake in both lean and obese male subjects.
population: Healthy male subjects, 10 lean (BMI 18-25 kg/m2) and 10 obese (BMI >30 kg/m2), with no diabetes, no gastrointestinal diseases, and no medical treatment

outcomes_secondary: Appetite profile (VAS questionnaire measuring hunger, fullness, satiety, thirst, desire to eat); plasma GLP-1, CCK, PYY, and Ghrelin concentrations over 2-hour period; well-being symptoms (headache, nausea, stomach-ache, diarrhea)
extraction_notes: Single-blind, randomized controlled crossover design with 1 week washout between visits. Only male subjects included due to concerns about hormonal fluctuations in females. Primary outcome not explicitly labeled as such in the text.

title: Exenatide decreases hepatic fibroblast growth factor 21 resistance in non-alcoholic fatty liver disease in a mouse model of obesity and in a randomised controlled trial.
population: Type 2 diabetes mellitus patients aged 30-70 years on diet and/or metformin therapy with stable body weight for at least 3 months, fasting plasma glucose 7.0-14.5 mmol/l, excluding patients with ALT or AST greater than 2.5 times upper limit of normal, and those who received insulin, sulfonylureas, sitagliptin, exenatide or thiazolidinedione within previous 3 months

outcomes_secondary: Body weight change

title: A thorough QT study to evaluate the effects of singledose exenatide 10 μg on cardiac repolarization in healthy subjects.

title: Pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, safety, and tolerability of JNJ-38431055, a novel GPR119 receptor agonist and potential antidiabetes agent, in healthy male subjects.
population: Healthy male volunteers
intervention: JNJ-38431055 single oral doses (2.5-800 mg), administered as oral suspension formulation
comparison: Placebo
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Food effect on pharmacokinetics was also evaluated. This was a phase 1 study in healthy subjects, not diabetic patients.

title: Changes in postprandial gut hormones after metabolic surgery: a comparison of gastric bypass and sleeve gastrectomy.
journal: Surgery for obesity and related diseases : official journal of the American Society for Bariatric Surgery
population: Patients with low body mass index and type 2 diabetes mellitus undergoing metabolic surgery; participants from a previous randomized trial

comparison: Laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (SG)
outcomes_secondary: Glucose homeostasis, postprandial gut hormones (acyl ghrelin, des-acyl ghrelin, cholecystokinin, resistin, obestatin, gastric inhibitory peptide, glucagon-like peptide-1, leptin), T2DM remission, weight loss, waist circumference, glucose levels, hemoglobin A1c, insulin resistance
extraction_notes: Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in abstract. Sample size was 16 per group at follow-up, with 13 per group completing gut hormone evaluation at 2 years. This appears to be a follow-up study of participants from a previous randomized trial.

title: The gut hormones PYY 3-36 and GLP-1 7-36 amide reduce food intake and modulate brain activity in appetite centers in humans.
population: Healthy right-handed subjects, age 21-36 years, body mass index 18.3-25.1 kg/m2. Exclusion criteria: smoking, substance abuse, eating disorders, regular medication (except oral contraceptives), pregnancy, medical or psychiatric illness

Primary outcomes not explicitly designated as primary/secondary in text; classification based on study objectives and discussion emphasis.

title: Effects of variations in duodenal glucose load on glycaemic, insulin, and incretin responses in type 2 diabetes.
journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
population: Males with well-controlled Type 2 diabetes, managed by diet alone

comparison: Saline control infusion; healthy controls
outcomes_primary: Blood glucose responses, plasma insulin responses, plasma GLP-1 responses, plasma GIP responses
extraction_notes: Single-blind randomized crossover design. Sample size is 8 males with Type 2 diabetes; sample size for healthy controls not specified in abstract. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract.

title: Exenatide exerts a potent antiinflammatory effect.

population: Patients with type 2 diabetes; 24 patients prospectively randomized
intervention: Exenatide 10 μg injected subcutaneously twice daily for 12 weeks; also single dose of exenatide 5 μg for acute effect assessment
comparison: Placebo injected subcutaneously twice daily for 12 weeks; single dose placebo for acute effect assessment
outcomes_primary: Antiinflammatory effect measured by reactive oxygen species generation, nuclear factor-κB binding, and mRNA expression of inflammatory markers (TNFα, IL-1β, JNK-1, TLR-2, TLR-4, SOCS-3) in mononuclear cells
outcomes_secondary: Fasting blood glucose, glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c), free fatty acids, plasma concentrations of monocyte chemoattractant protein-1, matrix metalloproteinase-9, serum amyloid A, and IL-6; body weight
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the abstract; classification based on stated objective focusing on antiinflammatory effect. Baseline characteristics (age, BMI, HbA1c) reported as group means but not specified as inclusion/exclusion criteria.

title: Short-term exenatide treatment leads to significant weight loss in a subset of obese women without diabetes.
population: Obese nondiabetic women aged 18-70 years with BMI 28-40 kg/m2, stable weight within 6 months of screening. Exclusion criteria: type 1 or type 2 diabetes, uncontrolled hypertension or dyslipidemia, antiobesity medication within 1 year, history of bariatric surgery, previous exenatide treatment
intervention: Exenatide 5 μg subcutaneous injection twice daily (before breakfast and supper) for 2 weeks, then increased to 10 μg twice daily, for 16 weeks total treatment period

extraction_notes: Crossover design with 3-week washout period between two 16-week treatment periods. No lifestyle intervention. Study explicitly states it was a 35-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover study.

title: Effects of vildagliptin on postprandial markers of bone resorption and calcium homeostasis in recently diagnosed, well-controlled type 2 diabetes patients.
population: Drug-naïve patients with type 2 diabetes, recently diagnosed, well-controlled
intervention: Vildagliptin 100 mg once daily for 1 year
comparison: Placebo for 1 year
outcomes_primary: Postprandial serum cross-linked C-terminal telopeptide (s-CTx) concentrations
outcomes_secondary: Fasting serum alkaline phosphatase, serum calcium, serum phosphate
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly labeled; categorization based on emphasis in abstract. Exact glycemic criteria for 'well-controlled' or 'mild hyperglycemia' not specified.

title: Comparisons of the effects of 12-week administration of miglitol and voglibose on the responses of plasma incretins after a mixed meal in Japanese type 2 diabetic patients.
population: Japanese type 2 diabetic patients
intervention: Miglitol (alpha-glucosidase inhibitor) administered for 12 weeks
comparison: Voglibose (alpha-glucosidase inhibitor) administered for 12 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) levels, gastric inhibitory polypeptide (GIP) levels, plasma glucose, serum insulin, body weight, responses during 2-hour meal tolerance test
extraction_notes: Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in abstract. Sample sizes: 26 patients assigned to miglitol, 24 patients assigned to voglibose. Doses, routes, and frequencies of drug administration not specified.

title: Effect of additional treatment with EXenatide in patients with an Acute Myocardial Infarction (EXAMI): study protocol for a randomized controlled trial.
population: Patients with acute ST elevation myocardial infarction successfully treated with primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI)

outcomes_primary: Myocardial infarct size as a percentage of the area at risk, measured by MRI with delayed enhancement at 4 months (infarct size) and T2 weighted images at 3-7 days (area at risk)
outcomes_secondary: Left ventricular function, cardiac function assessed by echocardiography, major cardiovascular events (death, myocardial re-infarction, coronary artery bypass grafting, repeat PCI), cardiac arrhythmias, heart failure, repeat coronary angiography, stroke, hospital admission
extraction_notes: This is a study protocol, not results. Standard treatment includes aspirin, heparin, clopidogrel, aggressive lipid-lowering treatment, ACE inhibitor or ARB, and beta-blocker. Target enrollment is 108 patients. Detailed inclusion/exclusion criteria referenced in Table 1 but not fully provided in text.

title: Exenatide as a weight-loss therapy in extreme pediatric obesity: a randomized, controlled pilot study.
population: Children and adolescents aged 8-19 years with extreme obesity (BMI ≥1.2 times the 95th percentile or BMI ≥35 kg/m2); exclusion criteria: diabetes mellitus (type 1 or 2), use of weight-loss medication within 3 months of screening, initiation of new drug therapy within 30 days of screening, BMI ≥55 kg/m2, history of bariatric surgery, obesity from established genetic cause or known syndrome (e.g., Prader-Willi)
intervention: Exenatide 5 mcg twice daily by subcutaneous injection for 1 month, then uptitrated to 10 mcg twice daily for remaining 2 months (3-month drug phase total), plus clinically-offered lifestyle modification
comparison: Clinically-offered lifestyle modification alone (control phase); crossover design with participants randomized to phase order (control-drug or drug-control) without washout period
outcomes_primary: Change in body mass index (BMI)

extraction_notes: Open-label study design (no blinding); crossover design without washout period; actual enrolled age range was 9-16 years though inclusion criteria specified 8-19 years; lifestyle modification intervention varied by center

title: Effect of bile acid sequestrants on glucose metabolism, hepatic de novo lipogenesis, and cholesterol and bile acid kinetics in type 2 diabetes: a randomised controlled study.
population: Participants with type 2 diabetes, HbA1c 6.7-10.0% (50-86 mmol/mol), fasting glucose <16.7 mmol/l, fasting triacylglycerols <3.9 mmol/l, LDL-cholesterol >1.55 mmol/l, treated with diet and exercise, sulfonylurea, metformin or a combination thereof
intervention: Colesevelam 3.75 g/day for 12 weeks
comparison: Placebo for 12 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline in glucose kinetics
outcomes_secondary: Fasting and postprandial glucose pathways, lipid pathways, bile acid pathways measured using stable isotope techniques; plasma glucose, insulin, total glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), total glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), glucagon, and fibroblast growth factor-19 (FGF-19) concentrations during fasting and following meal tolerance test; HbA1c; hepatic de novo lipogenesis; cholesterol synthesis; bile acid synthesis; HOMA-beta cell function; HOMA-insulin resistance; gluconeogenesis; endogenous glucose production; glycogenolysis; glycolytic disposal of oral glucose; fasting plasma glucose clearance; appearance rate of oral glucose
extraction_notes: Secondary outcomes were not explicitly labeled as such in the abstract; outcomes listed are those measured as stated in methods section

title: Preventive effects of exenatide on endothelial dysfunction induced by ischemia-reperfusion injury via KATP channels.
population: Healthy volunteers
intervention: Subcutaneous exenatide 10 μg administered 30 minutes before ischemia-reperfusion injury protocol (15 minutes of ischemia at the level of the brachial artery followed by 15 minutes of reperfusion)
comparison: Placebo (crossover design with 7-day washout period); separate protocol with glibenclamide (glyburide 5 mg) pretreatment
outcomes_primary: Endothelium-dependent flow-mediated dilatation (FMD) of the radial artery measured before and after ischemia-reperfusion injury
outcomes_secondary: Pre-IR radial artery diameter; baseline radial artery diameter after IR injury
extraction_notes: Sample size n=20 for main protocol, n=7 for glibenclamide sub-protocol. Double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover design. Primary outcome not explicitly labeled as such but FMD appears to be the main outcome measure.

title: Dosing rationale for liraglutide in type 2 diabetes mellitus: a pharmacometric assessment.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus
intervention: Liraglutide (GLP-1 receptor agonist) as adjunct treatment to diet and exercise; specific doses not stated in abstract
comparison: Not explicitly stated
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly stated
outcomes_secondary: Exposure-response relationships for fasting plasma glucose, hemoglobin A1c, and calcitonin; variability in exposure across demographic subgroups
extraction_notes: This is a pharmacometric/regulatory review article rather than a primary clinical trial. No specific dosing regimens, comparators, or formal primary/secondary outcome designations are provided in the abstract. The outcomes mentioned are analytical endpoints for pharmacometric assessment rather than clinical trial outcomes.

title: Efficacy and safety of exenatide once weekly versus metformin, pioglitazone, and sitagliptin used as monotherapy in drug-naive patients with type 2 diabetes (DURATION-4): a 26-week double-blind study.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes, drug-naive (not treated with any antihyperglycemic drug for >7 days within 3 months of screening), suboptimally treated with diet and exercise, HbA1c 7.1–11.0%, BMI 23–45 kg/m2, history of stable weight
intervention: Exenatide once weekly (EQW) 2.0 mg subcutaneous injection + oral placebo, administered weekly for 26 weeks
comparison: Metformin 2,000 mg/day oral (titrated up to 2,500 mg/day based on glycemic control) + subcutaneous placebo; Pioglitazone 45 mg/day oral (titrated to maximum-tolerated dose) + subcutaneous placebo; Sitagliptin 100 mg/day oral + subcutaneous placebo
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline at 26 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of patients achieving HbA1c <7.0% and ≤6.5%; change in fasting serum glucose; seven-point self-monitoring of blood glucose (SMBG); change in body weight; change in serum lipids; homeostasis model assessment of pancreatic β-cell function (HOMA-B) and insulin sensitivity (HOMA-S); safety and tolerability (adverse events, clinical laboratory assessments, vital signs, hypoglycemia, antibodies to exenatide); patient-reported outcomes including Impact of Weight on Quality of Life Questionnaire-Lite (IWQOL-Lite), Binge Eating Scale (BES), Diabetes Treatment Satisfaction Questionnaire (DTSQ), and EuroQol-5 dimensions (EQ-5D)

title: The role of the stomach in the control of appetite and the secretion of satiation peptides.

population: Healthy subjects
intervention: Rapid intragastric load of glucose or mixed liquid meal
comparison: Continuous intraduodenal infusion of glucose or mixed liquid meal at 3 kcal/min
extraction_notes: This appears to be a mechanistic/physiological study rather than a clinical trial. Primary and secondary outcomes are not explicitly designated. Outcomes measured include appetite, plasma GLP-1 levels, plasma PYY levels, and plasma ghrelin levels. Sample size not specified. Study design not clearly stated as randomized controlled trial.

title: Comparative effects of variations in duodenal glucose load on glycemic, insulinemic, and incretin responses in healthy young and older subjects.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
population: Healthy young subjects (age approximately 22 years) and healthy older subjects (age approximately 69 years), males and females
intervention: Intraduodenal infusions of glucose at 1, 2, or 3 kcal/min for 60 minutes
comparison: Intraduodenal infusion of saline for 60 minutes; comparison between healthy young and older subjects
outcomes_secondary: Blood glucose, serum insulin, plasma incretin hormones (glucagon-like peptide-1 and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide), insulin resistance (homeostatic model assessment), β-cell function corrected for insulin sensitivity
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; all outcomes listed under secondary. Study design is double-blinded and randomized crossover comparing multiple glucose load rates against saline control.

title: Effects of intravenous exenatide in type 2 diabetic patients with congestive heart failure: a double-blind, randomised controlled clinical trial of efficacy and safety.
population: Male and female patients aged 18-80 years with type 2 diabetes and congestive heart failure (ejection fraction ≤35%, New York Heart Association functional class III or IV)
intervention: Intravenous exenatide 0.12 pmol/kg/min infusion for 6 hours
comparison: Intravenous placebo infusion for 6 hours
outcomes_primary: Increase in cardiac index (CI) of ≥20% or decrease in pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) of ≥20%
outcomes_secondary: Tolerability and safety of exenatide infusion
extraction_notes: Crossover trial design with 18-hour washout period. Although eligibility included male and female patients, only 20 male patients participated in the trial.

title: Satiety scores and satiety hormone response after sucrose-sweetened soft drink compared with isocaloric semi-skimmed milk and with non-caloric soft drink: a controlled trial.
population: Obese individuals
intervention: 500 ml of sugar-sweetened soft drink (regular cola: 900 kJ)
comparison: 500 ml semi-skimmed milk (950 kJ); 500 ml aspartame-sweetened soft drink (diet cola: 7.5 kJ); 500 ml water
outcomes_primary: Subjective appetite scores (fullness, hunger); appetite-regulating hormone concentrations (ghrelin, GLP-1, GIP) measured at baseline and continuously 4 hours post intake
outcomes_secondary: Ad libitum energy intake measured 4 hours after intake of test drinks; total energy intake (ad libitum energy intake plus energy intake from the drink)
extraction_notes: Crossover trial design. Sample size of 24 participants. Primary versus secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract; classification based on presentation order.

title: Beverage consumption, appetite, and energy intake: what did you expect?
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
population: Healthy adults
intervention: Oral liquid and solid preloads with cognitive manipulation of perceived gastric form: oral liquid/perceived gastric liquid, oral liquid/perceived gastric solid, oral solid/perceived gastric liquid, or oral solid/perceived gastric solid (all preloads designed to present a liquid gastric challenge)
comparison: 4-arm crossover design comparing all four preload conditions against each other
outcomes_secondary: Appetite (hunger and fullness sensations), gastric-emptying time, orocecal transit time, endocrine responses (insulin, glucagon-like peptide 1, ghrelin), total energy intake
extraction_notes: Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in the abstract. This is a mechanistic study examining cognitive and sensory contributions to postingestive responses rather than a traditional therapeutic trial.

title: Addition of liraglutide in patients with Type 2 diabetes well controlled on metformin monotherapy improves several markers of vascular function.
journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
population: Patients with Type 2 diabetes, age 30-65 years, pretreated with metformin on a stable dosage, HbA1c < 53 mmol/mol (7.0%)
intervention: Addition of liraglutide to metformin, 1.2 mg for 6 weeks then 1.8 mg for 12 weeks
comparison: Continued metformin monotherapy
outcomes_primary: Laboratory markers of vascular and endothelial function (asymmetric dimethylarginine, E-selectin, plasminogen activator inhibitor 1, intact proinsulin, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, monocyte chemotactic protein 1, vascular cell adhesion molecule), retinal microvascular endothelial function (response to flicker light), arterial stiffness parameters
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the abstract. Total study duration unclear - mentions 6 weeks at 1.2 mg and 12 weeks at 1.8 mg but relationship between these timepoints is ambiguous.

title: Impaired incretin-induced amplification of insulin secretion after glucose homeostatic dysregulation in healthy subjects.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
population: Healthy Caucasian males without risk factors for type 2 diabetes
intervention: Glucose homeostatic dysregulation intervention for 12 days consisting of: high-calorie diet, sedentary lifestyle, and prednisolone 37.5 mg once daily oral administration
comparison: Pre-intervention vs post-intervention measurements; during hyperglycemic clamps: GIP infusion vs GLP-1 infusion vs saline infusion (physiological doses)
outcomes_primary: Insulinotropic effect of GIP and GLP-1 measured using hyperglycemic clamps
outcomes_secondary: Insulin resistance assessed by homeostatic model assessment; glucose tolerance assessed by area under curve for plasma glucose during 75-g oral glucose tolerance test
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=10). This is an experimental study inducing glucose homeostatic dysregulation rather than a traditional treatment trial. Route of prednisolone administration not explicitly stated but implied oral.

title: Investigation of the haemodynamic effects of exenatide in healthy male subjects.
population: Healthy male volunteers
intervention: Single 10 µg subcutaneous injection of exenatide
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Haemodynamic measurements including heart rate, cardiac output, total peripheral resistance, blood pressure (measured using Finometer, venous occlusion plethysmography and Doppler ultrasound)
outcomes_secondary: Urinary sodium:creatinine excretion ratio
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; classification based on presentation order and study focus on haemodynamic effects

title: Effects of JNJ-38431055, a novel GPR119 receptor agonist, in randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled studies in subjects with type 2 diabetes.
population: Male and female subjects aged 25-60 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed 6 months to 10 years before screening, with mean body mass index between 22 and 39.9 kg/m2
intervention: JNJ-38431055 100 mg single dose, JNJ-38431055 500 mg single dose, or JNJ-38431055 500 mg once daily for 14 consecutive days
comparison: Placebo; Sitagliptin 100 mg single dose (positive control in single-dose study)
outcomes_primary: Effects on stimulated plasma glucose, insulin, C-peptide and incretin concentrations
extraction_notes: Pre-specified outcomes were listed but not explicitly designated as primary vs secondary. Two separate experiments were conducted: a single-dose crossover study (n=25) and a multiple-dose parallel design study (n=32). Pharmacokinetics, safety and tolerability were also stated objectives.

title: Pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and tolerability of a generic formulation of exenatide: a randomized, open-label, single- and multiple-dose study in healthy Chinese volunteers.
population: Healthy Chinese volunteers, 24 subjects
intervention: Generic formulation of exenatide, subcutaneous administration, single dose of 5 μg or 10 μg followed by twice daily dosing on days 2-4 and once on day 5
comparison: 5 μg versus 10 μg dose groups (dose-escalating design); no placebo or active comparator
outcomes_primary: Pharmacokinetic parameters (Cmax, AUC0-t, AUC0-∞, tmax, t1/2)
outcomes_secondary: Pharmacodynamics (serum glucose concentrations), tolerability (physical examination, vital signs, laboratory analysis, adverse events), effect of gender on pharmacokinetics
extraction_notes: Open-label study design; no placebo control group; primary versus secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract

title: Anorexigenic effects of miglitol in concert with the alterations of gut hormone secretion and gastric emptying in healthy subjects.
journal: Hormone and metabolic research = Hormon- und Stoffwechselforschung = Hormones et metabolisme
population: Healthy volunteers
intervention: Miglitol 50 mg administered before test meal; additional substudy with miglitol 50 mg three times daily for 1 week
comparison: No miglitol (control condition in crossover design)
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly designated. Outcomes assessed included: glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) levels, peptide YY (PYY) levels, ghrelin levels, appetite scores using visual analogue scales (VAS), and gastric emptying rate (GER) measured using breath 13CO2 appearance. Study included 20 subjects total, with GER measured in subset of 10 subjects and 1-week administration in 12 subjects. Open-label design.

title: The effect of exenatide and erythromycin on postprandial symptoms and their relation to gastric functions.
population: Healthy volunteers
intervention: Exenatide (dose, route, frequency, and duration not specified)
comparison: Placebo; Erythromycin
outcomes_primary: Postprandial symptoms; Gastric volumes (fasting and postprandial) measured by 3-dimensional single photon emission computed tomography
outcomes_secondary: Electrogastrography (EGG) rhythm; Ratio of postprandial over fasting gastric volume
extraction_notes: Crossover design with 3-way treatment and 1-week intervals between studies. Doses, routes, frequencies, and durations for exenatide and erythromycin not specified. Sample size of 10 participants. Primary versus secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract.

title: Metabolic and hormonal changes after laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and sleeve gastrectomy: a randomized, prospective trial.
population: Non-diabetic morbidly obese patients undergoing bariatric surgery; subgroup of the Swiss Multicenter Bypass or Sleeve Study (SM-BOSS); BMI approximately 44-48 kg/m²
intervention: Laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (LRYGB) with small gastric pouch, 25-mm circular pouch-jejunostomy to 150-cm antecolic Roux limb, and 50 cm biliopancreatic limb exclusion
comparison: Laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG) performed along a 35-F bougie from the angle of His to approximately 3-4 cm oral to the pylorus
outcomes_primary: Metabolic and hormonal changes including weight loss, BMI, glucose homeostasis (HOMA index), and gut hormone profiles (cholecystokinin, ghrelin, glucagon-like peptide 1, peptide YY) measured at fasting and after standardized test meal
outcomes_secondary: Fasting glucose, fasting insulin, excessive BMI loss (EBMIL), area under the plasma concentration time profiles (AUC) and maximum plasma concentrations (Cmax) for hormones
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the text; outcomes listed represent the main focus of the investigation. Study is described as a subgroup analysis from an ongoing larger trial (SM-BOSS). Sample size small (n=23 total).

title: Safety and efficacy of once-weekly exenatide compared with insulin glargine titrated to target in patients with type 2 diabetes over 84 weeks.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes failing to maintain sufficient glycemic control using metformin alone or in combination with sulfonylurea
intervention: Exenatide once weekly (EQW) 2 mg subcutaneous injection added to existing oral blood glucose-lowering regimen
comparison: Insulin glargine (IG) once daily, starting at 10 IU/day, titrated to target fasting glucose of 4.0-5.5 mmol/L using the INITIATE dosing algorithm, added to existing oral blood glucose-lowering regimen
outcomes_primary: Change in A1C from baseline to study treatment end point
outcomes_secondary: Time to failure to maintain glycemic control (defined as time from randomization to first visit after week 18 when A1C was ≥7.0%); proportions of patients achieving A1C <7.0% and ≤6.5%; change in body weight; fasting serum glucose; self-monitored blood glucose; fasting serum lipids; incidence of hypoglycemia; adverse events; exploratory measures including urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, homeostasis model assessment of β-cell function, waist and hip circumference
extraction_notes: This is an 84-week extension study of a previously reported 26-week phase 3 trial. Open-label design. Data collected after treatment regimen changes at 48 weeks or after (other than IG titration) were excluded from analyses.

title: A randomized non-inferiority study comparing the addition of exenatide twice daily to sitagliptin or switching from sitagliptin to exenatide twice daily in patients with type 2 diabetes experiencing inadequate glycaemic control on metformin and sitagliptin.
journal: Diabetic medicine : a journal of the British Diabetic Association
population: Patients with Type 2 diabetes experiencing inadequate glycaemic control on metformin and sitagliptin
intervention: Exenatide twice daily plus sitagliptin and metformin (ADD group)

outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 20 (non-inferiority margin 0.4%)
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of patients reaching HbA1c target <7.0% (<53 mmol/mol); fasting serum glucose; daily mean postprandial self-monitored blood glucose; incidence of nausea and vomiting
extraction_notes: Non-inferiority design with 0.4% margin. Treatment duration was 20 weeks. Sample sizes: SWITCH n=127, ADD n=128.

title: Effects of diet soda on gut hormones in youths with diabetes.
population: Youths aged 12-25 years with type 1 diabetes (n=9), type 2 diabetes (n=10), or healthy controls (n=25). Type 2 diabetes subjects were overweight or obese (BMI >85th centile for age, or >25 kg/m2 after age 20 years) and lacked classic family history suggestive of monogenic diabetes.
intervention: 240 mL cola-flavored caffeine-free diet soda (Diet Rite Cola, containing sucralose and acesulfame-K) ingested orally 10 minutes before a 75-g oral glucose load

outcomes_secondary: Glucose AUC, C-peptide AUC, glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide (GIP) AUC, peptide Tyr-Tyr (PYY) AUC measured over 180 minutes
extraction_notes: Randomized cross-over design. Glucose, insulin, and GLP-1 results from 22 of 25 healthy subjects previously reported. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; GLP-1 AUC inferred as primary based on study focus. This was described as an exploratory study without adjustment for multiple comparisons.

title: Metabolic effects of short-term GLP-1 treatment in insulin resistant heart failure patients.
journal: Experimental and clinical endocrinology & diabetes : official journal, German Society of Endocrinology [and] German Diabetes Association

title: Efficacy and safety of the once-daily GLP-1 receptor agonist lixisenatide in monotherapy: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in patients with type 2 diabetes (GetGoal-Mono).

title: Exenatide twice daily versus glimepiride for prevention of glycaemic deterioration in patients with type 2 diabetes with metformin failure (EUREXA): an open-label, randomised controlled trial.

title: The role of endogenous incretin secretion as amplifier of glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in healthy subjects and patients with type 2 diabetes.

outcomes_primary: First-phase insulin secretion rate (ISR) measured as incremental area under the curve during first 10 minutes of hyperglycemic clamp; second-phase insulin secretion rate measured as incremental AUC between 60-120 minutes of hyperglycemic clamp; incretin effect calculated as difference in ISR between meal perfusion and isoglycemic fasting control conditions

extraction_notes: This is a mechanistic physiology study using hyperglycemic clamp technique rather than a therapeutic clinical trial. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly designated; classification based on study objectives and emphasis in methods/results. intervention: Exendin-(9-39) administered intravenously in escalating doses: 100 pmol/kg/min (0.02 mg/kg/h) for 2 hours, then 300 pmol/kg/min (0.06 mg/kg/h) for 2 hours, then 500 pmol/kg/min (0.1 mg/kg/h) for 2 hours, preceded by 1 hour of vehicle infusion, after 12-hour overnight fast

title: Weight change with liraglutide and comparator therapies: an analysis of seven phase 3 trials from the liraglutide diabetes development programme.

title: Exenatide at therapeutic and supratherapeutic concentrations does not prolong the QTc interval in healthy subjects.

outcomes_secondary: Time-matched ΔΔQTc at individual time points within ECG assessment window; concentration-effect relationship between ΔΔQTcP and plasma exenatide concentration; assay sensitivity confirmed by moxifloxacin effect; QTc outlier values (QTc >450 ms, ΔQTc >30 ms); changes in PR interval, QRS interval, and heart rate
extraction_notes: Crossover design with Williams randomization to one of six treatment sequences. Minimum 5 days washout between periods. Sample size of 60 evaluable subjects planned; 74 subjects in evaluable population, 86 in ITT population.

title: Efficacy and safety profile of exenatide once weekly compared with insulin once daily in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes treated with oral antidiabetes drug(s): results from a 26-week, randomized, open-label, parallel-group, multicenter, noninferiority study.

extraction_notes: Open-label study design; noninferiority margin predefined at 0.4%

title: Lower ghrelin levels and exaggerated postprandial peptide-YY, glucagon-like peptide-1, and insulin responses, after gastric fundus resection, in patients undergoing Roux-en-Y gastric bypass: a randomized clinical trial.

title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 decreases intracerebral glucose content by activating hexokinase and changing glucose clearance during hyperglycemia.

title: Efficacy and tolerability of exenatide monotherapy in obese patients with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes: a randomized, 26 weeks metformin-controlled, parallel-group study.

title: Effect of low- and high-glycemic load on circulating incretins in a randomized clinical trial.
population: Healthy adults aged 18 years or older from the Seattle area with BMI between 18.5-25.0 kg/m2 (lean) or 28.0-39.9 kg/m2 (overweight-obese); exclusions: personal dietary restrictions, physician-diagnosed conditions or medications influencing metabolism, pregnancy or lactation, tobacco use, excessive alcohol consumption (≥2 bottles beer, ≥2 glasses wine, or ≥3 ounces hard liquor per day), fasting glucose >100 mg/dL

comparison: Low-glycemic load diet (GL 125) for 28 consecutive days; controlled weight-maintaining diet with 15% energy from protein, 30% energy from fat, 55% energy from carbohydrate, fiber content 55 g/day; all food provided by study; low-GL test breakfast meal at end of dietary period; 28-day washout period (habitual diet) between intervention periods

Parent study enrolled 89 participants; only 16 participants who had incretin testing comprise the analysis group for this ancillary post-prandial study. Primary outcomes stated as post-prandial testing; secondary outcomes inferred from analysis structure as fasting measures were also assessed.

title: Effect of exenatide on cholecystokinin-induced gallbladder emptying in fasting healthy subjects.

extraction_notes: Crossover study design (randomized, 2-period, double-blind). CCK infusion protocol: 0.003 μg/kg infused over 50 min at 2 mL/min. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated; classification based on emphasis in abstract.

title: Effects of pre-meal drinks with protein and amino acids on glycemic and metabolic responses at a subsequent composite meal.

outcomes_secondary: Postprandial plasma amino acid responses, plasma GIP and GLP-1 concentrations, plasma ghrelin responses, subjective appetite ratings (fullness, hunger, desire to eat) measured by 100mm Visual Analogue Scales
extraction_notes: Randomized single-blind within-subject crossover trial with 7 test occasions. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in text; classification inferred from study objectives. Sample size n=14 with some exclusions for specific analyses due to protocol deviations.

title: The glycemic, insulinemic and plasma amino acid responses to equi-carbohydrate milk meals, a pilot- study of bovine and human milk.

outcomes_secondary: Plasma incretin hormones (GIP and GLP-1) concentrations; plasma amino acid responses; correlations between plasma amino acids, insulin, and incretin secretion
extraction_notes: This is a pilot study with small sample size (n=9). Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in text; classification based on prominence in reporting. Study described as a randomized crossover design where each subject served as their own reference.

title: A dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor, sitagliptin, exerts anti-inflammatory effects in type 2 diabetic patients.

outcomes_primary: Satiety (assessed by visual analog scales), serum glucose, insulin, ghrelin, and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)

title: The fate of taspoglutide, a weekly GLP-1 receptor agonist, versus twice-daily exenatide for type 2 diabetes: the T-emerge 2 trial.
population: Adults aged 18-75 years with type 2 diabetes, HbA1c between 7 and 10%, BMI ≥25 kg/m2 (>23 kg/m2 for Asians) and ≤45 kg/m2, stable body weight (±5%) for 3 months, receiving stable dose of metformin ≥1,500 mg/day and/or thiazolidinedione (rosiglitazone ≥4 mg/day or pioglitazone ≥30 mg/day) for ≥3 months. outcomes_secondary: Changes in HbA1c (%), fasting plasma glucose, and body weight during 52 weeks of treatment; changes in fasting proinsulin, fasting proinsulin/insulin ratio, and homeostasis model assessment of β-cell function after 52 weeks of treatment. extraction_notes: Open-label study design. 24-week core phase with 28-week extension phase and optional 104-week long-term extension phase. Background antihyperglycemic treatment maintained at prestudy doses throughout.

title: Exenatide once weekly versus liraglutide once daily in patients with type 2 diabetes (DURATION-6): a randomised, open-label study.

title: Efficacy and safety comparison between liraglutide as add-on therapy to insulin and insulin dose-increase in Chinese subjects with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes and abdominal obesity.

outcomes_primary: HbA1c; composite endpoint of HbA1c ≤7.0% with no weight gain and no hypoglycemia

title: Effects of liraglutide on neurodegeneration, blood flow and cognition in Alzheimer´s disease - protocol for a controlled, randomized double-blinded trial.

extraction_notes: This is a protocol paper describing planned trial design. Dose, route, and frequency of liraglutide not specified in abstract. Sample size: n=20 per group.

title: Treatment with exenatide once weekly or twice daily for 30 weeks is associated with changes in several cardiovascular risk markers.

Primary and secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in the source; outcomes categorized based on analysis focus.

title: Long-term results of a randomized clinical trial comparing Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with vertical banded gastroplasty.

title: Effect of sitagliptin on post-prandial glucagon and GLP-1 levels in patients with type 1 diabetes: investigator-initiated, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial.

extraction_notes: Study design was investigator-initiated, double-blind, randomized-parallel, 20 weeks total duration with 4-week run-in phase and 16 weeks of treatment. A subset of 85 patients wore blinded CGM for 5 separate 7-day periods.

title: Dipeptidyl peptidase 4 inhibition may facilitate healing of chronic foot ulcers in patients with type 2 diabetes.
population: Type 2 diabetic patients with chronic nonhealing diabetic foot ulcers for more than 3-month duration; at least one full-thickness wound below the ankle; adequate distal perfusion (dorsum transcutaneous oxygen test >30 mmHg, ankle-brachial index values >0.7 and <1.2 with toe pressure >30 mmHg, or Doppler arterial waveforms triphasic or biphasic at the ankle); exclusions: active Charcot disease, ulcers from electrical/chemical/radiation burns, collagen vascular disease, ulcer malignancy, untreated osteomyelitis, cellulitis, normothermic or hyperbaric oxygen therapy, corticosteroids, immunosuppressive medications, chemotherapy, recombinant or autologous growth factor products, skin and dermal substitutes within 30 days, enzymatic debridement treatments, pregnant or nursing mothers

title: Inulin-enriched pasta improves intestinal permeability and modifies the circulating levels of zonulin and glucagon-like peptide 2 in healthy young volunteers.

outcomes_primary: Intestinal barrier function assessed by lactulose-mannitol excretion ratio in urine
outcomes_secondary: Urinary lactulose recovery; urinary mannitol levels; serum zonulin values; basal glucagon-like peptide 2 (GLP-2) levels
extraction_notes: Crossover design with 2-week run-in period and 8-week washout period between study periods. Sample size of 20 participants. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; classification based on study hypothesis.

title: Coadministration of glucagon-like peptide-1 during glucagon infusion in humans results in increased energy expenditure and amelioration of hyperglycemia.
population: Overweight or obese healthy volunteers without diabetes, aged adults, premenopausal females with regular menstrual cycles, determined healthy by medical history, physical examination, hematological and biochemical testing, and 12-lead electrocardiogram

extraction_notes: Randomized double-blinded crossover study design with four-way randomization. Primary outcome not explicitly designated but resting energy expenditure appears to be the main focus based on study objectives. Sample size is 10 volunteers.

title: The effect of a bile acid sequestrant on glucose metabolism in subjects with type 2 diabetes.

intervention: Colesevelam hydrochloride 3.75 g daily (three 625-mg tablets twice daily, taken before breakfast and before evening meal) for 12 weeks

outcomes_primary: Disposition index (DI) calculated from total β-cell responsivity (ϕtotal) multiplied by insulin sensitivity (SI)
outcomes_secondary: Fasting and postprandial glucose concentrations, HbA1c, GLP-1 concentrations, insulin concentrations, C-peptide concentrations, glucagon concentrations, endogenous glucose production (EGP), rate of meal glucose appearance (Meal Ra), glucose disappearance (Rd), insulin action (SI), insulin-mediated glucose disposal (SI*), β-cell responsivity indices (ϕdynamic, ϕstatic, ϕtotal)

title: Zinc-α2-glycoprotein is associated with insulin resistance in humans and is regulated by hyperglycemia, hyperinsulinemia, or liraglutide administration: cross-sectional and interventional studies in normal subjects, insulin-resistant subjects, and subjects with newly diagnosed diabetes.
population: Patients with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus (nT2DM), age 40-75 years, BMI 20-40 kg/m2, HbA1c levels between 6.5% and 9.0%, not treated with hypoglycemic agents or insulin. The abstract states 12 weeks of treatment but the conclusions section mentions 16 weeks - this is an inconsistency in the original text. outcomes_primary: Absolute change in HbA1c from baseline to week 24.
outcomes_secondary: Change from baseline to week 24 in: 2-hour postprandial plasma glucose during standardized breakfast meal test, blood glucose excursion during standardized breakfast meal test, seven-point self-measurement of plasma glucose, fasting plasma glucose, body weight, average daily insulin glargine dosage. Percentage of participants achieving HbA1c <7% or ≤6.5% at week 24. Percentage of participants requiring rescue therapy. Safety assessments including treatment-emergent adverse events, symptomatic and severe symptomatic hypoglycemia, injection site reactions, allergic events, and laboratory tests (including amylase, lipase, calcitonin, plasma lipoproteins, albumin-to-creatinine ratio).
extraction_notes: Study included 12-week run-in phase with insulin glargine initiation and titration before randomization. Sulfonylureas and glinides were discontinued after enrollment. Randomization stratified by HbA1c (<8%, ≥8%) and TZD use.

title: Glucagon-like peptide 1 reduces endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and oxidative stress induced by both hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia in type 1 diabetes.

extraction_notes: Open-label study with no placebo or active comparator arm. Primary and secondary outcomes were not explicitly distinguished in the abstract. This was a tolerability and pharmacokinetic study rather than an efficacy trial.

title: Mechanisms of glucose lowering of dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor sitagliptin when used alone or with metformin in type 2 diabetes: a double-tracer study.

title: Quality of life in patients with short bowel syndrome treated with the new glucagon-like peptide-2 analogue teduglutide--analyses from a randomised, placebo-controlled study.

title: Independent and combined effects of eating rate and energy density on energy intake, appetite, and gut hormones.

outcomes_secondary: Hypoglycaemia, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, abdominal pain, treatment intensification rates at week 12

title: Effect of vildagliptin on glucose and insulin concentrations during a 24-hour period in type 2 diabetes patients with different ranges of baseline hemoglobin A1c levels.

title: Efficacy and safety of lixisenatide once daily versus placebo in type 2 diabetes insufficiently controlled on pioglitazone (GetGoal-P).

title: Adding once-daily lixisenatide for type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled by established basal insulin: a 24-week, randomized, placebo-controlled comparison (GetGoal-L).
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes diagnosed ≥1 year, using basal insulin regimen for ≥3 months with stable dose (±20%) ≥30 units/day for ≥2 months before screening, HbA1c 7-10%, with or without metformin (if used, stable dose ≥1.5 g/day for ≥3 months). intervention: Lixisenatide 20 μg once daily subcutaneously within 1 hour before morning meal for 24 weeks, with two-step dose titration (10 μg for 1 week, 15 μg for 1 week, then 20 μg), added to established basal insulin therapy with or without metformin

outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from randomization to week 24

extraction_notes: Basal insulin dosage was to remain relatively stable (±20%) throughout the study except for adjustments to limit hypoglycemia. Randomization stratified by HbA1c (<8.0% vs ≥8.0%) and metformin use at screening. Randomization ratio was 2:1 (lixisenatide:placebo).

title: Randomized trial of continuous subcutaneous delivery of exenatide by ITCA 650 versus twice-daily exenatide injections in metformin-treated type 2 diabetes.

outcomes_primary: Change from baseline in HbA1c to end point at weeks 12 and 24, and for overall 24-week trial (day 0 to week 24)

title: Thirty days of resveratrol supplementation does not affect postprandial incretin hormone responses, but suppresses postprandial glucagon in obese subjects.

Baseline characteristics reported may represent sample characteristics rather than strict eligibility criteria.

title: Effects of lixisenatide once daily on gastric emptying in type 2 diabetes--relationship to postprandial glycemia.

extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the abstract; outcomes listed based on study objectives

title: High protein intake stimulates postprandial GLP1 and PYY release.

outcomes_primary: Postprandial gut hormone levels (ghrelin, PYY, GLP-1) measured half-hourly for 4 hours; energy intake at subsequent ad libitum meal
outcomes_secondary: Hunger and fullness scores assessed by visual analogue scales; plasma glucose and insulin concentrations
extraction_notes: Randomized three-way crossover design with 8 participants; study occasions separated by at least 1 week; primary outcomes not explicitly designated as primary versus secondary in the text

title: Liraglutide suppresses postprandial triglyceride and apolipoprotein B48 elevations after a fat-rich meal in patients with type 2 diabetes: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, cross-over trial.

title: Rationale and design of the glycemia reduction approaches in diabetes: a comparative effectiveness study (GRADE).

title: Efficacy and safety of lixisenatide once daily versus exenatide twice daily in type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled on metformin: a 24-week, randomized, open-label, active-controlled study (GetGoal-X).

outcomes_primary: Absolute change in HbA1c from baseline to week 24 (noninferiority assessment with predefined margin of 0.4% for upper limit of 95% CI)
outcomes_secondary: Percentage of participants attaining HbA1c <7.0% at week 24; percentage of participants attaining HbA1c ≤6.5% at week 24; change in fasting plasma glucose from baseline to week 24; change in body weight from baseline to week 24; safety and tolerability including adverse events, treatment-emergent adverse events, symptomatic hypoglycemia (defined as symptoms consistent with hypoglycemia with blood glucose <3.3 mmol/L and/or prompt recovery with carbohydrate/glucagon/IV glucose), severe hypoglycemia (requiring assistance and plasma glucose <2.0 mmol/L or prompt recovery with IV glucose/glucagon/oral carbohydrate by third party), clinical laboratory data (hematology, creatinine, microalbuminuria, serum chemistry including amylase, lipase, calcitonin); Patient Assessment of Upper Gastrointestinal Disorders-Quality of Life (PAGI-QOL) questionnaire

title: Characterisation of oral and i.v. glucose handling in truncally vagotomised subjects with pyloroplasty.
population: Truncally vagotomised subjects with pyloroplasty (n=16, including 7 with prior truncal vagotomy and pyloroplasty for uncomplicated duodenal ulcer and 9 with cardia resection including truncal vagotomy and pyloroplasty for oesophageal cancer) and matched healthy controls without family history of diabetes (n=10). outcomes_primary: Gastrointestinal-mediated glucose disposal (GIGD); Incretin effect calculated from beta cell secretory responses to oral and isoglycaemic IV glucose
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucose concentrations; Total and intact GLP1 concentrations; Intact GIP concentrations; Insulin, C-peptide, and insulin secretion rates; Glucagon concentrations; Gastric emptying (paracetamol absorption); Beta cell glucose sensitivity; Insulinogenic index; Disposition index; Pancreatic polypeptide (PP) response during sham-feeding

title: Effect of laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery on type 2 diabetes mellitus with hypertension: a randomized controlled trial.

title: Exenatide and the treatment of patients with Parkinson's disease.

title: One-year sustained glycemic control and weight reduction in type 2 diabetes after addition of liraglutide to metformin followed by insulin detemir according to HbA1c target.

title: Liraglutide and the preservation of pancreatic β-cell function in early type 2 diabetes: the LIBRA trial.
population: Patients with early type 2 diabetes mellitus, disease duration 2.6 ± 1.9 years, A1C 6.8 ± 0.8% (51 ± 8.7 mmol/mol), who completed 4 weeks of intensive insulin therapy before randomization

comparison: Daily subcutaneous placebo injection for 48 weeks, following initial 4-week intensive insulin therapy
outcomes_primary: Baseline-adjusted Insulin Secretion-Sensitivity Index-2 (ISSI-2) at 48 weeks, measured by oral glucose tolerance test
outcomes_secondary: Baseline-adjusted HbA1c at 48 weeks; glucose tolerance status; incidence of hypoglycemia; ISSI-2 two weeks after stopping treatment; serial β-cell function assessment every 12 weeks
extraction_notes: Specific liraglutide dose not reported in abstract. Study design included pre-randomization intensive insulin therapy phase for all participants to eliminate glucotoxicity.

title: Albiglutide does not impair the counter-regulatory hormone response to hypoglycaemia: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, stepped glucose clamp study in subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
population: Subjects with type 2 diabetes mellitus
intervention: Albiglutide 50 mg, single dose, administered on day 1, once weekly formulation
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Counter-regulatory hormone response to hypoglycaemia (glucagon, epinephrine, norepinephrine, growth hormone, cortisol) measured during stepped glucose clamp at plateaus of 9.0, 5.0, 4.0, 3.3 and 2.8 mmol/l
outcomes_secondary: Pancreatic β-cell secretion of C-peptide; recovery time to glucose level ≥3.9 mmol/l; adverse events and safety variables
extraction_notes: Study design is a stepped glucose clamp study with glucose measurements on day 4 to coincide with approximate albiglutide maximum plasma concentration. Sample size: n=22 per group.

title: LEADER 3--lipase and amylase activity in subjects with type 2 diabetes: baseline data from over 9000 subjects in the LEADER Trial.

intervention: Liraglutide 0.6 mg subcutaneous injection once daily, titrated up to maximum dose of 1.8 mg once daily, as add-on to baseline antihyperglycemic treatment, for minimum 3.5 years follow-up (up to 5 years)
comparison: Matching placebo injection once daily as add-on to baseline antihyperglycemic treatment
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly stated in this baseline report; the main LEADER trial evaluates cardiovascular safety of liraglutide
outcomes_secondary: Incidence of acute pancreatitis, incidence of acute gallstone disease, changes in serum lipase and amylase activity
extraction_notes: This publication reports baseline data only, prior to randomization and treatment initiation. Primary outcome of main LEADER trial not explicitly defined in this abstract/text. Lipase and amylase measurements at baseline, months 6 and 12, then annually until trial termination.

title: Treatment with a GLP-1 receptor agonist diminishes the decrease in free plasma leptin during maintenance of weight loss.
population: Healthy obese individuals aged >18 and <65 years with BMI >30 and <40 kg/m², excluding those with acute or chronic illness other than obesity, medical treatment affecting glucose/lipid metabolism or appetite/food intake, pregnancy or breast feeding, or fasting plasma glucose ≥7 mmol/L; participants had achieved diet-induced 12% body weight loss prior to randomization

outcomes_secondary: Weight change during weight maintenance period, number of meal replacements per day, fasting plasma glucose, triglyceride levels, blood pressure, glucose tolerance, meal responses of plasma PYY3-36, endogenous GLP-1, plasma glucose, serum insulin, and plasma ghrelin

title: Addition of sitagliptin or metformin to insulin monotherapy improves blood glucose control via different effects on insulin and glucagon secretion in hyperglycemic Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes.

outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucose response to meal tolerance test; glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) levels; glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) levels; C-peptide levels; glucagon response to meal challenge; HbA1c change
extraction_notes: Primary outcome not explicitly specified; study described as randomized open-label parallel group design with 25 subjects enrolled

title: Comparison of insulin glargine and liraglutide added to oral agents in patients with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes treated with metformin ± sulphonylurea, with glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) levels of 7.5-12%

outcomes_secondary: HbA1c reduction; fasting plasma glucose; weight change; symptomatic hypoglycaemia; gastrointestinal treatment-emergent adverse events; withdrawal due to adverse events

title: The effect of eating speed at breakfast on appetite hormone responses and daily food consumption.
journal: Journal of investigative medicine : the official publication of the American Federation for Clinical Research
population: Healthy participants; 68% men; age 25.9 (8.1) years; body mass index 25.0 (3.2) kg/m²
intervention: Slow eating speed at breakfast: consuming breakfast over 30 minutes
