extraction_notes: Randomized crossover design with same breakfast consumed under both conditions on separate days. Blood samples collected fasting and 3 hours postprandially. Sample size n=25. BMI units appear truncated in abstract (kg/m rather than kg/m²).

title: Postprandial glucose, insulin and incretin responses to different carbohydrate tolerance tests.
population: 240 participants with different glucose tolerance status (normal glucose tolerance and type 2 diabetes mellitus)
intervention: 75 g oral glucose (monosaccharide, liquid state)
comparison: 100 g standard noodle (polysaccharide, containing 75 g carbohydrates equivalent)
outcomes_primary: Plasma glucose, insulin, c-peptide, glucagon, and active glucagon-like peptide-1 (AGLP-1) measured at multiple timepoints
outcomes_secondary: Incremental area under curve above baseline from 0 to 120 min of insulin (iAUC(0-120 min)-INS) and AGLP-1 (iAUC(0-120 min)-AGLP-1); ratio of iAUC(0-120 min)-INS/iAUC(0-120 min)-AGLP-1
extraction_notes: Open-label, randomized, two-way crossover design with 5-7 day washout period. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; classification based on direct measurements vs. calculated parameters.

title: Efficacy and tolerability of albiglutide versus placebo or pioglitazone over 1 year in people with type 2 diabetes currently taking metformin and glimepiride: HARMONY 5.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus currently taking metformin (>1500 mg/day) and glimepiride (4 mg/day standardized before randomization)
intervention: Albiglutide 30 mg subcutaneous injection weekly, with blinded uptitration to 50 mg/week if needed, added to existing metformin and glimepiride therapy
comparison: Pioglitazone 30 mg/day orally (with blinded uptitration to 45 mg/day if needed); Placebo
outcomes_primary: Change in glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) at 52 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Fasting plasma glucose; confirmed hypoglycaemia; weight change; serious adverse events; injection site reactions
extraction_notes: Study was 156 weeks total duration but primary results reported at 52 weeks. Route of administration for albiglutide not explicitly stated but implied as injection based on injection site reactions. Glimepiride dose could be decreased if persistent hypoglycaemia occurred.

title: The protective effect of the Mediterranean diet on endothelial resistance to GLP-1 in type 2 diabetes: a preliminary report.
population: Type 2 diabetic patients without retinopathy, nephropathy, or neuropathy; not taking statins or antioxidant supplements; non-smokers; no high alcohol consumption; not participating in weight-reduction programs or other nutritional interventions in previous 6 months; taking metformin
intervention: Mediterranean diet enriched in monounsaturated fatty acids with 50 mL (4 tablespoons) extra virgin olive oil per day (approximately 1L/week) for 12 weeks
comparison: Control low-fat diet for 12 weeks
outcomes_primary: Plasma antioxidant capacity (FRAP, TRAP), endothelial function (flow mediated dilatation of brachial artery), plasma nitrotyrosine, 8-iso-PGF2a, IL-6, ICAM-1 levels at baseline and end of study; effect of GLP-1 during hyperglycemic clamp on these parameters
outcomes_secondary: GLP-1-induced insulin secretion during hyperglycemic clamp; glycemia; endothelium-independent vasodilation (response to nitroglycerin)
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=24 total, 12 per group). Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the text; classification based on study objectives. Study described as preliminary report.

title: Liraglutide promotes natriuresis but does not increase circulating levels of atrial natriuretic peptide in hypertensive subjects with type 2 diabetes.
population: Hypertensive subjects with type 2 diabetes; overweight and obese
intervention: Liraglutide, starting at 0.6 mg single dose acutely, titrated to 1.8 mg daily for 21 days
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Within-subject change from baseline in plasma ANP, Nt-proBNP, office BP, and HR at baseline and over 4 hours following single dose and after 21 days
outcomes_secondary: 24-hour ambulatory BP and HR monitoring, 24-hour urinary sodium excretion, body weight, HbA1c, cholesterol
extraction_notes: Double-blinded, randomized, placebo-controlled crossover clinical trial; ambulatory setting; primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract

title: Study protocol of a randomised controlled trial comparing perioperative intravenous insulin, GIK or GLP-1 treatment in diabetes-PILGRIM trial.
population: Adults aged 18-75 years with known type 2 diabetes mellitus for >3 months, treated with oral glucose lowering tablets or moderate dose insulin (daily insulin dosage <1 IU/kg body weight), scheduled for elective non-cardiac surgery. Exclusions: oral corticosteroid use, treatment with long-acting GLP-1 agonist or DPP-4 inhibitor, day-care (ambulatory) surgery, planned ICU stay postoperatively, planned bowel surgery, history of chronic pancreatitis or idiopathic acute pancreatitis, impaired liver function (ALAT ≥2.5 times upper normal limit), impaired renal function (serum creatinine ≥133 μmol/L for males, ≥115 μmol/L for females), pregnant or breastfeeding females, known or suspected allergy to trial products
intervention: Three arms: (1) Glucose-insulin-potassium infusion (GIK): 500 ml glucose 5% solution with 10 mmol potassium chloride and calculated insulin dose, started 30 minutes before surgery at 83 ml/hr, with evening long-acting insulin reduced by 50% day before surgery; (2) Insulin bolus regimen (BR): intravenous sliding-scale insulin boluses according to treatment algorithm, with evening long-acting insulin reduced by 50% day before surgery; (3) Liraglutide (LG): 0.6 mg liraglutide subcutaneously at 17:00 day before surgery, 1.2 mg subcutaneously morning of surgery, with insulin doses reduced by 50% from start of liraglutide treatment. All arms: capillary glucose measured every 60 minutes, additional intravenous insulin boluses given according to treatment algorithm if glucose >8 mmol/L, target glucose range 6-8 mmol/L, treatment continued up to 4 hours postoperatively
comparison: Three-arm comparison: GIK infusion vs insulin bolus regimen vs liraglutide pre-treatment (1:1:1 randomization with stratification for insulin use)
outcomes_primary: Difference in median serum glucose between the three study arms at 1 hour postoperatively
outcomes_secondary: Difference in median serum glucose at 4 hours and 1 day postoperatively; difference in amount of insulin administered; difference in occurrence of major complications (composite: death, re-admission, ICU-admission, re-operation, deep wound infection, pneumonia, sepsis/bacteremia, myocardial infarction, cerebrovascular event, deep venous thrombosis, lung embolus, stent thrombosis, bleeding, respiratory failure, renal failure); minor complications (composite: cystitis/urinary tract infection, superficial wound infection/wound leakage, pancreatitis, ileus, delirium, length of hospital stay); diabetes-related complications (hypoglycaemia requiring assistance, diabetic ketoacidosis requiring admission, unplanned medical appointments, medication changes); perioperative area under the curve outside target range; occurrence of mild hypoglycaemia (<4.0 mmol/L) or severe hypoglycaemia (<2.3 mmol/L); hypokalaemia (<3.5 mmol/L) or hyperkalaemia (>5.0 mmol/L); glucose variability (mean absolute glucose change)
extraction_notes: This is a study protocol publication, not results. The trial is described as open-label (unblinded). Sample size is 315 patients total (105 per arm).

title: Initial combination therapy with metformin, pioglitazone and exenatide is more effective than sequential add-on therapy in subjects with new-onset diabetes. Results from the Efficacy and Durability of Initial Combination Therapy for Type 2 Diabetes (EDICT): a randomized trial.
population: Drug-naïve adults with recently diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus (<2 years since diagnosis), age 30-75 years, BMI 24-50 kg/m2, negative glutamic acid decarboxylase antibodies, normal liver function/serum chemistries, stable body weight (±3 pounds within preceding year), negative pregnancy tests. Exclusion criteria: haematocrit <34%, medications known to affect glucose metabolism, previous treatment with any antidiabetic agent, evidence of diabetic proliferative retinopathy, albumin excretion >300 mg/day, major organ system disease
intervention: Initial triple combination therapy: metformin starting at 1000 mg/day increased to 2000 mg/day at 1 month; pioglitazone starting at 15 mg/day increased to 30 mg/day at 1 month (further increased to 45 mg/day if HbA1c >6.5% at 3 months); exenatide starting at 5 μg twice daily before breakfast and supper increased to 10 μg twice daily at 1 month
comparison: Conventional sequential add-on therapy: metformin starting at 1000 mg/day, increased to 2000 mg/day at 1 month if FPG >6.1 mmol/l; glipizide added at 5 mg/day and escalated to 10 mg then 20 mg/day based on FPG and HbA1c; glargine insulin added at 10 units/day (escalated weekly by 1-5 units up to 60 units/day) if targets not met at 3 months
outcomes_primary: HbA1c difference between participants receiving triple therapy versus conventional therapy
outcomes_secondary: Percentage of participants achieving HbA1c <6.5% and <7.0%; decrease in fasting plasma glucose; decrease in postprandial plasma glucose; change in body weight; rate of hypoglycaemic events
extraction_notes: This is an interim analysis with mean follow-up of 18.5 months from a planned 3-year study. Open-label, single-centre design. Treatment goal was HbA1c <6.5% for 2 years.

title: Evaluation of exenatide versus insulin glargine for the impact on endothelial functions and cardiovascular risk markers.
population: Insulin and incretin-naive patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus, body mass index 25-45 kg/m², receiving metformin for at least two months
intervention: Exenatide for 26 weeks
comparison: Insulin glargine for 26 weeks
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes measured included: endothelial functions (by ultrasonography, including flow mediated dilatation and endothelium independent vascular responses), cardiovascular risk markers (high sensitivity-C-reactive protein, endothelin-1, fibrinogen, monocyte chemoattractant protein-1, leptin, plasminogen activator inhibitor type 1, measured by ELISA), total body fat mass (by bioimpedance), and body weight. Small sample size (n=34 total).

title: Quantitative gastrointestinal and psychological traits associated with obesity and response to weight-loss therapy.
population: Adults aged 18 years or older with body mass index >18 kg/m2, including normal weight (BMI 18-24.9 kg/m2), overweight (BMI 25-29.9 kg/m2), obesity class I (BMI 30-34.9 kg/m2), or obesity class II/III (BMI ≥35 kg/m2). For the randomized trial: obese adults with BMI 30-40 kg/m2. Exclusion criteria: positive history of any systemic disease, concurrent treatment for gastrointestinal motility disorders, psychological disorders (eating disorder, anxiety, depression), or weight loss medications.
intervention: Extended-release phentermine-topiramate: 3.75mg phentermine and 23mg topiramate for first 5 days, then 7.5mg phentermine and 46mg topiramate for next 10 days, for total 15 days of combination treatment
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Weight loss; gastric emptying of solids and liquids; satiation (volume to fullness and maximal tolerated volume by nutrient drink test); satiety (total caloric intake at ad-libitum buffet meal); fasting and postprandial gastric volume; gastrointestinal hormones (ghrelin, cholecystokinin, GLP-1, PYY)
outcomes_secondary: Association of quantitative traits with BMI and waist circumference; latent dimensions of obesity identified by principal component analysis; prediction of weight loss response based on pre-specified quantitative traits (satiety by buffet meal, satiation volume to fullness, gastric emptying of solids, fasting gastric volume, peak plasma PYY)
extraction_notes: This is a complex study with three components: prospective observational study (n=328), retrospective databank analysis (n=181), and proof-of-concept randomized controlled trial (n=24). Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the text; categorization based on study aims. The RCT was a parallel-group, double-blinded trial.

title: Effects of targeted delivery of propionate to the human colon on appetite regulation, body weight maintenance and adiposity in overweight adults.
population: Men and women aged 40-65 years with body mass index 25-40 kg/m2. Exclusions: clinically significant illness including type 1 or type 2 diabetes, medication known to affect appetite and/or body weight, weight loss of 3 kg or greater in preceding 2 months, smoking, substance abuse, psychiatric illness, abnormalities on physical examination, electrocardiography or screening blood tests, pregnancy or breastfeeding.
intervention: 10 g/day inulin-propionate ester supplementation mixed into normal diet once daily for 24 weeks
comparison: 10 g/day inulin-control supplementation mixed into normal diet once daily for 24 weeks
outcomes_primary: Changes in body weight; food intake
outcomes_secondary: Change in adipose tissue distribution; intra-abdominal adipose tissue; internal adipose tissue; subcutaneous adipose tissue; total adipose tissue content; intrahepatocellular lipid content; postprandial plasma PYY concentration; postprandial plasma GLP-1 concentration; postprandial glucose response; postprandial insulin response; subjective appetite ratings (hunger, satiety, nausea via visual analogue scales); cardiovascular and diabetes risk factors (triglycerides, total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, HbA1c, C reactive protein, liver function tests, blood pressure, pulse)
extraction_notes: Study includes both acute crossover studies (n=20 for energy intake, n=14 for gastric emptying) and a 24-week parallel RCT (n=60 randomized). PICO extraction focused on the 24-week long-term study as the primary clinical trial. In vitro experiments on human colonic cells also described but not extracted as clinical PICO.

title: LX4211 therapy reduces postprandial glucose levels in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and renal impairment despite low urinary glucose excretion.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and renal impairment with estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <60 mL/min/1.73 m²
intervention: LX4211 400 mg orally for 7 days
comparison: Placebo for 7 days
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline to day 7 in postprandial glucose (PPG) levels
outcomes_secondary: Changes in fasting plasma glucose levels; glucagon-like peptide 1 levels (total and active); urinary glucose excretion (UGE); blood pressure
extraction_notes: Route of administration not explicitly stated but implied oral based on context. Subgroup analyses mentioned for eGFR <45 mL/min/1.73 m² and eGFR 45-59 mL/min/1.73 m².

title: Effect of exogenous intravenous administrations of GLP-1 and/or GIP on circulating pro-atrial natriuretic peptide in subjects with different stages of glucose tolerance.
population: Subjects with different stages of glucose tolerance
intervention: Exogenous intravenous administration of GLP-1 and/or GIP
comparison: Not explicitly stated
outcomes_primary: Circulating pro-atrial natriuretic peptide levels
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly stated
extraction_notes: Abstract text not available; extraction based solely on title. Specific doses, frequencies, durations, and comparator groups not stated. Primary/secondary outcome designation inferred from title focus.

title: Postprandial effects of polydextrose on satiety hormone responses and subjective feelings of appetite in obese participants.
population: Non-diabetic obese adults aged 20-55 years, BMI 30-37 kg/m², consuming moderately low fiber diet (typical fiber intake <19 g/day for men and <17 g/day for women), excluding those with critical illness, inflammatory bowel disease, celiac disease, GI malignancy, pregnancy, cardiovascular or metabolic diseases, lipid lowering medication affecting serum triglycerides, anti-obesity drugs, dietary supplements with high fiber content, regular use of fiber supplements/bran/seeds, regular abundant use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, or familial hyperlipidemia
intervention: High-fat meal (4293 kJ, 36% from fat; hamburger, french fries, carbonated drink) supplemented with 15 g polydextrose (Litesse Ultra) incorporated into the carbonated drink, consumed once in acute setting over 20 minutes
comparison: Same high-fat meal with placebo carbonated drink (no polydextrose added)
outcomes_primary: Postprandial changes in serum triglycerides
outcomes_secondary: Postprandial plasma concentrations of satiety-related peptides (ghrelin, cholecystokinin, glucagon-like peptide 1, peptide YY), short chain fatty acids, lactic acid measured at 0, 60, 120, 240, and 360 minutes; subjective feelings of appetite (hunger, satisfaction, desire to eat) assessed using 100 mm visual analogue scales at 0, 40, 70, 140, and 280 minutes, expressed as incremental areas under the curve during satiation and satiety periods
extraction_notes: Primary outcome (serum triglycerides) stated to be reported elsewhere (Tiihonen et al., unpublished observations). Crossover design with 10-day washout period. Sample size calculation based on primary outcome. n=18 participants.

title: Fasting gut hormone levels change with modest weight loss in obese adolescents.
population: Obese adolescents aged 10-17 years with body mass index (BMI) > 90th centile; subset of participants from the 'Eat Smart Study'
intervention: Structured reduced carbohydrate dietary intervention for 12 weeks; Structured low-fat dietary intervention for 12 weeks
comparison: Wait-listed control group
outcomes_primary: Fasting gut hormone levels including glucose, insulin, leptin, adiponectin, total amylin, acylated ghrelin, active glucagon-like peptide-1, glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), pancreatic polypeptide (PP), and total peptide tyrosine-tyrosine
outcomes_secondary: Pre- and postprandial subjective sensations of appetite assessed using visual analogue scales
extraction_notes: Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract; outcomes categorized based on study objective statement. The two dietary intervention groups (reduced carbohydrate and low-fat) were analyzed together as intervention groups.

title: Comparable liraglutide pharmacokinetics in pediatric and adult populations with type 2 diabetes: a population pharmacokinetic analysis.
population: Pediatric subjects aged 10-17 years with type 2 diabetes (T2D), HbA1c 6.5-11%, fasting plasma glucose 6.1-13.3 mmol/L (110-240 mg/dL), BMI >85th percentile for age and gender, treated with diet and exercise alone or in combination with stable dose of metformin for at least 4 weeks before screening; compared with adult subjects with T2D from two clinical pharmacology trials (Trial 2: HbA1c 6.5-10%, BMI 18.5-40 kg/m2, creatinine clearance ≥60 mL/min; Trial 3: HbA1c 7-9.5%)
intervention: Liraglutide subcutaneous injection, once daily, dose escalated weekly starting at 0.3 mg/day to 0.6, 0.9, 1.2, and 1.8 mg/day over 5 weeks based on tolerability and fasting plasma glucose (pediatric trial); liraglutide 1.8 mg once daily at steady state for 1 week (adult trials)
comparison: Adult subjects with T2D from Trial 2 (n=12) and Trial 3 (n=32) receiving liraglutide 1.8 mg; placebo (in pediatric trial)
outcomes_primary: Population pharmacokinetic parameters including apparent clearance (CL/F), apparent volume of distribution (Vd/F), area under the plasma-concentration time curve from 0-24 hours (AUC24); dose proportionality assessment
outcomes_secondary: Effects of covariates (body weight, gender, age category) on liraglutide exposure; comparison of steady-state liraglutide concentration-time profiles between pediatric and adult populations
extraction_notes: This is a population pharmacokinetic analysis, not a traditional efficacy trial. The pediatric trial was randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled (n=13 liraglutide), but this analysis focuses on pharmacokinetic comparisons rather than clinical outcomes. Safety and tolerability mentioned but not detailed as formal outcomes.

title: Effects of glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide on gastric emptying, glycaemia and insulinaemia during critical illness: a prospective, double blind, randomised, crossover study.
population: Critically ill patients without known diabetes, with blood glucose concentration >7.1 mmol/l when fasting and/or >10 mmol/l during enteral feeding, mechanically ventilated via tracheal tube expected to remain ventilated for at least 48 hours, with arterial catheter in situ. Exclusions: pregnancy, anaemia (haemoglobin <80 g/l), age <18 years, contraindication to enteral feeding, previous surgery on small intestine or gastrointestinal surgery during current hospital admission.
intervention: Intravenous glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) 4 pmol/kg/minute infused from T=-60 to T=300 minutes, delivered via central venous catheter at 1 ml/minute. At T=0, 100 ml liquid nutrient meal (2 kcal/ml TwoCal containing carbohydrate 43%, fat 40%, protein 17%) with 3 g 3-O-methylglucose, 100 mcg octanoic acid, and 20 MBq technetium-99m calcium phytate administered via nasogastric tube.
comparison: Placebo (0.9% saline) infused intravenously from T=-60 to T=300 minutes via central venous catheter at 1 ml/minute, with identical liquid nutrient meal at T=0. Crossover design: patients received both treatments on two consecutive days in randomised order.
outcomes_primary: Blood glucose concentrations (area under the concentration curve from T=-60 to T=300 minutes)
outcomes_secondary: Gastric emptying measured by scintigraphy (intragastric retention) and 13C-octanoic breath test (gastric emptying coefficient); glucose absorption measured by serum 3-O-methylglucose concentrations (area under curve); serum insulin concentrations (area under curve); serum glucagon concentrations (incremental area under curve); plasma GIP concentrations
extraction_notes: Crossover study design with each patient serving as own control. Primary outcome not explicitly labeled but glycaemia was central focus based on sample size calculation. Patients fasted for 4 hours and exogenous insulin ceased 2 hours prior to each study.

title: An enriched, cereal-based bread affects appetite ratings and glycemic, insulinemic, and gastrointestinal hormone responses in healthy adults in a randomized, controlled trial.
population: Healthy adults aged 19-32 years with body mass index of 19.2-28.5
intervention: Cereal-based bread containing wheat, oat, and spelt flours, 22% dried fruits (figs, apricots, raisins, and prunes), enriched with 7% fiber (from wheat cross-linked maltodextrins and pea) and 10-11% protein (from wheat gluten and hydrolyzed wheat proteins); consumed 2 times with 1-week wash-out period
comparison: Control bread consisting of white bread with margarine and jam (matched for energy density, fat, and sugar content); consumed 2 times with 1-week wash-out period
outcomes_primary: Appetite ratings (prospective consumption, satiety) measured using standardized visual analogue scales; postprandial glucose, insulin, and gastrointestinal hormone responses (ghrelin, glucagon-like peptide 1, gastric inhibitory polypeptide, pancreatic polypeptide) measured as areas under the curve over 4 hours
outcomes_secondary: Subsequent ad libitum energy intake at 4 hours
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; classification based on emphasis in methods and results sections. Crossover design with each participant receiving both interventions.

title: Association among weight change, glycemic control, and markers of cardiovascular risk with exenatide once weekly: a pooled analysis of patients with type 2 diabetes.
population: Adults aged ≥16 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus, A1C 7.1-11.0%, stable body weight for 3-6 months prior to enrollment, BMI 23-45 kg/m²
intervention: Exenatide once weekly (2 mg subcutaneous injection), with or without oral glucose-lowering medications, for 24-30 weeks
comparison: None (pooled analysis of exenatide once weekly arms only; patients stratified into quartiles by weight change for analysis)
outcomes_primary: A1C change from baseline; fasting plasma glucose (FPG) change from baseline
outcomes_secondary: Body weight change; systolic blood pressure (SBP); diastolic blood pressure (DBP); heart rate (HR); HDL-cholesterol; LDL-cholesterol; total cholesterol; triglycerides; alanine aminotransferase (ALT); aspartate aminotransferase (AST); adverse events including hypoglycemia and gastrointestinal events
extraction_notes: This is a pooled post-hoc analysis of 8 randomized controlled trials examining only the exenatide once weekly treatment arms. No comparator group was included in this analysis. Primary and secondary outcome designations not explicitly stated; outcomes listed based on analysis focus.

title: LEADER 2: baseline calcitonin in 9340 people with type 2 diabetes enrolled in the Liraglutide Effect and Action in Diabetes: Evaluation of cardiovascular outcome Results (LEADER) trial: preliminary observations.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus and at high risk of cardiovascular disease (with or without existing cardiovascular disease), either drug-naïve or treated with one or more antihyperglycaemic drugs including basal and premix insulins, with baseline serum calcitonin ≤50 ng/l. Exclusion criteria: personal or family history of multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 or familial medullary thyroid carcinoma, baseline calcitonin concentration ≥50 ng/l
intervention: Liraglutide once daily (dose not specified in this report), followed for up to 5 years
comparison: Placebo once daily
outcomes_primary: Cardiovascular outcomes (specific primary endpoint not defined in this report, which focuses on baseline calcitonin data)
outcomes_secondary: Serum calcitonin concentrations measured at baseline and annually thereafter; thyroid disease diagnoses reported as medical events of special interest
extraction_notes: This publication (LEADER 2) reports preliminary baseline calcitonin data only, prior to treatment randomization. The specific liraglutide dose is not stated in this report. The main LEADER trial cardiovascular outcomes are not the focus of this paper. This is a substudy focusing on calcitonin monitoring methodology and baseline characteristics.

title: Plant-rich mixed meals based on Palaeolithic diet principles have a dramatic impact on incretin, peptide YY and satiety response, but show little effect on glucose and insulin homeostasis: an acute-effects randomised study.
population: Healthy subjects
intervention: Palaeolithic-type meals (PAL 1 and PAL 2) comprising fish and a variety of plants, selected to be rich in fibre and phyto-nutrients. PAL1 contained more protein and energy; PAL2 matched reference meal for energy, protein, fat and carbohydrates
comparison: Reference meal based on WHO guidelines (REF)

outcomes_primary: Insulin sensitivity index (ISI) calculated according to Stumvoll et al. and Matsuda-DeFronzo methods during frequently sampled oral glucose tolerance test (FSOGTT)

title: Rationale, design, and baseline characteristics in Evaluation of LIXisenatide in Acute Coronary Syndrome, a long-term cardiovascular end point trial of lixisenatide versus placebo.

comparison: Placebo

outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly stated in abstract
extraction_notes: This is a trial design and baseline characteristics paper; intervention dosing details not provided in abstract. Safety outcomes systematically collected include hypoglycemia, pancreatitis, and malignancy but not explicitly labeled as secondary outcomes.

title: One-year efficacy and safety of a fixed combination of insulin degludec and liraglutide in patients with type 2 diabetes: results of a 26-week extension to a 26-week main trial.

title: Preserved pharmacokinetic exposure and distinct glycemic effects of insulin degludec and liraglutide in IDegLira, a fixed-ratio combination therapy.

title: Carbohydrate-rich breakfast attenuates glycaemic, insulinaemic and ghrelin response to ad libitum lunch relative to morning fasting in lean adults.

title: Effects of a high-protein/low-carbohydrate versus a standard hypocaloric diet on adipocytokine levels and cardiovascular risk factors during 9 months, role of rs6923761 gene variant of glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Once-Weekly Dulaglutide Versus Insulin Glargine in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes on Metformin and Glimepiride (AWARD-2).

title: Brain reward-system activation in response to anticipation and consumption of palatable food is altered by glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor activation in humans.

title: A Randomized, Controlled Trial of 3.0 mg of Liraglutide in Weight Management.

title: Effects of wheat bran extract rich in arabinoxylan oligosaccharides and resistant starch on overnight glucose tolerance and markers of gut fermentation in healthy young adults.
