title: A multifunctional diet improves cardiometabolic-related biomarkers independently of weight changes: an 8-week randomized controlled intervention in healthy overweight and obese subjects.
population: Healthy overweight and obese subjects, aged 51-72 years, BMI between 25 and 34, fasting glycemia ≤6.1 mmol/L
intervention: Multifunctional diet (MFD) including low-glycemic-impact meals, antioxidant-rich foods, oily fish, viscous dietary fibers, soybean and whole barley kernel products, almonds and plant stanols, consumed for 8 weeks in free-living conditions
comparison: Control diet (CD) devoid of the functional components, consumed for 8 weeks
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished. Measured outcomes included: fasting blood values of lipids, glucose, insulin, GGT, CRP, HbA1c, PAI-1, GLP-1, GLP-2, body weight, blood pressure, breath hydrogen, and Reynolds cardiovascular risk score. Sample size: MFD group n=23, CD group n=24.

title: Liraglutide treatment causes upregulation of adiponectin and downregulation of resistin in Chinese type 2 diabetes.
population: Chinese patients diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM)
intervention: Liraglutide, once daily, in combination with metformin 1 g twice daily, for 16 weeks
comparison: Glimepiride 4 mg once daily, in combination with metformin 1 g twice daily
outcomes_primary: Plasma levels of adiponectin and resistin
outcomes_secondary: HbA1c levels
extraction_notes: Liraglutide dose not explicitly specified in abstract. Study described as double-blinded double-dummy active-controlled. Primary vs secondary outcome designation not explicitly stated; classification based on study aims.

title: Glucagon-like peptide 1 decreases lipotoxicity in non-alcoholic steatohepatitis.
population: Adults aged 18-70 years with biopsy-proven non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) within 6 months of study, BMI ≥25 kg/m², with or without type 2 diabetes (if diabetic: diet-controlled or stable dose metformin ± gliclazide for minimum 3 months, HbA1c <9.0%)
intervention: Liraglutide 1.8 mg once daily subcutaneous injection, titrated by 0.6 mg every 7 days from starting dose of 0.6 mg until maximum dose of 1.8 mg achieved, for 12 weeks
comparison: Matching liraglutide-placebo control, once daily subcutaneous injection, for 12 weeks
outcomes_primary: Organ-specific insulin sensitivity (hepatic, adipose, muscle) assessed by hyperinsulinaemic euglycaemic clamps with stable isotope tracers; hepatic de novo lipogenesis; adipose tissue function assessed by subcutaneous adipose tissue microdialysis
outcomes_secondary: BMI; weight; fat mass; waist circumference; HbA1c; liver enzymes (AST, ALT, GGT); lipid profile (LDL cholesterol); serum adipocytokines (leptin, adiponectin, CCL-2); inflammatory markers (high-sensitivity C-reactive protein); fasting glucose; fasting insulin; circulating NEFA; Adipose-IR index
extraction_notes: This is a mechanistic sub-study of the LEAN trial (NCT01237119). Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly labeled as such; classification based on stated study aims. Sample size of 14 patients (7 per arm) for this metabolic sub-study.

title: Effect of breakfast omission on subjective appetite, metabolism, acylated ghrelin and GLP-17-36 during rest and exercise.
population: Male, habitual breakfast eaters
intervention: Breakfast omission (BO): overnight fasted state with breakfast omitted, followed by standardized lunch at 4.5 h and dinner at 10 h, with 60 min fixed-intensity cycling (50% VO2 peak) at 8 h
comparison: Breakfast consumption (BC): overnight fasted then consumed standardized breakfast (3085 kJ), followed by standardized lunch at 4.5 h and dinner at 10 h, with 60 min fixed-intensity cycling (50% VO2 peak) at 8 h
outcomes_secondary: Subjective appetite sensations (hunger, fullness, desire to eat, prospective food consumption); resting energy expenditure; substrate utilisation; active glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-17-36) concentrations; acylated ghrelin concentrations; heart rate during exercise; perceived exertion during exercise
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=8). Crossover randomised design. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract; all outcomes listed as secondary. Breakfast, lunch, and dinner energy content standardized across participants.

title: Effect on the Gastrointestinal Absorption of Drugs from Different Classes in the Biopharmaceutics Classification System, When Treating with Liraglutide.
population: Healthy subjects
intervention: Liraglutide 1.8 mg at steady state
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Rate and extent of gastrointestinal absorption of concomitantly orally taken drugs, measured by pharmacokinetic parameters (tmax, Cmax, AUC) for atorvastatin 40 mg, griseofulvin 500 mg, lisinopril 20 mg, and digoxin 1 mg
extraction_notes: Two-period crossover design. Study focused on drug-drug interaction assessment rather than therapeutic efficacy. No secondary outcomes explicitly specified.

title: IDegLira Improves Both Fasting and Postprandial Glucose Control as Demonstrated Using Continuous Glucose Monitoring and a Standardized Meal Test.
journal: Journal of diabetes science and technology
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes with inadequate glycemic control, subset of DUAL I trial participants
intervention: IDegLira (fixed-ratio combination of insulin degludec and liraglutide) administered once daily subcutaneously, initiated at 10 dose steps (10 units insulin degludec plus 0.36 mg liraglutide), titrated twice weekly to fasting plasma glucose target of 72-90 mg/dl, maximum 50 dose steps (50 units insulin degludec and 1.8 mg liraglutide), for 26 weeks
comparison: Insulin degludec alone (initiated at 10 units, titrated twice weekly to fasting plasma glucose target of 72-90 mg/dl, no dose limit) or Liraglutide alone (initiated at 0.6 mg/day, increased by 0.6 mg per week to target dose of 1.8 mg/day by week 3)
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline in mean postprandial glucose increment (normalized iAUC0-4h) during standardized meal test at 26 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Postprandial interstitial glucose profiles via continuous glucose monitoring (iAUC0-4h glucose averaged over 3 main meals), postprandial insulin increment (iAUC0-4h insulin), postprandial C-peptide increment (iAUC0-4h C-peptide), postprandial glucagon increment (iAUC0-4h glucagon), beta cell function (insulin secretion ratio and static index), safety including confirmed hypoglycemic events and adverse events
extraction_notes: This is a substudy of the DUAL I trial involving 260 of 1663 original participants. Randomization was 2:1:1 (IDegLira:insulin degludec:liraglutide). Primary outcome designation not explicitly stated; inference based on prominence in abstract and analysis. Open-label trial design.

title: Effect of Oxyntomodulin, Glucagon, GLP-1, and Combined Glucagon +GLP-1 Infusion on Food Intake, Appetite, and Resting Energy Expenditure.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
population: Young healthy male volunteers, aged 18-32 years, BMI 21-26 kg/m², fasting plasma glucose 4.4-5.4 mmol/L, glycated hemoglobin A1c 37-42 mmol/mol
intervention: Oxyntomodulin 3 pmol × kg⁻¹ × min⁻¹ intravenous infusion during 4-hour liquid meal test
comparison: Saline infusion; GLP-1 infusion (1 pmol × kg⁻¹ × min⁻¹); Glucagon infusion (0.86 pmol × kg⁻¹ × min⁻¹); Combined glucagon + GLP-1 infusion (same doses)
outcomes_primary: Resting energy expenditure (measured as oxygen uptake), gastric emptying, composite appetite scores, food intake
extraction_notes: Crossover design with 5 intervention arms. No distinction made between primary and secondary outcomes in abstract; all listed as main outcome measures.

title: The Glucagon-Like Peptide 1 Receptor Agonist Exenatide Inhibits Small Intestinal Motility, Flow, Transit, and Absorption of Glucose in Healthy Subjects and Patients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
population: Healthy subjects and patients with type 2 diabetes; 10 healthy subjects and 10 patients with type 2 diabetes
intervention: Intravenous exenatide 7.5 μg administered from -30 to 240 minutes, with intraduodenal glucose load (45 g glucose with 5 g 3-O-methylglucose and 20 MBq 99mTc-sulfur colloid, total volume 200 mL, given at t = 0-60 min at 3 kcal/min)
comparison: Intravenous saline (placebo) administered from -30 to 240 minutes
outcomes_primary: Duodenal motility (duodenal pressure waves), duodenal flow (antegrade flow events), small intestinal transit
outcomes_secondary: Serum 3-O-methylglucose concentrations (glucose absorption), blood glucose concentrations, insulin concentrations, nausea
extraction_notes: Double-blind randomized crossover design. Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in abstract; categorization based on study objectives. Motility and flow measured using combined manometry-impedance catheter; transit measured using scintigraphy.

title: Twelve-Week Treatment With Liraglutide as Add-on to Insulin in Normal-Weight Patients With Poorly Controlled Type 1 Diabetes: A Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Double-Blind Parallel Study.
population: Normal-weight patients with type 1 diabetes, HbA1c ≥8% (64 mmol/mol), on insulin treatment, poorly controlled
intervention: Liraglutide 1.2 mg once daily as add-on to insulin for 12 weeks
comparison: Placebo as add-on to insulin for 12 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c
outcomes_secondary: Change in insulin dose, change in weight, glycemic excursions, heart rate, blood pressure, incidence of hypoglycemia, gastrointestinal adverse effects
extraction_notes: Continuous glucose monitoring performed before and at end of treatment for glycemic excursion assessment

title: Liraglutide in people treated for type 2 diabetes with multiple daily insulin injections: randomised clinical trial (MDI Liraglutide trial).
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes treated with multiple daily insulin injections, HbA1c concentrations ≥58 mmol/mol (7.5%) and ≤102 mmol/mol (11.5%), body mass index 27.5-45 kg/m2, fasting C peptide level ≥0.1 nmol/L. Multiple daily insulin injections defined as separate basal and mealtime insulin components including at least two daily mealtime insulin doses. Premixed insulin users excluded.
intervention: Subcutaneous liraglutide, titrated from 0.6 mg during week 1, 1.2 mg during week 2, to 1.8 mg during week 3 and onwards (highest tolerated dose used), administered once daily at same timing each day, for 24 weeks, added to existing multiple daily insulin injection regimen
comparison: Placebo (same composition as liraglutide but without active pharmaceutical ingredient), same titration schedule and administration, added to existing multiple daily insulin injection regimen
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c level from baseline to week 24
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of participants reaching HbA1c <53 mmol/mol (7.0%), <58 mmol/mol (7.5%), and <64 mmol/mol (8.0%); change in body weight; change in total daily insulin dose (basal and mealtime); change in fasting and postprandial glucose levels; mean and standard deviation of glucose levels by masked continuous glucose monitoring; severe hypoglycaemic events; non-severe symptomatic and asymptomatic hypoglycaemia (<4.0 mmol/L and <3.0 mmol/L); treatment satisfaction (diabetes treatment satisfaction questionnaire); systolic and diastolic blood pressure; total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, triglycerides; adverse events; gastrointestinal symptoms
extraction_notes: Study conducted at 14 sites in Sweden. Minor changes to inclusion criteria during study (HbA1c lower cut-off changed from 64 to 58 mmol/mol, BMI from 28.0 to 27.5 kg/m2). 124 participants randomized 1:1 using minimisation allocation.

title: Postprandial hyperglycemia was ameliorated by taking metformin 30 min before a meal than taking metformin with a meal; a randomized, open-label, crossover pilot study.
population: Diabetic patients (human study); Zucker rats (animal model)
intervention: Metformin 1000 mg taken 30 min before a meal (pre-Met protocol) in humans; Metformin 600 mg/kg taken 10 min before meal in rats
comparison: Metformin taken with a meal (Met protocol); No medication control group (animal study only)
outcomes_primary: Peak glucose level
outcomes_secondary: Total GLP-1 level
extraction_notes: Small pilot study with only 5 diabetic patients in human component. Crossover design. Open-label study. Abstract does not specify patient baseline characteristics beyond diabetic status.

title: Effect of the GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Lixisenatide on Counterregulatory Responses to Hypoglycemia in Subjects With Insulin-Treated Type 2 Diabetes.
population: Subjects with type 2 diabetes treated with basal insulin and metformin
intervention: Lixisenatide for 6 weeks
comparison: Placebo for 6 weeks
outcomes_primary: Hormonal counterregulatory responses to insulin-induced hypoglycemia (glucagon, epinephrine, cortisol, pancreatic polypeptide, norepinephrine levels) measured during two-step hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemic clamp at 3.5 and 2.8 mmol/L
outcomes_secondary: HbA1c levels, fasting blood glucose concentration
extraction_notes: Crossover study design with 4-week washout period. Dose, route, and frequency of lixisenatide not specified in abstract. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract.

title: Acute load-dependent effects of oral whey protein on gastric emptying, gut hormone release, glycemia, appetite, and energy intake in healthy men.
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
population: Healthy lean men
intervention: Oral whey protein drinks containing either 30 g pure whey protein isolate (L) or 70 g pure whey protein isolate (H) in iso-osmolar, equally palatable drinks (approximately 450 mL)
comparison: Saline control drink (iso-osmolar, equally palatable, approximately 450 mL)
outcomes_primary: Gastric emptying measured using 3-dimensional ultrasound
outcomes_secondary: Plasma cholecystokinin, glucagon-like peptide 1, glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide, insulin, glucagon, total amino acids, blood glucose measured for 180 min after consumption; energy intake at a buffet-style lunch
extraction_notes: Study design is randomized, double-blind crossover with 3 separate occasions. Primary outcome not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in abstract. Population age and BMI provided as baseline characteristics rather than strict eligibility criteria.

title: The effect of encapsulated glutamine on gut peptide secretion in human volunteers.
population: Healthy male and female volunteers aged 18-65 years with BMI 18-35 kg/m2, and patients with type 2 diabetes aged 18-65 years with BMI 18-40 kg/m2. Excluded: anemia or other significant active diseases, pregnancy or breastfeeding, patients with T2DM taking insulin or injectable GLP-1 agonists.
intervention: Encapsulated ileal-release glutamine, doses of 3.6 g or 6.0 g, administered orally as a single dose (10 capsules containing 600 mg glutamine each), with enteric coating designed for release 20 min after exposure to alkaline environment
comparison: Placebo (10 capsules containing 300 mg microcrystalline cellulose each)
outcomes_primary: Circulating concentrations of total glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) in venous blood
outcomes_secondary: Safety, glucose tolerance (assessed via 75 g oral glucose tolerance test), meal size (ad libitum meal consumption), subjective feelings of hunger, fullness and nausea (visual analog scale)
extraction_notes: Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, cross-over design. Study involved multiple sub-studies: dose-ranging study (n=4), fasting study in healthy volunteers (n=10), glucose tolerance study in healthy volunteers (n=9) and T2DM patients (n=8), and meal size study in healthy volunteers (n=10). Total 32 participants recruited (24 healthy volunteers, 8 T2DM patients).

title: Effects of liraglutide on left ventricular function in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention.
population: Patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing primary percutaneous coronary intervention
intervention: Liraglutide: 1.8 mg administered 30 minutes before intervention, followed by 0.6 mg daily for 2 days, 1.2 mg daily for 2 days, then 1.8 mg daily for 3 days (total 7-day course)
comparison: Placebo for 7 days
outcomes_primary: Change in left ventricular ejection fraction at 3 months
outcomes_secondary: Rate of no-reflow; stress hyperglycemia; markers of inflammation; markers of endothelial function
extraction_notes: Route of administration for liraglutide not explicitly stated in abstract

title: Durable efficacy of liraglutide in patients with type 2 diabetes and pronounced insulin-associated weight gain: 52-week results from the Effect of Liraglutide on insulin-associated wEight GAiN in patients with Type 2 diabetes' (ELEGANT) randomized controlled trial.
population: Adult patients with type 2 diabetes with ≥4% weight gain within 16 months of insulin therapy
intervention: Liraglutide 1.8 mg per day added to insulin therapy for 26 weeks, followed by continuation for another 26 weeks (total 52 weeks)
comparison: Continuation of standard insulin therapy for first 26 weeks, then addition of liraglutide 1.8 mg per day for second 26 weeks
outcomes_primary: Body weight change
outcomes_secondary: Haemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) change; insulin dose change; proportion of patients able to discontinue insulin
extraction_notes: This is a 52-week follow-up report of an open-label trial; primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract

title: A Randomised Crossover Trial: The Effect of Inulin on Glucose Homeostasis in Subtypes of Prediabetes.
population: Volunteers with prediabetes, including subtypes: isolated-impaired fasting glucose and isolated-impaired glucose tolerance
intervention: Inulin (fermentable carbohydrate) 30 g/day for 2 weeks, following a 4-week dose-escalation run-in
comparison: Cellulose (placebo) 30 g/day for 2 weeks
outcomes_primary: Fasting insulin, fasting glucose, insulin resistance measured by homeostatic model assessment (HOMA)
outcomes_secondary: Insulin sensitivity, free fatty acids, glucagon-like peptide-1 concentrations, incremental AUC for insulin (0-30 min and 0-60 min) assessed via meal tolerance test
extraction_notes: Crossover design with double-blind, placebo-controlled methodology. Meal tolerance test conducted in subset of 15 subjects only. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract.

title: Effects of liraglutide on left ventricular function in patients with non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction.
population: Patients with non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI)
intervention: Liraglutide 0.6 mg for 2 days, then 1.2 mg for 2 days, then 1.8 mg for 3 days (total 7 days treatment)
comparison: Placebo for 7 days
outcomes_primary: Change in left ventricular ejection fraction at 3 months
outcomes_secondary: Change in serum glycosylated hemoglobin levels; inflammation markers; oxidative stress markers
extraction_notes: Left ventricular function assessed by transthoracic echocardiography. Specific inflammation and oxidative stress markers not named in abstract.

title: COMPARISON OF THE LONG-TERM EFFECTS OF LIRAGLUTIDE AND GLIMEPIRIDE MONOTHERAPY ON BONE MINERAL DENSITY IN PATIENTS WITH TYPE 2 DIABETES.
journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes aged 19 to 79 years
intervention: Liraglutide 1.8 mg/day or 1.2 mg/day monotherapy
comparison: Glimepiride 8 mg/day monotherapy
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline in total body bone mineral density (BMD) at 52 and 104 weeks
extraction_notes: This is a subgroup analysis of the LEAD-3 trial. The main trial randomized 746 patients but only 61 patients in this subgroup had BMD measurements. The original LEAD-3 trial was a 52-week double-blind phase III trial with a 52-week open-label extension. Secondary outcomes not specified in the abstract.

title: Efficacy and safety of once-weekly GLP-1 receptor agonist albiglutide (HARMONY 2): 52 week primary endpoint results from a randomised, placebo-controlled trial in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus inadequately controlled with diet and exercise.
population: Adults aged ≥18 years with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled by diet and exercise, not using a glucose-lowering agent, HbA1c 7.0–10.0% (53.00–85.79 mmol/mol), BMI 20–45 kg/m², fasting C-peptide ≥0.26 nmol/l. Key exclusion criteria included history of type 1 diabetes and recent cardiovascular and/or cerebrovascular disease.
intervention: Albiglutide 30 mg subcutaneously once weekly, or albiglutide 30 mg subcutaneously once weekly with uptitration to 50 mg at week 12, for 52 weeks
comparison: Matching placebo subcutaneously once weekly
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline at week 52
outcomes_secondary: Change in fasting plasma glucose (FPG) from baseline over time; time to hyperglycaemia rescue; proportion of patients meeting HbA1c treatment goals (<6.5% and <7.0%); body weight change from baseline over time; adverse events; serious adverse events; death; gastrointestinal events; injection-site reactions; cardiovascular events; hypoglycaemia; pancreatitis; thyroid tumours; potential systemic allergic reactions; immunogenicity
extraction_notes: Treatment duration for primary endpoint was 52 weeks within a 3-year trial. Stratification factors included screening HbA1c value (<8.0% vs ≥8.0%), history of myocardial infarction, and age (<65 vs ≥65 years).

title: Cardiovascular, renal and gastrointestinal effects of incretin-based therapies: an acute and 12-week randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, mechanistic intervention trial in type 2 diabetes.
population: Adults aged 35-75 years with type 2 diabetes, Caucasian, BMI 25-40 kg/m2, HbA1c 6.5-9.0% DCCT or 48-75 mmol/mol IFCC, on stable dose of oral antihyperglycaemic drugs (metformin and/or sulfonylurea) for at least 3 months, females must be postmenopausal. Exclusions: use of thiazolidinediones, GLP-1 receptor agonists, DPP-4 inhibitors, insulin, glucocorticoids, NSAIDs, antimicrobial agents, chemotherapeutics or immunosuppressants; history of pancreatic disease or impaired pancreatic exocrine function; active liver disease or threefold elevation of liver enzymes; malignancy; eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2; recent cardiovascular disease (<6 months); chronic heart failure NYHA grade II-IV; atrial fibrillation; alcohol abuse; gastroparesis; neurogenic bladder; mental illness; contraindications for MRI
intervention: Acute intervention: intravenous exenatide 10 µg diluted in saline, infused at 50 ng/min for 30 min then 25 ng/min for remainder of 5-hour test. 12-week intervention: subcutaneous liraglutide starting at 0.6 mg once daily for 1 week, then 1.2 mg once daily for 1 week, then 1.8 mg once daily for remainder of 12 weeks; OR oral sitagliptin 100 mg once daily for 12 weeks
comparison: Placebo (isotonic 0.9% saline for acute intravenous intervention; matching liraglutide-placebo prefilled pens and/or sitagliptin-placebo capsules for 12-week intervention)
outcomes_primary: Cardiovascular: resting heart rate variability assessed by beat-to-beat heart rate monitor and spectral analyses software. Renal: glomerular filtration rate assessed by inulin clearance methodology. Gastrointestinal (acute): pancreatic exocrine secreted volume assessed by secretin-enhanced MR cholangiopancreatography. Gastrointestinal (12-week): faecal elastase-1 levels
outcomes_secondary: Systemic haemodynamics (heart rate, blood pressure, cardiac output, vascular resistance), arterial stiffness, microvascular function; para-amino hippuric acid-measured effective renal plasma flow, tubular function, glomerular and tubular damage markers; exocrine pancreatic function, pancreatic structure/volume, gallbladder emptying, gastric emptying, hepatic fat content, gastrointestinal damage markers
extraction_notes: This is a protocol paper describing planned study design, not a results paper. Three integrated trials are described: main 12-week parallel-group trial (n=60, randomised 1:1:1 to liraglutide, sitagliptin, or placebo), acute parallel-group trial (n=60, randomised 1:1 to IV exenatide vs placebo), and acute cross-over trial (n=12 male patients for pancreatic MRI outcomes).

title: Glucose Variability and β- Cell Response by GLP-1 Analogue added-on CSII for Patients with Poorly Controlled Type 2 Diabetes.
population: Adults aged >20 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed >2 years, A1C level 8% to 12%, receiving premixed insulin twice daily with total insulin daily dose >0.6 u/kg/day. Exclusions: recent history of drug or alcohol abuse, sensitivity to analogous products, serious cardiovascular disorders, participation in another clinical investigation study, ongoing influenza, autoimmune disease or other metabolic disorders, pregnant or lactating women.
intervention: Exenatide 5 μg subcutaneous injection twice daily for 3 days added to continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII), following 3 days of glucose optimization with CSII during hospitalization
comparison: Placebo (normal saline injection) twice daily for 3 days added to continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII), following 3 days of glucose optimization with CSII during hospitalization
outcomes_primary: Standard deviation of plasma glucose (SDPG), mean glucose values, incremental area under the curve (AUC) of glucose during 75g OGTT, insulinogenic index (Insulin0–peak/Glucose0–peak)
outcomes_secondary: β-cell function measurements (C-peptide/glucose ratio, insulin increment, 2-hour glucose during OGTT), Matsuda index for insulin sensitivity, HOMA-IR, adiponectin levels, hsCRP, BNP, 24-hour urine 8-iso-PGF2α, 8-point blood glucose profiles, hypoglycemia frequency, adverse events
extraction_notes: This was a randomized, open-label, parallel, placebo-controlled trial conducted during hospitalization. Primary outcomes were not explicitly designated in the text; outcomes listed are inferred from the study objectives and analysis emphasis. Short study duration (6 days total, 3 days intervention).

title: Administration of resveratrol for 5 wk has no effect on glucagon-like peptide 1 secretion, gastric emptying, or glycemic control in type 2 diabetes: a randomized controlled trial.
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
population: Patients with diet-controlled type 2 diabetes
intervention: Resveratrol 500 mg twice daily orally for 5 weeks
comparison: Placebo for 5 weeks
outcomes_primary: GLP-1 secretion, gastric emptying, glycemic control (blood glucose, HbA1c)
outcomes_secondary: Body weight, daily energy intake
extraction_notes: Crossover design with 5-week washout period between interventions. Sample size is 14 patients. Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in the abstract.

title: Liraglutide safety and efficacy in patients with non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (LEAN): a multicentre, double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled phase 2 study.
population: Patients who are overweight with clinical evidence of non-alcoholic steatohepatitis, stratified by diabetes status
intervention: Liraglutide 1.8 mg daily, subcutaneous injection, for 48 weeks
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Resolution of definite non-alcoholic steatohepatitis with no worsening in fibrosis from baseline to end of treatment (48 weeks), assessed centrally by two independent pathologists
outcomes_secondary: Progression of fibrosis; adverse events including gastrointestinal disorders
extraction_notes: Trial designed using A'Hern's single-group method requiring 8 (38%) of 21 successes in liraglutide group for clinical significance. Secondary outcomes not explicitly labeled as such in abstract but fibrosis progression and safety were clearly reported endpoints.

title: Alogliptin, a Dipeptidyl Peptidase 4 Inhibitor, Prevents the Progression of Carotid Atherosclerosis in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes: The Study of Preventive Effects of Alogliptin on Diabetic Atherosclerosis (SPEAD-A).
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus free of a history of apparent cardiovascular diseases
intervention: Alogliptin treatment for 24 months
comparison: Conventional treatment
outcomes_primary: Changes in mean common intima-media thickness (IMT) of the carotid artery; changes in maximum intima-media thickness (IMT) of the carotid artery measured by carotid arterial echography
extraction_notes: Secondary outcomes not specified in abstract. Dose, route, and frequency of alogliptin not provided. Specific details of conventional treatment not described.

title: Lixisenatide in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes and Acute Coronary Syndrome.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes who had had a myocardial infarction or who had been hospitalized for unstable angina within the previous 180 days
intervention: Lixisenatide (a glucagon-like peptide 1-receptor agonist) in addition to locally determined standards of care
comparison: Placebo in addition to locally determined standards of care
outcomes_primary: Composite end point of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina
outcomes_secondary: Rate of hospitalization for heart failure; rate of death; serious adverse events; severe hypoglycemia; pancreatitis; pancreatic neoplasms; allergic reactions
extraction_notes: Dose, route, and frequency of lixisenatide not specified in abstract. Secondary outcomes inferred from reported safety and efficacy endpoints mentioned in results section.

title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist exenatide has no acute effect on MRI-measured exocrine pancreatic function in patients with type 2 diabetes: a randomized trial.
population: Male patients with type 2 diabetes, treated with oral glucose-lowering agents
intervention: Exenatide administered intravenously
comparison: Placebo (saline 0.9%) administered intravenously
outcomes_primary: Secretin-stimulated pancreatic excretion volume
outcomes_secondary: Maximum secretion speed; time to reach maximum secretion speed; changes in pancreatic duct diameter
extraction_notes: Sample size: 12 patients. Crossover study design with randomized order of treatments. Exocrine pancreatic function measured using secretin-enhanced magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography. Specific dose, frequency, and duration of exenatide infusion not provided in abstract.

title: Effects of Liraglutide Combined with Short-Term Continuous Subcutaneous Insulin Infusion on Glycemic Control and Beta Cell Function in Patients with Newly Diagnosed Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Pilot Study.
population: Newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus patients according to 1999 WHO diagnostic criteria, without previous usage of antihyperglycemic and antihyperlipidemic medication, aged 20-65 years, body mass index 20-35 kg/m2, fasting plasma glucose 7.0-16.7 mmol/L. Exclusion criteria: severe acute or severe chronic diabetic complications, severe intercurrent illness, positive for autoimmune antibodies against islets, recent history of treatment with corticosteroid, immunosuppressing drugs, or cytotoxic drugs.
intervention: Liraglutide 0.6 mg per day subcutaneously during hospitalization in combination with continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII) using insulin aspart or insulin lispro via insulin pump (initial dosage 0.5-0.7 IU/kg/d, divided 50/50 as basal and bolus), continued for 14 days after achieving glycemic targets, then liraglutide 1.2 mg per day continued until 12 weeks total treatment
comparison: Continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII) alone using insulin aspart or insulin lispro via insulin pump (initial dosage 0.5-0.7 IU/kg/d, divided 50/50 as basal and bolus), continued for 14 days after achieving glycemic targets, followed by diet and physical exercise guidance
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified as primary; outcomes assessed included: time to achieve euglycemia, glycemic control (HbA1c, fasting plasma glucose, postprandial glucose), beta cell function (acute insulin response via IVGTT, HOMA-B), insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), daily insulin dosage
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly specified as secondary; additional outcomes included: body weight change, proportion of patients achieving HbA1c ≤6.5%, hyperglycemia relapse rate (>7.0 mmol/L), hypoglycemia incidence, gastrointestinal symptoms
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the text. Trial duration 12 weeks. Registered at ClinicalTrials.gov NCT01471808. Sample size relatively small (n=39 randomized, 31 completed follow-up).

title: Efficacy and safety of liraglutide for overweight adult patients with type 1 diabetes and insufficient glycaemic control (Lira-1): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
population: Adults aged 18 years or older with type 1 diabetes, insufficient glycaemic control (HbA1c >8% [64 mmol/mol]), and overweight (BMI >25 kg/m²)
intervention: Liraglutide subcutaneous injection once daily as add-on to insulin treatment, starting at 0.6 mg/day, escalated to 1.2 mg/day after 1 week, then to 1.8 mg/day after another week, for 24 weeks
comparison: Placebo (saline solution) subcutaneous injection once daily plus insulin treatment
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 24
outcomes_secondary: Changes in hypoglycaemic events, glycaemic variability, glycaemic excursions, insulin dose, bodyweight, postprandial plasma concentrations of glucagon and GLP-1, gastric emptying, blood pressure, heart rate, patient-reported outcome measures, time spent in hypoglycaemia, near-normoglycaemia, and hyperglycaemia, plasma fasting glucose, mean glucose, and cholesterol
extraction_notes: Dose escalation intervals could be extended at investigator discretion

title: Once-weekly glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist dulaglutide significantly decreases glycated haemoglobin compared with once-daily liraglutide in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes: 52 weeks of treatment in a randomized phase III study.
population: Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes; men or women aged ≥20 years; OAM-naïve (diet and exercise only) or had discontinued oral antidiabetic medication monotherapy (excluding thiazolidinedione); body mass index between 18.5 and 35.0 kg/m2; HbA1c levels between 7.0 and 10.0%
intervention: Dulaglutide 0.75 mg subcutaneous injection once weekly, initiated at full dose, for 52 weeks
comparison: Liraglutide 0.9 mg subcutaneous injection once daily (uptitrated from 0.3 mg/day during week 1 to 0.6 mg/day during week 2 and 0.9 mg/day starting at week 3), for 52 weeks; Placebo (blinded, switched to dulaglutide 0.75 mg once weekly after 26 weeks)
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline in HbA1c at 26 weeks (superiority of dulaglutide versus placebo)
outcomes_secondary: Change from baseline in HbA1c at 52 weeks; proportions of patients achieving HbA1c targets (<7.0% or ≤6.5%); change from baseline in fasting serum glucose; change from baseline in seven-point self-monitored blood glucose profiles; change from baseline in body weight; updated homoeostasis model assessment of β-cell function (HOMA2-%β); updated homoeostasis model assessment of insulin sensitivity (HOMA2-%S); adverse events; hypoglycaemia; vital signs (pulse rate and blood pressure); ECGs; laboratory variables; dulaglutide antidrug antibodies
extraction_notes: Primary endpoint was at 26 weeks; paper reports 52-week results. Liraglutide arm was open-label throughout the study. Placebo arm results not fully reported as patients switched to dulaglutide at 26 weeks.

title: Equivalent Increases in Circulating GLP-1 Following Jejunal Delivery of Intact and Hydrolysed Casein: Relevance to Satiety Induction Following Bariatric Surgery.
population: Healthy subjects in the fasted state, n=13
intervention: Direct jejunal infusion of intact casein
comparison: Direct jejunal infusion of casein hydrolysate
outcomes_primary: Circulating GLP-1 release
outcomes_secondary: Ratings of hunger and fullness; food intake at ad libitum meal; water intake at ad libitum meal; kinetics and magnitude of satiation
extraction_notes: Double-blind cross-over trial with 1 week washout between interventions; infusions administered in random order; ad libitum meal provided 30 minutes after infusion

title: Efficacy and Safety of Liraglutide Versus Placebo as Add-on to Glucose-Lowering Therapy in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes and Moderate Renal Impairment (LIRA-RENAL): A Randomized Clinical Trial.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes and moderate renal impairment (estimated glomerular filtration rate 30-59 mL/min/1.73 m² by MDRD), HbA1c 7-10%, BMI 20-45 kg/m², with inadequately controlled diabetes on existing glucose-lowering medications
intervention: Liraglutide 1.8 mg once daily as add-on to existing glucose-lowering therapy for 26 weeks
comparison: Placebo as add-on to existing glucose-lowering therapy
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 26
outcomes_secondary: Fasting plasma glucose, body weight, renal function (eGFR), adverse events including gastrointestinal adverse effects, hypoglycemic episodes, lipase levels
extraction_notes: Primary outcome not explicitly labeled but inferred from study design and reporting emphasis. Secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from primary.

title: Evaluation of Efficacy and Safety of the Glucagon Receptor Antagonist LY2409021 in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes: 12- and 24-Week Phase 2 Studies.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes
intervention: LY2409021 (glucagon receptor antagonist), once-daily oral administration. Phase 2a: 10 mg, 30 mg, or 60 mg for 12 weeks. Phase 2b: 2.5 mg, 10 mg, or 20 mg for 24 weeks
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: HbA1c change from baseline, glucose levels
outcomes_secondary: Serum aminotransferase levels (including ALT), fasting glucagon levels, total fasting GLP-1 levels, fasting glucose, incidence of hypoglycemia, overall tolerability and safety
extraction_notes: Two separate studies (Phase 2a and Phase 2b) with different doses and durations. Abstract does not explicitly distinguish primary vs secondary outcomes; classification inferred from emphasis in text.

title: Predictors of weight-loss response with glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist treatment among adolescents with severe obesity.
population: Adolescents aged 12-19 years with severe obesity (BMI ≥1.2 times the 95th percentile or BMI-SDS >2.3). Exclusion criteria: prior diagnosis of diabetes mellitus (type 1 or 2), use of medications associated with weight loss/gain within 3 months of screening, history of bariatric surgery, initiation of any new prescription drug within 30 days of screening, current pregnancy/plans to become pregnant, history of pancreatitis, obesity-associated genetic disorders.
intervention: Exenatide 5 mcg subcutaneously twice daily for 1 month, then increased to 10 mcg twice daily for 2 additional months, plus lifestyle modification therapy (dietary and physical activity counseling)
comparison: Placebo (in double-blind placebo-controlled trial) or lifestyle modification alone (control phase in crossover trial)
outcomes_primary: Percent change in BMI from baseline at 3 months
outcomes_secondary: Predictor variables including baseline BMI, BMI percent change at 1 month, incidence of nausea/vomiting, baseline appetite and satiety measures (assessed using Child Eating Behavior Questionnaire subscales)
extraction_notes: This is a pooled analysis of two previously conducted clinical trials with near-identical design. The analysis is described as hypothesis-generating and secondary/post-hoc in nature. Appetite and satiety data were available only from the first study (n=22).

title: Patient-reported outcome results in patients with type 2 diabetes treated with once-weekly dulaglutide: data from the AWARD phase III clinical trial programme.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes
intervention: Dulaglutide 1.5 mg and 0.75 mg, once-weekly administration
comparison: Insulin glargine, exenatide, metformin
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified
outcomes_secondary: Impact of Weight on Self-Perception (IW-SP), Impact of Weight on Ability to Perform Physical Activities of Daily Living (APPADL), Impact of Weight on Quality of Life-Lite, EQ-5D, Diabetes Treatment Satisfaction Questionnaire (DTSQ), Diabetes Symptom Checklist-Revised, Adult Low Blood Sugar Survey
extraction_notes: This is a pooled analysis of PRO measures from the AWARD clinical trial programme (multiple studies). Primary and secondary outcome designations not explicitly stated; all listed outcomes appear to be PRO measures analyzed across one or more AWARD studies.

title: Subgroup analysis of phase 3 studies of dulaglutide in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes.
population: Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes
intervention: Dulaglutide 0.75 mg, subcutaneous (implied), once weekly, for up to 26 weeks
comparison: Subgroup comparisons based on: sex (male, female), age (<65, ≥65 years), body weight (<70, ≥70 kg), body mass index (<25, ≥25 kg/m²), duration of diabetes (<7, ≥7 years), HbA1c (≤8.5%, >8.5%), concomitant sulfonylurea use (yes, no), concomitant biguanide use (yes, no)
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified as primary
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly specified as secondary; efficacy measures: change from baseline in HbA1c, change from baseline in body weight, percentage of patients achieving HbA1c <7.0%; safety measures: incidence of hypoglycemia, incidence of nausea, change from baseline in seated pulse rate
extraction_notes: Post hoc subgroup analysis of three phase 3 trials; primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished; this is a pooled analysis rather than a single RCT; original comparator arms from the parent trials not described in this abstract

title: Meal sequence and glucose excursion, gastric emptying and incretin secretion in type 2 diabetes: a randomised, controlled crossover, exploratory trial.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes (n=12) and healthy volunteers (n=10), aged 30-75 years, HbA1c 9.0% (75 mmol/mol) or less, BMI 35 kg/m2 or less. Exclusion criteria: type 1 diabetes, gastrointestinal tract disease including gastroparesis, history of gastrointestinal operation, cardiac disease, pulmonary disease, pancreatic disease, liver disease, renal disease, alcohol or drug abuse, glucose-lowering medication, diabetogenic medication, malignancy, pregnancy, or allergy to mackerel.
intervention: Fish before rice (FR): 920 kJ boiled mackerel ingested first, followed by 1,004 kJ steamed rice 15 minutes later. Meat before rice (MR): 920 kJ grilled beef ingested first, followed by 1,004 kJ steamed rice 15 minutes later.
comparison: Rice before fish (RF): 1,004 kJ steamed rice ingested first, followed by 920 kJ boiled mackerel 15 minutes later.
outcomes_primary: Postprandial glucose excursion (AUC glucose), glucose variability (SD glucose)
outcomes_secondary: Gastric emptying rate measured by 13C-acetate breath test (Time50%), insulin levels (AUC insulin), C-peptide levels (AUC C-peptide), glucagon levels (AUC glucagon), GLP-1 secretion (AUC GLP-1), GIP secretion (AUC GIP)
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the text; classification based on study objectives. Study was a randomised controlled crossover exploratory trial conducted at single centre in Osaka, Japan. Participants, measurers, and outcome assessors were not blinded to group assignment.

title: L-rhamnose as a source of colonic propionate inhibits insulin secretion but does not influence measures of appetite or food intake.
population: Healthy unrestrained eaters
intervention: L-rhamnose 25.5 g/d alongside standardized breakfast and lunch, following a 6-day run-in period
comparison: Inulin 22.4 g/d; No supplement (control)
outcomes_secondary: Postprandial qualitative appetite; Breath hydrogen; Plasma glucose; Plasma insulin; Plasma triglycerides; Plasma non-esterified fatty acids; Ad libitum meal intake; Quantitative appetite measures; Meal desire; Desire to eat sweet
extraction_notes: Primary outcome not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in the abstract. Sample size n=13. Single-blind randomized crossover study design.

title: Capsaicin-induced satiety is associated with gastrointestinal distress but not with the release of satiety hormones.
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
population: Healthy volunteers; 13 participants (7 women), mean age 21.5 years, BMI 22.8 kg/m²
intervention: Intraduodenal infusion of 1.5 mg pure capsaicin administered via nasoduodenal catheter over 30 minutes
comparison: Placebo (physiologic saline) intraduodenal infusion
outcomes_primary: Hunger, satiety, and gastrointestinal symptoms measured using visual analog scale scores; plasma GLP-1 and PYY concentrations
outcomes_secondary: Gallbladder volumes measured using real-time ultrasonography
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the abstract; outcomes listed are inferred from study objectives. Population characteristics include baseline statistics which may serve descriptive rather than eligibility-defining purposes.

title: Effects of exenatide and liraglutide on 24-hour glucose fluctuations in type 2 diabetes.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled by sulfonylureas
intervention: Add-on exenatide 10 μg/day twice daily
comparison: Add-on liraglutide 0.3-0.9 mg/day once daily
outcomes_primary: Daily blood glucose fluctuations assessed by mean amplitude of glycemic excursion (MAGE) and standard deviation (SD) via 24-hour continuous subcutaneous glucose monitoring
outcomes_secondary: Mean blood glucose levels at specific time points (3 hours after breakfast, 3 hours after dinner, between 0000h and 0600h)
extraction_notes: Open-label trial design. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated; outcomes categorized based on study objectives. Duration of treatment not specified.

title: Efficacy and safety of liraglutide 3.0 mg for weight management are similar across races: subgroup analysis across the SCALE and phase II randomized trials.
population: Adults with body mass index (BMI) ≥27 kg/m2 with at least one comorbidity, or BMI ≥30 kg/m2; analyzed by racial subgroups (white, black/African-American, Asian, other)
intervention: Liraglutide 3.0 mg once-daily subcutaneous injection, starting at 0.6 mg with weekly 0.6 mg increments to 3.0 mg, as adjunct to reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity; treatment duration 32-56 weeks depending on trial
comparison: Placebo once-daily subcutaneous injection as adjunct to reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity
outcomes_primary: Mean and categorical weight loss from baseline to end of treatment
outcomes_secondary: Cardiovascular risk markers (including HbA1c, fasting plasma glucose, blood pressure); health-related quality of life (Impact of Weight on Quality of Life-Lite questionnaire, SF-36); safety outcomes including adverse events, serious adverse events, events leading to discontinuation, gastrointestinal disorders, resting pulse
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc pooled analysis of five randomized controlled trials (four SCALE phase IIIa trials and one phase II trial). Primary/secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in text; categorization based on emphasis in reporting. Individual trial durations varied (3 trials of 56 weeks, 1 of 32 weeks, 1 of 52 weeks).

title: Effect of meal composition on postprandial glucagon-like peptide-1, insulin, glucagon, C-peptide, and glucose responses in overweight/obese subjects.
population: Overweight/obese participants without type 2 diabetes
intervention: High protein (HP) meal: 31.9% energy from protein
comparison: High monounsaturated fat (HMF) meal: 35.2% fat and 20.7% monounsaturated fat; both meals contained the same energy and carbohydrate content
outcomes_primary: GLP-1 response (active GLP-1, total GLP-1)
outcomes_secondary: Insulin, glucagon, C-peptide, glucose responses, appetite ratings, insulin sensitivity (Matsuda index), area under the curve for hormone responses
extraction_notes: Crossover design with meals consumed in random order. Sample size of 24 participants. Primary outcome not explicitly labeled but purpose statement indicates GLP-1 response as main focus.

title: Jejunal feeding is followed by a greater rise in plasma cholecystokinin, peptide YY, glucagon-like peptide 1, and glucagon-like peptide 2 concentrations compared with gastric feeding in vivo in humans: a randomized trial.
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
population: Healthy young men, mean age 21 ± 2 years
intervention: Continuous enteral nutrition containing noncoagulating proteins for 12 hours via nasojejunal tube placed 30-40 cm distal to the ligament of Treitz
comparison: Continuous enteral nutrition containing noncoagulating proteins for 12 hours via nasogastric tube
outcomes_secondary: Postprandial rise in plasma glucose concentrations, postprandial rise in plasma amino acid concentrations, plasma gastrointestinal hormone concentrations (insulin, cholecystokinin, peptide YY, glucagon-like peptide 1, glucagon-like peptide 2, ghrelin), peak plasma concentrations, postprandial incremental AUC
extraction_notes: Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in abstract. Randomized crossover study design with n=12 participants.

title: A Protein Preload Enhances the Glucose-Lowering Efficacy of Vildagliptin in Type 2 Diabetes.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes treated with metformin
intervention: Vildagliptin 50 mg (administered on the evening before and the morning of each study day) combined with a preload drink containing 25 g whey protein given 60 minutes after morning dose and 30 minutes before a mashed potato meal
comparison: Placebo with control flavoring (PLBO/CTRL), Placebo with whey protein preload (PLBO/WHEY), Vildagliptin with control flavoring (VILD/CTRL)
outcomes_primary: Plasma glucose, postprandial peak glycemia, area under the curve for glucose
outcomes_secondary: Plasma hormones (insulin, glucagon, incretin hormones including total and intact GLP-1 and GIP), gastric emptying
extraction_notes: Crossover study design with four treatment occasions. Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in the abstract.

title: Effects of endogenous GLP-1 and GIP on glucose tolerance after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery.
journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
population: Glucose-tolerant patients after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) surgery
intervention: Oral sitagliptin (DPP-4 inhibitor), exendin-(9-39) (Ex-9) infusion (GLP-1 receptor antagonist), or combined Ex-9-sitagliptin, administered with standard mixed-meal tests
comparison: Placebo
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes measured include glucose excursions/tolerance, β-cell function, insulin secretion, and glucagon secretion. Sample size is 12 patients. This is a randomized, placebo-controlled, 4-day crossover study design.

title: Protein-Enriched Liquid Preloads Varying in Macronutrient Content Modulate Appetite and Appetite-Regulating Hormones in Healthy Adults.
population: Healthy adults, mean age 27 ± 5 years, body mass index 24.3 ± 1.6 kg/m²
intervention: Liquid preloads with high protein content (40% of energy from protein) combined with varying carbohydrate-to-fat ratios (0.4, 2, or 3.6), isovolumetric (670 mL) and isoenergetic (2100 kJ), consumed at breakfast
comparison: Liquid preloads with low protein (9% of energy) or medium protein (24% of energy) combined with varying carbohydrate-to-fat ratios (0.4, 2, or 3.6), matched for volume, energy, energy density, and sensory properties
outcomes_primary: Appetite ratings (including prospective consumption, fullness), energy intake at ad libitum lunch test meal served 3.5 hours after breakfast
outcomes_secondary: Biomarkers of satiety including glucose, insulin, glucagon-like peptide 1, and ghrelin measured at baseline and every 60 minutes until lunch
extraction_notes: Within-subjects crossover design with 7 preload conditions using 2-level factorial design. Sample size n=36. Appetite ratings collected every 30 minutes, blood samples every 60 minutes.

title: A 24-week study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of once-weekly dulaglutide added on to glimepiride in type 2 diabetes (AWARD-8).
population: Adult men and women aged ≥18 years with type 2 diabetes, BMI ≤45 kg/m², HbA1c ≥7.5% and ≤9.5% (≥58 and ≤80 mmol/mol), on stable sulphonylurea monotherapy at least 50% of maximum dose for ≥3 months. Exclusions: treatment with other antihyperglycaemic medication (including insulin) <3 months before screening, history of pancreatitis, signs or symptoms of liver disease, impaired renal function (eGFR <30 ml/min/1.73 m²), elevated serum calcitonin concentration (≥20 ng/L), or recent history of severe hypoglycaemia.
intervention: Dulaglutide 1.5 mg once weekly, administered as subcutaneous injection, initiated at full 1.5 mg dose, added to glimepiride background therapy, for 24 weeks
comparison: Matching placebo once weekly subcutaneous injection added to glimepiride background therapy
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline at 24 weeks (superiority of dulaglutide versus placebo)
outcomes_secondary: Percentage of patients achieving HbA1c <7.0% (<53 mmol/mol); change from baseline in fasting serum glucose; change from baseline in body weight; percentage of patients achieving HbA1c ≤6.5% (≤48 mmol/mol); seven-point self-monitored plasma glucose profiles. Safety outcomes: adverse events, serious adverse events, hypoglycaemia (plasma glucose ≤3.9 mmol/l and <3.0 mmol/l thresholds), severe hypoglycaemia, vital signs, ECG parameters, antidrug antibodies, pancreatic events, cardiovascular events, serum calcitonin, C-cell hyperplasia/neoplasms, allergic/hypersensitivity reactions
extraction_notes: Randomization ratio was 4:1 dulaglutide:placebo. Sequential gatekeeping strategy used for secondary endpoints. Background glimepiride dose could be reduced for hypoglycaemia or adverse events.

title: Circulating adiponectin levels in type 2 diabetes mellitus patients with or without non-alcoholic fatty liver disease: Results of a small, open-label, randomized controlled intervention trial in a subgroup receiving short-term exenatide.
population: Type 2 diabetes mellitus patients with abnormal aminotransferases; subgroup assessed for eligibility criteria (n=110) for intervention trial
intervention: 6-month exenatide supplementation on glargine insulin
comparison: Intense, self-regulated insulin therapy alone
outcomes_primary: Circulating adiponectin levels
outcomes_secondary: Weight loss, HbA1c (glycemic control), C-reactive protein, ALT levels
extraction_notes: Small, open-label study design. Exenatide dose, route, and frequency not specified in abstract. The study also included a non-randomized observational component (group A, n=17) with liver biopsy for NAFLD assessment, separate from the randomized intervention trial.

title: Liraglutide is effective and well tolerated in combination with an oral antidiabetic drug in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes: A randomized, 52-week, open-label, parallel-group trial.
population: Male and female Japanese patients aged ≥20 years with type 2 diabetes for at least 6 months, HbA1c levels of 7.0–10.0%, body mass index <40.0 kg/m2, receiving OAD monotherapy (glinide, metformin, α-glucosidase inhibitor or thiazolidinedione) inadequately controlled, with diet and exercise therapy. Exclusions: use of GLP-1 receptor agonist, DPP-4 inhibitor or insulin within past 12 weeks; personal history of non-familial medullary thyroid carcinoma; family or personal history of multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 or familial medullary thyroid carcinoma; malignant tumor; history of chronic pancreatitis or idiopathic acute pancreatitis; calcitonin ≥160 pg/mL; contraindications to liraglutide or OADs; recurrent severe hypoglycemia, hypoglycemia unawareness or hospitalization for diabetic ketoacidosis during previous 6 months
intervention: Liraglutide 0.9 mg/day subcutaneous injection once daily (starting dose 0.3 mg/day escalated to 0.6 mg/day after 1 week, then to 0.9 mg/day after a further week) added to pretrial OAD (glinide, metformin, α-glucosidase inhibitor or thiazolidinedione) for 52 weeks
comparison: Additional OAD (DPP-4 inhibitor, SU, glinide, metformin, α-glucosidase inhibitor or thiazolidinedione with mechanism of action different from pretrial OAD) added to pretrial OAD for 52 weeks; type, dosage and administration chosen by investigator within approved labeling
outcomes_primary: Incidence of adverse events during 52 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Number of hypoglycemic episodes during 52 weeks; changes from baseline in vital signs (blood pressure and pulse rate); change from baseline in HbA1c; change from baseline in fasting plasma glucose; proportion of patients achieving target HbA1c <7.0%; change from baseline in bodyweight; change from baseline in β-cell function (HOMA-B, proinsulin:insulin ratio, proinsulin:C-peptide ratio); seven-point self-measured plasma glucose profiles (change from baseline in mean plasma glucose and mean prandial plasma glucose increment)
extraction_notes: Open-label trial design. Randomization ratio was 2:1 (liraglutide:additional OAD). The 0.9 mg/day dose is the maximum approved dose in Japan, which is half the maximum dose in Europe and USA (1.8 mg/day).

title: Comparison of short-term energy intake and appetite responses to active and seated video gaming, in 8-11-year-old boys.
population: 8-11-year-old boys
intervention: 90-minute active video gaming session with ad libitum food and drinks provided
comparison: 90-minute seated video gaming session with ad libitum food and drinks provided
outcomes_primary: Energy intake during gaming sessions
outcomes_secondary: Blood glucose, plasma glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-17-36), subjective appetite (hunger, prospective food consumption, fullness), energy intake at post-gaming test meal 1 hour later, relative energy intake, estimated energy expenditure
extraction_notes: Randomised crossover design with n=22 boys. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; inferred from study focus. Study examines acute effects rather than long-term intervention.

title: Efficacy and tolerability of exenatide twice daily and exenatide once weekly in Asian versus White patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: A pooled analysis.
population: Asian and White patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), race self-identified
intervention: Exenatide 10 μg twice daily (BID) for 12-30 weeks or exenatide 2 mg once weekly (QW) for 24-30 weeks
comparison: Asian patients versus White patients (within each exenatide formulation group)
outcomes_primary: Glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) change from baseline
outcomes_secondary: Fasting glucose (FG), body weight, post-prandial glucose (PPG), PPG excursions, adverse events including nausea, headache, and diarrhea
extraction_notes: Post-hoc pooled analysis of trials from exenatide clinical development program; primary outcome not explicitly designated but HbA1c appears to be the main efficacy endpoint based on presentation

title: The insulinotropic effect of pulsatile compared with continuous intravenous delivery of GLP-1.
population: Healthy individuals aged 18-35 years
intervention: Pulsatile intravenous GLP-1 infusion: 3.6 pmol/kg GLP-1 bolus every 6 minutes with placebo continuous infusion at 1 ml/min
comparison: Continuous intravenous GLP-1 infusion: 0.6 pmol kg-1 min-1 at 1 ml/min with 1 ml placebo bolus every 6 minutes; Placebo: placebo infusion at 1 ml/min with 1 ml placebo bolus every 6 minutes
outcomes_primary: Insulinotropic response (insulin secretion), dextrose requirement during hyperglycaemic clamp
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucagon concentrations
extraction_notes: Cross-over design with three treatment arms administered on separate days. Hyperglycaemic clamp maintained blood glucose at 9 mmol/l between 45 and 120 minutes. Study duration for each treatment day not explicitly stated beyond the 120-minute measurement period.

title: GLP-1 receptors exist in the parietal cortex, hypothalamus and medulla of human brains and the GLP-1 analogue liraglutide alters brain activity related to highly desirable food cues in individuals with diabetes: a crossover, randomised, placebo-controlled trial.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes (defined as fasting plasma glucose > 6.94 mmol/l and/or HbA1c > 6.5% or 47.5 mmol/mol) currently being treated with lifestyle changes or metformin
intervention: Liraglutide subcutaneous injection, dose-escalated over 17 days total (0.6 mg daily for 7 days, 1.2 mg daily for 7 days, 1.8 mg daily for 3 days)
comparison: Placebo (matching dose-escalation schedule over 17 days)
outcomes_primary: Neural responses to food cues measured by functional MRI (fMRI) brain activation in response to highly desirable versus less desirable food images
outcomes_secondary: Expression of GLP-1 receptors in human brain tissue (hypothalamus, medulla oblongata, parietal cortex) via immunohistochemistry; subjective ratings of hunger, appetite, and nausea using visual analogue scale (VAS); neurocognitive testing; metabolic changes including fasting blood glucose, HbA1c, fructosamine; anthropometric measurements (weight, BMI, waist circumference, fat mass); energy intake; resting metabolic rate; safety parameters (amylase, lipase)
extraction_notes: This paper includes two distinct studies: Study 1 is an immunohistochemistry study of postmortem brain tissue (n=22 brains), and Study 2 is the RCT (n=21 randomized, n=18 analyzed). The crossover design included minimum 3 weeks, maximum 3 months wash-out period between arms.

title: Exposure-response analyses of liraglutide 3.0 mg for weight management.
population: Adults with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2) or overweight with weight-related comorbidities (BMI 27-29.9 kg/m2 with hypertension and/or dyslipidaemia), or overweight/obese adults with type 2 diabetes (BMI ≥27 kg/m2, HbA1c 7.0-10.0%)
intervention: Liraglutide subcutaneous injection at doses of 1.2 mg, 1.8 mg, 2.4 mg, or 3.0 mg daily, as adjunct to diet and exercise; treatment duration 20 weeks (phase II trial) or 56 weeks (phase IIIa trials)
comparison: Placebo; orlistat 120 mg three times daily (phase II trial only)
outcomes_primary: Exposure-response relationship for body weight change from baseline; exposure-response relationship for HbA1c change (in type 2 diabetes population)
outcomes_secondary: Proportion achieving ≥5% and >10% weight loss; safety outcomes including nausea, vomiting, hypoglycaemia, pulse rate, serum calcitonin; adverse events of special interest including gallbladder adverse events, acute pancreatitis, malignant neoplasms, breast neoplasms, benign colorectal neoplasms
extraction_notes: This is a pooled exposure-response analysis of one phase II and two phase IIIa trials (n=4372 total from safety analysis sets). Primary outcomes are exposure-response relationships rather than between-group comparisons. The analysis is secondary/exploratory in nature.

title: Phase III Study on Efficacy and Safety of Triple Combination (Exenatide/Metformin/Biphasic Insulin Aspart) Therapy for Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
population: Patients with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus
intervention: Normal-dose triple combination therapy: exenatide 2 μg twice daily, biphasic insulin aspart 30 (BIA30) 0.2 U·kg·d twice daily, and metformin 0.05 g twice daily for 48 weeks
comparison: Low-dose triple combination therapy: exenatide 0.5 μg twice daily, biphasic insulin aspart 30 (BIA30) 0.05 U·kg·d twice daily, and metformin 0.01 g twice daily for 48 weeks
outcomes_primary: Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) levels
outcomes_secondary: Weight change; insulin sensitivity; adiponectin levels; C-reactive protein levels; tumor necrosis factor-α levels; resistin levels; adverse effects
extraction_notes: No placebo or standard care comparator; both groups received triple combination therapy at different doses. Primary versus secondary outcome designation not explicitly stated in abstract.

title: Effects of liraglutide on no-reflow in patients with acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction.
population: Patients with acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI)
intervention: Liraglutide 1.8 mg administered 30 minutes before PCI
comparison: Placebo administered 30 minutes before PCI
outcomes_primary: Prevalence of no-reflow phenomenon after PCI
outcomes_secondary: Serum high-sensitivity C-reactive protein levels at 6-hour reperfusion; incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events at 3-month follow-up
extraction_notes: 210 of 284 enrolled patients were randomized; route of administration not specified

title: LEADER-4: blood pressure control in patients with type 2 diabetes and high cardiovascular risk: baseline data from the LEADER randomized trial.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus aged at least 50 years with concomitant cardiovascular disease, cerebrovascular disease, peripheral vascular disease, chronic renal failure, or chronic heart failure; or aged at least 60 years with one or more cardiovascular risk factors (microalbuminuria or proteinuria, hypertension, left ventricular hypertrophy, left ventricular dysfunction, or ankle-brachial index less than 0.9); baseline HbA1c at least 7.0%
intervention: Liraglutide (GLP-1 receptor agonist), dosing details not specified in this baseline analysis paper, treatment duration at least 3.5 years and up to 5 years
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Composite cardiovascular endpoint: cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke
outcomes_secondary: Blood pressure control in relation to international targets (less than 130/80 mmHg, less than 140/85 mmHg, less than 140/90 mmHg)
extraction_notes: This paper reports baseline data only from the LEADER trial, not trial results. The main trial outcomes are described but results are not yet available as the trial was ongoing at time of publication. Liraglutide dose not specified in this publication.

title: Difference in postprandial GLP-1 response despite similar glucose kinetics after consumption of wheat breads with different particle size in healthy men.
population: Healthy men, age 24 ± 0.6 years, BMI 22 ± 0.2 kg/m2. Exclusion criteria: use of medication, blood donation or use of antibiotics in past three months, gastrointestinal surgery or dysfunction, inflammatory diseases, diabetes mellitus.
intervention: Kernel bread (KB): 13C-enriched wheat bread with 85% broken wheat kernels substituted for flour, 137g portion providing 50g available carbohydrates, consumed with 10g light margarine, 2 slices lean ham, and 250mL tap water within 20 minutes, single administration
comparison: Control bread (CB): 13C-enriched wheat bread made from wheat flour combined with wheat bran (same dietary fiber content as KB), 138g portion providing 50g available carbohydrates, consumed with 10g light margarine, 2 slices lean ham, and 250mL tap water within 20 minutes
outcomes_primary: Postprandial glucose kinetics including rate of appearance of exogenous glucose (RaE), endogenous glucose production (EGP), and glucose clearance rate (GCR); postprandial plasma concentrations of glucose, insulin, glucagon, incretins (GIP, GLP-1), cholecystokinin (CCK), and bile acids
outcomes_secondary: 13CO2 excretion in breath (reflecting oxidation rate of 13C-labeled substrate), visual analog scale ratings of appetite (hunger), discomfort (abdominal pain, flatulence), and meal liking
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the text; classification inferred from study objectives. Sample size n=10. Randomized crossover design with at least 1 week washout between study days.

title: Ghrelin, GLP-1, and leptin responses during exposure to moderate hypoxia.
journal: Applied physiology, nutrition, and metabolism = Physiologie appliquee, nutrition et metabolisme
population: Healthy males

title: LEADER 5: prevalence and cardiometabolic impact of obesity in cardiovascular high-risk patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: baseline global data from the LEADER trial.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus at high cardiovascular risk: (1) aged ≥50 years with prior cardiovascular disease (CVD), cerebrovascular disease, peripheral vascular disease, chronic renal failure, or chronic heart failure; (2) aged ≥60 years with one or more cardiovascular risk factors (microalbuminuria or proteinuria, hypertension and left ventricular hypertrophy, left ventricular dysfunction by imaging, or ankle-brachial index <0.9). intervention: Liraglutide up to 1.8 mg daily (glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist)
comparison: Placebo

title: Flaked sorghum biscuits increase postprandial GLP-1 and GIP levels and extend subjective satiety in healthy subjects.

population: Obese participants with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus, aged 45 to 65 years, BMI 30-40 kg/m². Panel A: obese but otherwise healthy subjects. Panel B: obese patients with T2DM who were treatment naive with hemoglobin A1c ≥6.5% and ≤10.0%

title: Gender-related different effects of a combined therapy of Exenatide and Metformin on overweight or obesity patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

Study design is randomized crossover with 5 treatment conditions.

title: Effect of chenodeoxycholic acid and the bile acid sequestrant colesevelam on glucagon-like peptide-1 secretion.

title: Inhibitory effect of the C-terminal octapeptide of oxyntomodulin on pentagastrin-stimulated gastric acid secretion in man.

extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=8). Double-blind randomized protocol specified. Study appears to be a crossover design based on context but not explicitly stated. Duration of follow-up limited to acute effects post-injection.

title: GLP-1 Restores Altered Insulin and Glucagon Secretion in Posttransplantation Diabetes.

comparison: Intravenous saline infusion (same protocol on separate experimental day)

Measured outcomes included glucagon suppression, first- and second-phase insulin secretion, fasting plasma glucose, insulin response to arginine, glucagon response to arginine, and proinsulin response. This appears to be a mechanistic/physiological study rather than a typical therapeutic trial.

title: Mechanisms of Action of Liraglutide in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Treated With High-Dose Insulin.

extraction_notes: Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract; outcomes listed under 'Main Outcome Measures' were grouped together

title: Short-term effects of liraglutide on kidney function and vasoactive hormones in type 2 diabetes: a randomized clinical trial.

title: Rationale and design of Short-Term EXenatide therapy in Acute ischaemic Stroke (STEXAS): a randomised, open-label, parallel-group study.
population: Adults aged >18 years with clinically defined acute ischaemic stroke with consistent neuroimaging (CT brain, CT perfusion or MRI brain) and blood glucose levels >10 mmol/L during the first 72 hours after admission to the acute stroke ward. Exclusions: Type 1 diabetes mellitus, initial NIHSS >20, life expectancy below 12 months, premorbid Modified Rankin Score above 3, impaired liver function (ALT ≥3 times upper limit of normal), impaired renal function (eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m²), history of pancreatitis, history of pancreatic cancer, history of medullary thyroid cancer or multiple endocrine neoplasia II, known allergy to exenatide, suspected or known abuse of alcohol or narcotics, pregnancy or lactation

outcomes_primary: Percentage of time that participant's blood glucose levels remain within target glucose range of 5-10 mmol/L as determined by continuous glucose monitoring
outcomes_secondary: Frequency and duration of hypoglycaemia (capillary blood glucose/interstitial glucose level <4 mmol/L); percentage of time blood glucose levels remain within target range (5-10 mmol/L) in the first 24 hours after commencing treatment; change in National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale from baseline at 24 hours, 3 days and 3 months; Modified Rankin Scale rating at 3 months; frequency of low blood sugars (4-5 mmol/L); feasibility of exenatide administration in acute ischaemic stroke setting; safety and tolerability of exenatide therapy
extraction_notes: This is a study protocol/design paper, not a completed trial. Sample size is 30 patients total (15 per arm). Open-label design with block randomisation.

title: Comparison of efficacy and safety of taking miglitol dissolved in water during a meal and taking a miglitol tablet just before a meal in patients with type 2 diabetes.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes
intervention: Miglitol 50 mg dissolved in water, taken in divided doses: 1/3 just before breakfast, 1/3 during breakfast, and 1/3 just after breakfast (intake schedule C)
comparison: Intake schedule A: no miglitol; Intake schedule B: miglitol 50 mg tablet taken just before breakfast
outcomes_primary: Area under the curve (AUC) for postprandial plasma glucose
outcomes_secondary: AUC for plasma insulin; AUC for total glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP); AUC for total glucagon like peptide-1 (GLP-1); Coefficient of variation (CV) of plasma glucose
extraction_notes: Crossover design with three intake schedules in each subject. Sample size not reported in abstract. Blood samples collected at 0, 30, 60, 120, and 180 min after breakfast.

title: Effect of Insulin Glargine Up-titration vs Insulin Degludec/Liraglutide on Glycated Hemoglobin Levels in Patients With Uncontrolled Type 2 Diabetes: The DUAL V Randomized Clinical Trial.
population: Patients with uncontrolled type 2 diabetes treated with insulin glargine (20-50 U) and metformin (≥1500 mg/d), with glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels of 7% to 10% and body mass index of 40 or lower

comparison: Insulin glargine up-titration (no maximum dose), with twice-weekly titration to a glucose target of 72 to 90 mg/dL, for 26 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c level after 26 weeks, with a noninferiority margin of 0.3% (upper bound of 95% CI <0.3%)
outcomes_secondary: Change in HbA1c level (superiority), change in body weight, rate of confirmed hypoglycemic episodes
extraction_notes: Open-label trial design. 1:1 randomization. Metformin continued as background therapy in both groups.

title: Mechanisms Regulating Insulin Response to Intragastric Glucose in Lean and Non-Diabetic Obese Subjects: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Parallel-Group Trial.
population: Normal weight healthy volunteers (BMI 19.0-24.9 kg/m2) and non-diabetic obese participants (BMI >30, range 30.5-48.4 kg/m2); 6 men and 6 women in each group; exclusions included smoking, substance abuse, regular intake of medications, psychiatric or medical illness (especially diabetes), gastrointestinal disorders, food allergies or dietary restrictions

outcomes_primary: Plasma GLP-1 and GIP concentrations; plasma glucagon, glucose, insulin, and C-peptide concentrations; gastric emptying rate
outcomes_secondary: Gastric emptying rates of different glucose loads; HOMA-IR index; insulin clearance (insulin:C-peptide molar ratio); plasma PYY concentrations
extraction_notes: Study registered after enrolment began (NCT01875575). Sample size was based on practical considerations rather than statistical estimation. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly differentiated in abstract; classification inferred from methods section stating primary outcome was characterizing glycemia-regulating parameters and secondary was gastric emptying rates.

title: Relationship between weight change and glycaemic control in patients with type 2 diabetes receiving once-weekly dulaglutide treatment.
population: Adult patients with type 2 diabetes enrolled in six AWARD phase III clinical trials
intervention: Dulaglutide 1.5 mg or 0.75 mg administered once weekly subcutaneously, used as monotherapy, combination therapy with one or two oral antihyperglycaemic medications, or combination therapy with mealtime insulin lispro
comparison: Metformin, sitagliptin, exenatide twice daily, insulin glargine, liraglutide, or placebo (depending on individual trial)
outcomes_primary: HbA1c reduction from baseline
outcomes_secondary: Weight change from baseline; composite endpoint of achieving weight change ≤0 kg and HbA1c change ≤0%; correlation between weight change and HbA1c change; proportion of patients with both weight loss and HbA1c reduction; incidence of nausea and/or vomiting
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc pooled analysis of six AWARD trials rather than a single RCT. Data extracted at 26 weeks across all studies. Background therapies varied across trials including metformin, sulphonylurea, pioglitazone, and insulin lispro.

title: Effect of adding insulin degludec to treatment in patients with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled with metformin and liraglutide: a double-blind randomized controlled trial (BEGIN: ADD TO GLP-1 Study).
population: Adults aged ≥18 years with type 2 diabetes not previously treated with insulin, BMI ≤45 kg/m2, receiving metformin (≥1500 mg daily or maximum tolerated dose) plus liraglutide 1.8 mg daily, with inadequate glycaemic control (HbA1c 7.0–9.0% [53–75 mmol/mol]) after a 15-week run-in period with liraglutide initiation and dose escalation
intervention: Insulin degludec (IDeg) 10 U once daily subcutaneously, titrated according to guideline aiming at self-measured plasma glucose values of 4.0–5.0 mmol/l, added to liraglutide 1.8 mg daily and metformin (≥1500 mg daily), for 26 weeks
comparison: Placebo once daily subcutaneously (dispensed from identical pen, measured in 'dummy units'), titrated according to same guideline, added to liraglutide 1.8 mg daily and metformin (≥1500 mg daily), for 26 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline in HbA1c after 26 weeks of randomized treatment
outcomes_secondary: Change in fasting plasma glucose at 26 weeks; percentage of responders achieving HbA1c <7.0% (<53 mmol/mol); change from baseline in mean pre-breakfast self-measured plasma glucose (SMPG) measurements; change from baseline in 8-point SMPG profile; change from baseline in mean of the 8-point SMPG profile; change from baseline in body weight; change from baseline in health-related quality of life (HRQoL); dose of IDeg/placebo; adverse events; hypoglycaemic episodes (confirmed, nocturnal confirmed, severe); changes from baseline in clinical evaluations and central laboratory assessments
extraction_notes: Run-in period of 15 weeks preceded randomization; only patients who failed to reach HbA1c target on maximum liraglutide dose after run-in were randomized; previous antihyperglycaemic therapies except metformin were discontinued at run-in entry

title: Rationale and design of the EXenatide Study of Cardiovascular Event Lowering (EXSCEL) trial.
