title: Effect of liraglutide 3.0 mg in individuals with obesity and moderate or severe obstructive sleep apnea: the SCALE Sleep Apnea randomized clinical trial.
population: Non-diabetic adults aged 18-64 years with stable body weight (<5% change during previous 3 months), BMI ≥30 kg/m², diagnosed with moderate (AHI 15.0-29.9 events/h) or severe (AHI ≥30.0 events/h) obstructive sleep apnea, unable or unwilling to use CPAP therapy. intervention: Liraglutide 3.0 mg once daily subcutaneous injection (initiated at 0.6 mg/day and escalated in weekly 0.6 mg increments to 3.0 mg by week 4, then maintained for 28 weeks) as adjunct to diet (500 kcal/day deficit below estimated total energy expenditure, approximately 30% fat, 20% protein, 50% carbohydrates) and exercise counseling (advised to increase physical activity to at least 150 min per week) for 32 weeks.

outcomes_primary: Change in apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) from baseline to week 32, using American Academy of Sleep Medicine 2007 definition (hypopnea scoring requiring ≥30% reduction in nasal pressure signal excursions from baseline and ≥4% desaturation from pre-event baseline).
outcomes_secondary: Changes from baseline to week 32 in: OSA severity category; blood oxygen saturation parameters (lowest oxygen saturation, percentage of time with oxygen saturation <90%, oxygen desaturation ≥4% index); sleep architecture parameters (total sleep time, wake time after sleep onset, proportion of sleep spent in supine position, sleep stage distribution); body weight-related parameters (fasting body weight, proportion losing ≥5% or >10% baseline weight, BMI, waist circumference, neck circumference); glycemic parameters (HbA1c, fasting plasma glucose); vital signs (systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, pulse); fasting lipids (HDL, LDL, VLDL, total cholesterol, triglycerides); cardiovascular biomarkers (high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, urinary albumin:creatinine ratio); daytime sleepiness (Epworth Sleepiness Scale); self-reported quality of life (Functional Outcomes of Sleep Questionnaire, SF-36 health status survey).
extraction_notes: Safety outcomes were assessed but listed as safety assessments rather than formal secondary efficacy endpoints.

title: Comparison of exenatide with biphasic insulin aspart 30 on glucose variability in type 2 diabetes: study protocol for a randomized controlled trial.

outcomes_primary: Absolute change in mean amplitude of glycemic excursion (MAGE) from baseline to week 16, assessed by continuous glucose monitoring system (CGMS)
outcomes_secondary: HbA1c at baseline and week 16; hours of hypoglycemia assessed by CGMS; self-monitored blood glucose; blood pressure and lipids; body weight, BMI and waist circumference; inflammatory markers (MCP-1, hs-CRP); urinary albumin; safety outcomes including adverse events, vital signs, clinical hypoglycemia, clinical chemistry/hematology parameters, and electrocardiogram
extraction_notes: Study protocol publication; open-label design; 16-week treatment period; multicenter trial in China with 8 sites

title: Post-prandial anorexigenic gut peptide, appetite and glucometabolic responses at different eating rates in obese patients undergoing laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy.

title: Acute renal effects of the GLP-1 receptor agonist exenatide in overweight type 2 diabetes patients: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
population: White, overweight (BMI 25–40 kg/m²) men and postmenopausal women, aged 35–75 years, with type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 48–75 mmol/mol; 6.5–9.0%), estimated GFR ≥60 ml min⁻¹ 1.73 m⁻², on stable dose of metformin and/or sulfonylurea for at least 3 months. title: Effects of the Novel Long-Acting GLP-1 Agonist, Albiglutide, on Cardiac Function, Cardiac Metabolism, and Exercise Capacity in Patients With Chronic Heart Failure and Reduced Ejection Fraction.

title: Ghrelin Impairs Prandial Glucose Tolerance and Insulin Secretion in Healthy Humans Despite Increasing GLP-1.

title: Efficacy and safety of liraglutide versus sitagliptin, both in combination with metformin, in Chinese patients with type 2 diabetes: a 26-week, open-label, randomized, active comparator clinical trial.

title: Linearity of β-cell response across the metabolic spectrum and to pharmacology: insights from a graded glucose infusion-based investigation series.

title: Intensive Behavioral Therapy for Obesity Combined with Liraglutide 3.0 mg: A Randomized Controlled Trial.

Exclusions: personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer or multiple endocrine neoplasia syndrome; types 1 or 2 diabetes; renal, hepatic, or recent cardiovascular disease; blood pressure ≥160/100 mm Hg; medications that substantially affect body weight; substance abuse; current major depression, suicidal ideation, or history of suicide attempts; bariatric surgery; use of weight loss medications or products; weight loss ≥4.5 kg in past 3 months; pregnancy/lactation
intervention: IBT-liraglutide: Intensive behavioral therapy (21 counseling sessions of 15 minutes each over 1 year: 4 weekly visits in month 1, every-other-week visits in months 2-6, monthly visits in months 7-12) combined with liraglutide 3.0 mg/day subcutaneous injection (titrated from 0.6 mg/day, increasing by 0.6 mg/day weekly until 3.0 mg/day achieved). Multi-component: Same IBT plus liraglutide regimen, plus a 1000-1200 kcal/day portion-controlled meal-replacement diet for 12 weeks (starting at week 4) consisting of four liquid shakes (160 kcal each) and an evening meal of frozen food entrée (250-300 kcal) with fruit and salad
comparison: IBT-alone: Intensive behavioral therapy only (21 counseling sessions of 15 minutes each over 1 year following CMS schedule) with calorie-controlled diet of conventional foods (1200-1499 kcal/d for those <113.6 kg, 1500-1800 kcal/d for those ≥113.6 kg) and physical activity building to ≥180 minutes/week by week 24 and ≥225 minutes/week from weeks 25-52
outcomes_primary: Mean percentage reduction in baseline body weight at week 52
outcomes_secondary: Percentage of participants achieving ≥5%, ≥10%, and ≥15% weight loss; percentage achieving ≥3 kg weight loss; weight change at week 24; changes in waist circumference, blood pressure, fasting glucose, insulin, triglycerides, C-reactive protein, lipids (LDL, HDL cholesterol), hemoglobin A1c, heart rate; quality of life; symptoms of depression
extraction_notes: Open-label trial design without placebo control. All three groups received seven brief (5 minute) medical visits over the year. 150 participants randomized in equal numbers to three groups (50 per arm).

title: Effects of Meal Timing on Postprandial Glucose Metabolism and Blood Metabolites in Healthy Adults.
population: Healthy young men aged 21-30 years; inclusion criteria: not using glucose/insulin-lowering or related medication, no change in body weight of more than 5% within past six months, not heavy drinkers (men: <40 g/day), not diagnosed with diabetes or dyslipidemia by a doctor, not taking any anti-oxidant, anti-obesity, or anti-diabetes supplementation
intervention: Evening meal (~1700 h) consisting of rice, pork, onion, green pepper, asparagus, bok-choy, enoki, cod roe, egg, vermicelli, carrot, leek and yogurt; prescribed at 60 kJ energy/kg body mass (15% fat, 70% carbohydrate, 15% protein); consumed within 20 min after 4-hour fasting state
comparison: Morning meal (~0900 h) with identical composition; consumed within 20 min after minimum 10-hour overnight fast
outcomes_primary: Postprandial glucose concentrations measured at 30, 60 and 120 min after meal provision; postprandial glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) concentrations; postprandial glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) concentrations; postprandial insulin concentrations; incremental area under the curve (iAUC) for blood glucose, insulin, GIP, and GLP-1
outcomes_secondary: Blood metabolome analysis using capillary electrophoresis-mass spectrometry including glycolysis, tricarboxylic acid cycle and nucleotide-related metabolites and amino acid-related metabolites; total metabolic change assessed by partial least-squares analysis
extraction_notes: Randomized crossover design; metabolome analysis conducted on subset of 8 participants; no explicit designation of primary vs secondary outcomes in the text - categorization based on apparent study focus

title: LY3298176, a novel dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus: From discovery to clinical proof of concept.
population: Phase 1 study comprised of three parts: (1) Single-ascending dose (SAD) and (2) 4-week multiple-ascending dose (MAD) in healthy subjects; (3) 4-week multiple-dose Phase 1b proof-of-concept (POC) in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM)
intervention: LY3298176 (dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist), fatty acid modified peptide for once-weekly subcutaneous administration. SAD: doses 0.25-8 mg single dose; MAD: doses 0.5-10 mg once weekly for 4 weeks (Days 1, 8, 15, 22), including non-titrated arms (0.5-4.5 mg) and titration arm (5/5/8/10 mg); POC: doses 0.5-15 mg once weekly for 4 weeks, including fixed doses (0.5 mg, 5 mg) and titration schedules (5/5/10/10 mg and 5/5/10/15 mg)
comparison: Placebo (normal saline matching volume); Dulaglutide 1.5 mg/week subcutaneously (positive control in MAD healthy subjects only)
outcomes_primary: Safety and tolerability following single and multiple doses of LY3298176 in healthy subjects and patients with T2DM
outcomes_secondary: Pharmacokinetics of LY3298176; pharmacodynamics including changes in HbA1c, fasting glucose, fasting insulin, body weight, 7-point self-monitored blood glucose (SMBG) profiles, and glucose and insulin response following oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT); hypoglycaemia events; laboratory parameters; vital signs; electrocardiogram (ECG) parameters; LY3298176 antidrug antibodies (ADAs)
extraction_notes: This is a Phase 1 study with preclinical and clinical components. The clinical trial included three sequential parts (SAD, MAD, POC) with different populations (healthy subjects vs T2DM patients). Randomization ratios varied by study part: SAD 3:1, MAD 6:1:1, POC 4:1. Dulaglutide comparator was only included in MAD healthy subjects portion. ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT02759107

title: Sleep and meal timing influence food intake and its hormonal regulation in healthy adults with overweight/obesity.
population: Healthy adults aged 20-49 years with overweight/obesity (BMI 25-34.9 kg/m2), intermediate chronotype, habitual sleep duration 7-9 hours/night, midpoint of sleep 0400h or earlier, habitual breakfast eaters (food intake within 1 hour of awakening at least 4 times/week), without sleep, eating, or other psychological disorders
intervention: Late sleep timing (0330-1130h) and/or late meal timing (meals at 4.5, 8.5, 14.5, and 16 hours after awakening) in a 2x2 factorial design with 4 inpatient phases
comparison: Normal sleep timing (0000-0800h) and normal meal timing (meals at 1, 5, 11, and 12.5 hours after awakening)
outcomes_primary: Self-selected food intake (energy intake, macronutrient composition) on day 5 of each phase
outcomes_secondary: Appetite-regulating hormone concentrations (ghrelin, leptin, glucagon-like peptide 1) during overnight period and in response to meal tolerance test; visual analog scale assessments of appetite (hunger, satisfaction, fullness, desire to eat, energy level, cravings for sweet/salty/savory foods and fruits/vegetables)
extraction_notes: This is a crossover study design where each participant serves as their own control across all 4 conditions. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly designated; classification based on study objectives. Only 5 of 6 enrolled participants completed all phases.

title: Phytosterols and inulin-enriched soymilk increases glucagon-like peptide-1 secretion in healthy men: double-blind randomized controlled trial, subgroup study.

outcomes_secondary: Differences in AUC of plasma glucose, insulin, and GLP-1 between intervention and control groups
extraction_notes: This is a subgroup study of a larger RCT (240 participants), including only male participants (26 men). One participant with extreme fasting insulin value was removed before primary analysis. Neither specific dietary control nor exercise intervention was given.

title: Thromboxane-Dependent Platelet Activation in Obese Subjects with Prediabetes or Early Type 2 Diabetes: Effects of Liraglutide- or Lifestyle Changes-Induced Weight Loss.
population: Obese subjects (BMI ≥30) with prediabetes (impaired glucose tolerance or impaired fasting glucose) or newly-diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus (diagnosis <12 months), on metformin treatment at highest tolerated dose (up to 3000 mg/day). Exclusion criteria: type 1 diabetes, MODY, BMI <30, diabetes diagnosis >12 months, oral antidiabetic agents other than metformin or insulin treatment in last 3 months, uncontrolled hypertension (>160/90 mmHg), kidney disease (GFR <60 mL), liver disease (AST or ALT >2x upper normal), pregnancy or lactation, chronic NSAID therapy, contraindications to liraglutide, contraindications for MRI, recent participation in other research projects.
intervention: Liraglutide 1.8 mg/day subcutaneous injection at bedtime, titrated over 3 weeks (0.6 mg/day week 1, 1.2 mg/day week 2, 1.8 mg/day week 3), plus general advice on physical activity and diet without structured intervention, continued until achieving 7% weight loss from initial body weight (maximum 15 months)
comparison: Lifestyle intervention program including low-calorie low-fat diet (1200-1800 kcal/day) and moderate intensity physical activity (≥150 min/week brisk walking, ≥700 kcal/week expenditure), with periodic individual counseling sessions (weekly first 4 weeks, biweekly for 20 weeks, then monthly), continued until achieving 7% weight loss from initial body weight
outcomes_primary: Change in urinary 11-dehydro-TXB2 excretion (thromboxane-dependent platelet activation) after achievement of 7% weight loss
outcomes_secondary: Change in urinary 8-iso-PGF2α excretion (lipid peroxidation); changes in subcutaneous adipose tissue (SAT) and visceral adipose tissue (VAT) distribution by MRI; insulin sensitivity (Matsuda Index); beta-cell function (OGTT beta-index); fasting plasma glucose; HbA1c; fasting insulin; high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP); TNF-α; leptin; IGF-I
extraction_notes: This is a post-hoc analysis of a previously published study. Sample size of 35 subjects completing the study (after exclusions for antiplatelet treatment). Median time-to-weight loss was 4 months. The study was designed to compare equal weight loss achieved through different interventions.

title: Predictors and correlates of systolic blood pressure reduction with liraglutide treatment in patients with type 2 diabetes.

intervention: Liraglutide
comparison: Placebo
extraction_notes: This is a secondary analysis of a double-blind, placebo-controlled trial. Liraglutide dose, route, frequency, and duration not specified in abstract.

comparison: Placebo suspended in a liquid meal with subsequent intravenous infusion of saline; Metformin 1,500 mg suspended in a liquid meal with subsequent intravenous infusion of GLP-1 receptor antagonist exendin9-39 (Ex9-39); Placebo suspended in a liquid meal with subsequent intravenous infusion of Ex9-39

extraction_notes: Study uses a 2x2 factorial design (metformin/placebo crossed with Ex9-39/saline) across 4 separate days. Blood sampling duration was 240 minutes. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly labeled in abstract.

title: Effect of baseline body mass index on glycemic control and weight change with exenatide monotherapy in Chinese drug-naïve type 2 diabetic patients.
population: Chinese drug-naïve patients with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes, aged 30 to 70 years, HbA1c 7.0% to 10.0%, BMI 18 to 35 kg/m2, stable body weight for ≥3 months; excluded: acute or severe chronic diabetic complications, positive glutamic acid decarboxylase antibodies, history of pancreatitis, triglyceride levels ≥5 mM, use of drugs affecting gastrointestinal motility, weight, or glucose
intervention: Exenatide 5 μg subcutaneous injection twice daily for 4 weeks, then increased to 10 μg twice daily for 48 weeks total (dose reduced to 5 μg twice daily in patients with frequent hypoglycemia or intolerable adverse events)
comparison: Comparison among baseline BMI groups: normal-weight (18.5 kg/m2 ≤ BMI < 24 kg/m2), overweight (24 kg/m2 ≤ BMI < 28 kg/m2), and obese (BMI ≥ 28 kg/m2)
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 48 compared among different BMI groups
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of patients achieving HbA1c <7.0% and ≤6.5% at Week 48; changes from baseline in fasting plasma glucose (FPG), 2-hour postprandial plasma glucose (PPG), lipid profiles, body weight, blood pressure, and β-cell function (HOMA-β, HOMA-IR, acute insulin response, proinsulin:insulin ratio); safety and tolerability
extraction_notes: This is a single-arm study with no placebo or active comparator; comparisons are made between BMI subgroups within the exenatide-treated population. The study is an ancillary analysis of the CONFIDENCE study (NCT01147627).

title: Predictive factors associated with three years of response to HbA1c goals with exenatide QW or insulin glargine: Post-hoc analysis of the DURATION-3 study.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes from the DURATION-3 study
intervention: Exenatide once weekly (QW)
comparison: Insulin glargine (IG)
outcomes_primary: Sustained glycaemic response, defined as achieving HbA1c <7.0% (<53 mmol/mol) at Week 26 and maintaining treatment target for ≥80% of remaining visits including one during the final 6 months
outcomes_secondary: Predictive factors associated with sustained response
extraction_notes: This is a post-hoc analysis of the DURATION-3 study. Specific dosing information for exenatide QW and insulin glargine not provided in abstract. Primary outcome definition combines initial response at Week 26 with sustained response criteria through Week 156.

title: Reduction of Cardiovascular Risk and Improved Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate by SGLT2 Inhibitors, Including Dapagliflozin, Is Consistent Across the Class: An Analysis of the Placebo Arm of EXSCEL.
population: Participants from the placebo arm of the EXSCEL trial (Exenatide Study of Cardiovascular Event Lowering) with type 2 diabetes
intervention: Drop-in open-label SGLT2 inhibitors, including dapagliflozin
comparison: Propensity-matched cohorts of SGLT2i nonusers
outcomes_primary: Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE)
outcomes_secondary: All-cause mortality (ACM), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) slope
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of the placebo arm of EXSCEL examining drop-in therapy. Doses, routes, and frequencies of SGLT2i not specified. The analysis used propensity-matched cohorts. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract.

title: Acute Effect of Resistant Starch on Food Intake, Appetite and Satiety in Overweight/Obese Males.
population: Healthy overweight/obese males aged 18-32 years with BMI 28-37 kg/m², fasting blood glucose ≤6.0 mmol/L, haemoglobin ≥13 g/dL, no history of gastrointestinal disease or endocrine disorders, stable weight for 3 months, restraint score <4 on Dutch Eating Behaviour Questionnaire, no chronic medical conditions, alcohol intake ≤21 units per week, no prescription medicines or supplements in last 6 months
intervention: 48 g resistant starch (Hi-Maize 260, comprising 60% RS type 2 and 40% rapidly digestible starch) divided into two 24 g doses mixed into mousse, consumed at breakfast and lunch on a single study day
comparison: 32 g placebo (Amioca, 100% rapidly digestible starch) divided into two 16 g doses mixed into mousse, consumed at breakfast and lunch on a single study day
outcomes_primary: Energy intake at ad libitum dinner meal
outcomes_secondary: 24-hour energy and macronutrient intake; subjective appetite ratings via visual analogue scale (fullness, hunger, prospective food consumption, desire to eat, thirst, nausea); postprandial glucose concentrations; postprandial insulin concentrations; postprandial C-peptide concentrations; postprandial GLP-1 concentrations; insulin sensitivity indices (HOMA-IR, Matsuda Index, disposition index, insulinogenic index); palatability and pleasantness of test product; gastrointestinal symptoms
extraction_notes: Single-blind randomized crossover design with minimum 1-week washout. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; ad libitum dinner energy intake appears to be main outcome of interest based on study aims. Sample size not explicitly stated in methods.

title: Safety and Pharmacokinetics of Single and Multiple Ascending Doses of the Novel Oral Human GLP-1 Analogue, Oral Semaglutide, in Healthy Subjects and Subjects with Type 2 Diabetes.
population: Healthy males (single-dose trial: n=135; multiple-dose trial: n=84) and males with type 2 diabetes (multiple-dose trial: n=23)
intervention: Oral semaglutide tablet co-formulated with sodium N-(8-[2-hydroxybenzoyl] amino) caprylate (SNAC). Single-dose trial: 2-20 mg semaglutide with 150-600 mg SNAC. Multiple-dose trial: 20 or 40 mg oral semaglutide with 300 mg SNAC, once daily for 10 weeks
comparison: Placebo with SNAC; placebo without SNAC
outcomes_primary: Safety; pharmacokinetics of oral semaglutide
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Two separate trials reported together (single-dose first-in-human trial and 10-week multiple-dose trial). Specific pharmacokinetic parameters measured not detailed in abstract.

title: Effects of Liraglutide on Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus With or Without History of Myocardial Infarction or Stroke.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and high cardiovascular risk, stratified by history of myocardial infarction/stroke, established atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease without MI/stroke, or cardiovascular risk factors alone
intervention: Liraglutide 1.8 mg (or maximum tolerated dose) subcutaneous injection
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Major adverse cardiovascular events (composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke)
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc subgroup analysis of the LEADER trial. Secondary outcomes not specified in abstract. Median follow-up was 3.8 years. Route of administration inferred from drug class (GLP-1 analog) but not explicitly stated.

title: Effects of Liraglutide Versus Placebo on Cardiovascular Events in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Chronic Kidney Disease.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (HbA1c ≥7.0% with no upper limit), high cardiovascular risk, drug-naive or treated with oral antihyperglycemic agents or insulin (human neutral protamine Hagedorn, long-acting analogue, or premixed only). Either (1) ≥50 years of age with ≥1 cardiovascular comorbidity including prior MI or stroke, prior coronary/carotid/peripheral arterial revascularization or >50% stenosis, documented coronary heart disease, CKD ≥stage 3, or chronic heart failure NYHA class II-III; or (2) ≥60 years of age with ≥1 cardiovascular risk factor including micro- or macroalbuminuria, hypertension and left ventricular hypertrophy, left ventricular systolic or diastolic dysfunction, or ankle-brachial index <0.9. Designed to recruit subgroup of ≥660 patients with eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2 including ≈220 with severe renal impairment (eGFR <30) and ≥440 with moderate renal impairment (eGFR 30-60)
intervention: Liraglutide 1.8 mg (or maximum tolerated dose) subcutaneous injection once daily, in addition to standard of care, following 2-week placebo run-in period
comparison: Matching placebo once daily, in addition to standard of care
outcomes_primary: Time from randomization to first occurrence of composite cardiovascular outcome consisting of cardiovascular death, nonfatal (including silent) myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke
outcomes_secondary: Expanded composite cardiovascular outcome (cardiovascular death, nonfatal MI, nonfatal stroke, coronary revascularization, or hospitalization for unstable angina pectoris or heart failure); cardiovascular death; all strokes (fatal and nonfatal); all MIs (fatal and nonfatal); all-cause death; change in HbA1c from baseline to 36 months; change in body weight from baseline to 36 months; change in blood pressure from baseline to 36 months; change in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol from baseline to 36 months
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc subgroup analysis of the LEADER trial (NCT01179048) stratified by baseline eGFR (<60 versus ≥60 mL/min/1.73 m2) and baseline albuminuria. The primary LEADER trial results were published previously; this publication focuses on the CKD subgroup analysis.

title: Gastrointestinal effects of extra-virgin olive oil associated with lower postprandial glycemia in type 1 diabetes.

intervention: High-glycemic index meal with high-monounsaturated fat from extra-virgin olive oil (EVOO)

extraction_notes: This is a secondary analysis of the Exenatide-PD trial focusing on mechanistic biomarkers using neuronal-derived exosomes from serum samples. The study is single-center.

title: Retinopathy, Neuropathy, and Subsequent Cardiovascular Events in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes and Acute Coronary Syndrome in the ELIXA: The Importance of Disease Duration.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and recent acute coronary syndrome (ACS), enrolled in the ELIXA trial

comparison: Placebo added to current T2DM therapy
outcomes_primary: Primary composite outcome: cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina
outcomes_secondary: CV composite (CV death, nonfatal MI, stroke, hospitalization for heart failure); individual components including myocardial infarction, heart failure hospitalization, stroke, CV death; all-cause mortality

title: Liraglutide effects in a paediatric (7-11 y) population with obesity: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, short-term trial to assess safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics.
population: Children aged 7-11 years with Tanner stage 1 pubertal development (children with premature adrenarche included); BMI corresponding to ≥30 kg/m² for adults by international cut-off points and BMI ≤45 kg/m² and BMI ≥95th percentile for age and sex. Key exclusions: secondary causes of childhood obesity, confirmed bulimia nervosa disorder, diagnosis of type 1 or 2 diabetes mellitus (HbA1c ≥6.5%), pubertal development Tanner stages 2-5, history of pancreatitis, severe comorbidities, family or personal history of multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2 or medullary thyroid carcinoma, history of major depressive disorder within 2 years before randomization.
intervention: Liraglutide administered as once-daily subcutaneous injection starting at 0.3 mg with weekly dose escalations up to 3.0 mg or maximum tolerated dose (escalated from 0.3 to 1.2 mg in weekly increments of 0.3 mg, then 0.6 mg weekly increments); treatment duration at least 7 weeks with allowance of up to 6 optional treatment weeks (maximum 13 weeks).

outcomes_primary: Number of adverse events from time of first dosing until completion of follow-up visit.

Pharmacodynamic exploratory endpoints: changes from baseline to end of treatment for BMI Z score, body weight, fasting plasma glucose, serum insulin, and serum HbA1c.

Blood samples collected after 12-hour fast at baseline, 6 months, and 18 months.

title: The use of liraglutide 3.0 mg daily in the management of overweight and obesity in people with schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder and first episode psychosis: Results of a pilot randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.

title: Liraglutide hospital discharge trial: A randomized controlled trial comparing the safety and efficacy of liraglutide versus insulin glargine for the management of patients with type 2 diabetes after hospital discharge.

title: Simplification of complex insulin regimens using canagliflozin or liraglutide in patients with well-controlled type 2 diabetes: A 24-week randomized controlled trial.

title: Managing pasireotide-associated hyperglycemia: a randomized, open-label, Phase IV study.

Patients receiving pasireotide at screening required fasting plasma glucose ≥126 mg/dL on two separate occasions, or diagnosis of diabetes mellitus (HbA1c ≥6.5% or random plasma glucose ≥200 mg/dL with classic symptoms of hyperglycemia). Key exclusion criteria: use of DPP-4 inhibitors or GLP-1 receptor agonists within 4 weeks before study entry; life-threatening diabetic ketoacidosis or diabetic hyperosmolar coma; HbA1c >10% at screening. For randomization: patients with average fasting SMBG ≥126 mg/dL on three consecutive days during 16-week pre-randomization period despite optimized treatment with metformin/other permitted OADs.
intervention: Incretin-based therapy: sitagliptin 50 or 100 mg/day orally (based on renal function) followed by liraglutide (GLP-1 receptor agonist) if SMBG elevated ≥126 mg/dL on three consecutive days on stable sitagliptin dose for ≥6 weeks. All patients received pasireotide (long-acting 40 mg IM once/28 days for acromegaly; 600 μg SC twice daily for Cushing's disease) with dose adjustments permitted. Metformin 1000 mg/day bid was initiated for patients with elevated SMBG.
comparison: Insulin therapy: suggested starting dose 10 IU/day administered at bedtime, with weekly titration to achieve SMBG <126 mg/dL on three consecutive days. Dose adjustments and addition of prandial insulin permitted. Non-randomized observational arms included: patients managed on metformin/other OADs alone; patients not requiring any antidiabetic drugs; patients receiving insulin at baseline.
outcomes_primary: Difference in mean change in HbA1c from randomization to end of core phase (16 weeks after randomization) between incretin-based therapy and insulin treatment arms.
outcomes_secondary: Evaluation and sustainability of glycemic control; change in FPG from randomization to end of core phase; proportion of patients achieving HbA1c targets (<6.5%, <7%); shift in HbA1c category; safety and tolerability of pasireotide in combination with antidiabetic medication including adverse events and serious adverse events.
extraction_notes: Open-label study design. Randomization stratified by disease (acromegaly or Cushing's disease) and baseline glycemic status (HbA1c <7% or ≥7%). GH/IGF-1 and urinary free cortisol data were collected locally for pasireotide titration but not recorded in study database.

intervention: Insulin degludec/liraglutide (IDegLira) subcutaneously once daily, starting dose 16 dose steps (16 U degludec/0.6 mg liraglutide), titrated twice weekly to target fasting plasma glucose of 4-5 mmol/L, maximum dose 50 U degludec/1.8 mg liraglutide, combined with metformin, for 26 weeks

title: Comparisons of efficacy and safety in insulin glargine and lixisenatide plus glulisine combination therapy with multiple daily injection therapy in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes.
population: Hospitalized Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus admitted for glycemic control; 40 participants (18 men and 22 women)
intervention: iGlarLixi (insulin glargine U100 and lixisenatide at fixed-dose ratio 1 U:1 μg) administered pre-breakfast (starting dose 5 doses, maximum 20 doses daily) plus insulin glulisine (Glu) 2-20 units pre-supper, titrated according to algorithm for 10 days
comparison: Multiple daily injection (MDI) therapy: insulin glargine U300 (Gla-300) 4-20 units pre-breakfast plus insulin glulisine (Glu) 2-20 units before each meal, titrated according to algorithm
outcomes_primary: Efficacy: time in range (TIR) of glucose level 70-180 mg/dL; Safety: time below range level 1 (TBR level 1) of glucose <70 mg/dL
outcomes_secondary: Time above range of glucose ≥180 mg/dL; TBR level 2 of glucose <54 mg/dL; nocturnal (00:00-06:00 hours) TBR level 1; standard deviation and coefficient of variation of glycemic variability (24-h and 06:00-18:00 hours); 24-h M-value; mean amplitude of glycemic excursion; mean of daily difference; mean glucose levels (24-h and by time periods); 7-point SMBG data; area under the glucose curve; changes in BMI, HbA1c level, glycated albumin level, C-peptide immunoreactivity, CPR index; titration period
extraction_notes: Outcomes measured using intermittently scanned continuous glucose monitoring (isCGM) data collected on days 11-13. DPP-4 inhibitor discontinued in iGlarLixi group if used at baseline. Study duration was short (15 days hospitalization period).

title: Impact of isoenergetic intake of irregular meal patterns on thermogenesis, glucose metabolism, and appetite: a randomized controlled trial.
journal: The American journal of clinical nutrition
population: Women who are overweight or with obesity and confirmed insulin resistance
intervention: Irregular meal pattern for 14 days (3-9 meals per day)
comparison: Regular meal pattern for 14 days (6 meals per day)
outcomes_primary: Thermic effect of food (TEF) measured over 3 hours after test drink consumption
outcomes_secondary: Glucose, insulin, HOMA-IR, lipid profile, adiponectin, leptin, glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1), peptide YY (PYY), ghrelin, subjective appetite ratings, ad libitum energy intake, continuous interstitial glucose monitoring
extraction_notes: Crossover design with 14-day washout interval. Small sample size (n=9). Primary outcome not explicitly designated; TEF appears to be main focus based on title and conclusions. Identical foods provided during both intervention periods.

title: Exploring potential mediators of the cardiovascular benefit of dulaglutide in type 2 diabetes patients in REWIND.
population: Adults aged 50 years or older with type 2 diabetes, HbA1c ≤9.5% on stable doses of up to 2 oral glucose lowering drugs with or without basal insulin, prior cardiovascular event or at least 2 cardiovascular risk factors, and body mass index ≥23 kg/m2. Key exclusions: estimated glomerular filtration rate <15 mL/min per 1.73 m2, cancer in previous 5 years, severe hypoglycemia in previous year, life expectancy less than 1 year, coronary or cerebrovascular event within previous 2 months, plans for revascularization.
intervention: Dulaglutide 1.5 mg subcutaneous injection once weekly plus usual standard of care
comparison: Placebo subcutaneous injection once weekly plus usual standard of care
outcomes_primary: Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE): composite of nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or death from cardiovascular causes or unknown causes
outcomes_secondary: Potential mediators of cardiovascular benefit: HbA1c, body weight, waist-to-hip ratio, systolic blood pressure, LDL cholesterol, urine albumin/creatinine ratio (UACR)
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc exploratory mediation analysis of the REWIND trial (NCT01394952). The analysis aimed to evaluate potential mediators of dulaglutide's cardiovascular benefit rather than efficacy outcomes per se. Median follow-up was 5.4 years.

title: Randomised clinical trial: semaglutide versus placebo reduced liver steatosis but not liver stiffness in subjects with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease assessed by magnetic resonance imaging.
population: Adults aged 18-75 years with BMI 25-40 kg/m2, liver stiffness 2.50-4.63 kPa by MRE and >4.0 kPa by VCTE, liver steatosis ≥10% by MRI-PDFF, with or without type 2 diabetes. Key exclusions: chronic liver disease other than NAFLD, hepatitis B/C or HIV positive, excessive alcohol consumption (>12 g/day women, >24 g/day men), treatment with vitamin E or pioglitazone, HbA1c >9.5%, type 1 diabetes, history of pancreatitis, prior obesity surgery, current weight-loss therapies, recent treatment with GLP-1RAs, SGLT2 inhibitors or insulin.
intervention: Subcutaneous semaglutide 0.4 mg once daily for 72 weeks (dose escalation: 0.05 mg/day for first 4 weeks, then increased every 4 weeks through 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 mg/day to reach target 0.4 mg/day by week 16)
comparison: Matching placebo subcutaneous injection once daily for 72 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline to week 48 in liver stiffness assessed by magnetic resonance elastography (MRE)
outcomes_secondary: Change from baseline to weeks 24 and 72 in liver stiffness by MRE; proportion of subjects achieving ≥15% reduction in liver stiffness by MRE; liver steatosis by MRI-PDFF; proportion of subjects achieving ≥30% reduction in liver fat content by MRI-PDFF; change from baseline in total liver volume, liver fat volume, visceral adipose tissue and abdominal subcutaneous adipose tissue by MRI; change from baseline in body weight, waist circumference and BMI
extraction_notes: Exploratory endpoints included liver enzymes (ALT, AST, GGT), glucose metabolism parameters (HbA1c, fasting plasma glucose, fasting glucagon, HOMA-IR), cardiovascular risk factors, and various biomarkers. Trial was stratified by baseline liver stiffness (<3.64 vs ≥3.64 kPa).

title: Associations between Postprandial Gut Hormones and Markers of Bone Remodeling.
population: Healthy adults aged 30-70 years with BMI 18.5-25 kg/m2. Exclusion criteria: history of eating disorder in past 3 years, weight change above 5 kg within last 3 months, HbA1C above 39 mmol/mol, uncontrolled medical issues, diabetes or other endocrine diseases, immunosuppression, treatment with medications affecting GI transit time or glucose metabolism or appetite, bariatric surgery, GI surgery within 3 months, GI diseases, alcohol/drug abuse, pregnancy or lactation.
intervention: Standardized mixed meal (498 kcal, 34E% fat, 49E% carbohydrate, 17E% protein) consisting of yoghurt, muesli, rye bread, wheat bread, cheese, butter and jam, consumed with 200 mL water within 10 minutes
comparison: Granola bar (SmartBar) (260 kcal, 7E% fat, 74E% carbohydrate, 19E% protein) consumed with 200 mL water within 10 minutes; cross-over design with each participant receiving both meal types
outcomes_primary: Associations between incremental area under the curve (iAUC) of bone remodeling markers (CTX - carboxyl-terminal collagen type I crosslinks, P1NP - procollagen type 1 N-terminal propeptide) and gut hormones (GIP - glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, GLP-1 - glucagon-like peptide 1, PYY - peptide YY) measured at 0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120, 180, and 240 minutes after meal intake
extraction_notes: This is a mechanistic/physiological study examining associations rather than a traditional intervention trial. The primary objective in the original PRESET study was gastrointestinal transit time using SmartPill technology (data unpublished), with gut hormone and bone marker associations being secondary analyses. Small sample size (n=14) with predominantly female participants including both pre- and postmenopausal women.

title: Effects of GLP-1 Receptor Agonists on Bone Mineral Density in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A 52-Week Clinical Study.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) of at least 6 months duration; age ≥40 years; HbA1c 6.5-10%; stable glycemic control for at least 90 days. Exclusion criteria: type 1 diabetes mellitus; gestational diabetes; prior GLP-1RA treatment; hormone replacement therapy or vitamin D/calcium supplementation; heavy smoking or alcohol intake (>60g daily); severe acute/chronic T2DM complications including ketoacidosis, hyperosmolality, severe cardiovascular disease, end-stage renal disease, severe infection, severe diabetic gastroparesis; metabolic diseases including hyperthyroidism, hypothyroidism, hypercortisolism, hypopituitarism; cancer metastasis to bone; history of glucocorticoid treatment
intervention: Exenatide 2 mg subcutaneous injection once weekly for 52 weeks; or dulaglutide 1.5 mg subcutaneous injection once weekly for 52 weeks
comparison: Insulin glargine 6 units/day for 52 weeks; placebo once weekly for 52 weeks
outcomes_primary: Changes in bone mineral density (BMD) measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA) at lumbar vertebrae (L1-L4), femoral neck, and total hip
outcomes_secondary: Glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c); occurrence of new fractures during treatment
extraction_notes: Single-blinded study; allocation ratio 2:2:1:2; route of administration for exenatide and dulaglutide not explicitly stated but implied subcutaneous based on drug class; all participants maintained original therapeutic drugs with study drug added

title: Liraglutide changes body composition and lowers added sugar intake in overweight persons with insulin pump-treated type 1 diabetes.
population: Overweight adults with insulin pump-treated type 1 diabetes and glucose levels above target
intervention: Liraglutide 1.8 mg daily for 26 weeks
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_secondary: Changes in body composition (total fat mass, lean body mass) measured by dual X-ray absorptiometry; changes in food intake including total energy intake and energy derived from added sugars assessed by questionnaire-based food frequency recordings
extraction_notes: This study reports secondary outcome analyses; primary outcomes were HbA1c and body weight reduction from the original trial. Primary outcomes for this specific analysis are not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes.

title: Effects of Tirzepatide, a Dual GIP and GLP-1 RA, on Lipid and Metabolite Profiles in Subjects With Type 2 Diabetes.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
population: Subjects with type 2 diabetes
intervention: Tirzepatide 1 mg, 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg administered weekly via subcutaneous injection for 26 weeks
comparison: Dulaglutide 1.5 mg weekly subcutaneous injection; placebo
outcomes_primary: Changes in metabolite levels in response to tirzepatide assessed against baseline levels, dulaglutide, and placebo
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc exploratory metabolomics and lipidomics analysis of a phase 2b trial. Primary outcomes of the original trial (HbA1c, body weight) are mentioned but the focus of this analysis is metabolite changes. No secondary outcomes explicitly defined.

title: Effects of short-acting exenatide added three times daily to insulin therapy on bone metabolism in type 1 diabetes.
population: Individuals with type 1 diabetes aged 18 years or older on basal-bolus therapy with HbA1c 59-88 mmol/mol (7.5%-10.0%) and body mass index of more than 22.0 kg/m²
intervention: Short-acting exenatide added three times daily to insulin therapy for 26 weeks
comparison: Placebo added to insulin therapy
outcomes_primary: Bone mineral density assessed by whole-body, hip, lumbar, and forearm dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry
outcomes_secondary: Fasting plasma levels of C-terminal telopeptides of type I collagen (marker of bone resorption); amino-terminal propeptide of type I procollagen (marker of bone formation)
extraction_notes: BMI cutoff appears truncated in abstract ('>22.0 kg/m' without completing the unit); dose of exenatide not specified; primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract

title: Efficacy of iGlarLixi in adults with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled (glycated haemoglobin ≥8%, ≥64 mmol/mol) on two oral antidiabetes drugs: Post hoc analysis of the LixiLan-O randomized trial.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes with baseline HbA1c ≥8% (≥64 mmol/mol) inadequately controlled on metformin plus a second oral antidiabetes drug at screening
intervention: iGlarLixi (titratable fixed-ratio combination of insulin glargine 100 U/mL plus lixisenatide) administered once daily for 30 weeks, on background of metformin (titrated to maximum tolerated dose, minimum ≥1500 mg/day)
comparison: Insulin glargine 100 U/mL (iGlar) alone once daily; Lixisenatide (Lixi) alone once daily; both on background of metformin
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline to Week 30
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of participants achieving HbA1c <7% (<53 mmol/mol); composite of HbA1c <7% with no body weight gain; composite of HbA1c <7% with no body weight gain and no documented symptomatic hypoglycaemia (plasma glucose ≤3.9 mmol/L); change in fasting plasma glucose (FPG) from baseline to Week 30; change in 2-hour postprandial glucose (PPG) from baseline to Week 30; change in body weight from baseline to Week 30; mean daily iGlar dose; rates of documented symptomatic hypoglycaemia (plasma glucose ≤3.9 mmol/L or <3.0 mmol/L); adverse events
extraction_notes: Post hoc subgroup analysis of the LixiLan-O randomized trial (NCT02058147). Original trial was open-label with 2:2:1 randomization ratio. Participants stopped second OAD during 4-week run-in period before randomization.

title: Efficacy and safety of oral semaglutide by baseline age in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes: A subgroup analysis of the PIONEER 9 and 10 Japan trials.
population: Japanese patients aged ≥20 years with type 2 diabetes. PIONEER 9: HbA1c 6.5%-9.5% (48-80 mmol/mol) if managed with oral agents, or HbA1c 7.0%-10.0% (53-86 mmol/mol) if managed by diet/exercise, diagnosed for ≥30 days before screening. PIONEER 10: HbA1c 7.0%-10.5% (53-91 mmol/mol), diagnosed for ≥60 days before screening. Subgroups analyzed by baseline age <65 years and ≥65 years.
intervention: Once-daily oral semaglutide 3 mg, 7 mg, or 14 mg for 52 weeks
comparison: PIONEER 9: placebo or once-daily subcutaneous liraglutide 0.9 mg; PIONEER 10: once-weekly subcutaneous dulaglutide 0.75 mg
outcomes_primary: PIONEER 9: change in HbA1c from baseline to week 26; PIONEER 10: number of treatment-emergent adverse events over 57 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Change from baseline in body weight at week 26; change from baseline in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) at week 26; adverse events up to end of follow-up (week 57); serious adverse events; premature trial product discontinuation; gastrointestinal adverse events; severe or blood glucose-confirmed symptomatic hypoglycaemic events; diabetic retinopathy and related complications
extraction_notes: This is a post-hoc exploratory subgroup analysis of two previously published trials (PIONEER 9 and PIONEER 10). Follow-up period was 5 weeks after 52-week treatment period.

title: Maintenance of glycaemic control with liraglutide versus oral antidiabetic drugs as add-on therapies in patients with type 2 diabetes uncontrolled with metformin alone: A randomized clinical trial in primary care (LIRA-PRIME).
population: Adults aged 18 years or older with type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 7.5%-9.0% [58.5-74.9 mmol/mol]) receiving stable dose of metformin (≥1500 mg/d or maximum tolerated dose) as monotherapy for 60 days or longer before screening; met local criteria for use of liraglutide and OAD treatment; excluded if pregnant or breastfeeding or had received any diabetes medication other than metformin 60 days or less before screening
intervention: Subcutaneous liraglutide added to metformin, dose escalated from 0.6 to 1.2 mg/d up to final dose of 1.8 mg/d, for up to 104 weeks
comparison: Oral antidiabetic drug (OAD) added to metformin, selected by investigator from: α-glucosidase inhibitor, dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor (DPP-4i), meglitinide, sodium-glucose co-transporter-2 inhibitor (SGLT-2i), sulphonylurea (SU), or thiazolidinedione; dose escalated to maximum approved/tolerated dose; for up to 104 weeks
outcomes_primary: Time to inadequate glycaemic control, defined as HbA1c >7.0% (>53.0 mmol/mol) at two scheduled consecutive visits after week 26
outcomes_secondary: Time to premature treatment discontinuation for any reason; changes from baseline in HbA1c, fasting plasma glucose, body weight, body mass index, and blood pressure at week 104 or at premature treatment discontinuation; proportion of patients achieving HbA1c ≤6.5% (≤47.5 mmol/mol); composite endpoints (HbA1c ≤7.0% without weight gain; HbA1c ≤7.0% without severe or blood glucose-confirmed symptomatic hypoglycaemia; HbA1c ≤7.0% without severe or blood glucose-confirmed symptomatic hypoglycaemia or weight gain); documented symptomatic and severe hypoglycaemic episodes; severe or blood glucose-confirmed symptomatic hypoglycaemic episodes; adverse events leading to permanent discontinuation; serious adverse events; changes from baseline in blood lipids, biochemistry, haemoglobin, and pulse

title: Effects of exenatide on urinary albumin in overweight/obese patients with T2DM: a randomized clinical trial.
population: Overweight/obese patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM); age 18-65 years; HbA1c ≥ 6.5%; BMI ≥ 24 kg/m²; systolic blood pressure 90-130 mmHg; diastolic blood pressure 60-90 mmHg; not using ACE inhibitors or angiotensin receptor blockers
intervention: Exenatide (EXE) 5 μg twice daily subcutaneously injected 15 minutes before breakfast and dinner for 4 weeks, then up-titrated to 10 μg twice daily for remaining weeks, total treatment period 24 weeks
comparison: Insulin glargine subcutaneously injected once daily for 24 weeks
outcomes_primary: Urine albumin concentration (UAC)
outcomes_secondary: Anthropometric parameters (height, weight, BMI, waist-hip ratio, visceral fat area); glucose parameters (fasting blood glucose, HbA1c, serum insulin, C-peptide, HOMA-IR); lipid parameters (triglycerides, total cholesterol, LDL-cholesterol, HDL-cholesterol); inflammation biomarkers (C-reactive protein, interleukin-6, interleukin-8, tumor necrosis factor-α); serum fibroblast growth factor 21 (FGF21); safety and tolerability (hypoglycemia, gastrointestinal adverse reactions)
extraction_notes: Study was open-label randomized controlled trial conducted in China; 159 patients randomized (79 EXE, 80 GLAR)

title: A phase 1 multiple-ascending dose study of tirzepatide in Japanese participants with type 2 diabetes.
population: Japanese participants with type 2 diabetes; age 20-70 years at screening; T2D for 1 year or longer prior to enrolment; T2D controlled with diet and exercise alone, or stable on metformin or a dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitor (except omarigliptin, trelagliptin, and linagliptin) for 3 months or longer; body mass index 20-35 kg/m2
intervention: Once-weekly subcutaneous tirzepatide for 8 weeks in three dose groups: 5 mg (5 mg weeks 1-8), 10 mg (2.5 mg weeks 1-2, 5 mg weeks 3-4, 10 mg weeks 5-8), and 15 mg (5 mg weeks 1-2, 10 mg weeks 3-6, 15 mg weeks 7-8)
comparison: Placebo (once-weekly subcutaneous injection for 8 weeks)
outcomes_primary: Safety and tolerability of tirzepatide after multiple subcutaneous doses, including laboratory values, vital signs, electrocardiogram variables, injection-site reactions, and hypoglycemia
outcomes_secondary: Pharmacokinetics (plasma tirzepatide concentrations) and pharmacodynamic effect (fasting plasma glucose levels). Exploratory outcomes: body weight, oral glucose tolerance test (0-2 hours), seven-point self-monitored plasma glucose, HbA1c, and subjective appetite sensation
extraction_notes: Participants who had been treated with metformin or DPP-4 inhibitors were required to withdraw treatment and have at least 28-day washout period before dosing. Phase 1 multiple-ascending dose study.

title: Glycemic Control and Metabolic Adaptation in Response to High-Fat versus High-Carbohydrate Diets-Data from a Randomized Cross-Over Study in Healthy Subjects.
population: Healthy, normal-weight volunteers aged 18-65 years with BMI between 18-25 kg/m2, self-reported good general health status, no history of drug abuse or smoking, no use of prescription medications within previous 14 days (except contraceptives), not pregnant or breastfeeding, no clinically significant abnormalities
intervention: High-fat diet (HFD) with 60% energy from fat, iso-caloric, individually adapted based on calculated daily energy needs, all meals/beverages/snacks provided, administered for 2 weeks
comparison: High-carbohydrate diet (HCD) with 60% energy from carbohydrates, iso-caloric, individually adapted based on calculated daily energy needs, all meals/beverages/snacks provided, administered for 2 weeks; cross-over design with minimum 2-week wash-out period between diets
outcomes_primary: Mixed meal test (MMT)-induced glycemia and insulinemia
outcomes_secondary: MMT-induced release of insulin, GLP-1 and GIP; metabolomic markers that may predict long-term risk of developing dysglycemia; HOMA-IR; appetite scoring (craving, hunger, satiation) via visual analogue scale; body weight; blood biochemistry including triglycerides, hemoglobin, LDL, HDL, total cholesterol; ketone bodies (acetoacetate, acetone, β-hydroxybutyrate); branched-chain amino acids (valine, leucine); creatine; α-hydroxybutyric acid; alanine; methionine; glutamine; α-aminobutyrate
extraction_notes: Randomized unblinded cross-over study. Sample size calculation based on epithelial surface enlargement (primary outcome in ClinicalTrials.gov), not glycemic control outcomes presented here. One participant excluded after first dietary period due to pregnancy, leaving n=15 for analysis.

title: Effects of Delayed-Release Olive Oil and Hydrolyzed Pine Nut Oil on Glucose Tolerance, Incretin Secretion and Appetite in Humans.
population: Overweight/obese individuals aged 40-70 years, BMI 27.5-40 kg/m2, with normal glucose tolerance (2-h plasma glucose <7.8 mmol/L), normal screening blood samples including markers of kidney and liver function, cholesterols, triglycerides and hematology, healthy with normal blood pressure (≤140/90 mmHg), no prescriptive medicine, no chronic diseases including gastrointestinal diseases or previous gastrointestinal surgery, no first-degree relatives with diabetes, no food allergies of importance, non-smokers with stable body weight (<3 kg change within three months prior), no intake of dietary supplements within 1 month prior, no adherence to restrictive diets
intervention: 6 g hydrolyzed pine nut oil (PNO-FFA) in delayed-release capsules consumed with 160 mL water 30 minutes prior to 75 g oral glucose tolerance test; or combination of 3 g hydrolyzed pine nut oil and 3 g olive oil (PNO-OO) in delayed-release capsules consumed with 160 mL water 30 minutes prior to 75 g oral glucose tolerance test
comparison: No oil intake (control) with 160 mL water 30 minutes prior to 75 g oral glucose tolerance test
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified as primary; outcomes measured included plasma glucose, serum insulin, C-peptide, plasma GLP-1, GIP, ghrelin, plasma free fatty acids assessed as area under the curve (AUCtotal and 2-hour segments) over 6-hour OGTT
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly specified as secondary; additional outcomes included subjective appetite assessed by visual analog scale (hunger, satiety, fullness, prospective food consumption, overall well-being), gastrointestinal tolerability (nausea/vomiting, bloating, flatulence, constipation, diarrhea, abdominal pain), OGTT-derived indices of insulin sensitivity (BIGTTSi, MATSUDA) and beta-cell function (BIGTTAIR, CIR30 min)
extraction_notes: Crossover design with three arms; n=9 completed study; primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly designated; washout period 1-4 weeks between OGTTs; first arm (no oil) corresponded to initial screening OGTT

title: Duodenal
population: Caucasian male subjects aged 21-69 years with body mass index 30-43 kg/m2, treatment-naïve with metabolic syndrome defined by presence of ≥3 of 5 criteria (fasting plasma glucose ≥5.6 mmol/L, triglycerides ≥1.7 mmol/L, waist circumference ≥102 cm, HDL cholesterol ≤1.04 mmol/L, blood pressure ≥130/85 mm Hg) plus HOMA-IR >2.5. Exclusion criteria: history of cardiovascular event, cholecystectomy, overt untreated gastrointestinal disease or abnormal bowel habits, liver enzymes >2.5 fold higher than upper limit of normal, smoking, alcohol abuse, use of proton pump inhibitors or antibiotics in past 3 months
intervention: Duodenal tube infusion of 10^11 cells of Anaerobutyricum soehngenii L2-7 in 10 mL of 10% glycerol-PBS solution, single dose, administered distally to the papilla of Vater
comparison: Placebo: 10 mL of 10% glycerol in PBS solution administered via same duodenal tube infusion method; cross-over design with 4-week washout period between interventions
outcomes_primary: Changes in duodenal transcriptomic profile assessed by RNA sequencing at 6 hours post-infusion
outcomes_secondary: Postprandial circulating incretins (GLP-1, GIP) measured during 2-hour mixed meal test at 6 hours post-infusion; faecal short-chain fatty acid concentrations; gut microbiota composition via 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing; 24-hour continuous glucose monitoring with glucose variability measured as median absolute deviations; postprandial glucose, insulin, triglycerides; plasma bile acids; safety laboratory parameters (inflammatory, kidney, liver parameters)
extraction_notes: Cross-over design with each subject receiving both intervention and placebo. 15 subjects enrolled but 3 excluded, leaving 12 for analysis. Study registered at Dutch Trial Register NTR-NL6630.

title: A higher non-severe hypoglycaemia rate is associated with an increased risk of subsequent severe hypoglycaemia and major adverse cardiovascular events in individuals with type 2 diabetes in the LEADER study.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes, HbA1c ≥53 mmol/mol (7%), either ≥50 years old with pre-existing cardiovascular disease or ≥60 years old with at least one cardiovascular risk factor
intervention: Liraglutide 1.8 mg (or maximum tolerated dose) subcutaneous injection once daily plus standard of care
comparison: Matching placebo once daily plus standard of care
outcomes_primary: Time to first major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE, composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, and non-fatal stroke)
outcomes_secondary: Time to first severe hypoglycaemic episode (requiring assistance of another person), time to cardiovascular death, time to all-cause mortality; association between annual rate of non-severe hypoglycaemic episodes and these outcomes
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of the LEADER trial. The primary outcome of the original LEADER trial was MACE. The post hoc analysis specifically examined associations between non-severe hypoglycaemic episodes and severe hypoglycaemia/cardiovascular outcomes. Non-severe hypoglycaemia defined as self-measured plasma glucose <3.1 mmol/l (56 mg/dl).

title: Short-term combined treatment with exenatide and metformin for overweight/obese women with polycystic ovary syndrome.
population: Overweight/obese women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) diagnosed via Rotterdam criteria, aged 18-40 years, BMI ≥25 kg/m². Exclusion criteria: diabetes; history of cancer; personal or family history of multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2; severe cardiovascular, kidney, or liver diseases; use of statins or other drugs known or suspected to affect reproductive or metabolic functions within 3 months before entering the study.
intervention: Metformin 500 mg three times daily (titrated from 500 mg/day to 1500 mg/day over 2 weeks) combined with exenatide 2 mg subcutaneous injection once weekly for 12 weeks. All patients also received Diane-35 (ethinylestradiol 0.035 mg and cyproterone acetate 2 mg) for 21 consecutive days per cycle.
comparison: Metformin 500 mg three times daily (titrated from 500 mg/day to 1500 mg/day over 2 weeks) alone for 12 weeks. All patients also received Diane-35 (ethinylestradiol 0.035 mg and cyproterone acetate 2 mg) for 21 consecutive days per cycle.
outcomes_primary: Anthropometric changes associated with obesity (body weight, BMI, waist circumference, hip circumference)
outcomes_secondary: Changes in reproductive hormone levels (follicle-stimulating hormone, luteinizing hormone, estradiol, total testosterone, dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate), glucose metabolism (fasting plasma glucose, OGTT glucose and insulin levels, HOMA-IR, HOMA-β, QUICKI, Matsuda index), lipid metabolism (total cholesterol, triglycerides, HDL-c, LDL-c, ApoA1, ApoB, free fatty acid), and C-reactive protein
extraction_notes: Open-label study design. Lifestyle intervention was not actively promoted. All patients received Diane-35 as co-intervention in both groups.

title: Liraglutide Improves Forced Vital Capacity in Individuals With Type 2 Diabetes: Data From the Randomized Crossover LIRALUNG Study.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes with baseline forced expiratory volume in 1 second (FEV1) <90% of predicted
intervention: Liraglutide administered for 7 weeks (2 weeks titration plus 5 weeks at 1.8 mg daily)
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Forced vital capacity (FVC)
outcomes_secondary: Serum surfactant protein D (SP-D) levels; other pulmonary function variables
extraction_notes: Crossover design specified. Route of administration not explicitly stated but liraglutide is typically subcutaneous. Primary vs secondary outcome designation not explicitly stated in abstract; FVC appears to be the main outcome of interest based on study objectives.

title: Pharmacokinetics, Pharmacodynamics, and Safety of Dulaglutide After Single or Multiple Doses in Chinese Healthy Subjects and Patients with T2DM: A Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Phase I Study.
population: Chinese healthy subjects (Part 1) and Chinese patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) (Part 2)
intervention: Dulaglutide 0.5 mg, 0.75 mg, or 1.5 mg subcutaneous injection; Part 1: single dose; Part 2: once weekly for 4 weeks
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Pharmacokinetics parameters (including maximum concentration), pharmacodynamics effects (in T2DM patients), safety parameters
extraction_notes: This is a Phase I study with two parts using different populations. Part 1 used crossover design where healthy subjects received placebo and two of three dulaglutide doses across three treatment periods. Specific primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract.

title: Safety, tolerability, pharmacodynamics, and pharmacokinetics of CJC-1134-PC in healthy Chinese subjects and type-2 diabetic subjects.
population: Study A: Healthy Chinese subjects. Study B: Chinese subjects with type 2 diabetes (T2D)
intervention: CJC-1134-PC (long-acting GLP-1 mimetic), subcutaneous injection. Study A: single dose (2 mg) or titrate doses (2 + 3 mg and 2 + 3 + 4 mg at weekly intervals). Study B: 10 weekly doses at 1, 2, 3, or 4 mg
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Safety and tolerability; pharmacokinetics (including maximum plasma concentrations); pharmacodynamics
extraction_notes: Abstract text appears truncated (maximum plasma concentrations description incomplete). Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished; all listed outcomes categorized as primary based on stated study objectives. Sample sizes: Study A n=30, Study B n=49.

title: Preserved pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of insulin degludec and liraglutide when administered as insulin degludec/liraglutide in a Chinese population.
population: Study 1 (China PK trial): Healthy Chinese individuals. Study 2 (DUAL I China): Chinese individuals with type 2 diabetes
intervention: Study 1: IDegLira 17 dose steps (17 U degludec/0.6 mg liraglutide) subcutaneously, single dose. Study 2: IDegLira (maximum 50 dose steps) once daily in combination with metformin for 26 weeks
comparison: Study 1: Degludec 17 U alone; Liraglutide 0.6 mg alone (randomized, three-period cross-over). Study 2: Degludec (no maximum dose) once daily with metformin; Liraglutide 1.8 mg once daily with metformin (randomized 2:1:1)
outcomes_primary: Study 1: Exposure (pharmacokinetics) for each component of IDegLira, and for degludec and liraglutide given alone, including AUC and Cmax
outcomes_secondary: Study 2: Dose proportionality of degludec and liraglutide exposures; effects of pre-specified covariates on exposure; exposure-response relationship for glycemic control
extraction_notes: This publication reports two separate trials: a single-dose PK trial in healthy volunteers (China PK trial, NCT03292185) and a 26-week phase III treat-to-target trial in patients with type 2 diabetes (DUAL I China, NCT03172494). PICO elements extracted separately for each trial where applicable.

title: Once-weekly cagrilintide for weight management in people with overweight and obesity: a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled and active-controlled, dose-finding phase 2 trial.
population: Adults aged at least 18 years without diabetes, with a body-mass index of at least 30 kg/m²
intervention: Cagrilintide 0.3-4.5 mg once weekly subcutaneous injection for 26 weeks

title: Cost-Effectiveness of Once-Weekly Semaglutide 1 mg versus Canagliflozin 300 mg in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus in a Canadian Setting.

title: Clinical Outcomes by Albuminuria Status with Dulaglutide versus Insulin Glargine in Participants with Diabetes and CKD: AWARD-7 Exploratory Analysis.

title: Exenatide for weight-loss maintenance in adolescents with severe obesity: A randomized, placebo-controlled trial.

extraction_notes: Randomisation ratio was 3:3:2 (tirzepatide:semaglutide:placebo). Phase 1 study with pharmacodynamic focus.

title: Effect of tirzepatide versus insulin degludec on liver fat content and abdominal adipose tissue in people with type 2 diabetes (SURPASS-3 MRI): a substudy of the randomised, open-label, parallel-group, phase 3 SURPASS-3 trial.

comparison: Insulin degludec

outcomes_secondary: Volume of visceral adipose tissue (VAT), volume of abdominal subcutaneous adipose tissue (ASAT)

title: Mechanisms underlying the blood pressure lowering effects of dapagliflozin, exenatide, and their combination in people with type 2 diabetes: a secondary analysis of a randomized trial.

outcomes_secondary: Estimated plasma volume (calculated by Strauss formula, bioimpedance spectroscopy, hematocrit), autonomic nervous system activity (heart rate variability including LF/HF ratio, SDNN, RMSSD), arterial stiffness (augmentation index from pulse wave applanometry), systemic hemodynamic parameters (peripheral vascular resistance, cardiac output, stroke volume from non-invasive monitoring), natriuresis (24-hour urine collection for sodium and glucose excretion), systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, heart rate

title: Combination therapy with exenatide decreases the dapagliflozin-induced changes in brain responses to anticipation and consumption of palatable food in patients with type 2 diabetes: A randomized controlled trial.
population: Men and postmenopausal women aged 18-75 years with type 2 diabetes, body mass index >27 kg/m2, stable body weight (<5% change during previous 3 months), treated with metformin with or without sulphonylurea derivatives (stable dose for ≥3 months), HbA1c 7-10% (53-86 mmol/mol) for metformin monotherapy or 7.5-10% (58-86 mmol/mol) for metformin plus sulphonylurea

outcomes_primary: Brain responses (BOLD fMRI signal) to anticipation of palatable food (chocolate milk versus tasteless solution) and receipt of palatable food (chocolate milk versus tasteless solution) measured using functional magnetic resonance imaging at baseline, 10 days, and 16 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Energy intake at ad libitum lunch buffet; body weight; HbA1c; carbohydrate intake
extraction_notes: This is a prespecified secondary analysis of the DECREASE study (NCT03361098). Primary and secondary outcomes were not explicitly labeled as such in the text; classification based on study description and analysis focus.

title: Effects of glepaglutide, a long-acting glucagon-like peptide-2 analog, on intestinal morphology and perfusion in patients with short bowel syndrome: Findings from a randomized phase 2 trial.
journal: JPEN. Journal of parenteral and enteral nutrition
population: Patients with short bowel syndrome (SBS) with malabsorption defined as fecal output ≥1500 g/day, stable in their SBS and parenteral support volume if required (<25% change in volume or energy content for four weeks before randomization), without intestinal strictures or active inflammatory bowel disease or fistula, with time from last intestinal resection of more than one year, excluding patients with radiation enteritis, celiac disease, or history of colon cancer

comparison: Two-period crossover design where patients served as their own control, receiving two of three different doses with a washout period of four to eight weeks between treatment periods

extraction_notes: This was a randomized, double-blind, dose-finding, single-center, proof-of-concept, phase 2 trial with crossover design. No placebo arm was included. Primary outcome was reported in a previous publication. The paper focuses on secondary and exploratory endpoints.

title: Effect of once-weekly semaglutide versus thrice-daily insulin aspart, both as add-on to metformin and optimized insulin glargine treatment in participants with type 2 diabetes (SUSTAIN 11): A randomized, open-label, multinational, phase 3b trial.
population: Adults with inadequately controlled type 2 diabetes (HbA1c >7.5% to ≤10.0%; >58 to ≤86 mmol/mol) treated with insulin glargine and metformin ± one additional oral antihyperglycaemic drug, willing to undergo individualized treatment intensification toward an HbA1c target of 6.5% to 7.5% (48-58 mmol/mol)

outcomes_secondary: Confirmatory secondary endpoints: time to first event adjudication committee-confirmed severe hypoglycaemic episode; time to first event adjudication committee-confirmed severe hypoglycaemic episode requiring hospitalization or documented medical help, or that was life-threatening; change in body weight (kg) from randomization to end of treatment. Supportive secondary endpoints: glycaemic control measures, hypoglycaemia (documented symptomatic, asymptomatic, pseudo-hypoglycaemia, clinically significant), anthropometric outcomes (body mass index, waist circumference), patient-reported outcomes (SF-36v2, DQLCTQ-R, TRIM-D questionnaires), blood pressure, pulse rate, lipids. Safety endpoints: adverse events, serious adverse events, adverse events with fatal outcome, adverse events leading to premature treatment discontinuation
extraction_notes: Open-label trial design. Hierarchical testing used for confirmatory secondary endpoints; superiority testing for body weight was not performed because the testing hierarchy was not completed at the severe hypoglycaemia endpoint step.

title: Association between inflammatory markers and survival in comatose, resuscitated out-of-hospital cardiac arrest patients.

intervention: Exenatide (dose, route, frequency, and duration not specified in abstract)
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Time to death for up to 180 days
outcomes_secondary: 180-day mortality; poor neurological outcome after 180 days, defined as cerebral performance category (CPC) of 3 to 5
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of a double-blind controlled trial (NCT02442791) focusing on inflammatory markers; the primary trial intervention (exenatide vs placebo) is noted but this analysis examines associations between inflammatory markers and outcomes rather than treatment effects. Exenatide dosing details not provided in abstract.

title: Effect of expanded dulaglutide weekly doses (3.0 mg and 4.5 mg) on cardiovascular disease risk factors in participants with type 2 diabetes at increased cardiovascular disease risk: a post hoc analysis of the AWARD-11 study.

intervention: Dulaglutide 3.0 mg or 4.5 mg once weekly subcutaneous injection for 52 weeks
comparison: Dulaglutide 1.5 mg once weekly subcutaneous injection for 52 weeks

For this analysis, outcomes included: serum lipids (total cholesterol, non-HDL-C, VLDL-C, LDL-C, HDL-C, triglycerides), vital signs (systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, heart rate), body weight, and HbA1c assessed at baseline and 52 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly distinguished from primary outcomes in this post hoc analysis; serum lipids and blood pressure were exploratory efficacy measures in the original AWARD-11 study
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of the AWARD-11 study (NCT03495102). No placebo group was included in the original trial design. The analysis focused on CVD risk factor changes in subgroups at increased CVD risk.

title: The effects of macronutrients composition on hormones and substrates during a meal tolerance test in drugnaive and sitagliptin-treated individuals with type 2 diabetes: a randomized crossover study.
population: Drug-naive individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed within 3 months, aged 40-70 years, BMI 20-35 kg/m2, confirmed by 2-hour oral glucose tolerance test with plasma glucose >200 mg/dL and HbA1c ≥6.5%. extraction_notes: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled crossover study. Three different meal tolerance tests (carbohydrate-rich, protein-rich, lipid-rich) were administered in each treatment period. Sample size of 16 participants (8 per treatment sequence). Primary outcomes not explicitly designated as such in the text; classification based on study objectives

title: Sperm count is increased by diet-induced weight loss and maintained by exercise or GLP-1 analogue treatment: a randomized controlled trial.

comparison: Placebo injection plus habitual activity; Exercise training plus placebo (150 min/week moderate physical activity or 75 min/week vigorous exercise)
outcomes_primary: Semen parameters including sperm concentration (million sperm/ml) and sperm count (million sperm/ejaculate)
outcomes_secondary: Semen volume, sperm motility (progressive motile, non-progressive motile, immotile), motile sperm count (million motile sperm/ejaculate), body weight, BMI, waist:hip ratio, body fat percentage, plasma CRP, HbA1c, plasma cholesterol, plasma triglycerides, HDL, LDL, VLDL, VO2 peak
extraction_notes: This is a substudy of the S-LITE trial. Semen parameter changes were preregistered as explorative endpoints, not primary outcomes of the main trial. The main trial primary endpoint was weight change. Participants were randomized to four groups in 1:1:1:1 ratio but analyses of semen parameters were primarily conducted by comparing good vs poor weight maintainers rather than by randomization group.

title: Effects of Semaglutide on Stroke Subtypes in Type 2 Diabetes: Post Hoc Analysis of the Randomized SUSTAIN 6 and PIONEER 6.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes at high cardiovascular risk: aged ≥50 years with established cardiovascular disease (myocardial infarction, history of symptomatic coronary heart disease, coronary/carotid/peripheral arterial revascularization, stroke, transient ischemic attacks, >50% stenosis of coronary/carotid/lower extremities arteries), chronic heart failure, or chronic kidney disease; or aged ≥60 years with cardiovascular risk factors
intervention: Semaglutide: subcutaneous 0.5 mg or 1.0 mg once weekly (SUSTAIN 6), or oral 14 mg once daily (PIONEER 6)
comparison: Placebo (subcutaneous in SUSTAIN 6, oral in PIONEER 6)
outcomes_primary: Time to first occurrence of any stroke (fatal and nonfatal); stroke subtypes including ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, and unknown subtypes; ischemic stroke subcategories per TOAST criteria (large artery atherosclerosis, cardioembolism, small-vessel occlusion, stroke of other determined cause, stroke of undetermined cause)
outcomes_secondary: Time to first major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE); subgroup analyses examining treatment effects on stroke risk by prior stroke, prior myocardial infarction or stroke, prior atrial fibrillation, age, sex, systolic blood pressure, and estimated glomerular filtration rate
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis pooling data from two completed cardiovascular outcome trials (SUSTAIN 6 and PIONEER 6). Primary outcomes in original trials were MACE; stroke outcomes in this analysis are exploratory. Trial durations not explicitly stated in this text.

title: Brain Activation in Response to Low-Calorie Food Pictures: An Explorative Analysis of a Randomized Trial With Dapagliflozin and Exenatide.
population: Men and postmenopausal women with type 2 diabetes, aged 18 to 75 years, stable body weight (<5% change during previous 3 months), BMI >25 kg/m2, using metformin with or without sulfonylurea (stable dose for ≥3 months), HbA1c 7%-10% for metformin monotherapy or 7.5%-10% for metformin plus sulfonylurea
intervention: Dapagliflozin 10 mg orally once daily at 8 PM; Exenatide 5 µg subcutaneous injection twice daily (15-30 minutes before breakfast and dinner) for 4 weeks then increased to 10 µg twice daily; Dapagliflozin 10 mg plus exenatide (same dosing as monotherapies); all for 16 weeks

title: Plasma metabolites associated with functional and clinical outcomes in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction with and without type 2 diabetes.

comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Global rank score based on three hierarchical tiers: time to death, time to rehospitalization for heart failure, and time-averaged proportional change in NT-proBNP level from baseline to 180 days
outcomes_secondary: Exercise capacity measured by 6-minute walk distance (6MWD) at baseline and 90 days; serum NT-proBNP at baseline and 90 days; plasma metabolite profiles; time to death or heart failure hospitalization
extraction_notes: This is a secondary analysis of the FIGHT trial (NCT01800968) focusing on metabolomic profiling rather than primary trial outcomes. Liraglutide dose, route, and frequency not specified in the text. The biomarker substudy included 254 of 300 original FIGHT trial participants.

title: Once-Weekly Dulaglutide for the Treatment of Youths with Type 2 Diabetes.

outcomes_secondary: Glycated hemoglobin level of less than 7.0%; change from baseline in fasting glucose concentration; change from baseline in BMI; safety
extraction_notes: Trial included a 26-week open-label extension study where placebo participants switched to dulaglutide 0.75 mg

title: Tirzepatide Once Weekly for the Treatment of Obesity.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Once-Weekly Efpeglenatide Monotherapy Versus Placebo in Type 2 Diabetes: The AMPLITUDE-M Randomized Controlled Trial.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled with diet and exercise alone (HbA1c ≥7% and ≤10% [53-86 mmol/mol] at screening), no glucose-lowering therapy within 3 months prior to screening. outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 30

extraction_notes: Treatment allocation was 1:1:1:1 ratio. Rescue medication (oral antihyperglycemic drugs or insulin, excluding DPP-4 inhibitors and other GLP-1 RAs) was permitted per predefined criteria

title: Once-Weekly Exenatide in Youth With Type 2 Diabetes.
population: Children and adolescents aged 10 to <18 years with type 2 diabetes, glycated hemoglobin 6.5-11% (not on insulin/sulfonylurea) or 6.5-12% (on insulin/sulfonylurea), treated with diet and exercise alone or in combination with stable dose of oral glucose-lowering drug (metformin and/or sulfonylurea) and/or insulin for at least 2 months prior to enrollment, C-peptide >0.6 ng/mL, serum creatinine ≤1.5 mg/dL (males) or ≤1.4 mg/dL (females)

extraction_notes: Randomization ratio was 5:2 (exenatide:placebo). Study included 28-week open-label extension with single-arm crossover but efficacy comparisons limited to 24-week randomized period.

title: Circulating total and intact GDF-15 levels are not altered in response to weight loss induced by liraglutide or lorcaserin treatment in humans with obesity.
population: Adults aged 26-64 years with obesity (BMI 35.6-37.4 kg/m2). Study 1: subjects with metabolic comorbidities (insulin resistance, hypertension, or dyslipidemia).
