intervention: Study 1: Liraglutide self-injected subcutaneously once daily for 5 weeks, escalating dose (0.6 mg/day week 1, increasing weekly to 1.2 mg/day, 1.8 mg/day, 2.4 mg/day, and 3.0 mg/day week 5). comparison: Study 1: Placebo injection for 5 weeks (cross-over design with 3-week wash-out period). Study 2: Placebo for 12 weeks

outcomes_secondary: Associations between total and intact GDF-15 with gender, body composition, clinical and hormonal outcomes; correlations with renal function (eGFR, creatinine); correlations with metabolo-lipidomic profile components

title: Liraglutide 3 mg on weight, body composition, and hormonal and metabolic parameters in women with obesity and polycystic ovary syndrome: a randomized placebo-controlled-phase 3 study.

title: Bromocriptine quick-release as adjunct therapy in youth and adults with type 1 diabetes: A randomized, placebo-controlled crossover study.

title: FGF21 contributes to metabolic improvements elicited by combination therapy with exenatide and pioglitazone in patients with type 2 diabetes.

title: Comparing the effects of twice-daily exenatide and insulin on renal function in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial.

title: A phase 1b randomised controlled trial of a glucagon-like peptide-1 and glucagon receptor dual agonist IBI362 (LY3305677) in Chinese patients with type 2 diabetes.

title: Liraglutide Plus Dapagliflozin for High Uric Acid and Microalbuminuria in Diabetes Mellitus Complicated With Metabolic Syndrome.

population: Treatment-seeking adults aged 18-70 years diagnosed with alcohol use disorder (AUD) according to DSM-5 and alcohol dependence according to ICD-10, with a minimum of 5 heavy drinking days (≥60g alcohol/day for men, ≥48g/day for women) in the past 30 days. Key exclusions: severe mental disorder, other drug use disorder, history of diabetes, pancreatitis, alcohol withdrawal seizures, current treatment with alcohol dependence medications (disulfiram, acamprosate, naltrexone, nalmefene)
intervention: Exenatide 2 mg subcutaneously once weekly for 26 weeks, administered as add-on to standard cognitive-behavioral therapy (motivational interviewing, cognitive therapy, family therapy sessions every second week)
comparison: Placebo subcutaneously once weekly for 26 weeks, plus standard cognitive-behavioral therapy
outcomes_primary: Change in number of heavy drinking days from baseline to week 26, recorded by Time-Line Follow Back method
outcomes_secondary: Total alcohol consumption; number of days with no alcohol consumption; Penn Alcohol Craving Scale score; AUDIT score; DUDIT score; Screen for Cognitive Impairment in Psychiatry (SCIP) test; Fagerström Test for Nicotine Dependence; blood γ-glutamyl transferase; blood alanine aminotransferase; blood phosphatidylethanol; mean cell volume; HbA1c; body weight; blood pressure; heart rate; SF-36; SCL-92; SPECT dopamine transporter specific binding ratio; fMRI BOLD signal change; subjective craving with alcohol cue reactivity task; fMRI spatial working memory task; change in heavy drinking days at 6-month follow-up
extraction_notes: Subgroup underwent fMRI and SPECT brain imaging at baseline and week 26. Healthy controls (n=25) included for fMRI comparison only. 6-month follow-up after treatment discontinuation was conducted.

title: Dulaglutide and cardiovascular and heart failure outcomes in patients with and without heart failure: a post-hoc analysis from the REWIND randomized trial.
population: People with type 2 diabetes at high risk for cardiovascular events, including those with and without prior heart failure
intervention: Dulaglutide (glucagon-like peptide 1 agonist), weekly administration
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE): composite endpoint of non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, or death from cardiovascular causes (including unknown causes)
outcomes_secondary: Heart failure event (adjudication-confirmed hospitalization or urgent evaluation for heart failure); combined cardiovascular death and heart failure events
extraction_notes: This is a post-hoc analysis of the REWIND randomized trial. Specific dulaglutide dose not stated in abstract. Primary outcome listed is the original REWIND trial MACE outcome; HF events appear to be the focus of this post-hoc analysis.

title: Risk of adverse events with liraglutide in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction: A post hoc analysis of the FIGHT trial.
population: Adults aged 18 years or older with established diagnosis of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (LVEF ≤40% within preceding 3 months), recent hospitalization for acute heart failure (within 14 days), and preadmission oral diuretic dose of at least 40 mg furosemide or equivalent per day. Exclusions: recent acute coronary syndrome or coronary intervention, known intolerance of GLP-1RA therapy, severe renal, hepatic or pulmonary disease. Patients with and without type 2 diabetes were enrolled.
intervention: Liraglutide subcutaneous injection, uptitrated as tolerated every 14 days from 0.6 mg/day to 1.2 mg/day to 1.8 mg/day during the first 30 days, then continued for 180 days total follow-up
comparison: Matching placebo (identically packaged to maintain blinding)
outcomes_primary: Total events (first and recurrent) of heart failure hospitalizations or all-cause death
outcomes_secondary: Total heart failure hospitalizations; all-cause death; total events of heart failure hospitalizations, urgent heart failure visits requiring intravenous diuretic treatment, or all-cause death; total events of urgent heart failure visit requiring intravenous treatment; total arrhythmic events (investigator reported); prespecified total events of interest (arrhythmias, sudden cardiac death, acute coronary syndrome, worsening heart failure, cerebrovascular event, venous thromboembolism, lightheadedness, presyncope or syncope, or worsening renal function)
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of the FIGHT trial. The original FIGHT trial primary outcome was a global rank score based on time to death, time to rehospitalization for HF, and time-averaged proportional change in NT-proBNP. The outcomes listed here are specific to this post hoc analysis.

title: Effects of liraglutide or lifestyle interventions combined with other antidiabetic drugs on abdominal fat distribution in people with obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus evaluated by the energy spectrum ct: A prospective randomized controlled study.
population: Adults aged 18-65 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus, BMI ≥28 kg/m², HbA1c ≥6.5%, previously treated with hypoglycemic drugs without lifestyle interventions. Exclusions: other diabetes types, severe acute/chronic diabetes complications, DPP-4 inhibitor use in past 3 months, severe liver function damage (ALT≥120U/L), severe renal insufficiency, severe heart failure (NYHA III-IV), severe hypertriglyceridemia (TG≥5mmol/L), mental disorders, pregnancy/lactation, secondary obesity, long-term weight-affecting drugs, alcoholism, high risk factors for medullary thyroid cancer or abnormal thyroid function, tumor history within 5 years, liraglutide allergy
intervention: Liraglutide once-daily subcutaneous injection (weight-based dosing) added to existing hypoglycemic treatment for 12 weeks
comparison: Lifestyle intervention (diet plan with daily energy reduction of 500-1000 kcal; male patients 1200-4000 kcal/day, female patients 1000-1200 kcal/day; carbohydrate 55-60% and fat 25-30% of total daily energy; at least 30 minutes moderate-intensity aerobic exercise 5 days per week) added to existing hypoglycemic treatment for 12 weeks
outcomes_primary: Visceral fat area measured by energy spectrum CT at L3 vertebral transverse process level
outcomes_secondary: Physical measurements (height, weight, waist circumference, hip circumference, BMI, waist-to-hip ratio); blood tests (fasting blood glucose, HbA1c, UAER, creatinine, BUN, AST, ALT); energy spectrum CT examination results (abdominal cross-sectional area, subcutaneous fat area of abdomen, liver fat content, abdominal subcutaneous fat thickness, back subcutaneous fat thickness, subcutaneous fat thickness outside erector spine, erector spinae intramuscular fat content); body composition analysis (body mass, skeletal muscle, body fat, body fat percentage); adverse events including gastrointestinal symptoms and hypoglycemia
extraction_notes: Liraglutide dose not specified beyond 'weight-based'; the text mentions 1.8 mg/d in discussion referencing LEAD study but does not confirm this was the dose used in this study

title: Prolonged lipopolysaccharide-induced illness elevates glucagon-like peptide-1 and suppresses peptide YY: A human-randomized cross-over trial.
population: Healthy young men aged 20-40 years with BMI 20-30 kg/m2, nonsmokers, without regular medicine intake, no ongoing signs of infection, no gastrointestinal conditions or prior abdominal surgery
intervention: Systemic inflammation condition: LPS injection 1 ng/kg intravenously at time -24h followed by overnight fast and immobilization, then second LPS injection 0.5 ng/kg at time 0, combined with standardized protein beverage (45g β-lactoglobulin protein, 20g maltodextrin, 28.2g lipid; 501 kcal total) and SmartPill capsule ingestion
comparison: Healthy conditions: overnight fast only followed by same standardized protein beverage and SmartPill capsule ingestion (no LPS injection, no bedrest/immobilization)
outcomes_primary: Whole gut transit time, gastric emptying time, small bowel transit time, colonic transit time, gastrointestinal motility (pressure measurements), gastrointestinal pH measurements
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) concentrations, peptide YY (PYY) concentrations, acylated ghrelin concentrations, glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide (GIP) concentrations, heart rate, body temperature, inflammatory markers (leucocytes, CRP, IL-6, TNF-α)
extraction_notes: This is a substudy of a larger randomized crossover trial (NCT04064268) with 8 participants. The trial had three arms but only two are reported in this substudy. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the text; classification based on stated aims. Small sample size (n=8).

title: The Effect of Short-term Mediterranean-DASH Intervention for Neurodegenerative Delay (MIND) Diet on Hunger Hormones, Anthropometric Parameters, and Brain Structures in Middle-aged Overweight and Obese Women: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
population: Healthy overweight and obese middle-aged women aged 40-60 years with BMI 30-35 Kg/m2, Mini-Mental State Examination score ≥24, no history of severe medical problems (psychosis, bipolar disorder, depression or psychiatric disorder, unstable cardiovascular disease or myocardial infarction in last six months, stroke, history of brain injury, liver disease or hepatitis C and HIV), no participation in weight loss programs or consumption of weight loss drugs in the last three months
intervention: Hypocaloric modified MIND (Mediterranean-DASH Intervention for Neurodegenerative Delay) diet with calorie intake restricted to at least 1500 Kcal/day, balanced mix of 50-55% carbohydrates, 30% fat, and 15-20% proteins, emphasizing green leafy vegetables, berries, nuts, fruits, legumes, olive oil as primary fat source, fish more than one meal per week, poultry more than two meals per week, with restricted red meat, butter, margarine, processed foods and sweets, for three months
comparison: Hypocaloric control diet with calorie intake restricted to at least 1500 Kcal/day, balanced mix of 50-55% carbohydrates, 30% fat, and 15-20% proteins, maintaining typical eating habits for three months
outcomes_primary: Changes in anthropometric parameters (weight, BMI, percentage of body fat, waist circumference, total body water, fat-free mass), hunger hormones (plasma levels of Leptin, Ghrelin, and GLP-1), and brain structures (whole brain and regional brain volume including fusiform, parahippocampal, medial, superior, and temporal gyrus)
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes were not explicitly distinguished in the text. Trial registration number: IRCT20190427043387N1. Study was single-blind with randomization by computer software. MRI scans performed on subgroup of 11 patients per group.

title: Weight Loss Outcomes Associated With Semaglutide Treatment for Patients With Overweight or Obesity.
population: Adults with body mass index (BMI) of 27 or more prescribed weekly semaglutide subcutaneous injections for weight loss with at least 3 months follow-up. Exclusions: history of bariatric procedures (surgical or endoscopic), taking other FDA-approved antiobesity medications, active malignant neoplasm, pregnancy, insurance denial, or affected by national shortage of semaglutide.
intervention: Weekly subcutaneous semaglutide injections at doses of 0.25, 0.5, 1, 1.7, and 2.4 mg for 3 to 6 months
comparison: No comparator group
outcomes_primary: Percentage of total body weight loss at 3 and 6 months after semaglutide initiation
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of patients achieving categorical weight loss of 5% or more, 10% or more, 15% or more, and 20% or more; percentage weight loss for patients with or without type 2 diabetes at 3 and 6 months
extraction_notes: This is a single-arm retrospective cohort study without a comparator group. Post hoc analyses included weight loss by diabetes status and by different semaglutide doses.

title: Glycemia Reduction in Type 2 Diabetes - Glycemic Outcomes.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes diagnosed at or after age 30 years (or age 20 years for American Indians or Alaska Natives), with known duration of diabetes less than 10 years, receiving at least 500 mg metformin per day for the previous 6 months without other glucose-lowering medications, willing to use injection therapy, and with glycated hemoglobin level of 6.8 to 8.5% at the end of run-in period
intervention: Insulin glargine U-100 administered daily at initial dose up to 20 U adjusted according to glucose levels; OR glimepiride 1-2 mg increased to maximum 8 mg per day in divided doses; OR liraglutide initiated at 0.6 mg escalated to maximum 1.8 mg daily; OR sitagliptin 100 mg with dose adjusted according to kidney function. All added to metformin at least 1000 mg per day (target 2000 mg per day). Mean follow-up 5.0 years
comparison: Four-way comparison among insulin glargine U-100, glimepiride, liraglutide, and sitagliptin, all added to background metformin therapy
outcomes_primary: Primary metabolic failure defined as confirmed glycated hemoglobin level of 7.0% or higher
outcomes_secondary: Secondary metabolic outcome: confirmed glycated hemoglobin level greater than 7.5%. Tertiary metabolic outcome: confirmed glycated hemoglobin level greater than 7.5% after secondary outcome. Other outcomes: serious adverse events; targeted adverse events including severe hypoglycemia requiring treatment, pancreatitis, pancreatic and other cancers; effects on microvascular complications; cardiovascular disease and risk factors; weight changes; gastrointestinal side effects
extraction_notes: Open-label trial with laboratory and reading center staff blinded to treatment assignment. Participants could receive additional treatments (glargine added to non-insulin groups after secondary outcome, rapid-acting insulin after tertiary outcome) per protocol

title: Glycemia Reduction in Type 2 Diabetes - Microvascular and Cardiovascular Outcomes.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
population: Adults diagnosed with type 2 diabetes mellitus at age 30 years or older (20 years or older for American Indians and Alaska Natives), diabetes diagnosed within the previous 10 years, treated with at least 500 mg metformin per day with no other glucose-lowering medications, glycated hemoglobin level 6.8-8.5% at randomization. Exclusions: history of major cardiovascular event within 1 year before randomization, New York Heart Association functional classification III or higher, estimated glomerular filtration rate less than 30 ml/min/1.73 m2
intervention: Four treatment groups added to metformin (at least 1000 mg/day, target 2000 mg/day): (1) Insulin glargine U-100 administered daily, initial dose up to 20 U adjusted based on glucose monitoring; (2) Glimepiride 1-8 mg/day in divided doses; (3) Liraglutide escalated to maximum 1.8 mg daily; (4) Sitagliptin 100 mg adjusted based on kidney function
comparison: Each of the four glucose-lowering medications compared with each other and with the other three groups combined
outcomes_primary: Glycated hemoglobin level maintenance below 7.0% (reported in companion article)
outcomes_secondary: Hypertension (defined as previously diagnosed hypertension, measured blood pressure at least 140/90 mm Hg, or treatment with blood pressure-lowering agents); Dyslipidemia (defined as fasting LDL cholesterol at least 100 mg/dL, triglycerides at least 150 mg/dL, HDL less than 40 mg/dL in men or less than 50 mg/dL in women, or use of lipid-lowering medications); Confirmed moderately increased albuminuria (albumin:creatinine ratio 30 or greater confirmed at subsequent visit); Confirmed severely increased albuminuria (albumin:creatinine ratio 300 or higher); Renal impairment (eGFR less than 60 ml/min/1.73 m2); Diabetic peripheral neuropathy (MNSI score 7 or higher or examination score 2.5 or higher); Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or death from cardiovascular causes); Hospitalization for heart failure; Any cardiovascular disease (MACE, unstable angina or heart failure warranting hospitalization, or revascularization in any arterial bed); Death from cardiovascular causes; All-cause death
extraction_notes: This is a companion article focusing on secondary outcomes; primary metabolic outcome results published separately. Mean follow-up 5.0 years in 5047 participants across 36 clinical centers.

title: Effects of tirzepatide versus insulin glargine on kidney outcomes in type 2 diabetes in the SURPASS-4 trial: post-hoc analysis of an open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial.
population: Adults aged ≥18 years with type 2 diabetes treated with any combination of metformin, sulfonylurea, or SGLT2 inhibitor, with high cardiovascular risk
intervention: Tirzepatide (dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist); specific dose, route, frequency, and duration not specified in abstract
comparison: Insulin glargine
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified as primary in abstract; kidney outcomes including rate of eGFR decline and UACR were analyzed
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly specified in abstract
extraction_notes: This is a post-hoc analysis of the SURPASS-4 trial. The original trial's primary outcome was HbA1c reduction; kidney outcomes were analyzed post-hoc. Specific tirzepatide dosing not provided in abstract. Baseline HbA1c inclusion criteria partially stated but cut off in abstract text. Study duration not specified in abstract.

title: Liraglutide for Weight Management in Children and Adolescents With Prader-Willi Syndrome and Obesity.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
population: Children aged 6 to <12 years (Tanner stage <2) and adolescents aged 12 to <18 years (Tanner stage 2-5) with genetically confirmed Prader-Willi syndrome and obesity (BMI corresponding to ≥30 kg/m2 for adults by international cut-off points and ≥95th percentile for age and sex), with stable body weight (self-reported weight change <10 kg during 90 days before screening). Key exclusions: diagnosis of type 1 or 2 diabetes, documented or untreated adrenal insufficiency, history or significant risk of gastroparesis.
intervention: Liraglutide 3.0 mg (or maximum-tolerated dose) administered once daily as subcutaneous injection for 52 weeks. Initiated at 0.6 mg and escalated in weekly increments of 0.6 mg until target or maximum-tolerated dose achieved. For children with body weight <45 kg, initiated at 0.3 mg up to maximum dose of 2.4 mg. All patients received individualized dietary and physical activity counseling as structured program.
comparison: Matched placebo for 16 weeks (double-blind period), then no treatment apart from diet and exercise from weeks 17-52 (open-label period). Randomization ratio 2:1 (liraglutide:placebo).
outcomes_primary: Change in BMI standard deviation score (BMI SDS) from baseline to 16 weeks and to 52 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of patients achieving ≥5% and ≥10% reduction in baseline BMI at weeks 16 and 52; proportion of patients with no increase in baseline BMI SDS at weeks 16 and 52; changes from baseline to weeks 16 and 52 in BMI, body weight (%, kg), waist circumference, waist-to-hip circumference ratio, hyperphagia score (total score, hyperphagic behavior, drive, and severity scores using Dykens 13-item questionnaire), high sensitivity C-reactive protein, fasting lipids, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, glucose metabolism parameters; safety endpoints including treatment-emergent adverse events and hypoglycemic episodes; mental health assessment in adolescents using Columbia-Suicide Severity Rating Score and Patient Health Questionnaire-9
extraction_notes: Open-label design after week 16 limits blinding for 52-week outcomes. Stratification by pubertal status and presence/absence of dysglycemia.

title: Change in pharmacodynamic variables following once-weekly tirzepatide treatment versus dulaglutide in Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes (SURPASS J-mono substudy).
population: Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus; age ≥20 years; diagnosis of T2D at least 8 weeks prior to screening; OAM-naive or taking OAM monotherapy with willingness to discontinue; HbA1c ≥53 mmol/mol to ≤86 mmol/mol (≥7.0% to ≤10.0%) for OAM-naive or ≥48 mmol/mol to ≤75 mmol/mol (≥6.5%–≤9.0%) at Visit 1 and ≥53 mmol/mol to ≤86 mmol/mol (≥7.0%–≤10.0%) at Visit 2 for patients on OAM monotherapy; stable weight (±5%) for 3 months prior to Visit 1; BMI ≥23 kg/m2; exclusions included type 1 diabetes, history of injectable therapy for T2D, chronic or acute pancreatitis, diabetic retinopathy requiring acute treatment, acute or chronic hepatitis, eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m2
intervention: Tirzepatide 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg subcutaneous injection once weekly for 52 weeks; starting dose 2.5 mg once weekly for 4 weeks, increased by 2.5 mg every 4 weeks until target dose reached
comparison: Dulaglutide 0.75 mg subcutaneous injection once weekly for 52 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline in area under the concentration versus time curve from time zero to 6 hours (AUC[0-6h]) for postprandial metabolic variables (glucose, insulin, glucagon, C-peptide, triglycerides) following meal tolerance test at Week 32
outcomes_secondary: Appetite assessed by visual analogue scale (fullness and hunger AUC[0-6h]) following meal tolerance test; body composition measured by bioelectrical impedance analysis (body weight, body fat mass, lean body mass, total body water, protein, minerals) at Weeks 0, 12, 32, and 52
extraction_notes: This is an exploratory substudy of SURPASS J-mono (n=48 from 636 participants in main study); primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly designated as such - categorized based on stated objectives; small sample sizes per treatment arm (n=9-19)

title: Factors associated with successful weight loss after liraglutide treatment for obesity.
population: Adults aged 18-65 years with obesity (BMI >30 kg/m2), otherwise healthy, residing within 125 miles of Mayo Clinic Rochester MN. Excluded: patients with delayed gastric emptying of solids (>90th percentile according to gender), psychiatric symptoms, alcohol use disorders, eating disorders, or intake of medications except multivitamins within 7 days of study
intervention: Liraglutide 3mg subcutaneous injection once daily for 16 weeks, escalated from 0.6mg daily increased by 0.6mg weekly increments until 3.0mg reached over 4 weeks, plus standardized dietetic and behavioral counseling for weight reduction
comparison: Placebo (saline) subcutaneous injection with similar weekly volume increments for 16 weeks, plus standardized dietetic and behavioral counseling for weight reduction
outcomes_primary: Weight loss >4kg at 16 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Gastric emptying of solids (GET1/2) at baseline, 5 weeks, and 16 weeks; fasting and postprandial gastric volumes; caloric intake during ad libitum buffet meal; volume to fullness and maximum tolerated volume during nutrient drink test; fasting and postprandial peptide YY levels
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of a previously published RCT (NCT03523273) examining predictors and factors associated with weight loss. The primary outcome of weight loss >4kg threshold was selected by authors as clinically relevant based on prior literature rather than being prespecified in original trial design. Study includes genotyping for TCF7L2 and GLP-1R variants as exploratory variables.

title: Two-year effects of semaglutide in adults with overweight or obesity: the STEP 5 trial.
population: Adults aged ≥18 years with obesity (BMI ≥30.0 kg/m²) or overweight (BMI ≥27.0 kg/m²) with at least one weight-related comorbidity (hypertension, dyslipidemia, obstructive sleep apnea, or cardiovascular disease), without diabetes (HbA1c <6.5%), with history of at least one self-reported unsuccessful dietary effort to lose body weight. Key exclusions: type 1 or type 2 diabetes, treatment with glucose-lowering agents within 90 days, body weight change >5 kg within 90 days, obesity medication within 90 days, previous obesity surgery, uncontrolled thyroid disease, major depressive disorder within 2 years, severe psychiatric disorders, history of pancreatitis, medullary thyroid carcinoma history, renal impairment (eGFR <15 ml/min/1.73m²), malignancy within 5 years, recent cardiovascular events within 60 days.
intervention: Subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg once weekly for 104 weeks, initiated at 0.25 mg weekly for first 4 weeks with fixed-dose escalation every 4 weeks to reach maintenance dose of 2.4 mg by week 16, plus behavioral intervention (counseling every 4 weeks on reduced-calorie diet with 500 kcal/day deficit and increased physical activity of 150 minutes/week)
comparison: Matching placebo subcutaneous injection once weekly for 104 weeks, plus identical behavioral intervention (counseling every 4 weeks on reduced-calorie diet with 500 kcal/day deficit and increased physical activity of 150 minutes/week)
outcomes_primary: Co-primary endpoints: (1) Percentage change in body weight from baseline to week 104; (2) Achievement of weight loss of at least 5% of baseline weight at week 104
outcomes_secondary: Confirmatory secondary endpoints (in hierarchical order): achievement of weight loss of ≥10% or ≥15% at week 104; change from baseline to week 104 in waist circumference and systolic blood pressure. Supportive secondary endpoints: achievement of weight loss ≥20% at week 104; change from baseline to week 104 in body weight (kg), BMI, HbA1c, fasting plasma glucose, fasting serum insulin, diastolic blood pressure, lipids (total cholesterol, HDL, LDL, VLDL, free fatty acids, triglycerides), and C-reactive protein. Safety endpoints: treatment-emergent adverse events and serious adverse events, change in pulse, amylase, lipase, and calcitonin
extraction_notes: Phase 3 randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial. Two estimands used: treatment policy estimand (primary analysis, intention-to-treat regardless of discontinuation) and trial product estimand (on-treatment analysis). Exploratory endpoints included glycemic category changes and medication use changes. 7-week treatment-free follow-up period after 104-week treatment period.

title: The metabolic effects of adding exenatide to basal insulin therapy when targeting remission in early type 2 diabetes in a randomized clinical trial.
population: Adults aged 30-80 years with type 2 diabetes of ≤7 years duration; treatment with up to 2 oral anti-diabetic medications (with no change in dose/regimen in preceding 4 weeks); screening A1c between 6.0-9.5% if on no anti-diabetic medications or between 5.5-9.0% if on anti-diabetic medication; exclusion criteria included treatment with insulin or GLP1-RA, renal dysfunction (eGFR <30 ml/min), history of pancreatitis, familial or personal history of Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2 or medullary thyroid carcinoma
intervention: Insulin glargine once daily at bedtime (starting dose 0.12 units/kg, titrated to target fasting glucose ≤5.3 mmol/l) plus exenatide 5 μg subcutaneously twice daily before breakfast and dinner for 4 weeks, then increased to 10 μg twice daily for 4 weeks (total 8 weeks treatment), followed by 12 weeks washout
comparison: (1) Insulin glargine alone once daily at bedtime (starting dose 0.12 units/kg, titrated to target fasting glucose ≤5.3 mmol/l) for 8 weeks; (2) Insulin glargine once daily at bedtime plus pre-meal insulin lispro three times daily (total starting dose 0.3 units/kg, 60% bolus/40% basal, titrated to target fasting glucose ≤5.3 mmol/l and 2-hour postprandial glucose <8 mmol/l) for 8 weeks; both followed by 12 weeks washout
outcomes_primary: Mean Insulin Secretion-Sensitivity Index-2 (ISSI-2) over the 8-week intervention
outcomes_secondary: Baseline-adjusted A1c at 8-weeks; baseline-adjusted ISSI-2 at 20-weeks; baseline-adjusted A1c at 20-weeks; additional outcomes included baseline-adjusted measures at 8-weeks and 20-weeks for supplementary beta-cell indices (insulinogenic index/HOMA-IR, ΔCpeptide0-120/Δgluc0-120 × Matsuda index, ΔISR0-120/Δgluc0-120 × Matsuda index), insulin sensitivity/resistance (Matsuda index, HOMA-IR), fasting and 2-hour glucose, anthropometric measures (weight, BMI, waist circumference), diabetes remission (A1c <6.5% after 3-months off anti-diabetic medications)
extraction_notes: Open-label, parallel-arm randomized controlled trial with 1:1:1 allocation; single academic center in Toronto; analyzed population n=102 (Glar n=33, Glar/Lispro n=35, Glar/Exenatide n=34)

title: Effects of GLP-1 Infusion Upon Whole-body Glucose Uptake and Skeletal Muscle Perfusion During Fed-state in Older Men.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
population: Healthy male volunteers aged 65-75 years without metabolic disease, lower limb musculoskeletal abnormalities, acute cerebrovascular or cardiovascular disease, active malignancy, uncontrolled hypertension, BMI 18-28 kg/m², not on medications affecting glucose metabolism or vascular tone, and without allergy to study infusions
intervention: Femoral arterial GLP-1 infusion at 1.2 pmol/kg/min for 3 hours, combined with peripheral IV infusions of octreotide (30 ng/kg/min), insulin Actrapid, 20% glucose, and mixed amino acids (Vamin 14-EF; prime 34 mg/kg followed by 102 mg/kg/h)
comparison: Placebo (0.9% saline) femoral arterial infusion combined with identical peripheral IV infusions of octreotide, insulin Actrapid, 20% glucose, and mixed amino acids
outcomes_primary: Skeletal muscle microvascular blood flow assessed via contrast-enhanced ultrasound (microvascular blood volume, microvascular flow velocity, microvascular blood flow); whole-body glucose uptake calculated from glucose infusion rate
outcomes_secondary: Leg blood flow measured via femoral artery; plasma GLP-1, insulin, and C-peptide concentrations; plasma phenylalanine concentrations; glucose infusion rate
extraction_notes: Randomized crossover trial with 8 participants studied on 2 occasions approximately 3 weeks apart. Single-blind design (volunteers blinded to GLP-1 allocation). Primary outcomes not explicitly designated as primary vs secondary in the text.

title: Response to: Letter to the Editor Regarding Efficacy of IDegLira Versus IDegAsp Therapy in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes: A Randomized Crossover Study by isCGM.
extraction_notes: No abstract text available for extraction. The title indicates this is a letter to the editor responding to a study about IDegLira versus IDegAsp in patients with type 2 diabetes, but no extractable content is provided.

title: The probiotic
population: Healthy adults aged 30-65 years with BMI 18.0-31.9 kg/m2, consuming typical American diet, with at least minimal complaints of abdominal bloating, burping, or flatulence (combined score ≥3 for these symptoms during baseline week), nonsmokers, no history of major illness, no clinically important GI conditions, not pregnant, no recent antibiotic use (<3 months), no recent use of medications or products known to influence GI function, no known allergies to study product ingredients
intervention: Bacillus subtilis BS50 2×10^9 CFU per capsule, one capsule daily taken orally with the largest meal of the day for 6 weeks
comparison: Matching maltodextrin placebo capsule, one capsule daily taken orally with the largest meal of the day for 6 weeks
outcomes_primary: Proportion of participants with improvement in the 7-day, 3-item composite score for flatulence, bloating, and burping (improvement defined as decrease of at least 2 points from baseline to week 6 where none of the 3 individual items increased by 1 or more points)
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of participants with improvement in individual GI symptoms (bloating, burping, flatulence, abdominal cramping, reflux/heartburn, borborygmus/stomach rumbling, nausea, vomiting); bowel habits (stool frequency, stool consistency via Bristol Stool Scale, straining, discomfort during bowel movements, sensation of incomplete evacuation); sleep quality; respiratory infection presence and duration; plasma intestinal permeability markers (zonulin, occludin, lipopolysaccharide-binding protein); plasma inflammatory markers (CRP, IL-8, IL-6, IL-10, IFN-γ, TNF-α); fasting plasma lipid profile (triglycerides, total cholesterol, LDL-C, HDL-C); safety outcomes including clinical chemistry, hematology, vital signs, body weight, adverse events
extraction_notes: Sample size: 76 participants randomized. Study was randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group design. Primary outcome analysis used chi-square test and logistic regression adjusted for sex and BMI category.

title: Postprandial Glucose and Gastrointestinal Hormone Responses of Healthy Subjects to Wheat Biscuits Enriched with L-Arginine or Branched-Chain Amino Acids of Plant Origin.
population: Healthy subjects, 30 participants (15 males, 15 females), mean age 26.5 ± 5.3 years, BMI 25.7 ± 4.6 kg/m². Exclusions: those modifying diet or exercise patterns to lose weight, known food allergies or intolerances, restrictive eaters, excessive exercisers or trained athletes, taking any medications or food supplements, pregnant, breastfeeding, or postmenopausal women.
intervention: Wheat-based biscuits enriched with plant flours from legumes/seeds: (1) BCAAsB - enriched in branched-chain amino acids (28.8% wheat flour, 18.9% millet flour, 4.7% white bean flour, 10.5% yellow lentil protein concentrate); (2) ArgB - enriched in L-arginine (41.2% wheat flour, 11.8% defatted sesame flour, 5.9% yellow lentil flour). Biscuit amounts yielding 50 g of available carbohydrates served with 250 mL tap water, consumed within 15 min, single dose in acute setting.
comparison: Common wheat biscuit (CB) containing only wheat flour (57.4%), yielding 50 g available carbohydrates with 250 mL tap water; Glucose solution (GS) containing 50 g anhydrous glucose diluted in 250 mL water as reference food.
outcomes_primary: Postprandial glucose response measured as incremental area under the curve (iAUC) over 180 minutes.
outcomes_secondary: Insulin response (iAUC), gastrointestinal hormone responses including total ghrelin, GLP-1, PYY, and glicentin (iAUC), postprandial amino acid concentrations (L-arginine, L-leucine, L-isoleucine, L-valine), subjective appetite sensations assessed by visual analogue scales (hunger, fullness, desire to eat).
extraction_notes: Acute single-blind randomized controlled crossover study with 1-week washout period between sessions. This was a mechanistic/exploratory study examining postprandial responses rather than a clinical efficacy trial. Sensory evaluation was performed separately with 25 trained testers.

title: Comparative effects of weight loss and incretin-based therapies on vascular endothelial function, fibrinolysis and inflammation in individuals with obesity and prediabetes: A randomized controlled trial.
population: Men and women aged 18 to 65 years with obesity (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m²) and pre-diabetes
intervention: Liraglutide 1.8 mg/day subcutaneous injection (dose escalation: 0.6 mg/day week 1, 1.2 mg/day week 2, 1.8 mg/day from week 3) for 14 weeks

outcomes_primary: Endothelial function measured by flow-mediated vasodilation (FMD); Fibrinolytic function measured by plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1); Urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR)
outcomes_secondary: Blood pressure; Heart rate; Fasting insulin; Fasting glucose; Monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1); P-selectin
extraction_notes: Randomization ratio was 2:1:1 (liraglutide:diet:sitagliptin). Treatment with liraglutide and sitagliptin was double-blind and placebo-controlled; diet intervention was unblinded. A subset of participants underwent additional crossover study with GLP-1R antagonist exendin (9-39).

title: Once-Weekly Semaglutide in Adolescents with Obesity.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
population: Adolescents aged 12 to <18 years with obesity (BMI in the 95th percentile or higher) or with overweight (BMI in the 85th percentile or higher) and at least one weight-related coexisting condition; at least one unsuccessful dietary weight-loss effort required; persons with type 2 diabetes eligible if treated with diet and exercise alone or with metformin and glycated hemoglobin level of 10.0% or less; exclusion criteria included weight change of more than 5 kg or use of obesity medication within 90 days before screening, previous bariatric surgery, uncontrolled thyroid disease, secondary causes of obesity, major depressive disorder within 2 years before screening, severe psychiatric disorders or bulimia nervosa, and history of suicide attempt
intervention: Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg for 68 weeks (dose escalated over 16 weeks from 0.25 mg to 2.4 mg or maximum tolerated dose) plus lifestyle intervention (behavioral lifestyle therapy including counseling about healthy nutrition and physical activity)
comparison: Matching placebo once-weekly subcutaneous injection for 68 weeks plus lifestyle intervention
outcomes_primary: Percentage change in BMI from baseline to week 68
outcomes_secondary: Weight loss of at least 5% at week 68 (secondary confirmatory endpoint); secondary supportive endpoints included changes in body weight (percentage and kilograms), BMI, BMI as percentage of 95th percentile, BMI standard-deviation score, waist circumference, blood pressure, glycated hemoglobin level, lipid levels, alanine aminotransferase level; BMI reduction of at least 5%; body weight reduction of at least 10%, 15%, and 20%; exploratory endpoints included percentage change in BMI at week 75 and change in Impact of Weight on Quality of Life-Kids (IWQOL-Kids) questionnaire score; safety endpoints included changes in heart rate, amylase levels, lipase levels, calcitonin levels, and adverse events
extraction_notes: Only one participant had overweight (remainder had obesity); 12-week lifestyle intervention run-in phase occurred before randomization; 7-week follow-up period after 68-week treatment period

title: Pharmacokinetics of Glepaglutide, A Long-Acting Glucagon-Like Peptide-2 Analogue: A Study in Healthy Subjects.
population: Healthy male and female subjects of any ethnic origin, aged 18-60 years inclusive, body mass index 18-30 kg/m2 inclusive, in good health as confirmed by no clinically significant findings from medical history, physical examination, electrocardiogram, vital signs measurements, and clinical laboratory evaluations

outcomes_primary: Pharmacokinetic parameters including area under the plasma concentration-time curve (AUC), maximum observed plasma concentration (Cmax), time to maximum concentration (tmax), apparent plasma terminal elimination half-life (t1/2,z), effective half-life (t1/2,eff), apparent total plasma clearance (CL/F), volume of distribution at steady state (Vss), accumulation index (RAAUC), metabolite to parent ratio (MRAUCτ) for parent drug and metabolites M1 and M2
outcomes_secondary: Plasma citrulline concentrations as pharmacodynamic biomarker; safety and tolerability assessed by adverse event recording, vital signs measurements, electrocardiograms, clinical laboratory evaluations including anti-glepaglutide antibodies, physical examinations, and monitoring for injection-site reactions
extraction_notes: This is a phase I clinical pharmacology study in healthy subjects, not the target patient population (short bowel syndrome). Part 1 of the study (daily dosing for 7 days) was mentioned but results not reported. The study is described as open-label and partially randomised.

title: Insufficient sleep predicts poor weight loss maintenance after 1 year.
population: Adults aged 18-65 years with obesity (BMI 32-43 kg/m2) who completed an 8-week low-calorie diet and lost at least 5% of initial weight. Exclusion criteria included serious chronic illnesses such as diabetes type 1 and 2.
intervention: 52-week weight loss maintenance phase with exercise (two weekly supervised sessions of 45 min plus two weekly individual sessions of 30 min involving interval-based spinning, circuit training, and aerobic exercise) and/or liraglutide 3.0 mg/day subcutaneously (initiated at 0.6 mg/day with weekly increments of 0.6 mg). All participants received monthly consultations with weighing and dietetic support.
comparison: Two-by-two factorial design: exercise versus no exercise (habitual physical activity); liraglutide 3.0 mg/day versus volume-matched placebo. Participants also stratified by sleep duration (<6 h/night versus ≥6 h/night) and sleep quality (PSQI score >5 versus ≤5).
outcomes_primary: Change in body weight during 1-year weight maintenance phase
outcomes_secondary: Change in body fat percentage; sleep duration measured by wrist-worn accelerometers (GENEActiv); sleep quality measured by Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) global score and factors (sleep efficiency, perceived sleep quality, daily disturbances); sleep efficiency; sedentary time; circulating leptin, soluble leptin receptor, and free leptin index
extraction_notes: This is a randomized controlled trial with sleep as a predefined exploratory endpoint, not a primary outcome. The study investigates associations between baseline sleep characteristics and weight outcomes, as well as effects of interventions on sleep. Primary and secondary outcome hierarchy not explicitly stated for sleep measures.

title: Glucometabolic control of once-weekly dulaglutide switched from DPP4 inhibitor versus daily empagliflozin add-on in patients with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled with metformin, sulfonylurea, and DPP4 inhibitor: A randomised trial.

title: Tirzepatide reduces the predicted risk of developing type 2 diabetes in people with obesity or overweight: Post hoc analysis of the SURMOUNT-1 trial.

title: The Use of Rescue Insulin in the Glycemia Reduction Approaches in Diabetes: A Comparative Effectiveness Study (GRADE).

title: The effects of exenatide and insulin glargine treatments on bone turnover markers and bone mineral density in postmenopausal patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.

outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly specified. Additional measurements included BMI, HbA1c, fasting glucose, and 25-hydroxy vitamin D levels.
extraction_notes: Study did not explicitly designate primary versus secondary outcomes. Small sample size (n=30 enrolled, 30 completed). Open-label design. Follow-up period was 24 weeks.

title: Diabetes Remission After LRYGBP With and Without Fundus Resection: a Randomized Clinical Trial.

intervention: Laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with fundus resection (LRYGBP+FR): creation of 30ml gastric pouch, 200cm biliopancreatic limb, 150cm alimentary limb, 25mm circular stapler gastrojejunal anastomosis, with additional mobilization of gastric body and fundus by dividing gastrocolic ligament and short gastric vessels, L-shaped gastric pouch creation, and horizontal fundus resection (approximately 5.5cm width and 10cm vertical length removed)
comparison: Standard laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (LRYGBP): creation of 30ml gastric pouch, 200cm biliopancreatic limb, 150cm alimentary limb, 25mm circular stapler gastrojejunal anastomosis without fundus resection
outcomes_primary: HbA1c levels at one-year follow-up

extraction_notes: Prospective non-blinded RCT with 1:1 randomization. Sample size was 24 patients (12 per group) based on power analysis for superiority design. Study conducted at University Hospital of Patras, Greece from September 2019 to March 2023.

title: Tirzepatide vs Insulin Lispro Added to Basal Insulin in Type 2 Diabetes: The SURPASS-6 Randomized Clinical Trial.

comparison: Dulaglutide 0.75 mg

Additional exclusions included HbA1c ≥6.5%, fasting glucose ≥126 mg/dL, body weight change >5 kg within 3 months before screening, prior bariatric surgery, eGFR <30 ml/min/1.73m², chronic pancreatitis, severe psychiatric disorders, lifetime history of suicide attempt, PHQ-9 score ≥15, uncontrolled hypertension, recent cardiovascular events, and use of weight-affecting medications.
intervention: Tirzepatide maximum tolerated dose (MTD, 10 or 15 mg) administered once weekly as subcutaneous injection for 72 weeks. Lifestyle counseling sessions occurred every 12 weeks focusing on healthy balanced diet with 500 kcal/day deficit and physical activity.

outcomes_primary: Per cent change in body weight from randomization to week 72; proportion of participants achieving ≥5% body weight reduction from randomization to week 72
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of participants achieving ≥10%, ≥15%, or ≥20% body weight reduction from randomization to week 72; proportion maintaining ≥80% of body weight loss achieved during lead-in period at week 72; change in waist circumference from randomization to week 72; change in absolute body weight and BMI; change in blood pressure, lipids, fasting glucose, HbA1c, and fasting insulin; SF-36v2 Physical Functioning domain score; IWQOL-Lite-CT Physical Function composite score; proportion achieving ≥25% body weight reduction (exploratory); treatment-emergent adverse events and serious adverse events
extraction_notes: Randomization was 1:1 and stratified by country, sex, and per cent weight reduction at end of lead-in (<10% vs ≥10%). Female enrollment was capped at 70%. The 12-week lead-in period with intensive lifestyle intervention (1,200-1,500 kcal/day diet, ≥150 min/week physical activity, eight counseling sessions) preceded randomization and only those achieving ≥5% weight loss were randomized.

title: Liraglutide treatment for the prevention of glucose tolerance deterioration in women with prior gestational diabetes mellitus: A 52-week randomized controlled clinical trial.

title: Inclusion of Oat Polar Lipids in a Solid Breakfast Improves Glucose Tolerance, Triglyceridemia, and Gut Hormone Responses Postprandially and after a Standardized Second Meal: A Randomized Crossover Study in Healthy Subjects.

title: Beneficial glycaemic effects of high-amylose barley bread compared to wheat bread in type 2 diabetes.

Abstract text appears truncated at results section ('changes in HbA |'). Specific doses and frequencies of iGlarLixi and SGLT2 inhibitors not specified. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in abstract.

title: Effect of inulin on breath hydrogen, postprandial glycemia, gut hormone release, and appetite perception in RYGB patients: a prospective, randomized, cross-over pilot study.

comparison: 300 ml orange juice containing equicaloric load of 15.5 g maltodextrin (MDX), consumed within 5 minutes after overnight fasting for at least 10 hours; same fixed portion snack at 180 minutes postprandially

title: Impact of exenatide on weight loss and eating behavior in adults with craniopharyngioma-related obesity: the CRANIOEXE randomized placebo-controlled trial.
population: Adults with craniopharyngioma-related obesity (body mass index > 30 kg/m²) without sign of recurrence of craniopharyngioma in the past year
intervention: Exenatide injected subcutaneously twice a day for 26 weeks
comparison: Placebo injected subcutaneously twice a day for 26 weeks
outcomes_primary: Mean change in body weight at week 26
outcomes_secondary: Eating behavior, calorie intake, energy expenditure, cardiovascular risk factors, metabolic risk factors, quality of life, tolerance profile
extraction_notes: Exenatide dose not specified in abstract. Combined with intensive lifestyle interventions (both groups).

title: Liraglutide for Lower Limb Perfusion in People With Type 2 Diabetes and Peripheral Artery Disease: The STARDUST Randomized Clinical Trial.

outcomes_secondary: Glycemic and metabolic parameters (HbA1c, weight, body mass index, systolic and diastolic blood pressure); lipid profile (total cholesterol, HDL and LDL cholesterol, triglycerides); C-reactive protein; kidney function parameters (urine albumin to creatinine ratio, estimated glomerular filtration rate); 6-minute walking test (exploratory outcome)
extraction_notes: Open-label randomized clinical trial; single-center study conducted in Italy; key exclusion criteria included contraindications to GLP-1RAs, acute coronary/cerebrovascular events within 14 days, plans for peripheral revascularization, eGFR below 15 mL/min/1.73 m2, neoplasms, and psychiatric disorders

title: Effect of Single Oral Coingestion of GABA and Malic Acid on Postprandial GLP-1, Glucose, and Insulin Responses in Healthy Volunteers: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Crossover Study.

outcomes_secondary: Postprandial blood glucose response; postprandial insulin response
extraction_notes: Crossover study design. Study also included in vitro experiments using murine STC-1 cell line which is not part of the human trial PICO extraction.

title: Jaboticaba peel improves postprandial glucose and inflammation: A randomized controlled trial in adults with metabolic syndrome.
population: Adults with metabolic syndrome
intervention: Jaboticaba peel (JP) powder supplement, 15 g/day, for 5 weeks
comparison: Matched placebo
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes assessed include: area under the curve of glucose, interleukin-6 (IL-6), anthropometry measurements, body composition, blood pressure, metabolic and inflammatory parameters (tumor necrosis factor-α, IL-1β, C-reactive protein), mixed-meal tolerance test, glucagon-like peptide-1, lipid metabolism, and insulin sensitivity and resistance indexes. title: Safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic modeling of cetagliptin in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
population: Chinese adults aged 18-65 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), newly diagnosed based on WHO 1999 criteria and treatment-naive, or diagnosed T2DM controlled by diet and exercise without hypoglycemic drugs in past 12 weeks; male weight ≥50.0 kg, female weight ≥45.0 kg; BMI 19.00-30.00 kg/m2; HbA1c 6.5% to <9%; fasting blood glucose <13.4 mmol/L; excluded if history of pancreatic injury, pancreatitis, significant diabetic complications, type 1 diabetes, gestational diabetes, special type diabetes, past severe hypoglycemic events, liver or kidney dysfunction, poor blood pressure or lipid control, or allergy to DPP-4 inhibitors

comparison: Placebo (matched to active drug) once daily for 14 days; Sitagliptin 100 mg (open-label positive control) orally once daily for 14 days

outcomes_secondary: Effects on glucose, insulin, C-peptide, and glucagon following oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT); fasting plasma glucose (FPG); 2-hour postprandial plasma glucose (2h PPG); glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c); glycated albumin (GA); population PK/PD model development
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the abstract or methods; classification inferred from study objectives. Randomization ratio was 10:2:4 (cetagliptin:placebo:sitagliptin) within each dose group. Sitagliptin was open-label while cetagliptin and placebo were double-blind.

title: Effects of Tirzepatide Versus Basal Insulins in People With Type 2 Diabetes and Different Baseline Glycemic Patterns: Post Hoc Analyses of the SURPASS-3 and SURPASS-4 Trials.

outcomes_primary: Change from baseline to week 52 in HbA1c
outcomes_secondary: Change from baseline to week 52 in fasting serum glucose (FSG), postprandial glucose (PPG), and body weight; hypoglycemia (blood glucose <54 mg/dL or severe); gastrointestinal-related treatment-emergent adverse events
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of two phase 3 trials (SURPASS-3 and SURPASS-4). Primary and secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated; outcomes listed are those assessed in the post hoc analysis. Treatment duration was 52 weeks in SURPASS-3 and ≥52 weeks in SURPASS-4.

title: Effects of Liraglutide, Empagliflozin and Their Combination on Left Atrial Strain and Arterial Function.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus treated with metformin, with poor glycemic control (HbA1c >7%), at high or very high cardiovascular risk (ten-year risk for cardiovascular event ≥5%). intervention: Liraglutide 1.8 mg subcutaneously once daily, or empagliflozin 25 mg orally once daily, or combination of liraglutide 1.8 mg subcutaneously once daily plus empagliflozin 25 mg orally once daily, all on top of metformin, for 6 months.
comparison: Basal insulin on top of metformin for 6 months (control group).

outcomes_secondary: Association of changes in arterial elastic properties (pulse wave velocity) with changes in left atrial strain; changes in left ventricular function (global longitudinal strain, E/e'); changes in central and brachial systolic blood pressure; changes in HbA1c.

title: Oral SSTR5 Antagonist SCO-240 for Growth Hormone Stimulation: A Phase I Single-Dose Study in Healthy Individuals.
population: Healthy Japanese and White individuals
intervention: SCO-240, an oral SSTR5 antagonist, ascending single oral doses
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics (gallbladder contractions, serum insulin levels, plasma glucagon-like peptide-1 levels)
outcomes_secondary: Levels of pituitary hormones (exploratory analysis)
extraction_notes: Specific doses, frequencies, and durations of SCO-240 not explicitly stated in the abstract. Study included both fed and fasted conditions as part of pharmacokinetic evaluation.

title: Colesevelam has no acute effect on postprandial GLP-1 levels but abolishes gallbladder refilling.
population: Individuals with type 2 diabetes
intervention: Single-dose oral colesevelam 3.75 g administered with mixed meal test, with or without intravenous infusion of GLP-1 receptor antagonist exendin(9-39)NH2

outcomes_secondary: Ultrasonography-assessed postprandial gallbladder motility (emptying and refilling), paracetamol absorption as proxy for gastric emptying, postprandial concentrations of glucose, C-peptide, cholecystokinin (CCK), fibroblast growth factor 19 (FGF19), and bile acids
extraction_notes: Primary outcomes inferred from hypothesis statement; distinction between primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly stated in abstract

title: Effect of vegetable consumption with chewing on postprandial glucose metabolism in healthy young men: a randomised controlled study.

comparison: Non-chewing trial: consumption of pureed cabbage (same ingredients as chewing trial - shredded cabbage, mineral water, pure lemon juice blended together) without chewing over 12 minutes, followed immediately by energy jelly (5.5 g/kg body mass) consumed in 3 minutes

extraction_notes: Randomized crossover design with at least 6 days washout between trials. Sample size of 19 participants.

title: Impact of the timing of metformin administration on glycaemic and glucagon-like peptide-1 responses to intraduodenal glucose infusion in type 2 diabetes: a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, crossover study.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes managed by stable dose of metformin monotherapy (500-2000 mg daily for at least 3 months). Exclusion criteria: significant gastrointestinal symptoms, impaired renal or liver function, history of gastrointestinal surgery, requirement for medication known to affect gastrointestinal function or appetite.
intervention: Metformin 1000 mg dissolved in 50 ml 0.9% saline administered as intraduodenal bolus infusion over 2 min at either t=-60 min, t=-30 min, or t=0 min before intraduodenal glucose infusion (12.56 kJ/min for 60 min). Saline placebo given at the other two timepoints on each metformin day.
comparison: 0.9% saline (50 ml) administered at t=-60, -30, and 0 min (control day with no metformin)
outcomes_primary: Plasma glucose levels and integrated area under the curve (iAUC) for plasma glucose between t=0 min and t=120 min in response to intraduodenal glucose infusion
outcomes_secondary: Plasma total GLP-1 levels and iAUC, plasma insulin levels and iAUC, insulin/glucose ratio, whole-body insulin sensitivity (Matsuda index), nausea and appetite sensations (visual analogue scales)
extraction_notes: This is a four-arm crossover study comparing three metformin timing conditions plus control. The study was originally powered to detect differences in small intestinal glucose absorption but endpoint was changed due to logistic challenges. Glucose and glucagon levels were not measured due to logistical issues.

title: Effect of liraglutide on thigh muscle fat and muscle composition in adults with overweight or obesity: Results from a randomized clinical trial.
journal: Journal of cachexia, sarcopenia and muscle
population: Adults aged ≥35 years without type 1 or type 2 diabetes with overweight or obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m² or BMI ≥27 kg/m² with metabolic syndrome); able to complete MRI body fat assessment; excluded if current or planned use of obesity therapy including GLP1RA, contraindication for GLP1RA use, high risk for serious adverse effect from GLP1RA, pregnancy, or breastfeeding

comparison: Matching placebo subcutaneous injection once daily for 40 weeks plus identical lifestyle intervention
outcomes_primary: Percent change in thigh muscle fat over 40 weeks assessed by MRI
outcomes_secondary: Muscle volume; muscle volume z-score; adverse muscle composition (defined as high thigh muscle fat >75th percentile for sex plus low thigh muscle volume z-score <-0.68); association between changes in thigh muscle fat and changes in body weight

title: Dual glucagon-like peptide-1 and glucagon receptor agonism reduces energy intake in type 2 diabetes with obesity.
population: Overweight and obese adults with type 2 diabetes
intervention: Cotadutide (GLP-1/glucagon receptor dual agonist), 100-300 μg daily, subcutaneous, 42 days, following a 16-day single-blind placebo run-in
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Percentage weight change
outcomes_secondary: Change in energy intake (EI); change in energy expenditure (EE) assessed by doubly labelled water and indirect calorimetry
extraction_notes: Randomization ratio was 2:1 (cotadutide:placebo). Study was phase 2a, single-centre, double-blind after run-in period.

title: Long-acting exenatide does not prevent cognitive decline in mild cognitive impairment: a proof-of-concept clinical trial.
population: Patients aged 50-80 years with Caucasian ethnicity, stable medications for past 3 months, and diagnosis of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) according to Petersen Clinical Criteria with Mini-Mental State Examination corrected scores from 24 to 27. Exclusion criteria included BMI ≤22 kg/m2, diagnosis of diabetes according to ADA criteria, significant neurologic disease other than MCI, clinically significant liver or kidney dysfunction, endocrine diseases other than well controlled hypothyroidism, personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN syndrome, severe gastrointestinal diseases, current or history of chronic or acute pancreatitis, current or history of cancer within last 5 years, current clinically significant psychiatric disorder, contraindication to exenatide, warfarin treatment. All eligible women were post-menopausal.

comparison: No active treatment
outcomes_primary: Change in ADAS-Cog11 (Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale, 11 items) cognitive test score at 32 weeks versus baseline
outcomes_secondary: Change in ADAS-Cog at 16 weeks versus baseline; absolute change in metabolic parameters (fasting glycemia, HbA1c) and hormone levels; neuropsychological evaluations including Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), quality score of MMSE, Phonemic verbal fluency test, Semantic verbal fluency test, Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS), Clinical Dementia Rating Scale (CDR), Neuropsychiatric Inventory (NPI), Activities of Daily Living (ADL), Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADL) at 16 and 32 weeks compared to baseline; plasma readouts of GLP-1 receptor engagement (insulin, C-peptide, glucagon, active GLP-1, total GIP)
extraction_notes: Open-label randomized controlled trial with 1:1 allocation. Analysis was intention-to-treat. Study was underpowered (target n=40, enrolled n=32). High dropout rate in treatment arm (35%) due to gastrointestinal adverse effects.

title: Glucose-regulatory hormones and growth in very preterm infants fed fortified human milk.
population: Very preterm infants (gestational age 26+0 to 30+6 weeks) with enteral intakes >100 mL/kg/d at start of fortification, clinical condition requiring fortification according to local guidelines (e.g. blood urea nitrogen <5 mmol/L), no major congenital anomalies or gastrointestinal surgery, and no formula received prior to enrollment

comparison: Conventional fortifier (CF) (PreNan FM85 powder, bovine milk-based) added to human milk, starting at 1.0 g/100 mL and increasing to maximum 4.0 g/100 mL within 3-4 days, administered every 2-3 hours, continued until 34+6 weeks postmenstrual age
outcomes_primary: Feasibility and safety of bovine colostrum fortifier, aiming to achieve similar growth rates and morbidities (e.g. necrotizing enterocolitis, late-onset sepsis) between groups
outcomes_secondary: Plasma concentrations of glucose-regulatory hormones (IGF-1, GLP-1, C-peptide, GIP, glucagon, insulin, leptin, pancreatic polypeptide) measured before fortification and at 7±3 and 14±3 days after start of fortification; glucose concentrations; HOMA2 index; QUICKI index; associations between hormone concentrations and fortification type, birth weight (AGA/SGA), milk intake, postnatal age, and growth (ΔZ-scores for weight, length, head circumference from birth to 35 weeks postmenstrual age)
extraction_notes: This is a secondary analysis of the FortiColos trial (NCT03537365). Primary outcomes listed are from the original trial; the current study focused on hormone concentrations and their associations with growth. Blood sample availability varied across timepoints due to strict volume limitations.

title: Semaglutide in Patients with Obesity-Related Heart Failure and Type 2 Diabetes.

comparison: Placebo for 52 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire clinical summary score (KCCQ-CSS); change in body weight
outcomes_secondary: Change in 6-minute walk distance; hierarchical composite end point including death, heart failure events, and differences in change in KCCQ-CSS and 6-minute walk distance; change in C-reactive protein (CRP) level

title: Trial of Lixisenatide in Early Parkinson's Disease.

title: Semaglutide versus placebo in people with obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: a pooled analysis of the STEP-HFpEF and STEP-HFpEF DM randomised trials.
population: Adults aged 18 years or older with obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (LVEF ≥45%), BMI ≥30 kg/m², New York Heart Association class II-IV symptoms, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score <90 points, 6-minute walk distance ≥100 m, and evidence of elevated left ventricular filling pressures, increased natriuretic peptide concentrations with echocardiographic abnormalities, or heart failure hospitalization within 12 months with ongoing diuretic treatment or echocardiographic abnormalities. STEP-HFpEF excluded people with diabetes or HbA1c ≥6.5%; STEP-HFpEF DM required type 2 diabetes diagnosis at least 90 days before screening with HbA1c ≤10%. Key exclusions: bodyweight change >5 kg within 90 days, type 1 diabetes, GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment within 90 days

outcomes_secondary: Change from baseline to week 52 in 6-minute walk distance; hierarchical composite endpoint comprising all-cause mortality, number and timing of heart failure events (adjudicated hospitalization for heart failure or urgent hospital visit requiring intravenous therapy), differences in KCCQ-CSS change of at least 15, 10, or 5 points, and difference of at least 30 m in 6-minute walk distance change; change in C-reactive protein concentrations from baseline to week 52
extraction_notes: This is a prespecified pooled analysis of individual patient data from STEP-HFpEF and STEP-HFpEF DM trials. Additional exploratory endpoints included NT-proBNP change, time to first heart failure event, time to cardiovascular death or first heart failure event, and time to cardiovascular death or total heart failure events

title: Substituting Carbohydrate at Lunch for Added Protein Increases Fat Oxidation During Subsequent Exercise in Healthy Males.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
population: Healthy males aged 18-40 years, recreationally active (1-10 hours per week), with stable body weight for 6 months prior to study. Exclusions: current smokers, clinically restrained/disinhibited/hungry eaters, severe dislike or intolerance of study foods, undergoing structured diet/exercise intervention for weight loss, history of gastric/digestive/cardiovascular/renal disease, taking medication affecting glucose/lipid metabolism or appetite, consuming >14 units alcohol per week.
intervention: LO-CARB: Lunch meal (35-40% estimated energy requirements, 1186 ± 140 kcal) containing 0.2 g/kg body mass carbohydrate and approximately 2 g/kg body mass protein, consumed at approximately 13:15, followed by 1 hour cycling at approximately 60% VO2peak at approximately 16:15 (3 hours post-lunch).

outcomes_primary: Fat oxidation during exercise (total grams oxidized during 1-hour cycling bout).
outcomes_secondary: Carbohydrate oxidation during exercise; energy expenditure; ad libitum dinner energy intake; snack energy intake; cumulative daily energy intake; substrate oxidation rates at rest; plasma concentrations of glucose, insulin, nonesterified fatty acids (NEFA), glycerol, peptide YY (PYY), glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1), and acylated ghrelin; subjective appetite sensations (hunger, fullness, desire to eat, prospective food consumption, nausea); pre-exercise subjective responses (motivation, readiness, tiredness, energy, positive/negative affect); exercise enjoyment; rating of perceived exertion; heart rate during exercise; meal perception ratings.
extraction_notes: Randomized crossover design with 3 conditions. Sample size of 12 completing participants. Participants served as their own controls. Primary outcome not explicitly labeled but fat oxidation during exercise appears to be the main metabolic outcome based on power calculation and study aims.

title: Early-Onset Type 2 Diabetes and Tirzepatide Treatment: A Post Hoc Analysis From the SURPASS Clinical Trial Program.
population: Adults aged ≥18 years with type 2 diabetes (HbA1c ≥7.0% to ≤10.5% at screening), BMI ≥23 kg/m2, on various oral background medications (metformin with or without SGLT2 inhibitors, or no background antihyperglycemic therapy); categorized as early-onset T2D (diagnosis at <40 years of age) versus later-onset T2D (diagnosis at ≥40 years of age); participants from SURPASS-1, SURPASS-2, and SURPASS-3 trials
intervention: Tirzepatide 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg administered once weekly subcutaneously for 40 weeks (SURPASS-1, SURPASS-2) or 52 weeks (SURPASS-3)

outcomes_primary: Change from baseline in HbA1c, body weight, and cardiometabolic markers including waist circumference, lipids (triglycerides, HDL-cholesterol), and blood pressure at week 40 or week 52
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of participants reaching HbA1c targets <7.0% and <5.7%; change from baseline in fasting serum glucose, eGFR, and HOMA2-IR; treatment-emergent adverse events; serious adverse events; study and treatment discontinuation rates
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of pooled data from three SURPASS trials (SURPASS-1, SURPASS-2, SURPASS-3). Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly labeled as such in the publication; outcomes listed are described as main outcomes of interest and additional outcomes. title: Tirzepatide and exercise training in obesity.

comparison: Placebo; Tirzepatide 5 mg alone; Tirzepatide 2.5 mg alone; Exercise training plus placebo; Exercise training plus Tirzepatide 5 mg; Exercise training plus Tirzepatide 2.5 mg (six groups total)
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished. Outcomes measured included: anthropometric measures (body weight, BMI, waist circumference, waist to hip ratio, fat mass), cardiorespiratory fitness (VO2max), muscle strength (chest press 1RM, leg press 1RM), and blood biochemistry (triglyceride, total cholesterol, LDL-C, HDL-C, fasting blood glucose, insulin level, HOMA-IR)

title: A pharmacokinetic study comparing the biosimilar HEC14028 and Dulaglutide (Trulicity®) in healthy Chinese subjects.
population: Healthy male Chinese adults aged 18-45 years with weight ≥50 kg and BMI 19.0-28.0 kg/m². Exclusion criteria included gastrointestinal, kidney, liver, nerve, blood, endocrine, tumor, lung, immune, mental or cardiovascular diseases; medical history or family history of medullary thyroid cancer or type 2 multiple endocrine neoplasia syndrome; history of pancreatitis, habitual constipation or intestinal obstruction; clinically significant drug allergy history; positive hepatitis B, hepatitis C, HIV, or syphilis tests; live attenuated vaccine within 3 months or inactivated vaccine within 1 month before screening; previous use of dulaglutide or any GLP-1 analog.

outcomes_secondary: Area under the blood concentration-time curve from zero time to last measurable concentration time (AUC0-t), time to maximum plasma concentration (Tmax), elimination half-life time (t1/2), apparent clearance (CL/F), apparent volume of distribution based on terminal phase (Vd/F), elimination rate constant (λz), immunogenicity (anti-drug antibodies and neutralizing antibodies), safety (adverse events, vital signs, 12-lead ECG, physical examination, laboratory tests, blood glucose, injection site evaluation)

title: Efficacy and Safety of Liraglutide in Patients With an Ileal Pouch-Anal Anastomosis and Chronic High Bowel Frequency: A Placebo-Controlled, Crossover, Proof-of-Concept Study.
population: Patients with ileal pouch-anal anastomosis (IPAA) with chronic high bowel frequency (>8 bowel movements per day average over 7-day screening period) refractory to antimotility agents, with high bowel frequency for more than 4 weeks despite use of antimotility agents. Exclusion criteria: endoscopic pouchitis disease activity index ≥4, treatment-refractory pouch strictures, or positive Clostridioides difficile assay.
intervention: Liraglutide (GLP-1 receptor agonist), daily administration, with dose escalation over treatment periods (specific dose not stated in text)
comparison: Placebo (crossover design - patients received both liraglutide and placebo in randomized sequence)
outcomes_primary: 30% reduction of bowel frequency at week 4 or 10 compared with baseline
outcomes_secondary: Reduction of bowel frequency at week 6 or 12; tolerability and safety of liraglutide; stool calprotectin concentrations
extraction_notes: Specific dose of liraglutide not stated in available text. Study terminated early after 8 of 10 planned patients due to interruption in placebo drug supply manufacturing. comparison: Matching placebo subcutaneous injection once weekly with identical dose escalation schedule
outcomes_primary: Major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE) defined as composite of cardiovascular mortality, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke (time to first event)

Recurrent event analyses for heart failure hospitalization/urgent visit, fatal/nonfatal myocardial infarction, fatal/nonfatal stroke, hospitalization for unstable angina, and coronary revascularization.
extraction_notes: This is a prespecified subgroup analysis of the SELECT trial examining cardiovascular outcomes by baseline HbA1c categories and change in HbA1c. The primary SELECT trial results were previously published; this paper reports subgroup analyses.

title: Tirzepatide for the Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Obesity.

comparison: Placebo (matched subcutaneous injection, once weekly for 52 weeks) plus lifestyle counseling
outcomes_primary: Change in apnea-hypopnea index (AHI, number of apneas and hypopneas per hour of sleep) from baseline to week 52
outcomes_secondary: Percent change in AHI; percentage of participants with AHI reduction ≥50%; percentage of participants with AHI <5 events/hour or AHI 5-14 events/hour with Epworth Sleepiness Scale score ≤10; percent change in body weight; change in high-sensitivity C-reactive protein concentration; change in sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden; change in PROMIS Short Form Sleep-related Impairment 8a scores; change in PROMIS Short Form Sleep Disturbance 8b scores; change in systolic blood pressure (assessed at week 48)
extraction_notes: Two parallel trials under one master protocol (SURMOUNT-OSA): Trial 1 enrolled PAP-naive/non-users, Trial 2 enrolled current PAP users. Blood pressure assessed at week 48 rather than week 52 to prevent PAP washout confounding in Trial 2.

title: Efficacy and safety of oral semaglutide vs sitagliptin in a predominantly Chinese population with type 2 diabetes uncontrolled with metformin: PIONEER 12, a double-blind, Phase IIIa, randomised trial.

extraction_notes: Four-arm trial with three oral semaglutide dose groups compared to one sitagliptin group. Double-blind, double-dummy design. Randomization stratified by China region vs elsewhere.

outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 26

extraction_notes: Randomisation criterion for HbA1c at visit 3 was 53-80 mmol/mol (7.0-9.5%), slightly different from screening criterion. Two estimands defined: trial product estimand (primary) and treatment policy estimand (secondary).

title: Pharmacokinetic Properties of a Once-Weekly Fixed-Ratio Combination of Insulin Icodec and Semaglutide Compared with Separate Administration of Each Component in Individuals with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.

outcomes_primary: Change in sperm parameters: semen volume, sperm concentration, total sperm number, total motility, morphologically normal sperm

title: Postprandial Effects of Four Test Meals Containing Wholegrain Rye or Refined Wheat Foods on Circulating Incretins, Ghrelin, Glucose, and Inflammatory Markers.

On third intervention day, participants were randomly assigned 50:50 to either rye or wheat diet with continuous blood sampling. Study reports this paper focuses on secondary objectives; primary aim was to evaluate self-reported appetite.

title: Weight Loss Induces Changes in Vitamin D Status in Women With Obesity But Not in Men: A Randomized Clinical Trial.

title: Glycemia reduction in type 2 diabetes-Hypoglycemia outcomes: A randomized clinical trial.

title: Effects of tirzepatide on circulatory overload and end-organ damage in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and obesity: a secondary analysis of the SUMMIT trial.

The primary trial endpoints (cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure) are reported separately. Estimated blood volume and plasma volume analyses, and regression analyses exploring correlations, were post hoc and not prespecified.

title: Tirzepatide for Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction and Obesity.

title: Effects of Tirzepatide on the Clinical Trajectory of Patients With Heart Failure, Preserved Ejection Fraction, and Obesity.
population: Adults ≥40 years of age with chronic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF; NYHA class II to IV, left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50%), body mass index ≥30 kg/m², 6-minute walk distance 100 to 425 m, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score ≤80, and objective evidence of heart failure (elevated NT-proBNP [≥200 pg/mL in sinus rhythm or ≥600 pg/mL in atrial fibrillation], structural heart disease defined by left atrial enlargement, or elevated filling pressures). intervention: Tirzepatide 2.5 mg subcutaneously weekly, titrated by 2.5 mg every 4 weeks as tolerated to a target dose of 15 mg weekly after 20 weeks, added to background heart failure therapy
comparison: Matching placebo subcutaneously weekly with identical titration schedule, added to background heart failure therapy
outcomes_primary: Composite of time to first cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure event; change in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score at 52 weeks

extraction_notes: Worsening heart failure event defined as exacerbation of symptoms requiring hospitalization, intravenous drugs for heart failure in urgent care setting, or intensification of oral diuretics (oral diuretic intensification without worsening symptoms not counted). Median follow-up 104 weeks. Alpha split between primary endpoints (0.04 for composite events, 0.01 for KCCQ-CSS). Study is SUMMIT trial (NCT04847557).

title: Gastrointestinal hormones and subjective ratings of appetite after low-carbohydrate vs low-fat low-energy diets in females with lipedema - A randomized controlled trial.

outcomes_secondary: Changes in satiety hormones (peptide YY, cholecystokinin, glucagon-like peptide 1) in fasting and postprandial states; subjective ratings of appetite

title: Tirzepatide Reduces LV Mass and Paracardiac Adipose Tissue in Obesity-Related Heart Failure: SUMMIT CMR Substudy.
