extraction_notes: Study duration was 52 weeks. Initial enrollment was 175 patients but only 106 completed CMR with adequate image quality for analysis (50 in treatment group, 56 in placebo group).

title: Osteoprotegerin, Osteopontin, and Osteocalcin Are Associated With Cardiovascular Events in Type 2 Diabetes: Insights From EXSCEL.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes enrolled in the EXSCEL trial
intervention: Once-weekly exenatide
comparison: Not explicitly stated in abstract (implied placebo/control from trial design)
outcomes_primary: First occurrence of major cardiovascular events (MACE): composite of cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke
outcomes_secondary: All-cause death, cardiovascular death, association of bone metabolism biomarkers (osteoprotegerin, osteopontin, sclerostin, osteocalcin) with cardiovascular events
extraction_notes: This is a secondary analysis of biomarker associations within the EXSCEL trial rather than a primary comparison of exenatide vs comparator. The abstract focuses on biomarker-outcome associations rather than treatment effect comparisons. Comparator arm not explicitly named in abstract.

title: Differential effects of imeglimin and metformin on insulin and incretin secretion-An exploratory randomized controlled trial.
population: Japanese patients with type 2 diabetes, aged 18-75 years, drug-naïve or on a single oral hypoglycaemic agent (sulfonylurea, glinide, alpha-glucosidase inhibitor, DPP-4 inhibitor, pioglitazone, or SGLT2 inhibitor), HbA1c 7.0-9.0% (drug-naïve) or 6.0-8.0% (on single OHA), BMI 18-35 kg/m2, Hb >12.5 g/dL (males) or >12.0 g/dL (females). Exclusions: renal dysfunction (eGFR <45 mL/min/1.73 m2), prior metformin/imeglimin/insulin/GLP-1 receptor agonist use, hepatic dysfunction (AST/ALT/γ-GTP >3x upper limit of normal), heart failure with SGLT2 inhibitor use, severe retinopathy, history of gastrointestinal surgery, malignancy within 5 years, severe infection/perioperative/severe trauma, excessive alcohol consumption

comparison: Metformin 250 mg orally twice daily initially, raised to 500 mg twice daily (1000 mg/day) for 24 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline to 12 and 24 weeks in each group
outcomes_secondary: Change in blood glucose, insulin, C-peptide, glucagon, total GLP-1, active GLP-1, total GIP, and active GIP during OGTT from baseline to 12 and 24 weeks; changes in insulinogenic index, HOMA-IR, and HOMA-β from baseline to 12 and 24 weeks; comparison of changes in primary and secondary endpoints between imeglimin and metformin groups
extraction_notes: 8-week washout period for patients previously on single OHA before randomization. Open-label design. Metformin dose (1000 mg/day) described as commonly used dose in Japan but lower than maximum dose.

title: Liraglutide and Colesevelam Change Serum and Fecal Bile Acid Levels in a Randomized Trial With Patients With Bile Acid Diarrhea.

comparison: Colesevelam 1,875 mg orally twice daily for 6 weeks
outcomes_primary: Changes in serum and fecal concentrations of individual bile acids; fecal microbiome composition
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly specified as separate from primary outcomes in this secondary endpoint analysis
extraction_notes: This report describes predefined secondary endpoints from a previously published head-to-head comparison trial. The primary endpoint of the original trial was reduction in number of daily bowel movements. Sample size n=52 (n=26 per group). Run-in period of at least 1 week with no BAD treatment before randomization.

title: Albiglutide and atrial fibrillation in patients with Type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease: insights from the Harmony Outcomes trial.
population: Patients aged >40 years with Type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease
intervention: Albiglutide, a glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Composite of major adverse cardiac events (MACE): non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, and cardiovascular death
outcomes_secondary: Atrial fibrillation and flutter (AF) events during follow-up; cardiovascular effects in patients with and without AF history
extraction_notes: This is a secondary analysis of the Harmony Outcomes trial focusing on AF-related outcomes. Dose, route, frequency, and duration of albiglutide not specified in abstract. Follow-up duration mentioned as 1.6 years.

title: Similar weight loss with semaglutide regardless of diabetes and cardiometabolic risk parameters in individuals with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease: Post hoc analysis of three randomised controlled trials.
population: Adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) confirmed by magnetic resonance imaging or biopsy-proven metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) with fibrosis stage F1-F4, including those with type 2 diabetes, pre-type 2 diabetes, or no diabetes

comparison: Placebo (subcutaneous)

outcomes_secondary: Weight changes analyzed by type 2 diabetes status; correlations between weight change and cardiometabolic risk parameters (fasting plasma glucose, glycated haemoglobin, C-peptide, fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, diabetes duration, lipid concentrations including triglycerides, low-density lipoprotein, high-density lipoprotein)
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis pooling data from three randomised controlled trials (NCT03357380, NCT02970942, NCT03987451). Weight change was a secondary endpoint in the original trials. The primary endpoints of the original trials related to liver outcomes were not the focus of this analysis.

title: Regulation of proglucagon derived peptides by carbohydrate and protein ingestion in young healthy males-A randomized, double-blind, cross-over trial.

comparison: Carbohydrate-rich breakfast consisting of 125 g of glucose
outcomes_primary: Levels of seven proglucagon-derived peptides (PGDPs): glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), glucagon-like peptide-2 (GLP-2), oxyntomodulin, glicentin, major pro-glucagon fragment (MPGF), glucagon, and proglucagon; glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide/gastric inhibitory polypeptide total and total plus (GIP total and GIP total plus) levels measured at baseline, every 15 minutes for the first hour, and every 30 minutes for the second and third hours after each meal
outcomes_secondary: Glycemic responses; insulinemic responses; total amino acids levels
extraction_notes: No explicit distinction between primary and secondary outcomes stated in the abstract; classification based on study aims. Study design is randomized, double-blind, crossover.

title: Impaired postprandial GLP-2 response enhances endotoxemia, systemic inflammation, and kidney injury in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH): effect of phospholipid curcumin meriva.
population: Adults with biopsy-proven metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), stratified for baseline diabetes, liver fibrosis stage (F0-2 vs F3-4), chronic kidney disease (presence/absence), and obesity status; plus age-, gender-, BMI-, and diabetes-matched controls without liver or kidney disease
intervention: Phospholipid curcumin formulation Meriva 2 g/day orally for 72 weeks
comparison: Placebo for 72 weeks
outcomes_primary: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) presence and regression defined according to KDIGO guidelines as sustained eGFR ≥90 mL/min/1.73 m2 and normalization of albumin excretion rate (<30 mg/d), documented on 2 occasions at least 3 months apart
outcomes_secondary: Change in absolute values and KDIGO categories of eGFR and albumin excretion rate (AER); postprandial response of incretins (GLP-1, GIP), GLP-2, zonulin, lipopolysaccharide (LPS), FGF-21, adiponectin, MCP-1, and NF-kB activation in circulating mononuclear cells during standardized 8-hour oral mixed tolerance test
extraction_notes: This is a secondary analysis from a multicenter randomized trial. Control group (n=26) was not randomized but matched for comparison purposes. Full trial protocol and patient eligibility criteria referenced as being detailed elsewhere in supplementary material.

title: Combined training and hormones/enzymes with insulinotropic actions in individuals with overweight and type 2 diabetes mellitus: A randomized controlled trial.
population: Adults aged 40-60 years with previously diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus and overweight (BMI 25-35 kg/m2), sedentary lifestyle, not having performed training and diet in the last 12 months, both sexes. Exclusion criteria: cardiac arrhythmia, cardiac ischemia, coronary artery disease, severe arterial hypertension, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, anemia, uncontrolled hypothyroidism, limiting bone-joint diseases, severe specific complications of T2DM, use of exogenous insulin, thiazolidinediones, beta-blockers, anticoagulants, anti-inflammatories, or any medication that could interfere with physiological responses to tests or training.
intervention: Combined training (CT) consisting of strength training (3 sets of 10-12 submaximal repetitions at approximately 50-75% of 1RM, 1 to 1 min 15 s interval) followed by aerobic training (35 min at 50-70% of VO2max) in the same session, performed 3 times per week for 16 weeks.
comparison: Control group with no training protocol, followed up monthly by telephone during the experimental period.
outcomes_primary: Concentrations of hormones/enzymes with insulinotropic actions: GLP-1, GIP, DPP-4, amylin/IAPP, and IDE.
outcomes_secondary: Functional variables, body composition, clinical markers (insulin, C peptide, glucose, HbA1c, triglycerides, total cholesterol, HDL, VLDL, LDL, HOMA-IR, HOMA-Beta), resting metabolic rate, resting heart rate, blood pressure, VO2max, 1RM leg press, 1RM bench press.
extraction_notes: This paper reports secondary results from a registered randomized controlled trial (UTN: U1111-1202-1476). Primary results were previously published. The primary versus secondary outcome designation is inferred from the study's stated aim focusing on hormones/enzymes with insulinotropic actions.

title: Metabolic and Hormonal Responses to Isomaltulose Ingestion Before or During Sustained Submaximal Exercise in Adults with Type 1 Diabetes Using Automated Insulin Delivery Systems.
population: Adults aged 18-75 years with type 1 diabetes for ≥2 years, HbA1c ≥7.5% (58 mmol/mol), using insulin pump treatment for ≥12 months, using continuous or intermittently scanned glucose monitoring system for ≥6 months, using insulin aspart for ≥1 week, treated with MiniMed 780G automated insulin delivery system for >4 weeks
intervention: Isomaltulose 0.75g carbohydrate per kg body mass given as three separate isocaloric servings (0.25g carbohydrate per kg body mass each) as 10% concentration mixed with water, administered immediately before exercise, at mid-point of exercise (t=+20 min), and toward end of exercise (t=+40 min), without bolus insulin, during 45 minutes of cycling at 60% VO2peak (DEC condition)
comparison: Isomaltulose 0.75g carbohydrate per kg body mass given as single serving as 10% concentration mixed with water, administered 90 minutes before 45 minutes of cycling at 60% VO2peak, with 25% reduction in usual meal time bolus insulin dose (PEC condition)
outcomes_primary: Plasma glucose concentrations and exercise-induced change in plasma glucose; glucoregulatory hormone responses including gut incretins (GLP-1 and GIP), pancreatic glucagon, and exogenous insulin concentrations
outcomes_secondary: Whole-body fuel oxidation rates (carbohydrate and lipid oxidation); plasma lactate concentrations; time in glycemic ranges (time below range <3.9 mmol/L, time in range 3.9-10.0 mmol/L, time above range >10.0 mmol/L); respiratory exchange ratio
extraction_notes: Randomized crossover trial with n=8 participants; this study was a sub-analysis of a larger randomized crossover clinical trial (NCT05133765); small sample size acknowledged as limitation

title: Dose-related effects of intraduodenal quinine on plasma glucose, glucoregulatory hormones and gastric emptying of a nutrient drink, and energy intake, in men with type 2 diabetes: a double-blind, randomised, crossover study.

intervention: Intraduodenal quinine hydrochloride (QHCl) at doses of 300 mg and 600 mg
comparison: Placebo (implied by double-blind, randomised, crossover design)

outcomes_secondary: Energy intake
extraction_notes: Abstract mentions HbA1c and age characteristics but text appears truncated. Specific timing, frequency, and duration of quinine administration not explicitly stated. Control/placebo condition implied by crossover design but not explicitly described in abstract.

title: Glepaglutide, a Long-Acting Glucagon-like Peptide-2 Analogue, Reduces Parenteral Support in Patients With Short Bowel Syndrome: A Phase 3 Randomized Controlled Trial.

extraction_notes: Route of administration not explicitly stated in abstract. Three-arm trial with 1:1:1 randomization.

title: Safety and efficacy of GLP-1/FGF21 dual agonist HEC88473 in MASLD and T2DM: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study.
population: Patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) combined with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM)
intervention: HEC88473 (GLP-1/FGF21 dual agonist) at doses of 5.1, 15.3, 30.6, 45.9, or 68.0 mg via weekly subcutaneous injection for 5 weeks
comparison: Placebo via weekly subcutaneous injection for 5 weeks (randomization ratio 10:2 HEC88473:placebo)
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified as primary outcome
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly specified as secondary outcomes; outcomes assessed included: MRI-proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF), HbA1c (glycated hemoglobin), fasting glucose levels, postprandial glucose levels, lipid profiles, safety and adverse events
extraction_notes: Phase Ib/IIa multiple-ascending-dose trial with 60 patients randomized. The abstract does not explicitly distinguish between primary and secondary outcomes. Trial registration: CTR20211088 and NCT05943886.

title: Determinants of Liraglutide Treatment Discontinuation in Type 1 Diabetes: A Post Hoc Analysis of ADJUNCT ONE and ADJUNCT TWO Randomized Placebo-Controlled Clinical Studies.

population: Participants with type 1 diabetes receiving insulin therapy
intervention: Liraglutide as adjunct to insulin therapy at doses of 1.8 mg, 1.2 mg, or 0.6 mg
comparison: Placebo
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of two phase 3 RCTs (ADJUNCT ONE NCT01836523 and ADJUNCT TWO NCT02098395) focused on determinants of treatment discontinuation. Primary and secondary outcomes of the original trials are not specified in this abstract. The outcomes analyzed in this post hoc analysis include treatment discontinuation rates due to adverse events/lack of tolerance, baseline characteristics comparison between completers and non-completers, and adverse event rates.

title: Tirzepatide Associated With Reduced Albuminuria in Participants With Type 2 Diabetes: Pooled Post Hoc Analysis From the Randomized Active- and Placebo-Controlled SURPASS-1-5 Clinical Trials.
population: Adults aged ≥18 years with type 2 diabetes; HbA1c 7.0-10.5% (varying by trial); BMI ≥23 or ≥25 kg/m² (varying by trial); stable weight in 3 months prior to enrollment; excluded: type 1 diabetes, history of pancreatitis, proliferative diabetic retinopathy, diabetic maculopathy, nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy requiring treatment, eGFR <30 or <45 mL/min/1.73 m² (varying by trial)
intervention: Tirzepatide 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg administered as weekly subcutaneous injections for 40-52 weeks
comparison: Placebo (SURPASS-1 and SURPASS-5); Semaglutide 1 mg once weekly (SURPASS-2); Insulin degludec daily (SURPASS-3); Insulin glargine (SURPASS-4 and SURPASS-5)
outcomes_primary: Percent change in urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR) from baseline to week 40 or week 42
outcomes_secondary: Change in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) over time measured at week 40/42; subgroup analyses by baseline UACR ≥30 mg/g, eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m², SGLT2i use, and RASi use; mediation analysis exploring effects of HbA1c and body weight changes on UACR
extraction_notes: This is a pooled post hoc analysis of five randomized trials (SURPASS-1 through SURPASS-5). The trials had varying designs: SURPASS-2, -3, and -4 were open-label while SURPASS-1 and -5 were double-blind. Randomization ratios varied (1:1:1:1 in most trials, 1:1:1:3 in SURPASS-4). UACR was not a prespecified primary outcome in the original trials.

title: Effect of semaglutide 2.4 mg on use of antihypertensive and lipid-lowering treatment in five randomized controlled STEP trials.
population: Adults aged ≥18 years with overweight or obesity with or without type 2 diabetes from STEP 1, 2, 3, 6, and 8 clinical trials. intervention: Semaglutide 2.4 mg subcutaneous injection (dose escalation to 2.4 mg) for 68 weeks with behavioral and lifestyle intervention
comparison: Placebo with behavioral and lifestyle intervention
outcomes_primary: Changes in antihypertensive or lipid-lowering treatment regimens from randomization to week 68, including treatment intensity increase (dose escalation or addition of medication), treatment intensity decrease (dose reduction or discontinuation), and discontinuation of all antihypertensive or lipid-lowering medications
outcomes_secondary: Systolic and diastolic blood pressure, lipid levels, hypertension remission (defined as BP <140/90 mm Hg without antihypertensive medications), changes in body weight from randomization to week 68, initiation of antihypertensive or lipid-lowering medications in participants not on these medications at randomization
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis pooling data from five STEP trials. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly labeled in text; outcomes listed are those assessed in the post hoc analysis. Participants treated with semaglutide 1.7 mg in STEP 6 or liraglutide 3.0 mg in STEP 8 were excluded.

title: Effects of Metformin on Postprandial Blood Pressure, Heart Rate, Gastric Emptying, GLP-1, and Prevalence of Postprandial Hypotension in Type 2 Diabetes: A Double-Blind Placebo-Controlled Crossover Study.

intervention: Metformin (dose, route, frequency, and duration not specified)

outcomes_primary: Postprandial blood pressure, postprandial hypotension (PPH) events
outcomes_secondary: Heart rate, glucose, insulin, glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1), gastric emptying
extraction_notes: Abstract does not specify metformin dose, route, frequency, or treatment duration. Study design is double-blind placebo-controlled crossover. Primary vs secondary outcome distinction is inferred from abstract emphasis; not explicitly stated.

title: Greater improvement in insulin sensitivity per unit weight loss associated with tirzepatide versus semaglutide: An exploratory analysis.

outcomes_primary: Relationship between change in body weight and change in insulin sensitivity determined from hyperinsulinemic euglycemic clamp (M value)
outcomes_secondary: Insulin sensitivity assessed by Matsuda index from mixed-meal tolerance testing; relationship between change in fat mass and change in insulin sensitivity
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc exploratory analysis of a 28-week double-blind randomized trial. Route and frequency of drug administration not specified in abstract. Primary and secondary outcome designations inferred from analysis structure as explicit designations not provided.

title: evoke and evoke+: design of two large-scale, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 studies evaluating efficacy, safety, and tolerability of semaglutide in early-stage symptomatic Alzheimer's disease.
population: Men or women aged 55–85 years with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) or mild dementia due to Alzheimer's disease with confirmed amyloid abnormalities (assessed by positron emission tomography or cerebrospinal fluid analysis); MCI defined as CDR global score of 0.5 with CDR domain score ≥0.5 in at least one of three activities of daily living categories; mild AD dementia defined as CDR global score of 1.0; RBANS delayed memory index score ≤85; MMSE score ≥22; evoke+ allows participants with significant small vessel pathology (defined as >1 lacunar infarct and/or age-related white matter changes >2)
intervention: Once-daily oral semaglutide with 8-week dose escalation regimen: 3 mg (weeks 0–4), 7 mg (weeks 4–8), 14 mg (weeks 8–156); total treatment duration 156 weeks (104-week main treatment phase and 52-week extension)
comparison: Matching placebo
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline to week 104 in Clinical Dementia Rating – Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) score
outcomes_secondary: Confirmatory secondary: Change from baseline to week 104 in AD Cooperative Study Activities of Daily Living – MCI (ADCS-ADL-MCI) score; time to progression to CDR global score ≥1.0 among participants with CDR global score 0.5 at baseline. Supportive secondary: Change in MMSE score; change in MoCA score; change in ADAS-Cog-13 score; change in ADCOMS score; change in NPI score; time to progression in disease stage based on global CDR score; number of treatment-emergent adverse events; change in high-sensitivity CRP level; time to first occurrence of stroke; time to first occurrence of MACE; change in EQ-5D-5L proxy score; assessed at weeks 104 and 156
extraction_notes: This is a trial design/protocol publication for two identical phase 3 trials (evoke and evoke+); anticipated enrollment of 1840 participants per trial; participants may receive standard of care AD therapies during trial; CSF sub-study with planned n=210 for biomarker analyses

title: Exploring Predictors of Treatment Response to GLP-1 Receptor Agonists for Smoking Cessation.
journal: Nicotine & tobacco research : official journal of the Society for Research on Nicotine and Tobacco
population: Smokers with prediabetes and/or overweight
intervention: Exenatide 2 mg subcutaneously once weekly, adjunct to nicotine patch 21 mg and brief smoking cessation counseling
comparison: Placebo once weekly, with nicotine patch 21 mg and brief smoking cessation counseling
outcomes_primary: Biologically confirmed 7-day point prevalence abstinence at week 6 (end-of-treatment)
extraction_notes: This is a secondary/post-hoc analysis of a parent pilot trial exploring predictors of treatment response. Secondary outcomes not specified in abstract. Sample size n=84 randomized 1:1.

title: Dose-related Effects of Calcium to Enhance the Effects of L-tryptophan on Gut Hormones and Energy Intake in Obesity.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
population: Adult males with obesity and without type 2 diabetes, age 18 years or older, body mass index approximately 30 kg/m2, weight-stable (less than 5% fluctuation in 3 months), no history of gastrointestinal disorders or symptoms, no history of cardiovascular or respiratory diseases or surgery, not using supplements or medications affecting gastrointestinal functions or appetite, not consuming protein supplements, consuming 2 or fewer standard drinks of alcohol 5 or fewer days per week, not lactose intolerant, not vegetarian, non-smokers, not high-performance athletes
intervention: 150-minute intraduodenal infusions of calcium 500 mg or 1000 mg administered alone during infusion period 1 (t = 0-75 minutes), then combined with L-tryptophan (load: 0.1 kcal/min) during infusion period 2 (t = 75-150 minutes), infused at 3 mL/min, isosmotic solutions (300 mOsm)
comparison: 150-minute intraduodenal infusion of 0 mg calcium (control) alone during infusion period 1, then combined with L-tryptophan (load: 0.1 kcal/min) during infusion period 2; randomized, double-blind, cross-over design with each participant receiving all three conditions
outcomes_primary: Energy intake at standardized buffet-style lunch measured by weighing food consumed
outcomes_secondary: Plasma concentrations of gut hormones (gastrin, cholecystokinin, glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon-like peptide-1, peptide tyrosine-tyrosine), antropyloroduodenal motility (antral pressures, isolated pyloric pressure waves number and amplitude, duodenal pressures), appetite perceptions (fullness, hunger), gastrointestinal symptoms (nausea, bloating), drowsiness assessed by visual analog scales
extraction_notes: This is a mechanistic physiological study with intraduodenal nutrient infusion rather than a standard clinical intervention trial. The study used a three-way crossover design. Primary outcome was not explicitly labeled as primary in the text but energy intake appears to be the main outcome of interest based on sample size calculation referencing CCK as marker.

title: Gastrointestinal tolerability and weight reduction associated with tirzepatide in adults with obesity or overweight with and without type 2 diabetes in the SURMOUNT-1 to -4 trials.
population: Adults aged 18 years or older with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m²) or overweight (BMI ≥27 kg/m²) with at least one weight-related comorbidity (hypertension, dyslipidemia, obstructive sleep apnea, or cardiovascular disease), with or without type 2 diabetes. Key exclusion criteria included type 1 diabetes, known clinically significant gastric emptying abnormality, and history of pancreatitis.
intervention: Tirzepatide administered once weekly subcutaneously at doses of 5 mg, 10 mg, 15 mg, or maximum tolerated dose (MTD: 10 or 15 mg) for 72 weeks (SURMOUNT-1, -2, -3) or 88 weeks (SURMOUNT-4), with a 20-week dose escalation period
comparison: Placebo administered once weekly subcutaneously
outcomes_primary: Percent change in weight from baseline to primary endpoint (Week 72 for SURMOUNT-1, -2, -3; Week 88 for SURMOUNT-4)
outcomes_secondary: Gastrointestinal adverse events (nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, dyspepsia), use of concomitant medications (antidiarrheal and antiemetic), treatment discontinuation due to gastrointestinal adverse events
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of four Phase 3 trials (SURMOUNT-1 to -4). SURMOUNT-3 included a 12-week intensive lifestyle programme prior to randomization. SURMOUNT-4 included a 36-week open-label tirzepatide lead-in period before randomization (randomized withdrawal design). Mediation analyses were exploratory and not controlled for multiplicity.

title: Subcutaneous weekly semaglutide with automated insulin delivery in type 1 diabetes: a double-blind, randomized, crossover trial.
population: Adults aged 18 years or older with type 1 diabetes diagnosed for 1 year or longer, using an insulin pump for 3 months or longer, HbA1c of 11% or less. Exclusion criteria included current or recent use of antihyperglycemic agents other than insulin, planned or ongoing pregnancy or breastfeeding, severe hypoglycemic episode within 3 months, diabetic ketoacidosis requiring medical attention within 6 months, history of acute or chronic pancreatitis or gallbladder disease, BMI of 21 kg/m² or less, personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer or type 2 multiple endocrine neoplasia, bariatric surgery within 6 months, prior adverse reaction to GLP1-RAs, clinically significant diabetic retinopathy or gastroparesis.
intervention: Subcutaneous semaglutide once weekly, titrated over 11 weeks (0.25 mg weekly for 4 weeks, then 0.5 mg weekly for 4 weeks, then 1 mg weekly or maximum tolerated dose), followed by 4 weeks of automated insulin delivery system use.
comparison: Placebo (saline) administered subcutaneously once weekly with identical titration schedule (0.19 ml, 0.37 ml, or 0.74 ml corresponding to equivalent volumes), followed by 4 weeks of automated insulin delivery system use. Crossover design with 2-week washout period between interventions.
outcomes_primary: Percentage of time spent in the target glucose range of 3.9–10.0 mmol/l during the last 4 weeks of each intervention.
outcomes_secondary: Mean glucose level; standard deviation and coefficient of variation of glucose levels; time spent in hyperglycemia (above 10.0 and 13.9 mmol/l); time spent in hypoglycemia (below 3.0 and 3.9 mmol/l); daytime and nighttime glucose outcomes; anthropometric measurements (weight, BMI, waist circumference, hip circumference); insulin requirements (total, basal, bolus); carbohydrate intake; laboratory analyses including HbA1c, fructosamine, lipid profile; adverse events including diabetic ketoacidosis, severe hypoglycemia, euglycemic ketosis.
extraction_notes: Crossover trial design with each participant receiving both interventions. Research-based automated insulin delivery system used during outcome assessment period. Post hoc analysis conducted in subgroup using commercial Control-IQ technology during titration period.

title: Allocation of Semaglutide According to Coronary Artery Calcium and BMI: Applying the SELECT Trial to MESA.
population: Adults aged 45-84 years without diabetes and without established clinical cardiovascular disease (myocardial infarction, stroke, heart failure, peripheral arterial disease) with BMI ≥27 kg/m2 who underwent coronary artery calcium scoring on noncontrast cardiac computed tomography; participants from the MESA (Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis) cohort including White, Black, Hispanic, and Chinese participants
intervention: Modeled allocation of semaglutide weight loss therapy based on coronary artery calcium (CAC) burden categories (CAC = 0, CAC 1-99, CAC 100-299, CAC ≥300); relative risk reductions from SELECT trial applied to observed MESA incidence rates
comparison: Comparison across CAC burden categories (CAC = 0 as reference vs CAC 1-99, CAC 100-299, CAC ≥300) and across BMI strata (27-29 kg/m2, 30-34 kg/m2, ≥35 kg/m2)
outcomes_primary: Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) defined as cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or nonfatal stroke; number needed to treat calculations for MACE
outcomes_secondary: Heart failure (defined by persistent symptoms plus objective criteria including physician diagnosis, pulmonary edema on chest x-ray, and/or abnormal ventricular function on echocardiography); chronic kidney disease (defined using ICD-9 and ICD-10 codes); all-cause mortality; composite outcomes including CVD (MACE or HF), CKM (MACE or HF or CKD), and any first obesity-related CKM event (MACE, HF, CKD, or all-cause mortality); number needed to treat calculations for secondary outcomes
extraction_notes: This is an observational modeling study applying SELECT trial relative risk reductions to MESA cohort data, not a randomized controlled trial of semaglutide. No direct intervention was administered; NNT values are projections based on modeling. Drug dosing details for semaglutide not specified as this was a modeling analysis.

title: Time to weight plateau with tirzepatide treatment in the SURMOUNT-1 and SURMOUNT-4 clinical trials.
population: Adults with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m²) or overweight (BMI ≥27-<30 kg/m²) with at least one adiposity-related complication, without type 2 diabetes. Post-hoc analysis included participants who received at least 75% of study doses, achieved at least 5% weight loss, reached assigned dose by week 24, had no dose reduction, and had weight measurement at primary endpoint.
intervention: Tirzepatide subcutaneous injection once weekly at doses of 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg for 72 weeks (SURMOUNT-1) or maximum tolerated dose of 10 or 15 mg for 88 weeks total including 36-week open-label lead-in followed by 52-week double-blind period (SURMOUNT-4)
comparison: Placebo (SURMOUNT-1: 1:1:1:1 randomization to tirzepatide 5, 10, 15 mg or placebo; SURMOUNT-4: randomization to continue tirzepatide or switch to placebo after open-label lead-in)
outcomes_primary: Time to weight plateau, defined as time from randomization to the start of the first 12-week interval with weight change <5% that was maintained through all subsequent 12-week intervals to end of study
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of participants reaching weight plateau by end of study; percent body weight change; association between baseline characteristics (tirzepatide dose, age, sex, race, BMI category, waist circumference) and time to weight plateau
extraction_notes: This is a post-hoc analysis of SURMOUNT-1 and SURMOUNT-4 trials. Weight plateau definition and analysis were exploratory. Original trials had different primary endpoints not specifically focused on time to weight plateau.

title: Once-weekly IcoSema versus once-weekly semaglutide in adults with type 2 diabetes: the COMBINE 2 randomised clinical trial.
population: Adults aged ≥18 years with type 2 diabetes inadequately managed (HbA1c 53.0–85.8 mmol/mol [7.0–10.0%]), treated with stable doses of daily or weekly GLP-1 receptor agonists (excluding once-weekly semaglutide with doses higher than 1.0 mg) for at least 90 days before screening, with or without stable doses of additional oral glucose-lowering medications
intervention: Once-weekly IcoSema (combination of basal insulin icodec and semaglutide), subcutaneous injection, starting dose 40 dose steps (equivalent to 40 U icodec and 0.114 mg semaglutide), titrated in 10 dose-step increments/decrements weekly based on pre-breakfast SMBG values (target 4.4–7.2 mmol/l), maximum dose 350 dose steps (350 U icodec/1.0 mg semaglutide), for 52 weeks
comparison: Once-weekly semaglutide 1.0 mg, subcutaneous injection, starting dose 0.25 mg, escalated to 0.5 mg after 4 weeks, then to 1.0 mg after another 4 weeks and maintained thereafter, for 52 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline to week 52
outcomes_secondary: Change in fasting plasma glucose from baseline to week 52; change in body weight from baseline to week 52; combined clinically significant (level 2; <3.0 mmol/l) or severe (level 3; associated with severe cognitive impairment requiring external assistance for recovery) hypoglycaemia from baseline to week 57; clinically significant hypoglycaemic episodes from baseline to week 57; severe hypoglycaemic episodes from baseline to week 57
extraction_notes: Pre-trial GLP-1 RA, sulfonylurea, glinide and DPP-4i therapies were discontinued at randomisation. Open-label trial design.

title: Clinical characteristics affecting weight loss in an East Asian population receiving semaglutide: A STEP 6 subgroup analysis.

intervention: Subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg or semaglutide 1.7 mg for 68 weeks
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline in body weight (%)
outcomes_secondary: Treatment-by-subgroup interactions for baseline characteristics including baseline body weight, body mass index, age, sex, glycemic status, dyslipidemia, and hypertension
extraction_notes: This is a post-hoc subgroup analysis of the STEP 6 trial. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly labeled; outcomes inferred from methods description. Specific inclusion criteria for overweight/obesity thresholds not provided.

title: The safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of an optimized dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist (BGM0504) in healthy volunteers: A dose-escalation Phase I study.
population: Chinese healthy volunteers
intervention: BGM0504 (GLP-1R/GIPR dual agonist), single dose (2.5 mg) and once-weekly administration for 2 weeks with titration to target doses (5, 10, and 15 mg)
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK), pharmacodynamics (PD)
extraction_notes: Abstract appears truncated in the results section. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly differentiated in the abstract; listed outcomes reflect stated study aims. This is a Phase I study in healthy volunteers, not patients with T2DM or obesity.

title: Semaglutide in obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and type 2 diabetes across baseline HbA
population: Adults aged 18 years or older with documented heart failure with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF; left ventricular ejection fraction ≥45%), type 2 diabetes, and obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m²)
intervention: Subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg once weekly
comparison: Placebo

title: Effects of Semaglutide Treatment on Psoriatic Lesions in Obese Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: An Open-Label, Randomized Clinical Trial.
population: Adults aged 18-70 years with moderately-severe to severe plaque psoriasis (PASI score ≥10), type 2 diabetes mellitus diagnosed at least 6 months prior and treated with metformin, and obesity (BMI >30 kg/m2, HbA1c >7%). Excluded: other forms of psoriasis, other chronic inflammatory diseases, use of lithium, systemic antimalarial drugs, systemic corticosteroids within 3 months, systemic psoriasis therapy within 3 months, other GLP-1 receptor agonists, SGLT-2 inhibitors, NSAIDs, photo UVB therapy, family history of medullary thyroid cancer.
intervention: Semaglutide 1.0 mg subcutaneously once weekly for 12 weeks, in addition to standard metformin therapy at maximally tolerated dose. Topical keratolytic therapy with salicylic acid permitted.
comparison: Continued standard metformin therapy at maximally tolerated dose without semaglutide. Topical keratolytic therapy with salicylic acid permitted.
outcomes_primary: Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI) score; Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI)
outcomes_secondary: Serum inflammatory markers (CRP, IL-1β, IL-6, IL-17, IL-23, homocysteine); body mass index (BMI); lipid parameters (total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, triglycerides); glycemic parameters (fasting glucose, fasting insulin, HbA1c); PASI 90 and PASI 100 response rates
extraction_notes: Open-label design acknowledged by authors. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly designated in text; classification inferred from study aims. IL-17 was not detectable in patient serum. Study duration was 12 weeks.

title: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Two-Way Cross-over Study to Evaluate the Efficacy of Liraglutide Treatment in Patients Undergoing Transoral Outlet Reduction Endoscopy for Weight Regain Post Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass.
population: Patients with weight regain after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass undergoing transoral outlet reduction endoscopy (TORe)
intervention: Subcutaneous liraglutide dosed daily for 12 months initiated immediately post-TORe, followed by subcutaneous saline for 12 months (group LP)
comparison: Subcutaneous saline (placebo) dosed daily for 12 months after TORe, followed by subcutaneous liraglutide for 12 months (group PL)
outcomes_primary: Percent total body weight loss (%TBWL) at 12 and 24 months
extraction_notes: Cross-over design where all participants received both liraglutide and placebo for equal duration over 24 months, differing only in sequence of administration. Secondary outcomes not explicitly specified. Liraglutide dose not specified in abstract.

title: Association of bodyweight loss with changes in lipids, blood pressure, and fasting serum glucose following tirzepatide treatment in Japanese participants with type 2 diabetes: A post hoc analysis of the SURPASS J-mono trial.
population: Japanese adults with type 2 diabetes (World Health Organization classification), who used diet and exercise alone to manage their T2D or were on oral antihyperglycemic medication monotherapy (except thiazolidinedione) and willing to discontinue the OAM
intervention: Tirzepatide 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg administered once weekly by subcutaneous injection for 52 weeks
comparison: Dulaglutide 0.75 mg administered once weekly by subcutaneous injection for 52 weeks
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly stated in abstract or methods for this post hoc analysis; analysis evaluated associations between bodyweight loss and changes in triglycerides, HDL-cholesterol, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, and fasting serum glucose
outcomes_secondary: 2-hour postprandial glucose from 7-point self-monitored blood glucose profile; weight loss-associated and weight loss-unassociated effects of tirzepatide compared to dulaglutide
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of the SURPASS J-mono trial (NCT03861052). Primary and secondary outcomes are not explicitly defined for this post hoc analysis; the outcomes listed reflect the metabolic parameters analyzed. The original SURPASS J-mono trial had HbA1c as primary endpoint.

title: Exenatide once a week versus placebo as a potential disease-modifying treatment for people with Parkinson's disease in the UK: a phase 3, multicentre, double-blind, parallel-group, randomised, placebo-controlled trial.
population: Adults aged 25-80 years with a diagnosis of Parkinson's disease, Hoehn and Yahr stage 2.5 or less when on dopaminergic treatment, on dopaminergic treatment for at least 4 weeks before enrolment, in the UK
intervention: Extended-release exenatide 2 mg by subcutaneous pen injection once per week for 96 weeks
comparison: Visually identical placebo by subcutaneous pen injection once per week for 96 weeks
outcomes_primary: Movement Disorder Society-sponsored revision of the Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (MDS-UPDRS) part III score, off dopaminergic medication at 96 weeks
extraction_notes: Secondary outcomes not explicitly defined in abstract. Study was multicentre across six research hospitals in the UK.

title: Postprandial plasma amino acid and appetite responses to a low protein breakfast supplemented with whey or pea protein in middle-to-older aged adults.
population: Active and otherwise healthy males and females aged 50-70 years old; BMI ≤30 kg/m²; no underlying metabolic health conditions or dietary intolerances which may cause allergic reactions
intervention: Low protein-containing whole-food mixed breakfast (0.07 g/kg body mass protein from muesli, yoghurt and blueberries) supplemented with 0.13 g/kg body mass whey protein concentrate in smoothie form (<150 mL), consumed once
comparison: Low protein-containing whole-food mixed breakfast (0.07 g/kg body mass protein from muesli, yoghurt and blueberries) supplemented with 0.13 g/kg body mass pea protein isolate in smoothie form (<150 mL), consumed once
outcomes_primary: Postprandial plasma amino acid concentrations (total amino acids, essential amino acids, leucine) measured over 180 minutes; incremental area under the curve for plasma amino acids
outcomes_secondary: Plasma appetite hormone concentrations (total GLP-1, total ghrelin); plasma glucose and insulin concentrations; perceived appetite ratings (hunger, fullness, satiety, thirst, satisfaction, eating capacity, taste preferences) measured using Visual Analogue Scales; composite appetite score
extraction_notes: Single-blind parallel-designed study with randomization. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the text; classification based on study aims. Complete plasma samples available for 22 of 27 enrolled participants (MB+WPC n=13, MB+PPI n=9).

title: Once-Weekly Semaglutide in Adults With Alcohol Use Disorder: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
population: Non-treatment-seeking adults aged 21-65 years with past-year DSM-5 alcohol use disorder (AUD), reporting more than 7 (women) or more than 14 (men) standard drinks per week with 2 or more heavy drinking episodes in the past month, able to attend weekly clinic visits and laboratory sessions. Key exclusions: currently seeking treatment for alcohol problems or attempting to reduce consumption, past use of GLP-1 receptor agonists, weight loss medications, BMI less than 23, past-year substance use disorder other than AUD/tobacco use disorder/mild cannabis use disorder, recent 30-day illicit drug use except cannabis, history of diabetes, current medical or neurological illness precluding participation.
intervention: Subcutaneous semaglutide: 0.25 mg/week for weeks 1-4, 0.5 mg/week for weeks 5-8, and 1.0 mg for week 9 (flexible, contingent on tolerability), administered at weekly clinic visits for 9 weeks total.
comparison: Placebo (subcutaneous injection at same schedule and weekly visits).
outcomes_primary: Laboratory alcohol self-administration measured at pretreatment and posttreatment (at 0.5 mg/week dose): estimated volume of alcohol consumed (grams of ethanol) and peak breath alcohol concentration.
outcomes_secondary: Average drinks per calendar day, cigarettes per day (in participants with current cigarette use). Exploratory outcomes: drinks per drinking day, number of heavy drinking days, number of drinking vs abstinent days, weekly alcohol craving, proportion of participants with zero heavy drinking days, body weight, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, side effects, adverse events, depression symptoms.
extraction_notes: Non-treatment-seeking population specified. Week 9 dose (1.0 mg) was flexible based on tolerability. Primary outcome collected between weeks 8-9 at 0.5 mg/week dose.

title: Effects of Oral Xylitol, Sucrose, and Acesulfame Potassium on Total Energy Intake During a Subsequent
population: Healthy participants aged 18-55 years with normal body weight (BMI 19.0-24.9 kg/m2), stable body weight (±5%) for at least three months prior to study. Exclusion criteria: fructose intolerance, specific diets (vegetarian, vegan, sugar free, no breakfast), regular consumption of xylitol and/or ace-K (>1/week), chronic or clinically relevant acute infections or diseases, regular medication use, pregnancy, alcohol or substance abuse, working night shifts, participation in another clinical study within 30 days
intervention: Oral preload containing 33.5 g xylitol dissolved in 300 mL water, consumed within 2 minutes, followed by ad libitum test meal 15 minutes later
comparison: Three comparator preloads: (1) 33.5 g sucrose dissolved in 300 mL water; (2) 0.1675 g acesulfame potassium (ace-K) dissolved in 300 mL water; (3) 300 mL pure water (control). All consumed within 2 minutes, followed by ad libitum test meal 15 minutes later
outcomes_primary: Energy intake during ad libitum test meal; Total energy intake (preload calories + ad libitum test meal)
outcomes_secondary: Plasma cholecystokinin (CCK) concentrations; plasma glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1total) concentrations; plasma glucose concentrations; plasma insulin concentrations; appetite-related sensations (hunger, prospective food consumption, satiety, fullness) measured by visual analogue scales; gastrointestinal tolerance assessed by symptom checklist; perceived sweetness and liking of preloads and test meal measured using Global Sensory Intensity Scale (GSIS) and Global Hedonic Intensity Scale (GHIS)
extraction_notes: This is a crossover trial with all participants receiving all four preloads across four study visits. Doses of sweeteners were matched to be equisweet. Sample size was 20 participants (10 women, 10 men).

title: Safety profile of semaglutide versus placebo in the SELECT study: a randomized controlled trial.
population: Adults aged 45 years or older with established cardiovascular disease and overweight or obesity (BMI ≥27 kg/m²) without diabetes
intervention: Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg in addition to standard of care
comparison: Placebo in addition to standard of care
outcomes_primary: Incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE)
outcomes_secondary: Serious adverse events (SAEs); adverse events leading to permanent treatment discontinuation; prespecified adverse events of special interest including gallbladder-related disorders, acute pancreatitis, malignant neoplasms, acute kidney failure, psychiatric disorders including suicide/self-injury, hypoglycemia, hepatic disorders, allergic reactions, and fractures
extraction_notes: This is a prespecified safety analysis of the SELECT trial; the primary endpoint (MACE reduction) was the efficacy outcome of the main trial while this paper focuses on detailed safety outcomes. Patients with history or presence of chronic pancreatitis, malignant neoplasms within 5 years, or severe psychiatric disorders were excluded.

title: Population Pharmacokinetics of Efsubaglutide Alfa in Healthy Subjects and Subjects with Type 2 Diabetes.
population: Healthy subjects and patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D); pooled data from 911 participants including 36 healthy subjects and 875 patients with T2D across four clinical trials
intervention: Efsubaglutide alfa, once-weekly subcutaneous injections at doses ranging from 0.375 mg to 9.0 mg, treatment durations from 1 to 24 weeks
comparison: Not explicitly stated; multiple dose arms within population pharmacokinetic analysis
outcomes_primary: Population pharmacokinetic model parameters; characterization of pharmacokinetic profile of efsubaglutide alfa
outcomes_secondary: Impact of intrinsic and extrinsic factors (covariates including baseline weight, baseline eGFR, neutralizing antibodies, study, and treatment arm) on pharmacokinetic parameters
extraction_notes: This is a population pharmacokinetic modeling study, not a traditional RCT comparing interventions. No formal comparator group was specified. The study pooled data from four clinical trials (NCT03745885, NCT04314622, NCT04994288, NCT04998032) for model development.

title: Acute decrease in the plasma tryptophan-to-large-neutral-amino-acids ratio attenuates the effects of L-tryptophan on gut hormones and energy intake in healthy males: a randomized, cross-over, exploratory trial.

outcomes_primary: Plasma cholecystokinin (CCK), glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1), pyloric pressures, energy intake

title: Body composition changes during weight reduction with tirzepatide in the SURMOUNT-1 study of adults with obesity or overweight.
population: Adults without type 2 diabetes with BMI ≥30 kg/m2 or BMI ≥27 kg/m2 with one or more weight-related complications, enrolled in the SURMOUNT-1 DXA substudy at sites with access to whole-body DXA scanners. Key exclusion criteria included recent procedure with oral contrast or radionuclides, body weight/height/width exceeding DXA manufacturer specifications, or implants/hardware/devices that could interfere with scan.
intervention: Once-weekly tirzepatide 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg subcutaneous injection for 72 weeks, combined with individualized lifestyle counselling (500 kilocalorie/day dietary deficit, physical activity ≥150 min/week)
comparison: Placebo (once-weekly injection) for 72 weeks with same lifestyle counselling
outcomes_primary: Percent change in fat mass from baseline to Week 72 (pooled tirzepatide vs placebo)
outcomes_secondary: Percent change from baseline in lean mass; absolute change from baseline in lean mass and fat mass. Exploratory endpoints: percent change from baseline in body weight, visceral fat mass, and waist circumference; proportion of body weight reduction as fat mass and lean mass
extraction_notes: This is a DXA substudy of the SURMOUNT-1 trial (NCT04184622). Subgroup analyses by age, sex, and weight reduction tertiles were conducted post hoc. Randomization was 1:1:1:1 to tirzepatide 5mg, 10mg, 15mg, or placebo. Primary analysis pooled all tirzepatide doses.

title: Differential Treatment Effects on β-Cell Function Using Model-Based Parameters in Type 2 Diabetes: Results From the Glycemia Reduction Approaches in Diabetes: A Comparative Effectiveness Study (GRADE).
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes on baseline metformin therapy
intervention: Liraglutide added to metformin; Sitagliptin added to metformin; Glimepiride added to metformin; Insulin glargine added to metformin
comparison: Four-arm comparative effectiveness study: insulin glargine vs glimepiride vs liraglutide vs sitagliptin (all added to baseline metformin)
outcomes_primary: β-cell function parameters derived from mathematical modeling of oral glucose tolerance tests including: insulin secretion rate (ISR), glucose sensitivity (insulin response to glucose), rate sensitivity (early insulin response), and potentiation; glycemic failure defined as A1C >7.5% (58.5 mmol/mol)
outcomes_secondary: Changes in β-cell function parameters at 1, 3, and 5 years following randomization; associations between model parameters and glycemic deterioration
extraction_notes: This is a secondary analysis of the GRADE study. Sample size N=4,712 at baseline. Duration of follow-up was 5 years. Specific doses, routes, and frequencies of interventions not stated in abstract.

title: The safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of GZR18 in healthy American and Chinese adult subjects.

outcomes_primary: Safety and tolerability of GZR18
outcomes_secondary: Pharmacokinetics (PK) of GZR18; Pharmacodynamics (PD) of GZR18; Population PK analysis to determine ethnic PK differences between American and Chinese adults

comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Change in bodyweight at week 72; proportion of participants achieving at least 5% bodyweight reduction
outcomes_secondary: Cardiometabolic indices; body composition indices; treatment-emergent adverse events; study discontinuations due to adverse events

title: Blood pressure changes during smoking cessation in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of dulaglutide treatment.
population: Participants undergoing smoking cessation programme
intervention: Dulaglutide 1.5 mg weekly injections for 12 weeks plus standard of care (behavioural counselling and varenicline)
comparison: Placebo weekly injections plus standard of care (behavioural counselling and varenicline)
outcomes_primary: Change in systolic blood pressure after 52 weeks in abstinent vs. smoking individuals
outcomes_secondary: Blood pressure changes at Week 12 and 52 according to smoking status and treatment arms; body weight changes at Week 12 and 52 according to smoking status and treatment arms
extraction_notes: This is a predefined secondary analysis of an RCT (NCT03204396). The original trial's primary outcome was likely weight gain mitigation. Population inclusion/exclusion criteria not explicitly stated in abstract.

title: Efficacy and safety of once-weekly semaglutide 2.4 mg for weight management in participants from China: A prespecified analysis of the STEP 7 randomized clinical trial.
population: Chinese adults aged ≥18 years with overweight or obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m² or BMI ≥27 kg/m² with ≥1 weight-related comorbidity including hypertension, dyslipidaemia, obstructive sleep apnoea, cardiovascular disease, or type 2 diabetes), with or without type 2 diabetes, with a history of ≥1 self-reported unsuccessful dietary effort to lose weight
intervention: Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg for 44 weeks (fixed-dose escalation from 0.25 mg initial dose, increased every 4 weeks to 0.5, 1.0, 1.7, and 2.4 mg/week until Week 16, then maintenance dose of 2.4 mg) as an adjunct to lifestyle intervention (approximately 500 kcal/day deficit in diet and 150 minutes/week of physical activity)
comparison: Placebo (once-weekly subcutaneous injection) with same lifestyle intervention
outcomes_primary: Percentage change in body weight from baseline to Week 44; proportion of participants achieving ≥5% reduction in body weight from baseline
outcomes_secondary: Confirmatory secondary endpoints: proportion achieving ≥10% and ≥15% body weight reduction; changes in waist circumference, systolic blood pressure, SF-36v2 physical functioning score, and IWQOL-Lite-CT physical function score. Supportive secondary endpoints: proportion achieving ≥20% body weight reduction; changes in body weight, BMI, HbA1c, fasting plasma glucose, fasting serum insulin, diastolic blood pressure, lipids, and fatty liver index score. Safety endpoints: incidence of adverse events
extraction_notes: This is a prespecified subgroup analysis of Chinese participants from the STEP 7 trial. Randomization was 2:1 (semaglutide:placebo). The analysis was not part of the statistical testing hierarchy for superiority.

title: Time spent in glycaemic control with sustained body weight reduction with tirzepatide: A post hoc analysis of the SURPASS clinical trial programme.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes from the SURPASS 1-5 clinical trial programme
intervention: Tirzepatide 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg administered once weekly subcutaneously for 40 weeks (SURPASS-1, -2, -5) or 52 weeks (SURPASS-3, -4)
comparison: Once weekly placebo (SURPASS-1, -5), once weekly semaglutide 1 mg (SURPASS-2), insulin degludec titrated to target (SURPASS-3), insulin glargine titrated to target (SURPASS-4, -5)
outcomes_primary: Continuous time spent with HbA1c <7.0% (53 mmol/mol); continuous time spent with HbA1c ≤6.5% (48 mmol/mol); continuous time spent with ≥5% body weight reduction from baseline
outcomes_secondary: Continuous time spent with fasting serum glucose ≤125 mg/dL (7 mmol/L); composite continuous time spent with HbA1c ≤6.5% (48 mmol/mol) and ≥5% body weight reduction; proportion of participants achieving glycaemic control and body weight reduction at any time point; proportion of participants achieving targets at end of primary study period
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis pooling data from SURPASS 1-5 trials. Primary outcomes in this analysis differ from the original SURPASS trials which had HbA1c change from baseline as primary endpoint. Distinction between primary and secondary outcomes in this post hoc analysis is not explicitly stated; categorization based on emphasis in objectives.

title: Early Fasting Serum Glucose or Weight Reduction With Tirzepatide and Metabolic Outcomes in People With Type 2 Diabetes: A Post Hoc Analysis of the SURPASS Trials.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes from the SURPASS-1 to -5 phase 3 clinical trials, with mean baseline HbA1c ranging from 7.94% to 8.52% and BMI ranging from 31.9 to 34.2 kg/m2
intervention: Tirzepatide 5, 10, or 15 mg subcutaneous injection once weekly, initiated at 2.5 mg once weekly for 4 weeks then escalated in increments of 2.5 mg every 4 weeks until randomized dose achieved; with varying background antihyperglycemic medications (none, metformin, metformin with or without SGLT2i, any combination of metformin/sulfonylurea/SGLT2i, or titrated insulin glargine with or without metformin depending on individual trial)
