title: Upper-gastrointestinal tract metabolite profile regulates glycaemic and satiety responses to meals with contrasting structure: a pilot study.
population: Healthy adults aged 18-65 years with BMI 18.5-30 kg/m², without history of cancer, diabetes, gastrointestinal disease, or medications likely to interfere with metabolic and hormone responses
intervention: Iso-nutrient chickpea meals with contrasting cellular structures: (1) Intact-C (tissue macroparticles with intact cell clusters), (2) Intact-S (separated intact cells), (3) Broken (blended before cooking to break open every cell); each serving containing approximately 242.7 kcal, 29.5 g starch, 2.3 g sugar, 6.6 g dietary fibre, 11.0 g protein and 3.7 g fat; administered on consecutive days in randomized crossover design
comparison: Three-way crossover comparison between Intact-C, Intact-S, and Broken cell structure chickpea meals
outcomes_primary: Gut hormone response (GIP, GLP-1, PYY)
outcomes_secondary: Intestinal content analysis (gastric and duodenal metabolite profiles via 1H-NMR, microscopy of aspirates, starch digestion products), blood glucose response, blood insulin response, subjective appetite changes (visual analogue scale scores for fullness, hunger, appetite for a meal, desire to eat), ad libitum energy intake at 4 hours postprandially
extraction_notes: Pilot study with small sample size (n=10). Randomized crossover design with 1-day washout between interventions. Participants fitted with nasoenteric tubes for simultaneous gastric and duodenal sampling.

title: Benefit of Semaglutide in Symptomatic Peripheral Artery Disease by Baseline Type 2 Diabetes Characteristics: Insights From STRIDE, a Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Double-Blind Trial.
population: Adults aged ≥18 years with symptomatic peripheral artery disease (Fontaine classification IIa) and type 2 diabetes, with ankle-brachial index ≤0.90 or toe-brachial index ≤0.70, on stable medications, without non-PAD-related conditions limiting functional capacity, without severe cardiovascular/neurologic/other disease, without history of recent cardiovascular event or arterial revascularization within 180 days, and without planned revascularization
intervention: Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 1.0 mg for 52 weeks
comparison: Matched placebo (once-weekly subcutaneous injection)
outcomes_primary: Ratio to baseline in maximum walking distance (MWD) on constant load treadmill test at week 52
outcomes_secondary: Change in MWD on constant load treadmill test at week 57; change in pain-free walking distance (PFWD) on constant load treadmill test at week 52; change in patient-reported PAD-specific vascular quality of life score from baseline to week 52
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc subgroup analysis of the STRIDE trial (NCT04560998). Primary focus was examining treatment consistency across diabetes-related subgroups (diabetes duration, BMI, HbA1c, concomitant medications). Treadmill parameters specified as fixed speed 3.2 kph (2 mph) and fixed inclination 12%.

title: Cagrilintide-Semaglutide in Adults with Overweight or Obesity and Type 2 Diabetes.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
population: Adults with body-mass index of 27 or more, glycated hemoglobin level of 7 to 10%, and type 2 diabetes
intervention: Once-weekly cagrilintide-semaglutide (2.4 mg each) plus lifestyle intervention for 68 weeks
comparison: Placebo plus lifestyle intervention
outcomes_primary: Percent change in body weight from baseline to week 68; percentage of patients with weight reduction of at least 5%
outcomes_secondary: Changes in glycemic measures; percentage of patients with weight reduction of at least 10%, 15%, and 20%; percentage of patients with glycated hemoglobin level of 6.5% or less; safety assessments
extraction_notes: Trial included a subgroup undergoing continuous glucose monitoring mentioned but not detailed in abstract

title: Coadministered Cagrilintide and Semaglutide in Adults with Overweight or Obesity.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
population: Adults without diabetes who had a body-mass index (BMI) of 30 or higher or a BMI of 27 or higher with at least one obesity-related complication
intervention: Cagrilintide 2.4 mg plus semaglutide 2.4 mg (CagriSema) plus lifestyle interventions, administered over 68 weeks
comparison: Semaglutide alone 2.4 mg plus lifestyle interventions; Cagrilintide alone 2.4 mg plus lifestyle interventions; Placebo plus lifestyle interventions
outcomes_primary: Relative change in body weight from baseline to week 68; Proportion achieving 5% or more reduction in body weight from baseline to week 68
outcomes_secondary: Proportion achieving 20% or more reduction in body weight; Proportion achieving 25% or more reduction in body weight; Proportion achieving 30% or more reduction in body weight; Safety assessments
extraction_notes: Route of administration not explicitly stated in abstract. Randomization ratio was 21:3:3:7 for CagriSema:semaglutide:cagrilintide:placebo.

title: Once-Monthly Maridebart Cafraglutide for the Treatment of Obesity - A Phase 2 Trial.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
population: Adults with obesity (obesity cohort) or adults with obesity with type 2 diabetes (obesity-diabetes cohort)
intervention: Maridebart cafraglutide (MariTide) administered subcutaneously at doses of 140 mg, 280 mg, or 420 mg every 4 weeks without dose escalation; 420 mg every 8 weeks without dose escalation; 420 mg every 4 weeks with 4-week dose escalation; or 420 mg every 4 weeks with 12-week dose escalation
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Percent change in body weight from baseline to week 52
outcomes_secondary: Change in glycated hemoglobin level (in obesity-diabetes cohort); gastrointestinal adverse events; safety signals
extraction_notes: Trial includes two cohorts with different randomization ratios. Obesity cohort randomized 3:3:3:2:2:2:3 across 7 groups; obesity-diabetes cohort randomized 1:1:1:1 across 4 groups. Secondary outcomes not explicitly labeled as such in abstract; glycated hemoglobin and adverse events inferred from reported measurements.

title: Semaglutide in Adults with Type 1 Diabetes and Obesity.
population: Adults with type 1 diabetes using an automated insulin delivery (AID) system and with a body mass index of 30 or higher
intervention: Once-weekly semaglutide up to 1 mg
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Composite end point consisting of achieving all of the following: continuous glucose monitoring (CGM)-based time between 70 and 180 mg/dl of greater than 70%, time below 70 mg/dl of less than 4%, and weight reduction of at least 5%
outcomes_secondary: Glycated hemoglobin change from baseline, percentage of time with CGM glucose levels between 70 and 180 mg/dl, body weight change, severe hypoglycemia events, diabetic ketoacidosis
extraction_notes: Secondary outcomes inferred from reported results as they were not explicitly labeled as secondary outcomes in the abstract

title: Improvements in Cardiometabolic Risk Factors by Weight Reduction: A Post Hoc Analysis of Adults With Obesity Randomly Assigned to Tirzepatide.
population: Adults with obesity without diabetes; BMI ≥30 kg/m² or BMI ≥27 kg/m² with at least one weight-related complication (hypertension, dyslipidemia, obstructive sleep apnea, or cardiovascular disease)
intervention: Once-weekly tirzepatide, 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Changes from baseline to week 72 in cardiometabolic risk factors by weight reduction
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of the SURMOUNT-1 trial. The abstract is truncated, cutting off participant details. Specific cardiometabolic risk factor outcomes are not explicitly listed. Primary and secondary outcome distinctions not clearly defined in this post hoc analysis abstract.

title: Tirzepatide on ingestive behavior in adults with overweight or obesity: a randomized 6-week phase 1 trial.
population: Male and female adults aged 18 to 65 years without diabetes, with body mass index 27 to 50 kg per m2 and stable weight in the last month (no weight change >4 kg)
intervention: Tirzepatide 5 mg subcutaneously once-weekly for first 3 weeks followed by 10 mg subcutaneously once-weekly for next 3 weeks (6 weeks total)
comparison: Placebo subcutaneously once-weekly (blinded); Liraglutide subcutaneously once-daily starting at 0.6 mg and escalated weekly by 0.6 mg until 3 mg reached at week 5 and maintained for remainder of study (open-label)
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline to week 3 in energy intake during ad libitum lunch meal test for tirzepatide versus placebo
outcomes_secondary: Change from baseline to week 3 for tirzepatide versus placebo in: fasting and postprandial appetite VAS ratings; Food Craving Inventory (FCI); Food Craving Questionnaire-State (FCQ-S); Eating Inventory; Power of Food Scale (PFS) questionnaire ratings; BOLD fMRI activation to photos of highly palatable foods (high-fat high-sugar and high-fat high-carbohydrate) relative to non-food during fasting state in prespecified principal reward brain regions of interest
extraction_notes: Liraglutide was open-label while tirzepatide and placebo were blinded; study described as partially blinded; 6-week treatment duration with 4-week safety follow-up

title: A Pharmacometric Method for Quantitative Determination of Improvement in Body Composition and Characterization of the Exposure-Response Relationship during Treatment of Obesity with Tirzepatide.
population: Adults with BMI ≥30 kg/m2 or BMI ≥27 kg/m2 with at least one weight-related complication (such as cardiovascular disease) without type 2 diabetes mellitus
intervention: Tirzepatide 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg administered subcutaneously once-weekly for up to 72 weeks
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Body weight reduction; changes in body composition (fat-free mass and fat mass)
extraction_notes: This is a pharmacometric modeling study using data from SURMOUNT-1 (NCT04184622) phase 3 trial. Primary outcomes focus on exposure-response relationships and body composition changes rather than traditional clinical endpoints. Secondary outcomes not explicitly defined.

title: GLP-1 Responses to a Single Meal Fortified With Oyster Mushroom Powder in Adults With Impaired Glucose Tolerance Depend on the Gut Microbiota Composition Before the Meal.
population: Adults with impaired glucose tolerance (IGT)
intervention: Single meal fortified with 20 g powder of oven-dried Pleurotus ostreatus (oyster mushroom), providing 8.1 g of β-glucans, equivalent to 200 g fresh mushroom serving size, consumed after minimum 12 h overnight fast
comparison: Non-enriched control meal (CON)
outcomes_primary: Postprandial GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide 1) response measured as incremental area under the curve over 4 hours
outcomes_secondary: Postprandial NEFA (non-esterified fatty acids) response measured as incremental area under the curve over 4 hours; association between baseline gut microbiota composition (alpha diversity, beta diversity, bacterial genera abundance, microbial functional pathways) and metabolic responses
extraction_notes: This is a secondary analysis of a randomized controlled crossover trial (DRKS00015244). The primary and secondary outcome distinction is not explicitly stated; GLP-1 and NEFA appear to be co-primary outcomes from the parent study. Blood samples collected at 0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120, 180, and 240 minutes post-meal.

title: Exenatide and glucagon co-infusion increases myocardial glucose uptake and improves markers of diastolic dysfunction in adults with type 2 diabetes.
population: Non-smoking adults with type 2 diabetes, BMI > 25 kg/m2, HbA1c < 65 mmol/mol. Excluded: females of childbearing potential, severe hypertension, clinically significant heart disease, chronic kidney disease (creatinine > 150 µmol/L), active malignancy, type 1 diabetes, patients prescribed insulin, GLP-1 receptor agonists or dipeptidyl peptidase 4 inhibitors, contraindications for PET and MRI scans
intervention: Exenatide:glucagon co-infusion (exenatide loading dose 50 ng/min IV for 30 min then 25 ng/min; glucagon 12.5 ng/kg/min IV) for total infusion duration of 150 minutes
comparison: 0.9% saline infusion; Glucagon alone (12.5 ng/kg/min IV)
outcomes_primary: Myocardial glucose uptake (MGU) assessed using 18F-FDG PET-MRI; Myocardial function parameters including LV global longitudinal strain, LV global peak diastolic circumferential strain rate, LV global peak diastolic radial strain rate, LV ejection fraction, LV stroke volume
outcomes_secondary: 18F-FDG influx rate (Ki); LV end systolic volume; LV end diastolic volume; Left atrial volumes; LV mass; LV global radial strain; LV global circumferential strain; Systolic and diastolic strain rates; Ratio between early and late filling (mitral flow); Deceleration time; Left atrial emptying fraction; Point of care blood glucose
extraction_notes: Single-centre, single-blinded, exploratory pilot study using Latin square block design with three randomised infusion visits. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly designated in the text; classification based on study aims and emphasis in results reporting. Small sample size (n=8) acknowledged as limitation.

title: Effect of Ebenatide on glycemic metabolism and body fat in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus aged 18-70 years, BMI 20-40 kg/m², HbA1c 7.0-11.0%. Included both treatment-naïve patients with newly diagnosed T2DM and patients who had received stable maximal tolerated doses of metformin for ≥3 months prior to enrollment. Exclusion criteria: hyperglycemia exceeding specified thresholds at defined timepoints, history of long-term use of medications affecting gastrointestinal motility, use of weight-loss drugs or hormonal therapy within past 3 months, impaired liver/kidney function (ALT/AST >2.5×ULN or total bilirubin >1.5×ULN, eGFR <60 mL/min), SBP >160 mmHg and/or DBP >100 mmHg, fasting triglycerides >5.64 mmol/L, serum amylase or lipase >3×ULN, history of gastric-related surgeries, history of pancreatitis, medullary thyroid carcinoma, or multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2, recent weight-loss attempts or pregnancy plans
intervention: Ebenatide 2 mg (0.2 ml) subcutaneous injection once weekly for 52 weeks. All subjects continued structured medical nutrition therapy and moderate-intensity physical activity throughout the study. Participants on metformin pre-enrollment continued their stable doses
comparison: Placebo subcutaneous injection once weekly for 24 weeks, followed by Ebenatide for 28 weeks. 2:1 allocation ratio (Ebenatide:placebo). All subjects continued structured medical nutrition therapy and moderate-intensity physical activity throughout the study
outcomes_primary: Glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) at 24 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Fasting blood glucose, continuous glucose monitoring parameters (mean blood glucose, time in range, time above range, time below range, standard deviation, coefficient of variation, area under the curve for hyperglycemia, area under the curve for hypoglycemia), triglyceride-glucose index, body composition parameters (body weight, BMI, percent body fat, visceral fat area, body fat mass, fat mass index, waist circumference, waist-to-height ratio, skeletal lean mass, fat free mass, skeletal muscle mass, skeletal muscle mass index), blood pressure (systolic and diastolic), hemoglobin levels, serum amylase, serum lipase, adverse events
extraction_notes: Primary endpoint explicitly stated as HbA1c at 24 weeks in sample size calculation section. Secondary outcomes not explicitly labeled as such but multiple additional outcomes were assessed. Placebo group crossed over to Ebenatide at week 24, limiting between-group comparisons at week 52

title: Effects of retatrutide on body composition in people with type 2 diabetes: a substudy of a phase 2, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled, randomised trial.
population: Adults aged 18-75 years with type 2 diabetes, HbA1c criteria (specific threshold not fully stated in abstract)
intervention: Retatrutide at doses of 0.5 mg, 4 mg (pooled), 8 mg (pooled), and 12 mg for 36 weeks
comparison: Placebo; Dulaglutide 1.5 mg
outcomes_primary: Percent change from baseline to week 36 in total body fat mass
outcomes_secondary: Lean mass loss as proportion of weight loss; adverse events; serious adverse events
extraction_notes: HbA1c eligibility criterion appears truncated in abstract. Route and frequency of administration not specified. This is a substudy of a larger phase 2 trial with body composition assessed via DXA scans.

title: Changes in β-Cell Function and Insulin Sensitivity During Treatment With Dapagliflozin Alone or in Combination With Exenatide in Type 2 Diabetes.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes (n=90)
intervention: Dapagliflozin alone, exenatide alone, or dapagliflozin/exenatide combination therapy
comparison: Placebo (n=15), dapagliflozin (n=25), exenatide (n=25), dapagliflozin/exenatide (n=25)
outcomes_primary: β-cell function (BCF) indices calculated during oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT)
outcomes_secondary: Corrected Matsuda index (cMI) for urinary glucose loss, insulin secretion, insulin sensitivity
extraction_notes: Specific doses, routes, and frequencies of dapagliflozin and exenatide not provided in abstract. Study design includes acute (single dose) assessment and chronic assessment at 1 and 4 months of therapy. 180-minute OGTT used for all measurements.

title: Dapagliflozin's impact on hormonal regulation and ketogenesis in type 1 diabetes: a randomised controlled crossover trial.
population: Adults with type 1 diabetes (C-peptide concentrations <0.1 nmol/l) with duration >5 years and BMI of 20-29 kg/m2; exclusion criteria: renal or hepatic dysfunction, history of malignancy, intake of drugs influencing glucose homeostasis during last 3 months, alcohol or drug abuse, active smoking (five or more cigarettes per day), pregnancy
intervention: Dapagliflozin 10 mg orally daily for 7 days as adjunct to insulin therapy
comparison: Placebo daily for 7 days as adjunct to insulin therapy (crossover design with 14 day washout period)
outcomes_primary: GLP-1 concentrations during OGTT clamp (OGTTC)
outcomes_secondary: GLP-1 concentrations during hyperinsulinaemic-euglycaemic clamp (HEC); glucagon concentrations during OGTTC and HEC; somatostatin concentrations during OGTTC and HEC; total ketone body concentrations during OGTTC and HEC; exploratory outcome: plasma glucose concentrations during OGTTC
extraction_notes: Open-label crossover study design; protocol change from AUC to unit-based outcomes for primary endpoint analysis

title: Long-acting PYY
population: Phase 1: Adult male participants aged 18-55 years, weight ≥70 kg, BMI 25.0-34.9 kg/m², HbA1c <6.5%. Phase 2: Male and female adult participants with obesity, BMI 30.0-45.0 kg/m², HbA1c <6.5%, no history of type 1 or type 2 diabetes.
intervention: Phase 1 Part 1: Single subcutaneous dose of PYY1875 (0.1, 0.3, 0.6, 1.2, or 2.1 mg). Phase 1 Part 2: Single subcutaneous dose of PYY1875 (0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 0.6, 1.2, or 1.7 mg) plus semaglutide 0.25 mg. Phase 2: Once-weekly subcutaneous PYY1875 1.0 mg or 2.0 mg (escalated over 8-10 weeks) as add-on to once-weekly semaglutide 2.4 mg for 16 weeks.
comparison: Phase 1: Placebo (randomized 6:2 PYY1875:placebo). Phase 2: Placebo as add-on to semaglutide 2.4 mg (randomized 2:1 PYY1875:placebo).
outcomes_primary: Phase 1: Number of treatment emergent adverse events (TEAEs) from day 1 to follow-up at day 36 (extended to day 54 for some cohorts). Phase 2 Part 1: Number of TEAEs from dosing (day 1) to end of study (week 24). Phase 2 Part 2: Change (percentage) in body weight from baseline (week 32) to end of treatment (week 48).
outcomes_secondary: Phase 1: PK endpoints (AUC0-INF, AUC0-168h, Cmax, tmax, t1/2); exploratory PD endpoints including change in body weight, fasting glucose, glucagon, insulin, C-peptide, ghrelin, leptin, and soluble leptin receptor. Phase 2: Number of TEAEs and serious TEAEs from week 0 to end of study; change from baseline to end of treatment in body weight (kg), HbA1c (percentage points), fasting plasma glucose, fasting insulin, waist circumference; relative change in total, HDL, LDL, VLDL cholesterol, triglycerides, and free fatty acids.
extraction_notes: This publication reports multiple studies: preclinical rat studies, a phase 1 first-in-human study (NCT03707990), and a phase 2 dose-finding study (NCT04969939). PICO extraction focused on the clinical studies. Phase 2 had two parts with different designs: Part 1 was coescalation, Part 2 included a 32-week semaglutide run-in before randomization.

title: Effect of the GLP-1 receptor agonist exenatide on pro-inflammatory and metabolic biomarkers in individuals with alcohol use disorder: Post hoc results from a randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled clinical trial.
population: Individuals diagnosed with alcohol use disorder (AUD), aged 18-70 years. Key exclusion criteria: severe psychiatric or somatic comorbidity, concomitant pharmacotherapy against AUD, diabetes, impaired renal and hepatic function. A comparison group of individuals without AUD matched on sex, age, and educational status was included.
intervention: Exenatide 2 mg subcutaneous injection once weekly for 26 weeks
comparison: Placebo once weekly for 26 weeks
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified as primary. 25 pro-inflammatory and metabolic biomarkers measured: IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-2, IL-4, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, IL-12p70, IL-13, MCP-1, C-peptide, GIP, GLP-1, glucagon, insulin, leptin, PP, adiponectin, hsCRP, FGF-21, total cholesterol, HDL, LDL, and triglycerides
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly specified
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of a previously conducted RCT. The original trial's primary outcome was alcohol intake, not the biomarkers evaluated in this study. No clear distinction between primary and secondary outcomes for this post hoc analysis. The 23 individuals without AUD served as a cross-sectional comparison group for baseline values only, not as a randomized comparator.

title: Predictors of Initial and Sustained Glycemic and Weight Response to Tirzepatide: A Post Hoc Analysis of SURPASS-4.
population: Adults aged ≥18 years with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled (HbA1c 58–91 mmol/mol [7.5–10.5%]) with any combination of metformin, sulfonylurea, and/or sodium–glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor, BMI ≥25 kg/m², stable weight during previous 3 months, and at increased cardiovascular risk
intervention: Tirzepatide 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg once weekly
comparison: Insulin glargine once daily (treat-to-target)
outcomes_primary: Mean change in HbA1c at 52 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Achievement of HbA1c ≤48 mmol/mol (6.5%), achievement of HbA1c <39 mmol/mol (5.7%), sustained glycemic control after 52 weeks, weight loss ≥10%, sustained weight loss after 52 weeks, predictors of initial and sustained glycemic and weight response
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of the SURPASS-4 trial (NCT03730662). The analysis focused on sustainability of outcomes and predictors of response rather than primary efficacy comparison. Variable treatment period up to 104 weeks with median 81 weeks exposure.

title: Semaglutide Improves Lipid Subfraction Profiles in Type 2 Diabetes: Insights from a One-Year Follow-Up Study.
population: Adults aged over 45 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus for at least 5 years, inadequate glycemic control on metformin monotherapy (HbA1c 6.5-10%), BMI >25 kg/m2, eGFR >60 mL/min/1.73 m2. Exclusions: type 1 diabetes, previous GLP-1RA or DPP-4 inhibitor treatment, active smoking, alcohol consumption, pregnancy, breastfeeding, documented coronary or cerebrovascular event, clinically significant heart failure (NYHA II-IV), acute pancreatitis, pancreatic or thyroid cancer, severe liver failure (Child-Pugh B and C), chronic systemic glucocorticoids or immunosuppressants, advanced diabetic retinopathy, diabetic nephropathy or severe renal impairment, active malignant disease
intervention: Subcutaneous semaglutide once weekly, titrated from 0.25 mg/week (weeks 0-4) to 0.5 mg/week (weeks 4-8) to 1 mg/week (week 8 onwards), added to metformin monotherapy, for 52 weeks
comparison: Oral sitagliptin 100 mg once daily added to metformin monotherapy; age- and body weight-matched non-diabetic obese controls (medication-free)
outcomes_primary: Changes in LDL and HDL lipoprotein subfractions measured by Lipoprint gel electrophoresis
outcomes_secondary: Changes in anthropometric measurements (BMI, waist circumference), glycemic parameters (fasting glucose, fructosamine, HbA1c), lipid parameters (total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, non-HDL cholesterol, triglycerides), apolipoprotein A1 and B levels, inflammatory markers (hsCRP), renal function parameters (creatinine, eGFR)
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the text; classification based on stated study objectives. Control group was non-diabetic and served for baseline comparison only, not as a treatment comparator.

title: Gradual Titration of Semaglutide Results in Better Treatment Adherence and Fewer Adverse Events: A Randomized Controlled Open-Label Pilot Study Examining a 16-Week Flexible Titration Regimen Versus Label-Recommended 8-Week Semaglutide Titration Regimen.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D)
intervention: Flexible titration of semaglutide: starting at 0.0675 mg (measured as five clicks made by the dose selector dial), with gradual increases by 0.0675 mg/week and delays for gastrointestinal adverse events, for 26 weeks
comparison: Label-recommended titration of semaglutide: 0.25 mg, 0.5 mg, 1 mg at 4-week intervals for 26 weeks
outcomes_primary: Treatment adherence (withdrawal due to gastrointestinal adverse events)
outcomes_secondary: Gastrointestinal adverse events (nausea, asthenia), days experiencing nausea, HbA1c change, BMI change
extraction_notes: Primary outcome not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in abstract; outcomes categorization inferred from study objective. Sample size: 104 patients randomized.

title: Weight reduction over time in tirzepatide-treated participants by early weight loss response: Post hoc analysis in SURMOUNT-1.
population: Adults with body mass index (BMI) ≥30 kg/m2 or ≥27 kg/m2 with at least one weight-related complication, excluding diabetes; post hoc analysis limited to participants treated with tirzepatide who received ≥75% of assigned treatment doses and had weight measurements at Weeks 0, 12, 24 and 72
intervention: Tirzepatide 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg once weekly subcutaneously; initiated at 2.5 mg once weekly and increased in 2.5 mg increments every 4 weeks through 20-week dose escalation period; target dose achieved at Week 4 (5 mg), Week 12 (10 mg), or Week 20 (15 mg); combined with lifestyle counselling (500 calorie/day deficit and at least 150 minutes physical activity per week); 72 weeks duration
comparison: Within-group comparison of late responders (<5% weight reduction at Week 12) versus early responders (≥5% weight reduction at Week 12); original trial included placebo arm but this post hoc analysis focused on tirzepatide-treated participants only
outcomes_primary: Proportion of participants achieving weight reduction targets (≥5%, ≥10%, ≥15%, ≥20%, ≥25%) at Week 24 and Week 72
outcomes_secondary: Mean percent body weight reduction trajectory over time; time to reach 5% weight reduction for late responders
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of the SURMOUNT-1 trial (NCT04184622). The original trial was a phase 3 RCT with placebo control, but this analysis only included tirzepatide-treated participants. Primary and secondary outcomes were not explicitly labeled as such in the post hoc analysis.

title: The effects of collagen peptide supplementation on appetite and post-exercise energy intake in females: a randomised controlled trial.
population: Healthy, physically active females aged 18-30 years, classified as Tier 1 (recreationally active meeting WHO minimum activity guidelines) or Tier 2 (trained/developmental, training regularly with specific sport identification), not taking supplements or medications that may interfere with appetite, free from health conditions or food allergies that could affect study outcomes
intervention: 15 g/day of bovine collagen peptides consumed orally upon waking for 7 days, provided in 150 ml volume in opaque bottles, with final dose consumed 10 minutes after 45-minute cycling exercise at ~55% Wmax on day 7
comparison: Taste-matched non-energy control (water with cherry flavoring) consumed in identical manner (15 ml upon waking for 7 days, with final dose post-exercise on day 7)
outcomes_primary: Ad libitum energy intake at pasta meal provided 60 minutes post-supplementation on day 7
outcomes_secondary: Subjective appetite sensations (hunger, fullness, desire to eat, thirst, prospective food consumption, composite appetite score) measured via visual analogue scale; gastrointestinal symptoms (nausea, headache, GI discomfort, urge to defecate); blood glucose concentrations; appetite-related hormone concentrations (total ghrelin, glucagon-like peptide-1, peptide YY, cholecystokinin, dipeptidyl peptidase-4, leptin, insulin); eating rate; heart rate and rating of perceived exertion during exercise
extraction_notes: Randomised double-blind crossover study design with minimum 7-day washout. n=15 completed study (n=17 recruited, 2 excluded). Blood data presented for n=14 due to sampling issues. CCK data presented for n=9 due to detection limits. Physical activity data for n=13 due to watch failures.

title: Tirzepatide Treatment and Associated Changes in β-Cell Function and Insulin Sensitivity in People With Obesity or Overweight With Prediabetes or Normoglycemia: A Post Hoc Analysis From the SURMOUNT-1 Trial.
population: Adults with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2) or overweight (BMI ≥27 kg/m2) with one or more weight-related comorbidity, excluding diabetes, with either prediabetes or normoglycemia at baseline
intervention: Once-weekly subcutaneous tirzepatide (5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg) for 72 weeks in conjunction with lifestyle modification
comparison: Placebo once weekly for 72 weeks in conjunction with lifestyle modification
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified as primary in this post hoc analysis; assessed outcomes include model-derived parameters of β-cell function (insulin secretion rate, β-cell glucose sensitivity, ISR at 5.4 mmol/L, total insulin secretion during OGTT, potentiation of ISR, β-cell rate sensitivity, 30-min insulinogenic index) and insulin sensitivity (Matsuda index, oral glucose insulin sensitivity, HOMA2-IR)
outcomes_secondary: Changes in HbA1c, fasting serum glucose, fasting serum insulin, body weight, glucose AUC during OGTT, insulin AUC during OGTT, C-peptide AUC during OGTT
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of the SURMOUNT-1 trial. Primary and secondary outcomes are not explicitly distinguished in this analysis; outcomes listed are those assessed in this post hoc investigation. The original SURMOUNT-1 trial had different primary outcomes.

title: Impact of Body Mass Index, Central Adiposity, and Weight Loss on the Benefits of Tirzepatide in HFpEF: The SUMMIT Trial.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
population: Patients with NYHA functional class II-IV heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and body mass index (BMI) ≥30 kg/m²
intervention: Tirzepatide (long-acting glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor and glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonist)
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Composite of cardiovascular death or worsening heart failure
outcomes_secondary: 6-minute walk distance (6MWD); Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score (KCCQ-CSS); body weight change; systolic blood pressure; waist circumference; C-reactive protein (CRP)
extraction_notes: This is a secondary analysis of the SUMMIT trial examining heterogeneity by baseline BMI and waist-to-hip ratio (WHR) tertiles. Full tirzepatide dosing details not provided in abstract. BMI threshold appears truncated in abstract (≥30 kg/m²).

title: Effect of semaglutide versus placebo on cardiorenal outcomes by prior cardiovascular disease and baseline body mass index: Pooled post hoc analysis of SUSTAIN 6 and PIONEER 6.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes at high cardiovascular risk, aged ≥50 years with established cardiovascular disease (including previous cardiovascular, cerebrovascular or peripheral vascular disease), chronic heart failure or chronic kidney disease, or aged ≥60 years with at least one cardiovascular risk factor. Exclusion criteria included long-term or intermittent haemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis; for PIONEER 6, estimated glomerular filtration rate <30 mL/min/1.73 m² was also an exclusion criterion.
intervention: Semaglutide: once-weekly subcutaneous 0.5 or 1.0 mg (SUSTAIN 6) or once-daily oral 14 mg (PIONEER 6)
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Time to first primary major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), defined as a composite of cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or non-fatal stroke
outcomes_secondary: Expanded MACE (primary MACE plus hospitalisation for unstable angina pectoris or heart failure); cardiovascular death; all-cause death; non-fatal myocardial infarction; non-fatal stroke; new or worsening nephropathy (composite of new onset of persistent macroalbuminuria ≥300 mg/g, persistent doubling of serum creatinine level and eGFR ≤45 mL/min/1.73 m², continuous kidney replacement therapy, or death due to kidney disease) assessed in SUSTAIN 6 population only
extraction_notes: This is a pooled post hoc analysis of two trials (SUSTAIN 6, N=3297 and PIONEER 6, N=3183). Kidney outcomes were only assessed in SUSTAIN 6 population. Subgroup analyses were performed by prior cardiovascular disease status and baseline BMI categories.

title: Effects of combined metformin and semaglutide therapy on body weight, metabolic parameters, and reproductive outcomes in overweight/obese women with polycystic ovary syndrome: a prospective, randomized, controlled, open-label clinical trial.
population: Overweight or obese women with PCOS diagnosed according to Rotterdam criteria, aged 18-40 years, BMI ≥24 kg/m², lack of response to lifestyle interventions for 3 months prior to enrollment, with infertility duration exceeding 2 years without contraceptive use. Exclusions: allergy to GLP-1 RAs or metformin, pre-existing diabetes (type 1 or 2), congenital adrenal hyperplasia, Cushing's syndrome, androgen-secreting tumors, abnormal liver function (ALT >2.5 times upper limit of normal), impaired kidney function (eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m²), use of glucocorticoids, estrogen, progesterone, insulin or other drugs affecting reproduction within 3 months, severe gynecological conditions causing infertility or severe male factor infertility, inability to comply with follow-up, planning pregnancy within 16 weeks or currently pregnant
intervention: Combination therapy (COM): Metformin 1000 mg twice daily plus semaglutide 1 mg once weekly for 16 weeks (semaglutide initiated at 0.25 mg, increased to 0.5 mg at 4 weeks and 1 mg at 8 weeks). comparison: Metformin monotherapy (MET): Metformin 1000 mg twice daily for 16 weeks (initiated at 500 mg daily, gradually increased by 500 mg every 3 days), then continued at 1000 mg twice daily for additional 24 weeks
outcomes_primary: Changes in anthropometric measures related to obesity (body weight, BMI, waist-to-hip ratio) assessed at Week 0 and Week 16
outcomes_secondary: Alterations in reproductive hormone levels, glucose and lipid metabolism, C-reactive protein (CRP) levels assessed at Week 0 and Week 16; pregnancy outcomes (natural pregnancy rate, total pregnancy rate) assessed between Weeks 16 and 40
extraction_notes: Metformin dose escalation described as starting at 500 mg QD and increasing until reaching 1000 mg BID. Semaglutide dose in abstract stated as 1-mg QW but titration schedule provided in methods section.

title: Early-Onset Obesity and Tirzepatide Treatment: A Post Hoc Analysis of the SURMOUNT Clinical Trials.
population: Adults aged 18 years or older with BMI ≥30 kg/m2 or BMI ≥27 kg/m2 with at least one weight-related comorbidity (e.g., hypertension, dyslipidemia, obstructive sleep apnea, cardiovascular disease), who reported one or more unsuccessful dietary efforts to lose weight, without diabetes. intervention: Tirzepatide once weekly subcutaneous injection at doses of 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg (SURMOUNT-1) or maximum tolerated dose (SURMOUNT-3 and SURMOUNT-4) for 72-88 weeks
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Percent change and absolute change from baseline in body weight at week 72 (SURMOUNT-1 and SURMOUNT-3) or week 88 (SURMOUNT-4)
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of participants reaching body weight reduction thresholds (≥5%, ≥10%, ≥15%, ≥20%, ≥25%); changes in cardiometabolic parameters including waist circumference, HbA1c, systolic blood pressure, triglycerides, HDL cholesterol, LDL cholesterol; changes in insulin sensitivity (HOMA2-IR); safety measures including treatment-emergent adverse events and serious adverse events
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis pooling data from three phase 3 randomized controlled trials (SURMOUNT-1, SURMOUNT-3, SURMOUNT-4). SURMOUNT-2 was excluded because participants had type 2 diabetes. SURMOUNT-3 included participants who achieved ≥5% body weight reduction after a 12-week intensive lifestyle intervention. SURMOUNT-4 included a 36-week open-label tirzepatide lead-in period before randomization. Age at obesity diagnosis was derived from patient-reported duration of obesity.

title: Efficacy and safety of beinaglutide with continuous subcutaneous infusion in newly diagnosed patients with type 2 diabetes: a randomized, control, open-labeled clinical trial.

comparison: Continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII) alone for 4 weeks
outcomes_primary: Body weight change from baseline to endpoint
outcomes_secondary: BMI change, proportion achieving ≥5% body weight loss, glycemic control, insulin dose requirements, β-cell function, adverse events
extraction_notes: Open-label study design. Sample size small (n=30). Randomization ratio 1:1. Secondary outcomes not explicitly labeled as such but inferred from methods description of OGTT and CGM assessments.

title: Exenatide Once Weekly in the Treatment of Patients with Multiple System Atrophy.
population: Men and women aged 30 to 80 years with diagnosis of possible or probable multiple system atrophy (MSA) of parkinsonian (MSA-P) or cerebellar subtype (MSA-C) according to Gilman Criteria, less than 5 years from documented MSA diagnosis or from previously documented parkinsonian/ataxic neurological condition later re-diagnosed as MSA, able to walk at least 10 meters with or without assistance, anticipated survival of at least 3 years. intervention: Subcutaneous exenatide (Bydureon or Bydureon BCise) 2 mg once weekly for 48 weeks in addition to standard of care, followed by 48-week washout period
comparison: Standard of care alone (contemporaneous controls) for 48 weeks followed by 48-week washout period
outcomes_primary: Unified Multiple System Atrophy Rating Scale (UMSARS) parts I + II combined score at 48 weeks
outcomes_secondary: At 48 and 96 weeks: loss of independent ambulation (score of 4 in UMSARS part I item 7), timed walk, MSA-Quality of Life (MSA-QOL) scores, UMSARS parts I, II, III, and IV scores, anti-parkinsonian or anti-orthostatic hypotension medication use, number of falls, proportion of participants reaching score ≥ 3 on UMSARS part I items 1 (speech), 2 (swallowing), and 8 (falling), Clinician Global Impression of Change (CGI), Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) scores. Exploratory outcomes: digital mobility outcomes (daily step count, walking speed, stride length), grey matter/white matter volume on MRI, plasma and CSF neurofilament light chain levels, CSF alpha-synuclein oligomer levels
extraction_notes: Open-label, single-center, randomized parallel-group trial. Stratified randomization by disease subtype (MSA-P vs MSA-C). Single rater performed UMSARS assessments.

title: Effects of Semaglutide With or Without Concomitant Mineralocorticoid Receptor Antagonist Use in Participants With Type 2 Diabetes and Chronic Kidney Disease: A FLOW Trial Prespecified Secondary Analysis.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease, with eGFR 25-75 mL/min/1.73 m2 and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio >300 to <5,000 mg/g (if eGFR ≥50 mL/min/1.73 m2) or >100 to <5,000 mg/g (if eGFR 25 to <50 mL/min/1.73 m2), receiving stable maximal labeled or tolerated dose of renin-angiotensin system inhibitor (or unable to tolerate/contraindicated)
intervention: Subcutaneous semaglutide 1.0 mg once weekly
comparison: Matching placebo once weekly

outcomes_secondary: Rate of loss of kidney function defined as total eGFR slope (annual rate of change in eGFR based on serum creatinine); time to first major adverse cardiovascular event (MACE: composite of nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or cardiovascular death); death from any cause; four-component kidney-specific composite outcome (excluding cardiovascular death from primary outcome); change in urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio; eGFR slope based on serum cystatin C; hyperkalemia; serious adverse events
extraction_notes: This is a prespecified secondary analysis of the FLOW trial examining effects by baseline mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA) use. The subgroup analysis compared outcomes in participants with baseline MRA use (n=257) versus without baseline MRA use (n=3,276). Indication for MRA use was not collected.

title: The Effects of 8-Week Hydrogen-Rich Water Consumption on Appetite, Body Composition, Sleep Quality, and Circulating Glucagon-like Peptide-1 in Obese Men and Women (HYDRAPPET): A Randomized Controlled Trial.
population: Adults aged 18-65 years, classified as obese (body fat >30% for women and >25% for men), sedentary (engaging in less than 150 min of moderate physical activity per week). Exclusion criteria: major chronic diseases or acute injuries, dietary supplement use within four weeks prior to study, obesity-related pharmaceutical use within eight weeks prior to study, refusal to consent to randomization, concurrent participation in other trials.
intervention: Hydrogen-rich water, 1.0 L daily (containing 15 mg of H2 total; 5 mg per 333 mL serving), administered three times daily (morning, early afternoon, and before dinner), for eight weeks
comparison: Control water (tap water), 1.0 L daily (containing 0 mg of H2), administered three times daily (333 mL per serving), identical appearance, texture, and sensory characteristics to intervention drink, for eight weeks
outcomes_primary: Change in appetite (total cravings score) from baseline to 8-week follow-up, assessed using the Food Cravings Questionnaire (FCQ)
outcomes_secondary: Appetite assessments (five dimensions of food cravings); body composition indices (body weight, BMI, waist circumference, fat mass, fat-free mass, muscle mass, body water compartments, protein mass, mineral mass, total body calcium, glycogen mass); obesity-related quality of life (IWQOL-Lite questionnaire covering physical function, self-esteem, sexual life, public distress, and work); sleep quality components (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index covering subjective sleep quality, sleep latency, sleep duration, sleep efficiency, sleep disturbance, use of sleep medication, and daytime dysfunction); biochemical markers (fasting glucose, total cholesterol, triglycerides, lipoproteins, short-chain fatty acids including acetic acid, propionic acid, and butyric acid, plasma GLP-1 levels, breath molecular hydrogen levels); prevalence and severity of side effects
extraction_notes: Primary endpoint explicitly stated as change in appetite (total cravings score) from baseline to follow-up. Sample size calculation was based on primary outcome. 36 participants randomized but 35 completed the study (1 lost to follow-up).

title: Germinated and Extruded Sorghum Beverage Presented Good Sensorial Acceptance and Improves Insulin and Satiety in Normoglycemic Adults: An Acute Randomized Controlled Crossover Trial.

title: Exenatide for diagnosing endogenous hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia: a randomized placebo-controlled, double-blind, cross-over proof-of-principle study.

title: Oral Semaglutide in an East Asian Population With Overweight or Obesity, With or Without Type 2 Diabetes: The OASIS 2 Randomized Clinical Trial.

title: Insulin DEgludec/LIraglutide versus multiple daily insulin injections in the transition from hospital to outpatient management assessed by continuous glucose monitoring: the DELI transition trial.
population: Adults aged over 18 years with type 2 diabetes, HbA1c levels ≥64 mmol/mol (≥8.0%) and ≤140 mmol/mol (≤15%), hospitalized in a general ward, requiring multiple daily insulin injections during hospitalization and eligible for MDI therapy at transition from hospital to outpatient care. All patients were Hispanic. Exclusions: eGFR <15 ml/min per 1.73 m², history of acute or chronic pancreatitis in last 3 months, hypersensitivity to IDegLira components, pregnant or breastfeeding women, receiving GLP-1 receptor agonists for obesity treatment, previous MDI therapy with total daily dose >70 units/day or <10 units/day, steroid-associated hyperglycemia.
intervention: Insulin degludec/liraglutide (IDegLira) fixed combination, starting at 10 IU if no insulin used prior to hospitalization or 16 IU if insulin previously used at any dose, administered once daily starting on day 1 after hospital discharge, with dose titration according to DUAL VII study protocol over 4 weeks.
comparison: Multiple daily insulin injections (MDI) with total daily dose reduced by 20% from end of hospitalization for outpatient treatment, with basal and preprandial insulin titrated according to DUAL VII study protocol over 4 weeks.
outcomes_primary: Percentage of patients with at least one hypoglycemic episode (defined as more than 15 minutes with glucose levels <3.0 mmol/l documented by continuous glucose monitoring) within the first 4 weeks after hospital discharge.
outcomes_secondary: CGM metrics including time in range (TIR 3.8–10 mmol/l), coefficient of variation (CV), time above range (TAR >10 mmol/l or >13.9 mmol/l), time below range (TBR <3.0 mmol/l or <3.8 mmol/l), glucose management indicator (GMI), hypoglycemia event density, severe hypoglycemic episodes, composite outcomes (percentage of patients with TIR >70% without hypoglycemia episodes, mean glucose <8.5 mmol/l without hypoglycemia episodes <3.0 mmol/l), body weight change, adverse events.
extraction_notes: Open-label randomized controlled trial. Follow-up duration was 4 weeks (28 days). Single-center study conducted in Bogotá, Colombia.

title: Effect of tirzepatide treatment on patient-reported outcomes among SURMOUNT-OSA participants with obstructive sleep apnea and obesity.
population: Adults with moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea (AHI ≥15 events per hour) and obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m²). Study 1 included participants unable or unwilling to use PAP therapy. outcomes_secondary: Change from baseline to Week 52 in: PROMIS Short-Form Sleep-related Impairment 8a scores, PROMIS Short-Form v1.0 Sleep Disturbance 8b scores, Epworth Sleepiness Scale scores (excessive daytime sleepiness), Functional Outcomes of Sleep Questionnaire (FOSQ) Total score and domain scores, FOSQ-10 Total score, SF-36v2 acute form domain and component summary scores, EQ-5D-5L Health State Index and Visual Analog Scale scores, Patient Global Impression of Status (PGIS-OSA) symptom scales, Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC-OSA) symptom scales
extraction_notes: This is a secondary analysis of the SURMOUNT-OSA trials (NCT05412004). The primary endpoint of the parent SURMOUNT-OSA trial (AHI reduction) is referenced but not the focus of this analysis. Week 20 analyses were exploratory.

title: Comparative Efficacy of Endoscopic Sleeve Gastroplasty (Esg) Versus Liraglutide in Weight Loss and Remission Of Obesity-Related Comorbidities: Twelve Months Follow-Up Results.

outcomes_primary: Weight loss outcomes including percentage of excess weight loss (%EWL) and total weight loss (%TWL)
outcomes_secondary: Resolution of obesity-related comorbidities; safety (major complications and significant side effects)
extraction_notes: Liraglutide dose, route, and frequency not specified in abstract. Follow-up period is 12 months with assessments at 3, 6, and 12 months post-intervention.

title: Gut Hormones and Postprandial Metabolic Effects of Isomaltulose vs. Saccharose Consumption in People with Metabolic Syndrome.
population: Adults with metabolic syndrome; normal glucose tolerance confirmed by oral glucose tolerance test (75g glucose); 15 participants included from 24 screened

outcomes_primary: Prandial incretin responses to subsequent meal including GLP-1, GIP, and PYY concentrations; glucose ascent rate; second meal effect

extraction_notes: Primary outcome not explicitly labeled as such; outcomes inferred from study aims stated as assessing most effective preprandial interval to enhance prandial incretin responses. Blood samples collected at 15 predefined time points over 9 hours. Technical error noted with DPP-4 inhibitor application during Intervention B affecting GLP-1/GIP measurements at time points 195, 210, and 240 min.

title: Glycemic Benefit of Insulin Degludec/Insulin Aspart Compared to Basal Insulin in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Associated with Impaired Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Response: A Randomized Crossover Trial.
population: Adults aged 18 years or older with type 2 diabetes mellitus; on once-daily basal insulin (glargine U-100, glargine U-300, or degludec) for at least 4 months at a dose of less than 1.0 unit/kg/day; HbA1c levels between 7.0% and 10.0%; fasting plasma glucose lower than that predicted by concurrent HbA1c at least two times consecutively; regularly prescribed in a referral hospital

outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline after 20 weeks of treatment

extraction_notes: Randomized crossover design with two 20-week treatment periods without washout period. Incretin profile analysis (GLP-1 and GIP response) was an additional exploratory analysis. Trial registration: KCT0004597

title: Efficacy and safety of oral semaglutide in Chinese participants with type 2 diabetes: Subgroup analyses by baseline characteristics in the PIONEER 11 and 12 randomised controlled trials.
