Exclusion criteria included: current or past GLP-1 agonist use, insulin treatment within previous 3 months, metabolic acidosis or ketonemia, positive GAD or IA-2A autoantibodies, allergy to study medications or milk protein, hemoglobin <11 g/dL, triglycerides ≥500 mg/dl, body weight ≤58 or ≥205 kg.

title: An experimental medicine protocol for exploring the haemodynamic effects of dual agonism at the glucagon-like peptide-1 and glucagon receptor in healthy subjects.
population: Healthy non-smoking adult male participants aged 18-40 years with body mass index 18-30 kg/m2, without hypertension, clinically significant heart disease, renal or liver impairment, or diabetes
intervention: Part A: Intravenous glucagon at 25 ng/kg/min (low dose) or 50 ng/kg/min (high dose) for 120 minutes. Part B: Intravenous exenatide (50 ng/min loading dose for 30 minutes then 25 ng/min) and/or glucagon 25 ng/kg/min for 60 minutes, including exenatide:glucagon co-infusion
comparison: 0.9% normal saline (placebo control); participants acted as their own control in a crossover design with Latin square block randomization
outcomes_primary: Heart rate, rate pressure product (heart rate multiplied by systolic blood pressure), cardiac output, stroke volume, blood pressure (brachial and central systolic and diastolic, mean arterial pressure), peripheral vascular resistance, augmentation index, heart rate variability
outcomes_secondary: Metabolic parameters including blood glucose, plasma insulin, C-peptide, total GLP-1, total active GLP-1, glucagon, glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), peptide YY, free fatty acids, triglycerides; adverse events including hypoglycaemia, nausea, vomiting
extraction_notes: This was an exploratory pilot study without formal power calculations. Primary and secondary outcomes were not explicitly distinguished in the abstract or methods; outcomes listed are based on measurement descriptions. Part A was a dose-comparison study (n=7) and Part B was the dual-agonism study (n=12). Single-blinded design (participants blinded, study team unblinded).

title: RISING STARS: Effects of a GLP-1 receptor polymorphism on responses to liraglutide.
population: Adults aged 18 to 65 years with obesity (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2) and pre-diabetes as defined by American Diabetes Association criteria
intervention: Liraglutide 1.8 mg/day subcutaneous injection for 14 weeks
comparison: Sitagliptin 100 mg/day oral; Hypocaloric diet
outcomes_primary: Effects of rs6923761 GLP-1R variant on anthropometric, metabolic, and circulating measures including weight change, fasting glucose, fasting insulin, C-peptide, glucagon, HOMA-IR, hemoglobin A1c, insulinogenic index, Matsuda index of insulin sensitivity, disposition index
outcomes_secondary: Plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1), inflammatory markers (MCP-1, IFNg, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, TNFa), fasting GLP-1, fasting GIP
extraction_notes: This is a pre-specified genetic subgroup analysis of an RCT (NCT03101930). Treatment with liraglutide and sitagliptin was double-blind and placebo-controlled; hypocaloric diet was unblinded. Randomization was 2:1:1 ratio stratified by race. Primary and secondary outcome distinction based on explicit mention of 'pre-specified analyses' and protocol references.

title: Semaglutide and Exercise Function in Obesity-Related HFpEF: Insights From the STEP-HFpEF Program.
population: Patients with obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF); left ventricular ejection fraction ≥45%; body mass index ≥30 kg/m²; NYHA functional class II to IV; Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Clinical Summary Score <90 points; objective evidence of HF defined by elevated filling pressures, elevated natriuretic peptide levels with echocardiographic abnormalities, or HF hospitalization in preceding 12 months with ongoing diuretic treatment and/or echocardiographic abnormalities; baseline 6-minute walk distance ≥100 m; STEP-HFpEF enrolled patients without type 2 diabetes, STEP-HFpEF DM enrolled patients with type 2 diabetes
intervention: Semaglutide 2.4 mg subcutaneously once weekly for 52 weeks on top of standard of care
comparison: Matching placebo subcutaneously once weekly for 52 weeks on top of standard of care
outcomes_primary: Change in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire-Clinical Summary Score (KCCQ-CSS) from baseline to 52 weeks; percent change in body weight from baseline to 52 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Change in 6-minute walk distance (6MWD) from baseline to 52 weeks; hierarchical composite endpoint comprising all-cause death, HF events, and differences in thresholds of change in KCCQ-CSS and 6MWD from baseline to 52 weeks; change in C-reactive protein from baseline to 52 weeks; change in plasma NT-proBNP levels (exploratory); serious adverse events including cardiac SAEs and SAEs leading to permanent treatment discontinuation
extraction_notes: This is a prespecified secondary analysis of pooled data from two trials (STEP-HFpEF and STEP-HFpEF DM). The focus of this analysis was on 6MWD and its correlates, which was a confirmatory secondary endpoint in the original trials.

title: Relationship Between Metabolic and Histological Responses in People With Metabolic Dysfunction- Associated Steatohepatitis With and Without Type 2 Diabetes: Participant-Level Exploratory Analysis of the SYNERGY-NASH Trial With Tirzepatide.
population: Adults aged 18-80 years with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) with stage 2 or 3 fibrosis, BMI 27-50 kg/m2, with or without type 2 diabetes, NAFLD activity score ≥4 with at least 1 point for each subcomponent (steatosis, hepatocellular ballooning, lobular inflammation). Key exclusions: other chronic liver diseases, cirrhosis, evidence of hepatic decompensation, alcohol consumption exceeding 14 or 21 standard drinks per week for women and men respectively, uncontrolled type 2 diabetes (HbA1c >9.5%), treatment with insulin, GLP-1 receptor agonist, or other medications with potential to result in weight gain or loss.
intervention: Tirzepatide once-weekly subcutaneous injection at maintenance doses of 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg. Starting dose was 2.5 mg, increased by 2.5 mg every 4 weeks until target maintenance dose was achieved. Treatment duration: 52 weeks.
comparison: Placebo once-weekly subcutaneous injection
outcomes_primary: Resolution of MASH without worsening of fibrosis
outcomes_secondary: Improvement in fibrosis stage by at least one stage without worsening of MASH
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc participant-level exploratory analysis of the SYNERGY-NASH trial (NCT04166773). The analysis focused on 154 participants who completed study treatment, had an end-of-treatment liver biopsy, and were not treated with insulin. The analyses pooled all tirzepatide treatment groups for responder versus nonresponder status comparisons.

title: Acute effects of GIP and GLP-1 receptor antagonism in totally pancreatectomized individuals: A randomized double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover study.
population: Totally pancreatectomized individuals
intervention: Infusion of GIP receptor antagonist GIP(3-30)NH2 and/or GLP-1 receptor antagonist exendin(9-39)NH2 during 270-minute liquid mixed meal tests (480 kcal)
comparison: Placebo infusion
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes mentioned include: postprandial bone resorption, glucose metabolism, gastric emptying, appetite, food intake, triglycerides, and haemodynamics. Sample size is 12 participants. The abstract contains truncated text (GIP(3-30)NH appears incomplete in multiple locations). Study design is randomized double-blind placebo-controlled crossover with four conditions.

title: Efficacy and safety of iGlarLixi versus IDegAsp by baseline β-cell function in Chinese people with type 2 diabetes: Exploratory analyses of the Soli-D study.
population: Chinese adults aged ≥18 years with type 2 diabetes for ≥12 months, receiving stable metformin therapy (± one additional oral antidiabetic drug), with HbA1c 7.5%–11.0% (58–97 mmol/mol) if treated with metformin with or without SGLT-2 inhibitor, or HbA1c 7.0%–10.0% (53–86 mmol/mol) if treated with metformin plus a second non-SGLT-2i oral antidiabetic drug
intervention: iGlarLixi (insulin glargine 100 U/mL plus lixisenatide fixed-ratio combination), self-administered once daily within 1 hour before the first meal of the day, for 24 weeks
comparison: IDegAsp (insulin degludec plus insulin aspart; Ryzodeg 70/30), self-administered once daily prior to the largest meal of the day, for 24 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline to Week 24
outcomes_secondary: Proportion of participants achieving HbA1c <7.0% at Week 24; proportion achieving HbA1c <7.0% with no body weight gain and no hypoglycaemia at Week 24; change in fasting plasma glucose from baseline to Week 24; change in postprandial glucose from baseline to Week 24; change in body weight from baseline to Week 24; total insulin daily dose at Week 24 (absolute dose and dose by body weight); incidence and event rate of hypoglycaemia (ADA Levels 1, 2, or 3); incidence of gastrointestinal events (diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting)
extraction_notes: This is an exploratory subgroup analysis of the Soli-D study (NCT05413369) stratified by baseline fasting C-peptide and HOMA-β quartiles. The primary Soli-D study results were previously published. All OADs except metformin and SGLT-2 inhibitors were discontinued prior to randomisation.

title: Long-term comparative effectiveness of once-weekly semaglutide versus alternative treatments in a real-world US adult population with type 2 diabetes: a randomized pragmatic clinical trial.
population: Adults aged ≥18 years with type 2 diabetes treated with 1-2 oral antidiabetic medications (excluding semaglutide) requiring further treatment intensification for glycemic control, with recorded HbA1c value within past 90 days before randomization, current members of health plan with pharmacy benefits. Key exclusions: treatment with any medication indicated for diabetes other than metformin (later amended to 1-2 oral medications) in 30 days before eligibility assessment, pregnancy, breastfeeding, or intention to become pregnant.
intervention: Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide as add-on therapy to existing 1-2 oral antidiabetic medications. Starting dose, escalation regimen, and maintenance dose determined by treating physician according to local practice and product labeling. Maximum allowed dose was 1.0 mg per protocol. Treatment duration: 2 years.
comparison: Alternative treatment chosen by treating physician from commercially available oral or injectable glucose-lowering medications other than semaglutide, as add-on therapy to existing 1-2 oral antidiabetic medications. Participants in alternative treatment group could not switch to semaglutide.
outcomes_primary: Proportion of participants achieving HbA1c <7.0% (53.0 mmol/mol) at year 1
outcomes_secondary: Confirmatory secondary endpoints: change in HbA1c (percentage point) from baseline to years 1 and 2; proportion of participants achieving HbA1c <7.0% at year 2. Key secondary endpoints: change in body weight (percentage and kg) from baseline to years 1 and 2; change in systolic and diastolic blood pressure; time to treatment intensification, discontinuation, or change; patient-reported outcomes including Diabetes Treatment Satisfaction Questionnaire (DTSQ), 12-Item Short Form version 2 (SF-12), and Work Productivity and Activity Impairment: General Health (WPAI:GH) questionnaire at years 1 and 2. Safety endpoints: serious adverse events, adverse events leading to study drug discontinuation.
extraction_notes: Pragmatic open-label trial design with physician's choice comparator group. Protocol amended during enrollment to broaden eligibility criteria. Copayments equalized at maximum US$20 per month to minimize differential out-of-pocket costs. 71.3% of alternative treatment group received GLP-1 RAs (primarily dulaglutide 58.5%), 15.5% received SGLT-2 inhibitors.

title: Exposure-Response Analysis of Efsubaglutide Alfa in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
population: Drug-naïve patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus
intervention: Efsubaglutide alfa 1 mg, 2 mg, or 3 mg once-weekly subcutaneous injection
comparison: Placebo
extraction_notes: This is an exposure-response analysis rather than a standard efficacy trial. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly designated in abstract. Efficacy endpoints mentioned include HbA1c, fasting plasma glucose, area under the concentration-time curve for glucose during mixed-meal tolerance test, body weight, waist circumference, and body mass index. Study duration was 24-week double-blind period followed by 28-week open-label period.

title: Tirzepatide for sleep-disordered breathing in SURMOUNT-OSA: Time course and association with body weight.
population: Adults with moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea (AHI ≥15 events per hour) and obesity (BMI ≥30, or ≥27 in Japan). Study 1 included participants not using positive airway pressure (PAP) therapy at screening; Study 2 included participants using PAP therapy at screening.
intervention: Tirzepatide maximum tolerated dose (10 mg or 15 mg) once weekly subcutaneous injection for 52 weeks, plus structured lifestyle intervention
comparison: Placebo once weekly injection for 52 weeks, plus structured lifestyle intervention
outcomes_primary: Change in apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) measured by laboratory polysomnography; change in peripheral apnea-hypopnea index (pAHI) measured by WatchPAT 300
outcomes_secondary: Change in sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden (SASHB) measured by polysomnography and WatchPAT 300; percent change in body weight; oxygen desaturation index (ODI); time course of AHI and SASHB improvements; association between weight reduction and OSA improvements
extraction_notes: This is a post-hoc analysis of data from the SURMOUNT-OSA program (Study 1 and Study 2), both 52-week randomized double-blind placebo-controlled Phase 3 studies. Primary outcomes for the original trials (systolic blood pressure, hsCRP, self-reported daily functioning) were not the focus of this analysis. WatchPAT data collected only in Study 1.

title: Semaglutide and cardiovascular outcomes by baseline and changes in adiposity measurements: a prespecified analysis of the SELECT trial.
population: Patients aged at least 45 years with BMI of at least 27 kg/m², with overweight or obesity, with cardiovascular disease, without diabetes
intervention: Semaglutide
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE)
outcomes_secondary: Relationships between baseline adiposity measures (bodyweight, waist circumference), treatment-induced adiposity changes, and subsequent MACE risk; mediation analysis of waist circumference reduction on MACE benefit
extraction_notes: This is a prespecified secondary analysis of the SELECT trial. Semaglutide dose, route, frequency, and duration not specified in abstract. BMI threshold appears truncated in abstract text.

title: Changes to insulin requirements over time with semaglutide in adults with type 1 diabetes on insulin pump therapy: A post-hoc analysis of a double-blinded, randomised, crossover trial.
population: Adults aged ≥18 years with type 1 diabetes for ≥1 year, on insulin pump use for ≥3 months, HbA1c ≤11%, body mass index >21 kg/m², and no product monograph-based contraindications to semaglutide
intervention: Semaglutide up to maximum tolerated dose (≤1 mg), subcutaneously weekly, titrated as per product monograph: 0.25 mg weekly for 4 weeks, 0.5 mg weekly for 4 weeks, then 1 mg weekly onward, with de-escalation if subjective intolerance or investigator concern; 15 weeks duration per intervention period
comparison: Placebo (crossover design with randomised sequence of placebo and semaglutide, with 2-week washout between interventions)
outcomes_primary: Changes to insulin requirements over time (total, basal, and bolus insulin) during semaglutide titration
outcomes_secondary: Frequency of pump parameter adjustments at follow-ups; relative changes to pump parameters from baseline (insulin:carbohydrate ratios, pre-programmed basal rates, correction factors); CGM metrics (time-in-range 3.9-10 mmol/L, time below 3.9 mmol/L, time above 10 mmol/L); carbohydrate input changes
extraction_notes: This is a post-hoc analysis of a previously published double-blinded, randomised, crossover trial. The original trial's primary outcome was semaglutide versus placebo effects during automated insulin delivery after 15 weeks; this analysis focuses on the first 11 weeks of titration on routine pump therapy. Original trial enrolled 28 participants, 26 completed the semaglutide intervention and were included in this analysis.

title: Liraglutide and Weight Loss Among Suboptimal Responders to Metabolic Bariatric Surgery: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
population: Adults aged 20 to 65 years with anatomically correct adjustable gastric band, sleeve gastrectomy, one anastomosis gastric bypass, or Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (confirmed with barium swallow and/or endoscopy) at 12 to 36 months after surgery, with BMI greater than 35, stable weight (within 4-kg range during 3-month period), and suboptimal weight loss defined as: excess body weight loss 25% to 40% or total body weight loss 5% to 12% for adjustable gastric band; excess body weight loss 25% to 60% or total body weight loss 10% to 20% for sleeve gastrectomy, Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, and one anastomosis gastric bypass; or weight regain of 10% excess body weight loss or 5% total body weight loss after reaching nadir
intervention: Liraglutide 6 mg/mL in prefilled multidose disposable pens, self-administered daily subcutaneously, self-titrated from 0.6 mg in week 1 increasing by 0.6 mg/day per week until 3.0 mg reached by week 5, intended treatment duration 12 months
comparison: Placebo (saline) in prefilled multidose disposable pens, self-administered daily with same titration schedule
outcomes_primary: Percentage of weight loss achieved after enrollment at 12 months
outcomes_secondary: Safety measures including mortality, adverse effects (grade 3 or higher), need for reoperation for complication of MBS procedure; health benefit measures including improvement in diabetes and hypertension; nutrition measures including iron, vitamins B12, B1, and D, calcium, and albumin; function and well-being measures including SF-36, Beck Depression Index, Euro QOL 5-dimensions health utility survey, quality of swallowing, reflux, and satisfaction questionnaire; drug adherence
extraction_notes: Study halted early due to nonavailability of study medication. COVID-19 pandemic caused significant delays and impacted data collection. Eligibility criteria expanded during trial to include sleeve gastrectomy, OAGB, and RYGB in addition to original adjustable gastric band focus.

title: Efficacy and safety of tirzepatide added to basal insulin in patients with type 2 diabetes in China (SURPASS-CN-INS): a double-blind, multicentre, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.
population: Adults aged 18 years or older with uncontrolled type 2 diabetes receiving once-daily insulin glargine alone or in combination with metformin with or without an SGLT2 inhibitor, in China
intervention: Once-weekly tirzepatide 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg by subcutaneous injection for 40 weeks, added to basal insulin
comparison: Placebo by subcutaneous injection once weekly for 40 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change in HbA1c from baseline
extraction_notes: Abstract text appears truncated; primary outcome inferred from mention of 'HbA' being cut off and context of glycaemic control assessment. Secondary outcomes not explicitly stated in available abstract text. Stratification by HbA1c mentioned but cutoff value truncated.

title: Semaglutide Use With Automated Insulin Delivery in Adults With Type 1 Diabetes: Qualitative Analyses and Patient-reported Outcomes From a Randomized Controlled Trial.
population: Adults with type 1 diabetes using automated insulin delivery
intervention: Semaglutide for 15-week intervention period
comparison: Placebo (crossover design, double-blind)
outcomes_secondary: Patient-reported outcomes including: Diabetes Distress Scale; Hypoglycemia Fear Survey; Diabetes Treatment Satisfaction Questionnaire; Insulin-delivery Systems: Perceptions, Ideas, Reflections and Expectations (INSPIRE); Diabetes Bowel Symptom Questionnaire (DBSQ); qualitative themes from semistructured interviews regarding personal experience with the drug
extraction_notes: Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in abstract. Dose, route, and frequency of semaglutide not specified. This is a secondary analysis (qualitative and patient-reported outcomes) from a parent randomized crossover trial.

title: Liraglutide in Acute Minor Ischemic Stroke or High-Risk Transient Ischemic Attack With Type 2 Diabetes: The LAMP Randomized Clinical Trial.
population: Adults aged ≥50 years with type 2 diabetes (known or newly diagnosed) who had minor acute ischemic stroke (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score ≤3) or high-risk transient ischemic attack (ABCD2 score ≥4) within 24 hours of symptom onset; for patients with stroke history, no sequelae (modified Rankin Scale score 0-1); exclusions included intracranial hemorrhage on CT, iatrogenic or cardiogenic stroke, thrombolysis or endovascular treatment, or GLP-1RA treatment within previous 3 months
intervention: Liraglutide subcutaneous injection once daily for 90 days (0.6 mg daily for first week, increased to 1.2 mg in week 2, then 1.8 mg from week 3 until day 90) plus standard therapy according to guidelines
comparison: Standard therapy alone according to guidelines (secondary prevention medications for acute ischemic stroke, blood pressure and blood glucose management per AHA/ASA and China guidelines)
outcomes_primary: Stroke recurrence (ischemic or hemorrhagic) at 90 days
outcomes_secondary: New clinical vascular events (ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, TIA, myocardial infarction, vascular death) at 90 days; excellent functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score ≤1) at 90 days; favorable functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score ≤2) at 90 days; safety outcomes including symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (ECASS II definition), hypoglycemia, gastrointestinal disorders, pneumonia, pancreatitis, and all-cause death within 90 days
extraction_notes: Trial was terminated early before reaching target sample size of 1708 patients due to lower-than-expected enrollment and financial limitations; 636 patients were randomized; study conducted only in Chinese patients at 27 sites in China

title: People With Lowest Physical Functioning Scores Showed Greatest Improvement After Tirzepatide Treatment.
population: Adults aged 18 years or older with obesity (body mass index ≥30 kg/m2 or ≥27 kg/m2 with at least one obesity-related complication) and a history of at least one self-reported unsuccessful dietary attempt to lose body weight, without diabetes
intervention: Tirzepatide 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg administered subcutaneously once weekly for 72 weeks (SURMOUNT-1 and SURMOUNT-3) or 88 weeks (SURMOUNT-4), as adjunct to lifestyle counseling (500 kcal/day deficit diet and at least 150 minutes of physical activity per week)
comparison: Placebo administered subcutaneously once weekly as adjunct to lifestyle counseling
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline in body weight, waist circumference, and body mass index; change from baseline in SF-36v2 Physical Functioning domain score; change from baseline in IWQOL-Lite-CT Physical Function composite score
outcomes_secondary: Change from baseline in IWQOL-Lite-CT Total score; change from baseline in IWQOL-Lite-CT Psychosocial composite score; change from baseline in SF-36v2 domain scores (General Health, Role-Physical, Bodily Pain, Vitality, Social Functioning, Role-Emotional, Mental Health); correlation between weight reduction and improvement in SF-36v2 Physical Functioning scores
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis pooling data from three SURMOUNT trials (SURMOUNT-1, SURMOUNT-3, SURMOUNT-4). Primary and secondary outcomes were not explicitly designated in the abstract; outcomes listed are based on those assessed in the post hoc analysis. SURMOUNT-3 included a 12-week intensive lifestyle modification lead-in requiring ≥5% weight reduction before randomization. SURMOUNT-4 included a 36-week tirzepatide lead-in period before randomization.

title: Improved health-related quality of life with tirzepatide versus semaglutide in adults with obesity or overweight from the SURMOUNT-5 trial.
population: Adults aged 18 years or older with obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2) or overweight (BMI ≥27 kg/m2 with at least one weight-related complication including hypertension, dyslipidaemia, obstructive sleep apnoea, or cardiovascular disease), experiencing at least one unsuccessful dietary effort for weight reduction, without type 2 diabetes. Key exclusion criteria included diabetes diagnosis, past or planned surgical treatment for obesity, treatment with weight reduction medication or GLP-1 receptor agonist, or body weight change >5 kg within 3 months prior to screening.
intervention: Tirzepatide subcutaneous injection once weekly at maximum tolerated dose (MTD: 10 mg or 15 mg) for 72 weeks, with dose escalation consistent with US Prescribing Information
comparison: Semaglutide subcutaneous injection once weekly at maximum tolerated dose (MTD: 1.7 mg or 2.4 mg) for 72 weeks, with dose escalation consistent with US Prescribing Information
outcomes_primary: Changes from baseline in Short Form-36 Health Survey Version 2 (SF-36v2) norm-based scores including Physical Component Summary (PCS), Mental Component Summary (MCS), and individual domains (Physical Functioning, Role-Physical, Bodily Pain, General Health, Vitality, Social Functioning, Role-Emotional, Mental Health) at Week 72
outcomes_secondary: Categorical shift from baseline in Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) score at Week 72 (depression severity); Categorical shift from baseline in Patient Global Impression of Status (PGI-S) for Physical Activity score at Week 72 (physical limitations). Post hoc analyses: changes in SF-36v2 scores in participants with limited baseline physical function; changes in SF-36v2 scores by body weight reduction thresholds (<5%, <10%, 10 to <20%, 20% to <30%, ≥30%)
extraction_notes: This is a phase 3b open-label trial (SURMOUNT-5). The study was randomized 1:1. Analysis used on-treatment data from participants receiving ≥1 dose. Health-related quality of life outcomes were prespecified; some analyses were post hoc. Study not powered for exploratory endpoints and not adjusted for multiplicity.

title: Tirzepatide and change in uric acid and its association with weight reduction: post hoc analyses of the SURMOUNT-1 randomised placebo-controlled trial.
population: Adults with obesity or overweight (body mass index ≥30 kg/m² or ≥27 kg/m² with weight-related comorbidities)
intervention: Tirzepatide 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg (dual GLP-1RA/GIP agonist)
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Change in serum uric acid (SUA) levels
outcomes_secondary: Association between weight reduction and SUA reduction; SUA change across baseline uric acid quartiles; SUA change across baseline BMI values
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of the SURMOUNT-1 trial. Full population BMI criteria appear truncated in abstract. Route, frequency, and duration of tirzepatide administration not explicitly stated in abstract. Total sample size stated as 2539 adults. Treatment duration appears to be 72 weeks based on outcome timepoint.

title: Adjunctive Semaglutide in Patients Undergoing Intragastric Balloon for Weight Loss: 12-Month Prospective Comparative Study.
population: Adults aged 18 to 65 years with body mass index (BMI) of 27 kg/m² or higher, diagnosed with overweight or obesity, scheduled for endoscopic intragastric balloon placement. Exclusion criteria: history of previous bariatric surgery, contraindications to IGB insertion or semaglutide use, gastrointestinal disorders (inflammatory bowel disease or gastroparesis), severe organ dysfunction (renal, hepatic, or cardiac), pregnancy, current use of other anti-obesity medications.
intervention: Intragastric balloon (Spatz3, liquid-filled, 400-700 ml saline with methylene blue, maintained for 6 months) plus subcutaneous semaglutide (Ozempic): 0.5 mg once weekly during month 2, escalated to 1 mg once weekly during months 3-4, paused during months 5-6, reintroduced at 1 mg once weekly during months 7-8, then discontinued. All participants received standardized dietary protocol and lifestyle modification support.
comparison: Intragastric balloon (Spatz3, liquid-filled, 400-700 ml saline with methylene blue, maintained for 6 months) alone with standardized dietary protocol and lifestyle modification support.
outcomes_primary: Percentage change in body weight from baseline to 12 months after intervention; Total Body Weight Loss (TBWL) percentage; Excess Weight Loss (EWL) percentage; weight and BMI measured at baseline, 3, 6, and 12 months.
outcomes_secondary: Safety outcomes including incidence and nature of treatment-related complications (nausea, vomiting, gastroparesis, pancreatitis, serious complications requiring discontinuation, hospitalization, or posing significant health risks); adherence to treatment protocol; patient-reported tolerance.
extraction_notes: Open-label trial; randomization performed but no blinding. No semaglutide-only or placebo control group. Single-center study conducted at Alexandria Main University Hospital, Egypt.

title: Semaglutide for the treatment of cognitive dysfunction in major depressive disorder: A randomized clinical trial.
population: Adults meeting DSM-5-defined criteria for major depressive disorder (MDD), with pre-treatment evidence of cognitive impairment, and overweight/obese
intervention: Adjunctive oral semaglutide 14 mg for 16 weeks
comparison: Adjunctive placebo
outcomes_primary: Executive function composite score comprising the digit symbol substitution test, the Stroop test, and the n-back test
outcomes_secondary: Global cognition composite score, measures of functioning, depressive symptom severity, suicidality, body weight

title: Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass Improves Insulin Response and Secretion of GLP-1 and PYY in Response to Postprandial Acute Exercise.
population: Women with severe obesity (age 37 ± 7 years; BMI 47.6 ± 5.6 kg/m²)
intervention: Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery followed by postprandial acute exercise session (resistance training plus aerobic exercise) at 3 months post-surgery
comparison: Pre-surgery exercise session (same participants before bariatric surgery)

Outcomes measured include glucose metabolism, insulin response, gut hormones (GLP-1, PYY), and inflammatory markers assessed at baseline, immediately after, and 30 minutes after exercise. This is a pre-post single-arm study design with 13 participants.

title: Effect of ketogenic diet plus dulaglutide on glucose and lipid metabolism in diabetes mellitus.
population: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus
intervention: Dulaglutide plus ketogenic diet
comparison: Dulaglutide alone
outcomes_secondary: Blood glucose levels; blood lipid levels; insulin resistance index; insulin sensitivity index; Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index score; quality of life

title: Tirzepatide in Adults With Type 1 Diabetes: A Phase 2 Randomized Placebo-Controlled Clinical Trial.
population: Adults aged 18-60 years with at least 2-year history of type 1 diabetes and BMI ≥30 kg/m2. Excluded: use of GLP-1 receptor agonist, sodium-glucose cotransporter inhibitor, or glucocorticoids within 6 weeks prior; history of diabetic ketoacidosis, severe hypoglycemia, coronary event, or stroke in preceding 3 months; history of gastroparesis, pancreatitis, cholecystitis, previous weight loss surgery; estimated glomerular filtration rate <45 mL/min/1.73 m2; significant liver disease; currently pregnant or breastfeeding; history of proliferative diabetic retinopathy or macular edema.

outcomes_primary: Change in body weight at 12 weeks

extraction_notes: Phase 2, double-blind, randomized placebo-controlled trial. Single-site study conducted at Garvan Institute of Medical Research, Sydney. 24 participants randomized (1:1 allocation). Randomization stratified by sex.

title: Cardiometabolic Parameter Change by Weight Regain on Tirzepatide Withdrawal in Adults With Obesity: A Post Hoc Analysis of the SURMOUNT-4 Trial.
population: Adults with obesity (BMI ≥30) or overweight (BMI ≥27) with at least 1 weight-related complication; excluded diabetes, prior or planned surgical treatment for obesity, and treatment with weight reduction medication within 3 months prior to enrollment; must have achieved ≥10% weight reduction at week 36 with maximum tolerated dose of tirzepatide (10 or 15 mg)
intervention: Tirzepatide once-weekly (maximum tolerated dose 10 mg or 15 mg) for 36 weeks as open-label lead-in, then withdrawal to placebo for 52 weeks (week 36 to 88), as adjunct to reduced calorie diet (500 kcal/day deficit) and increased physical activity (≥150 minutes/week)
comparison: Degree of weight regain categories from week 36 to week 88 as percentage of weight lost during tirzepatide treatment: <25%, 25% to <50%, 50% to <75%, and ≥75% weight regain
outcomes_primary: Changes from week 36 to week 88 in cardiometabolic parameters by categories of weight regain: waist circumference, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, triglycerides, non-HDL cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, hemoglobin A1c, fasting serum glucose, fasting insulin, HOMA2-IR, HOMA2-B
outcomes_secondary: Changes from week 0 to week 36 and changes over week 0 to week 88 in weight, BMI, and cardiometabolic parameters by categories of weight regain
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of the SURMOUNT-4 trial (NCT04660643). Analysis focused only on participants randomized to placebo arm (tirzepatide withdrawal) who achieved ≥10% weight reduction at week 36. The comparison is between weight regain categories within the same treatment group rather than between different treatment arms.

title: Effects of liraglutide treatment for 18 days on metabolic parameters, regional body composition and the myostatin-activin-follistatin-IGF-1 axis: Results from an exploratory, randomized, placebo-controlled, crossover study.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM)
intervention: Liraglutide up to 1.8 mg/day for 18 days
comparison: Placebo for 18 days, separated by a washout period (crossover design)
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes assessed included: total body mass, regional body composition (fat, lean, and bone compartments assessed by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry including android fat, trunk fat mass), circulating C-peptide, and myostatin-activin-follistatin-IGF-1 (MAFI) axis components measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Study described as exploratory with N=20 participants.

title: Effects of semaglutide in obesity-related heart failure with preserved ejection fraction across the age spectrum: Findings from the STEP-HFpEF programme.
population: Adults with symptomatic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF, left ventricular ejection fraction ≥45%) and obesity (body mass index ≥30 kg/m2) with objective evidence of HFpEF based on elevated filling pressures or elevated natriuretic peptide levels and echocardiographic abnormalities, or heart failure hospitalization in the previous 12 months. STEP-HFpEF DM trial included only patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
intervention: Semaglutide 2.4 mg subcutaneous once weekly for 52 weeks in addition to standard care
comparison: Matching placebo once weekly for 52 weeks in addition to standard care
outcomes_primary: Change in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire clinical summary score (KCCQ-CSS) from baseline to 52 weeks; Percentage change in body weight from baseline to 52 weeks
outcomes_secondary: Change in 6-minute walk distance (6MWD); Change in C-reactive protein (CRP); Hierarchical composite endpoint comprising all-cause death (from baseline to 57 weeks), heart failure events (hospitalizations or urgent visits requiring intravenous therapy), changes in KCCQ-CSS and 6MWD; Change in N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) concentrations (exploratory); Serious adverse events, serious adverse events leading to permanent treatment discontinuation, cardiac and gastrointestinal serious adverse events, atrial fibrillation events, and bone/joint injuries (safety endpoints)
extraction_notes: This is a pre-specified pooled subanalysis of STEP-HFpEF and STEP-HFpEF DM trials stratified by age groups (<55, 55-64, 65-74, ≥75 years). Route of administration not explicitly stated but semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly is typically subcutaneous.

title: Association of baseline characteristics with clinical outcomes of tirzepatide treatment in Japanese patients with obesity disease: A subgroup analysis of the SURMOUNT-J trial.
population: Japanese adults aged ≥20 years without type 2 diabetes meeting Japanese Society for the Study of Obesity criteria for obesity disease requiring pharmacological treatment: BMI ≥27 kg/m2 and <35 kg/m2 plus two or more obesity-related health disorders (ORHDs) or BMI ≥35 kg/m2 plus one or more ORHDs. ORHDs included impaired glucose tolerance, hyperlipidemia, and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. Key exclusion criteria included diabetes, treatment with DPP-4 inhibitors, oral GLP-1 receptor agonists, or injectable T2D therapy within 3 months prior to screening, and liver disease other than MASLD.
intervention: Once-weekly subcutaneous tirzepatide 10 mg or tirzepatide 15 mg, escalated by 2.5 mg from initial 2.5 mg every 4 weeks until assigned maintenance dose reached, as adjunct to lifestyle modifications, for 72 weeks
comparison: Placebo (once-weekly subcutaneous injection) as adjunct to lifestyle modifications
outcomes_primary: Percentage change from baseline body weight to week 72; proportion of participants achieving at least 5% body weight reduction at week 72
outcomes_secondary: Change from baseline in blood pressure, lipids, and fasting serum glucose at week 72; proportion of participants experiencing treatment-emergent adverse events, treatment-related adverse events, serious adverse events, and discontinuations due to adverse events
extraction_notes: This is a prespecified subgroup analysis of the SURMOUNT-J trial (NCT04844918), analyzing efficacy and safety by baseline characteristics including sex, age (<65 vs ≥65 years), and BMI (<35 vs ≥35 kg/m2). Post hoc analyses were conducted for cardiometabolic parameters by subgroup. The distinction between primary and secondary outcomes was not explicitly stated in the abstract; classification based on emphasis in methods section.

title: The Effect of Increased Sodium Intake with a Carbohydrate-Rich Meal on Glucose Homeostasis in People without Diabetes after Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass: a Proof-of-Concept, Randomized, Open-Label, Crossover Study.
population: Adults without diabetes who had undergone Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) surgery at least 12 months prior to study participation. Key exclusion criteria included established diagnosis of post-bariatric hypoglycaemia (PBH), treatment with medications affecting glucose homeostasis (e.g., glucose-lowering agents, systemic steroids), current diagnosis of diabetes, and previous revisional metabolic and bariatric surgery.
intervention: Standardized mixed meal tolerance test (MMTT) consisting of 170 mL smooth orange juice with 2 g of sodium chloride (NaCl, containing 785 mg sodium) dissolved, followed by a yoghurt snack pot (total: 245 kcal, 40 g carbohydrates, 7.5 g protein, 5.5 g fat, 108 mg sodium). Consumed orally within 10 minutes after overnight fasting.
comparison: Standardized mixed meal tolerance test (MMTT) without additional NaCl (same meal composition: 170 mL smooth orange juice and yoghurt snack pot). Crossover design with washout period of at least 7 days between conditions.
outcomes_primary: Difference in nadir (lowest) postprandial plasma glucose between conditions
outcomes_secondary: Differences in area under the curve (AUC 0-180 minutes), fasting, and peak plasma glucose concentrations; fasting, peak, and AUC 0-180' insulin concentrations; fasting, peak, and AUC 0-180' c-peptide concentrations; fasting, peak, and AUC 0-180' glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) concentrations; Edinburgh Hypoglycemia Symptom Scale (EHSS) scores; Sigstad dumping syndrome symptom questionnaire scores
extraction_notes: Proof-of-concept study with small sample size (n=11 analyzed). Open-label design due to inability to blind intervention (detectable taste of NaCl). Single-center study.

title: Effects of CT-388, a once-weekly signaling-biased dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist, on weight loss and glycemic control in preclinical models and participants with obesity.
population: Adults aged 18-65 years with overweight (BMI ≥25 kg/m2) or obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m2) without current diagnosis of diabetes; participants with prediabetes controlled by diet and exercise alone were allowed
intervention: CT-388, a cAMP signal-biased dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist, administered subcutaneously. Single ascending dose (SAD): single doses of 0.5, 2.0, 5.0, 6.0, or 7.5 mg. Multiple ascending dose (MAD): once-weekly doses over 4 weeks with titration schemes: cohort 6 (5/5/5/7.5 mg on days 1, 8, 15, 22), cohort 7 (5/5/8/12 mg), cohort 8 (5/8/12/12 mg)
comparison: Volume-matched placebo administered subcutaneously (randomized 3:1 CT-388:placebo in each cohort)
outcomes_primary: Safety and tolerability including treatment-emergent adverse events, serious adverse events, adverse events leading to discontinuation, safety laboratory parameters, vital signs, and electrocardiogram parameters
outcomes_secondary: Pharmacokinetics (AUC, Cmax, elimination half-life, time to maximum concentration); pharmacodynamics including change from baseline in body weight, hip and waist circumference, glycated hemoglobin, fasting glucose, fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, appetite and satiety by visual analog scale, and glucose and insulin responses during oral glucose tolerance test
extraction_notes: Phase 1 first-in-human study (NCT04838405). SAD portion conducted in Australia, MAD portion in Mexico. The paper also includes extensive preclinical data from mouse and cynomolgus monkey studies which were not extracted as the focus was on the clinical trial PICO elements.

title: Liraglutide in mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease: a phase 2b clinical trial.
population: Adults aged 50 years or older with clinical diagnosis of mild to moderate Alzheimer's disease syndrome (MMSE score 15 or higher, CDR Global score of 0.5, 1, or 2) without diabetes mellitus, based on National Institute of Neurological and Communicative Diseases and Stroke/Alzheimer's Disease and Related Disorders Association criteria
intervention: Liraglutide subcutaneous injection, starting at 0.6 mg once daily, escalated to 1.8 mg once daily within 4 weeks (with option to remain at 1.2 mg if 1.8 mg not tolerated), for 52 weeks
comparison: Matching placebo subcutaneous injection once daily for 52 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change in cerebral glucose metabolic rate (rCMRglc) in cortical regions (composite of hippocampal, medial temporal lobe, and posterior cingulate) from baseline to 52 weeks, measured by fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography ([18F] FDG PET)
outcomes_secondary: Safety and tolerability (incidence and severity of treatment-emergent adverse events and clinically important changes in safety assessments); change in ADAS-Exec z-score (composite of ADAS-Cog and Executive domain scores from Neuropsychological Test Battery); change in Alzheimer's Disease Cooperative Study-Activities of Daily Living (ADCS-ADL); change in Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes (CDR-SoB); MRI volumetric changes in ventricles and composite region (hippocampus and entorhinal cortex)
extraction_notes: Exploratory outcomes included MRI volumes of temporal lobe, total gray matter, parietal lobe, frontoparietal lobe, and voxel-based morphometry analyses. APOE genotype, plasma biomarkers, tau PET, TSPO PET, and amyloid PET were planned but not completed or not yet analyzed.

title: CagriSema Reduces Blood Pressure in Adults With Overweight or Obesity: REDEFINE 1.
population: Adults without diabetes with body mass index ≥30 kg/m2, or ≥27 kg/m2 with ≥1 obesity-related complication
intervention: CagriSema (fixed-dose combination of semaglutide 2.4 mg/cagrilintide 2.4 mg) administered once-weekly subcutaneously for 68 weeks, plus lifestyle intervention
comparison: Semaglutide 2.4 mg once-weekly, cagrilintide 2.4 mg once-weekly, or placebo, all with lifestyle intervention; randomization ratio 21:3:3:7 (CagriSema:semaglutide:cagrilintide:placebo)
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified as primary in abstract; change in systolic blood pressure from baseline to week 68 was a secondary confirmatory efficacy end point
outcomes_secondary: Change in systolic blood pressure from baseline to week 68 for CagriSema versus placebo (secondary confirmatory); change in diastolic blood pressure for CagriSema versus placebo (secondary supportive); change in number of participants taking antihypertensive medication (exploratory); proportion of participants achieving ACC/AHA blood pressure targets (<130/80 mm Hg); changes in blood pressure by subgroups including baseline hypertension status, resistant hypertension, BMI categories (post hoc)
extraction_notes: Primary outcome not explicitly stated; the abstract describes blood pressure outcomes as secondary and post hoc analyses of the REDEFINE 1 trial. The primary outcome of the original REDEFINE 1 trial (body weight change) is referenced but this publication focuses on blood pressure as secondary/post hoc analyses.

title: Semaglutide and Early-Stage Metabolic Abnormalities in Individuals With Schizophrenia Spectrum Disorders: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
population: Adults aged 18-65 years with schizophrenia spectrum disorders, clozapine or olanzapine treatment initiated within the past 5 years, early-stage glycemic dysregulation (hemoglobin A1c 5.4%-7.4%), not receiving antidiabetic therapy
intervention: Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 1 mg, administered adjunctively to second-generation antipsychotic therapy for 26 weeks
comparison: Matching placebo once-weekly subcutaneous injection, administered adjunctively to second-generation antipsychotic therapy for 26 weeks
outcomes_primary: Change in hemoglobin A1c level from baseline to week 26
outcomes_secondary: Body weight change, waist circumference change, fat mass change, lipid levels, liver function, blood pressure, psychiatric symptoms, achievement of low-risk HbA1c levels (<5.4%), gastrointestinal adverse events, psychiatric adverse events
extraction_notes: Secondary outcomes noted as exploratory by study authors

title: Impact of Oral Semaglutide on Kidney Outcomes in People With Type 2 Diabetes: Results From the SOUL Randomized Trial.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and/or chronic kidney disease (CKD, defined as eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2 with no lower limit); participants receiving kidney replacement therapy at screening were excluded
intervention: Oral semaglutide 14 mg once daily in addition to standard of care
comparison: Matching placebo once daily in addition to standard of care
outcomes_primary: Five-point composite kidney outcome: persistent ≥50% reduction in eGFR from baseline, persistent eGFR <15 mL/min/1.73 m2, initiation of long-term kidney replacement therapy (dialysis or kidney transplant), or death from kidney-related or cardiovascular causes
outcomes_secondary: Four-point kidney-specific composite outcome (excluding cardiovascular death from the five-point composite); annual rate of change in eGFR (total eGFR slope) from baseline to end of treatment
extraction_notes: The kidney outcomes were prespecified secondary outcomes in this cardiovascular outcomes trial (SOUL). The primary outcome of the SOUL trial was major adverse cardiovascular events. Urinary albumin was not measured in this trial.

title: Combination metformin and liraglutide in PCOS: clinical efficacy in women and preclinical insights from gut microbiome modulation in rats.
population: Overweight or obese women with PCOS (BMI ≥24 kg/m2), aged >18 years, premenopausal, diagnosed by Rotterdam criteria (hyperandrogenemia, menstrual abnormalities, polycystic ovarian morphology). Excluded: cardiovascular, kidney, hepatic, pituitary, or thyroid disease; use of antiandrogen agents, diabetic drugs, glucocorticoids, or other steroid agents within 90 days before study.
intervention: Combination therapy (COM group): metformin 0.85g orally twice daily plus liraglutide 1.2mg subcutaneously once daily (starting at 0.6mg once daily for 1 week then increased to 1.2mg) for 12 weeks
comparison: MET group: metformin 0.85g orally twice daily for 12 weeks; LIRA group: liraglutide 1.2mg subcutaneously once daily (starting at 0.6mg once daily for 1 week then increased to 1.2mg) for 12 weeks
outcomes_primary: Absolute changes from baseline to week 12 in: body weight, hormonal parameters, lipid profiles, and measures of glucose metabolism
outcomes_secondary: BMI, visceral fat area, body fat percentage, waist-to-hip ratio, fasting blood glucose, fasting insulin, postprandial plasma glucose, HbA1c, HOMA-IR, free testosterone, total testosterone, SHBG, LH, FSH, LH/FSH ratio, free androgen index (FAI), HDL-C, LDL-C/HDL-C ratio, TC/HDL-C ratio, proportion achieving ≥5% weight reduction, safety and tolerability (adverse events)
extraction_notes: This study includes both a clinical RCT in women and a parallel animal experiment in rats. PICO extraction focuses on the clinical trial component. Primary outcomes were explicitly defined. Secondary outcomes were not explicitly labeled but were assessed throughout the study.

title: Long-acting GIPR agonist LY3537021 reduces body weight and fasting blood glucose in patients with T2D: Preclinical development and phase 1 randomized ascending dose studies.
population: Healthy participants and patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D) aged 21-70 years with BMI 18.5-40 kg/m2. Healthy participants had HbA1c ≤6.5%. Patients with T2D had screening HbA1c 6.5%-11.0% (SAD) or 6.5%-10.0% (MAD), treated with diet and exercise alone or stable dose of metformin for at least 3 months. MAD patients with T2D could use one other oral antihyperglycemic medication (dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitor, sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitor, or sulfonylurea).
intervention: LY3537021 (long-acting GIPR agonist) administered subcutaneously. SAD portion: single doses of 0.3 mg, 1 mg, 3 mg, 10 mg, or 25 mg (healthy participants) or 25 mg (patients with T2D in crossover design). MAD portion: 4 mg, 12 mg, or 25 mg administered once weekly on days 1, 8, 15, and 22.
comparison: Placebo. SAD portion: randomized 3:1 (LY3537021:placebo) for healthy participants; 1:1 crossover for T2D patients. MAD portion: randomized 2:1 (LY3537021:placebo).
outcomes_primary: Safety and tolerability assessed through treatment-emergent adverse events, serious adverse events, electrocardiograms, vital sign measurements, and clinical safety laboratory tests.
outcomes_secondary: Pharmacokinetics of LY3537021 (maximum observed drug concentration, area under the concentration-time curve, time of maximum concentration). Exploratory endpoints: body weight and fasting glucose (assessed approximately weekly). Gastric emptying assessed via acetaminophen pharmacokinetics. Appetite/satiety assessed using visual analog scale.
extraction_notes: Phase 1 study with both preclinical and clinical components. Clinical study conducted at single center in Singapore. Study registered as NCT04586907.

title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist in large vessel occlusion treated by reperfusion therapy-a phase 2 randomized trial.
population: Adults aged 18 years or older with acute large vessel occlusion (LVO) at the terminal internal carotid artery or M1 segment of middle cerebral artery, ASPECTS 6-10, NIHSS ≥10 at randomization, stroke onset or last-known-well ≤12 hours at randomization, pre-stroke mRS ≤2, undergoing endovascular therapy. Patients presenting 6-12 hours from symptom onset required CT perfusion demonstrating clinical-core or perfusion-core mismatch according to DAWN or DEFUSE3 criteria.
intervention: Semaglutide 0.5 mg subcutaneous injection before arterial puncture and 7 days after endovascular therapy, plus reperfusion therapy (EVT with or without intravenous thrombolysis)
comparison: Standard therapy (reperfusion therapy alone: EVT with or without intravenous thrombolysis)
outcomes_primary: Favorable neurological recovery defined as modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-2 at 90 days
outcomes_secondary: Composite safety outcome (death, malignant brain edema, and intracranial hemorrhage); ordinal shift in mRS at 90 days; mRS 0-3 at 90 days; mRS 0-1 at 90 days; death; final infarct size on MRI 14-21 days after randomization; malignant brain edema; intracranial hemorrhage (Heidelberg Bleeding Classification class 2 or above); changes between day-3 and baseline NIHSS; changes between day-3 and baseline blood glucose level
extraction_notes: Phase 2 trial conducted in China at two thrombectomy centers. Open-label design with blinded endpoint assessment. IVT was administered to approximately half of participants in each group.

title: Insulin therapy DE-intensificAtion with iGlarLixi: A phase 4, open-label, parallel-group randomised controlled trial.
population: Adults aged 18-80 years diagnosed with type 2 diabetes, treated with multiple daily injections (MDI) insulin regimen (≥3 insulin injections/day) and metformin (unless not tolerated) ± SGLT2i on stable doses ≥3 months prior to screening, total daily dose of insulin ≤0.8 IU/kg body weight, HbA1c ≤9% (≤75 mmol/mol) or 9.1%-10% (76-86 mmol/mol) in case of non-compliance with MDI regimen, and fasting C-peptide levels above the lower limit of the normal range (0.37-1.47 nmol/L)
intervention: Once-daily fixed-ratio combination iGlarLixi (basal insulin glargine 100 U/mL plus lixisenatide 50 mcg/mL or 33 mcg/mL) subcutaneous injection, with starting dose and pen assignment based on prior insulin type and dose, titrated over 24 weeks
comparison: Continuation with multiple daily injections (MDI) insulin regimen with re-education
outcomes_primary: Mean change in HbA1c from baseline to 24 weeks after randomisation
outcomes_secondary: Mean change in body weight, BMI, waist circumference, total daily dose of insulin, fasting plasma glucose, postprandial glucose; CGM-related outcomes including time in range (3.9-10.0 mmol/L), time in predefined interstitial glucose ranges, mean sensor glucose, glycaemic variability (coefficient of variation), glycaemia risk index; safety endpoints including frequency of hypoglycaemia, proportion of participants with hypoglycaemia, adverse events, serious adverse events; patient-reported outcomes (DTSQs, DTSQc, HABS, ADDQoL)
extraction_notes: Open-label trial design. Randomisation stratified by gender, BMI (<30 vs ≥30 kg/m2), and T2D duration (<10 vs ≥10 years). 24-week active treatment period with 12-week follow-up.

title: Mazdutide versus placebo in Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes.
population: Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes
intervention: Mazdutide (dose, route, frequency, and duration not specified in abstract)
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Not explicitly specified in abstract
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly specified in abstract
extraction_notes: Abstract appears truncated. Only background information provided. No specific eligibility criteria, intervention details, or outcome definitions are stated. Dose, route, frequency, duration of mazdutide not specified. Primary and secondary outcomes not defined in available text.

title: Mazdutide versus dulaglutide in Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes.
population: Chinese adults with type 2 diabetes
intervention: Mazdutide, once-weekly, glucagon and glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor dual agonist
comparison: Dulaglutide
extraction_notes: Abstract incomplete - only provides background information about mazdutide mechanism. No outcomes, dosing details, or study design information available. Primary and secondary outcomes not specified.

title: Effects of combined intraduodenal administration of lauric acid and L-tryptophan on postprandial plasma glucose, glucoregulatory hormones and gastric emptying in type 2 diabetes: a double-blind, randomised, crossover study.
population: Men with type 2 diabetes
intervention: Combined intraduodenal administration of lauric acid (C12) and L-tryptophan (Trp) at loads of 1.26 and 0.42 kJ/min respectively
comparison: Control, lauric acid (C12) alone, L-tryptophan (Trp) alone
outcomes_primary: Postprandial plasma glucose
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1), gastric emptying, cholecystokinin (CCK), glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), insulin, C-peptide
extraction_notes: Sample size n=11; study performed at University of Adelaide Clinical Research Facility; HbA1c inclusion criteria value appears truncated in abstract

title: Efficacy of tirzepatide versus semaglutide in achieving therapeutic targets in type 2 diabetes: a post hoc analysis of the SURPASS-2 Trial.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes from the SURPASS-2 trial (n=1879)
intervention: Tirzepatide 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg
comparison: Semaglutide 1 mg
outcomes_primary: Attainment of standard therapeutic targets (HbA1c, body weight, blood pressure); attainment of intensive therapeutic targets
outcomes_secondary: Achievement of specific therapeutic goals for HbA1c, body weight, and blood pressure at standard and intensive thresholds
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of the SURPASS-2 trial. Route, frequency, and duration of drug administration not specified in abstract. Specific threshold values for standard vs intensive targets are truncated in the abstract text.

title: Once-weekly semaglutide versus placebo for the treatment of type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease in Denmark: A long-term cost-effectiveness analysis based on FLOW.
population: Adults with type 2 diabetes (T2D) and chronic kidney disease (CKD); participants enrolled across KDIGO stages 1-5 (1%, 20%, 30%, 38%, 11% in stages 1, 2, 3a, 3b, 4-5 respectively); mean diabetes duration 17.4 years; 61.4% receiving insulin at baseline; receiving maximally tolerated dose of RAAS inhibitors as standard of care
intervention: Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide 1 mg in addition to standard of care
comparison: Placebo in addition to standard of care; subgroup analyses stratified by baseline SGLT-2 inhibitor use (receiving vs not receiving SGLT-2 inhibitors at baseline)
outcomes_primary: Major kidney disease events: composite of onset of kidney failure (dialysis, transplantation, or eGFR <15 mL/min/1.73 m²), at least 50% reduction in eGFR from baseline, or death from kidney-related or cardiovascular causes
outcomes_secondary: Life expectancy; quality-adjusted life expectancy (QALYs); cumulative incidence of diabetes-related complications; direct costs; incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs)
extraction_notes: This is a cost-effectiveness modeling analysis based on the FLOW clinical trial (NCT03819153), not the primary trial itself. The primary outcome definition is from the original FLOW trial. Secondary outcomes listed are health economic modeling outputs. Baseline characteristics referenced in supplementary materials not provided in abstract/text.

title: Effect of Semaglutide on Insulin Dose Reduction in Adults With Type 1 Diabetes and Obesity Using Automated Insulin Delivery Systems: ADJUST-T1D Post Hoc Analysis.
population: Adults aged 18-65 years with type 1 diabetes who used FDA-approved automated insulin delivery systems and had BMI of 30 kg/m2 or higher. Major exclusion criteria included current or planned pregnancy, use of concomitant glucose-lowering medications, and contraindications to GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy.
intervention: Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide up to 1 mg (initiated at 0.25 mg weekly for first 4 weeks, increased to 0.5 mg at week 4, and further to 1 mg at week 8) for 26 weeks
comparison: Placebo (once-weekly subcutaneous injection)
outcomes_primary: Composite endpoint consisting of CGM-based time in range (70-180 mg/dL) greater than 70%, time below 70 mg/dL less than 4%, and weight reduction of at least 5%
outcomes_secondary: Total daily insulin dose (TDD), basal insulin dose, bolus insulin dose, basal-to-TDD ratio, insulin dose per kilogram body weight (units/kg/day), carbohydrate intake per day, number of user-initiated boluses per day, number of automated correction boluses, HbA1c, weight change, time in range
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of the ADJUST-T1D trial (NCT05537233). The primary outcome listed is from the parent trial; this post hoc analysis focused on insulin dose changes and mediation analysis of weight loss contribution to insulin dose reduction.

title: Differential Longitudinal Effects of Glucose-Lowering Medications on Glucagon and C-peptide Responses in the Glycemia Reduction Approaches in Diabetes: A Comparative Effectiveness Study (GRADE).
population: Adults aged ≥30 years (≥20 years if American Indian) with type 2 diabetes diagnosed <10 years before screening, taking 1,000–2,000 mg metformin daily, with HbA1c 6.8%–8.5%
intervention: Insulin glargine U100, glimepiride, liraglutide, or sitagliptin added to metformin
comparison: Four-way comparison between insulin glargine U100, glimepiride, liraglutide, and sitagliptin treatment groups
outcomes_primary: Confirmed HbA1c ≥7.0%
outcomes_secondary: Confirmed HbA1c >7.5%; longitudinal measures of α-cell function (fasting glucagon concentration and glucagon index [GGI]); β-cell function measures (fasting C-peptide and C-peptide index [CPI])
extraction_notes: This is a glucagon substudy (n=724) nested within the larger GRADE trial (n=5,047). The substudy subset was a non-random convenience sample selected post hoc based on availability of OGTT samples at baseline and year 1.

title: Semaglutide and Hospitalizations in Patients With Obesity and Established Cardiovascular Disease: An Exploratory Analysis of the SELECT Randomized Clinical Trial.
population: Patients aged 45 years or older with established cardiovascular disease and body mass index of 27 or higher without diabetes
intervention: Once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide, 2.4 mg
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Total number of hospital admissions; days in hospital
extraction_notes: This is a prespecified exploratory analysis of the SELECT trial. The abstract does not explicitly distinguish primary from secondary outcomes for this exploratory analysis.

title: Combining glucagon-like peptide 1 analogues with sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors to treat patients with type 1 diabetes, BMI > 25 kg/m
population: Patients with type 1 diabetes, BMI > 25 kg/m²
intervention: GLP-1 analogue plus SGLT2 inhibitor combination; GLP-1 analogue plus SGLT2 inhibitor plus lifestyle modification; duration 6 months
comparison: Usual care; GLP-1 analogue alone; SGLT2 inhibitor alone
outcomes_primary: Change in bodyweight
outcomes_secondary: Markers of kidney disease; glycaemic control; blood pressure; lipids
extraction_notes: Abstract appears truncated at conclusions. Specific drug names, doses, routes, and frequencies for GLP-1 analogues and SGLT2 inhibitors not specified. BMI threshold unit appears cut off but contextually is kg/m². Trial registration: NCT05390307. Single-centre pilot study with 60 participants randomised across 5 groups.

title: Efficacy and safety of cAMP signalling-biased GLP-1 analogue ecnoglutide monotherapy versus placebo in patients with type 2 diabetes (EECOH-1): a multi-centre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.
population: Adults aged 18–75 years with type 2 diabetes mellitus inadequately controlled with diet and exercise alone or with only one oral hypoglycaemic agent; BMI 20.0–35.0 kg/m²; HbA1c 7.5%–11.0% at screening and 7.0%–10.5% at randomisation; fasting plasma glucose ≤13.9 mmol/L at screening and randomisation; excluded if type 1 diabetes or other diabetes mellitus, received GLP-1 drug or DPP-4 inhibitor within preceding 3 months, insulin within preceding 6 months, or experienced diabetic ketoacidosis, hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state, lactic acidosis, or severe chronic diabetes complications within prior 6 months
intervention: Ecnoglutide 0.6 mg or 1.2 mg administered once weekly via subcutaneous injection using injector pens; dose-escalation regimen starting at 0.3 mg with fixed double-dose increments every 4 weeks until maintenance dose reached (0.6 mg reached at week 4, 1.2 mg reached at week 8); 24-week double-blind treatment period followed by 28-week open-label extended treatment period
comparison: Volume-matched placebo (0.6 mg or 1.2 mg) administered once weekly via subcutaneous injection, identical in appearance to active drug
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline in glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) at week 24
outcomes_secondary: Proportions of participants achieving HbA1c <7.0% and ≤6.5% at weeks 24 and 52; proportion achieving composite endpoint of HbA1c <7.0%, no severe hypoglycaemia, and no bodyweight gain at week 24; changes from baseline at weeks 24 and 52 in fasting plasma glucose, 2h-postprandial plasma glucose, seven-point self-monitored blood glucose profiles, fasting insulin, HOMA-β, HOMA-IR, blood lipids, bodyweight, waist circumference, and hip circumference; incidences of treatment-emergent adverse events, serious TEAEs, and TEAEs of special interest (hypoglycaemia, cardiovascular events, gastrointestinal events, pancreatitis, gallbladder-related disorders)
extraction_notes: Randomisation ratio was 2:2:1:1 for ecnoglutide 0.6 mg, ecnoglutide 1.2 mg, placebo volume-matched to 0.6 mg, and placebo volume-matched to 1.2 mg; stratified by baseline HbA1c (≤8.5% or >8.5%); trial conducted at 32 sites in China only

title: Proteomic effects of short-term liraglutide vs. placebo in a blinded crossover RCT: Implications for efficacy, safety, and comparison with semaglutide.
population: Adults with obesity
intervention: Liraglutide 3 mg daily for 5 weeks
comparison: Placebo for 5 weeks, with 3-week washout period between crossover periods
extraction_notes: Crossover design with each participant receiving both treatments. Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly designated in abstract.
