title: Changes of gut microbiota, hormone and glycolipid metabolism by dietary fiber (oat bran) supplementation in patients with laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy and Roux-en-Y gastric bypass: A randomized controlled study.
population: Post-bariatric surgery patients who underwent laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy or Roux-en-Y gastric bypass
intervention: Standard care plus 30 g/day oat bran (providing 9.0 g dietary fiber) for 12 weeks
comparison: Standard care alone (control group)
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in the abstract. Outcomes mentioned include: gut microbiota composition, GLP-1 levels, PYY levels, glycolipid parameters (FBG, HDL-C), and percentage of excess weight loss (EWL%). The abstract does not clearly designate which outcomes are primary versus secondary.

title: ARD-101, a gut-restricted TAS2R agonist, reduces hunger in adults and promotes weight loss in DIO mice with DPP-4 inhibition.
population: Adults with obesity (BMI between 30 and 45 kg/m2) for the Phase 2 study; healthy adult participants for the clinical pharmacology study
intervention: ARD-101 (oral denatonium acetate) 200 mg twice daily for 28 days (Phase 2 study); ARD-101 800 mg once daily for 2 days (clinical pharmacology study)
comparison: Matching placebo (containing the same inactive excipients as ARD-101 but lacking denatonium acetate)
outcomes_primary: Body weight change from baseline; Control of Eating Questionnaire (CoEQ) scores measuring hunger, cravings, and eating control on visual analog scale
outcomes_secondary: Metabolic markers including lipid parameters (cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, non-HDL cholesterol, triglycerides), HbA1c; plasma gut hormone levels (GLP-1 total, PYY, CCK, ghrelin total); safety and tolerability (adverse events)
extraction_notes: This publication reports both preclinical mouse studies and two separate clinical studies in humans. PICO extraction focused on the human clinical studies. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly designated in the text; classification based on narrative emphasis. The Phase 2 study was single-blind; the clinical pharmacology study was double-blind.

title: Holding vs Continuing GLP-1/GIP Agonists Before Upper Endoscopy: The OCULUS Randomized Clinical Trial.
population: Adults aged 18 years or older scheduled for elective upper endoscopy (EGD, EUS, or ERCP) with or without colonoscopy, under moderate sedation or monitored anesthesia care, taking a stable dose of a GLP-1 or GLP-1/GIP agonist for at least 1 month. Exclusion criteria: prior foregut surgery, achalasia, documented gastroparesis based on 4-hour solid phase gastric emptying study, residual gastric volume on previous endoscopy, gastric outlet obstruction, planned general anesthesia, or chronic opioid use.
intervention: Continue GLP-1 or GLP-1/GIP agonist medication at the same dosage and scheduled times prior to the procedure
comparison: Hold 1 dose of GLP-1 or GLP-1/GIP agonist medication (medication-free period of 7 to 13 days before upper endoscopy for weekly medications or at least 1 day for daily medications)
outcomes_primary: Clinically significant residual gastric volume (RGV), defined as a composite of gastric contents that (1) precludes endoscopic examination, (2) requires premature termination of the procedure or endotracheal intubation, and/or (3) results in an aspiration event that necessitates extended monitoring, unplanned therapeutics, or hospital admission
outcomes_secondary: Increased RGV, defined as any amount of solid content or more than 0.8 mL/kg of fluid content
extraction_notes: Trial was terminated early at 50% interim analysis due to exceeding prespecified O'Brien-Fleming stopping boundary. Single-masked trial (endoscopists and anesthesiologists masked to group assignment). Conducted at 2 tertiary care centers in the US.

title: Exploratory Analysis of Liraglutide Effects on Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Health-Related Quality of Life in Individuals With Obesity and COPD: A Secondary Analysis of a Randomised Controlled Trial.
population: Adults aged 40-70 years with COPD (defined as FEV1/FVC < 70% after maximal bronchodilation), former smokers, BMI > 27 kg/m2. Exclusion criteria: current smoker, treatment with systemic corticosteroids, diabetes mellitus of any type, interstitial pulmonary disease, severe hepatic, renal or heart disease, pancreatitis, pregnancy, or breastfeeding.
intervention: Liraglutide 3.0 mg subcutaneous injection (titrated up to 3.0 mg) for 40 weeks
comparison: Placebo subcutaneous injection for 40 weeks
outcomes_primary: This is a secondary exploratory analysis; original trial primary outcome was pulmonary function. For this analysis, exploratory outcomes included: OSA prevalence and severity measured by Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI) and Oxygen Desaturation Index (ODI)
outcomes_secondary: Daytime sleepiness measured by Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS); Health-related quality of life measured by Short Form-36 version 2 (SF-36v2) including eight health domains: physical functioning, bodily pain, role limitations due to physical health problems, role limitations due to personal or emotional problems, emotional well-being, social functioning, energy/fatigue, and general health perceptions
extraction_notes: This is a secondary exploratory analysis of a randomized controlled trial. The original trial was primarily designed to investigate respiratory effects of liraglutide on pulmonary function. Sample size (n=40 randomized) was based on power calculation for the primary publication, not for these secondary outcomes. OSA-related outcomes and HRQoL outcomes described here were exploratory secondary outcomes.

title: Pharmacological and metabolic effects of Bifidobacterium triple viable capsules and Five-animal Play in patients with impaired glucose tolerance.
population: Ninety persons with impaired glucose tolerance (IGT)
intervention: Huatuo Five-animal Play exercise combined with Bifidobacterium triple viable capsules for four weeks
comparison: Low-intensity aerobic activity; Bifidobacterium triple viable capsules alone; Huatuo Five-animal Play exercise alone
outcomes_secondary: Fasting blood glucose (FBG); 2 h post-load glucose (2hFBG); glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c); fasting insulin; homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR); serum lipids (total cholesterol, triglycerides, LDL-C, HDL-C); circulating GLP-1; Wnt5a; Sfrp5; kidney and liver toxicity
extraction_notes: Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes in the abstract. The exact groupings and whether probiotic was given to all groups or as a separate arm is ambiguous. Intervention dose and frequency for Bifidobacterium capsules not specified.

title: Oral Semaglutide and Change in Cardiovascular Risk Factors in High-Risk Type 2 Diabetes: A Post Hoc Secondary Analysis of the SOUL Randomized Clinical Trial.
population: Adults aged 50 years or older with type 2 diabetes, HbA1c between 6.5% and 10.0%, and at least one of the following: coronary heart disease, cerebrovascular disease, symptomatic peripheral artery disease, and/or chronic kidney disease. Key exclusion criteria: myocardial infarction, stroke, hospitalization for unstable angina pectoris or transient ischemic attack within past 60 days prior to screening, planned coronary/carotid/peripheral artery revascularization known on day of screening, heart failure New York Heart Association class IV, and/or treatment with any GLP-1 RA within 30 days before screening.
intervention: Once-daily oral semaglutide (maximum dose 14 mg) in addition to standard of care for cardiovascular risk mitigation and glucose management
comparison: Matching placebo once daily in addition to standard of care for cardiovascular risk mitigation and glucose management
outcomes_primary: Association of oral semaglutide vs placebo with glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), body weight, and blood pressure using estimated treatment differences (ETDs) and with high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hsCRP) and lipid plasma levels using estimated treatment ratios (ETRs)
outcomes_secondary: Blood pressure components (systolic BP, diastolic BP, pulse pressure), pulse, plasma levels of hsCRP and lipids (total cholesterol, non-HDL cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, and triglycerides)
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc secondary analysis of the SOUL trial. The primary outcome description reflects the stated aim of this secondary analysis rather than the original SOUL trial primary outcome (MACE). Lipid measurements were taken in a nonfasting state.

title: Weight Changes With Tirzepatide and Concomitant Weight-Inducing Medications: Post Hoc Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
population: Adults with obesity (BMI ≥30) or overweight (BMI ≥27) with at least one weight-related condition, excluding type 2 diabetes, who initiated at least one weight-inducing medication during the SURMOUNT-1, -3, or -4 trials. Exposure to nonsteroid weight-inducing medication required use for ≥3 months; exposure to oral corticosteroid weight-inducing medication required use for ≥1 week.
intervention: Tirzepatide subcutaneous injection once weekly. SURMOUNT-1: tirzepatide 5 mg, 10 mg, or 15 mg for 72 weeks. SURMOUNT-3: tirzepatide maximum tolerated dose (10 or 15 mg) for 72 weeks after 12-week intensive lifestyle intervention. SURMOUNT-4: tirzepatide maximum tolerated dose (10 or 15 mg) for 88 weeks after 36-week open-label tirzepatide lead-in period.
comparison: Placebo
outcomes_primary: Percentage change in body weight from randomization to week 72 (SURMOUNT-1 and SURMOUNT-3) or week 88 (SURMOUNT-4)
extraction_notes: This is a post hoc analysis of three phase 3 randomized clinical trials. Secondary outcomes were not explicitly defined for this post hoc analysis. Original trials excluded participants with current or recent use of weight-inducing medications at entry, but these could be initiated during the study.

title: Safety and efficacy of switching from dulaglutide to tirzepatide across clinically relevant baseline characteristics in participants with T2D: subgroup analysis of SURPASS-SWITCH.
population: Adults ≥18 years of age with type 2 diabetes, HbA1c ≥7.0% to ≤9.5%, BMI ≥25 kg/m², on a stable non-maximal dose of once-weekly dulaglutide (0.75 mg or 1.5 mg) for at least 6 months, and treatment with a stable dose of 0-3 oral antihyperglycemic medications for at least 3 months (any combination of metformin, sulfonylurea, and sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitor), with stable body weight
intervention: Switch to tirzepatide 2.5 mg once weekly with escalation to 15 mg or maximum tolerated dose every 4 weeks using a single-dose pen, for 40 weeks
comparison: Continue with and escalate to dulaglutide 4.5 mg or maximum tolerated dose once weekly
outcomes_primary: Change from baseline in HbA1c at week 40
outcomes_secondary: Change from baseline in body weight at week 40; treatment-emergent adverse events collected throughout the study duration and during 4-week safety follow-up
extraction_notes: Phase IV, randomized, open-label, active-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter, multinational trial. This is a prespecified subgroup analysis of SURPASS-SWITCH examining baseline subgroups including age, HbA1c, duration of T2D, baseline dulaglutide dose, duration of dulaglutide dose, BMI, ethnicity, and sex.

title: GZR18, a GLP-1 analog with once-weekly or bi-weekly dosing for body weight management: A randomized, placebo-controlled, phase 1b/2a trial.
population: Chinese adults aged 18-65 years with overweight (BMI 24.0-28.0 kg/m2 with specified comorbidities) or obesity (BMI ≥28.0 kg/m2); Part A included overweight or obese participants, Part B included only obese participants
intervention: GZR18 (bofanglutide), a GLP-1 receptor agonist, administered subcutaneously; Part A: dose escalation from 0.6 mg to 4.8 mg once-weekly over 18 weeks then maintenance at 4.8 mg for 8 weeks (26 weeks total); Part B: dose escalation from 1.5 mg to 30 mg over 35 weeks, administered either once-weekly (QW) or bi-weekly (Q2W) after reaching 9 mg dose level
comparison: Placebo (subcutaneous injection matching GZR18 in appearance and administration); randomization ratio 3:1 (GZR18:placebo) in both parts
outcomes_primary: Safety assessed by incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs), including gastrointestinal adverse events, hypoglycemic episodes, injection site reactions, vital signs, physical examinations, 12-lead ECGs, clinical laboratory parameters, and immunogenicity (anti-GZR18 and neutralizing antibodies); Part A also included change from baseline in body weight at end of treatment as primary endpoint
outcomes_secondary: Changes from baseline in body weight, BMI, waist circumference, blood pressure (systolic and diastolic), fasting blood glucose, fasting insulin, and lipid profiles (total cholesterol, triglycerides); proportion of participants achieving ≥5% reduction in body weight from baseline; pharmacokinetic endpoints including trough concentrations of GZR18 following repeated doses
extraction_notes: Part A exploratory endpoints included changes in body weight, BMI, waist circumference, fasting blood glucose and fasting insulin during dose-maintenance phase from week 14 to week 26. Protocol amendments during trial conduct introduced bi-weekly dosing regimen and higher dose levels. Dosing frequency assignment in Part B was based on individual preference rather than randomization.

title: Dulaglutide and neurodegeneration biomarkers: REWIND post hoc analysis.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
population: Adults aged 50 years or older with type 2 diabetes and previous cardiovascular event or cardiovascular risk factors, glycated hemoglobin ≤9.5% (≤80 mmol/mol), body mass index ≥23 kg/m2, taking up to two oral glucose-lowering drugs with or without basal insulin at stable doses for at least 3 months. Exclusions: coronary or cerebrovascular event within previous 2 months, estimated glomerular filtration rate <15 mL/min/1.73 m2 or renal dialysis, severe hypoglycemia within past year, cancer within past 5 years, history of pancreatitis, bariatric surgery, or known abnormal gastric emptying, or previous participation in dulaglutide studies.
intervention: Dulaglutide 1.5 mg subcutaneous injection once weekly
comparison: Placebo subcutaneous injection once weekly
outcomes_primary: Association between dulaglutide treatment and 2-year changes in plasma ADRD biomarkers (neurofilament light chain [NfL], phosphorylated tau217 [p-tau217], glial fibrillary acidic protein [GFAP])
outcomes_secondary: Substantive cognitive impairment (SCI) defined as first occurrence of a follow-up score on Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) or Digit Symbol Substitution Test (DSST) with standard deviation of 1.5 or more below the mean baseline country-standardized score over 5-year follow-up; associations between dulaglutide treatment and SCI by baseline biomarker subgroups
extraction_notes: Post hoc analysis of the REWIND cardiovascular outcomes trial. Primary and secondary outcomes for this post hoc analysis were not explicitly labeled as such; classification based on analysis descriptions. Biomarker analysis restricted to 2-year follow-up while cognitive outcomes assessed over median 5.4-year follow-up.

title: Efficacy and safety of co-administered cagrilintide and semaglutide versus semaglutide alone in adults with overweight or obesity with or without type 2 diabetes in Japan and Taiwan (REDEFINE 5): a multicentre, randomised, active-controlled, phase 3a trial.
population: Adults aged at least 18 years with BMI of at least 27 kg/m², with or without type 2 diabetes, in Japan and Taiwan (east Asian population)
intervention: Fixed-dose combination of cagrilintide 2.4 mg and semaglutide 2.4 mg, subcutaneous (presumed), for 68 weeks
comparison: Semaglutide 2.4 mg alone
outcomes_primary: Change in bodyweight from baseline to week 68
outcomes_secondary: Adverse events, gastrointestinal disorders
extraction_notes: BMI threshold appears truncated in abstract text (shows 'at least 27 kg/m' without completing the unit). Route of administration not explicitly stated but presumed subcutaneous based on drug class. Dose escalation schedule not described.

title: Once-weekly semaglutide versus placebo in patients with alcohol use disorder and comorbid obesity: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
population: Treatment-seeking adults with moderate to severe alcohol use disorder and comorbid obesity
intervention: Semaglutide 2.4 mg subcutaneously once weekly for 26 weeks, in addition to standard cognitive behavioural therapy
comparison: Placebo (saline subcutaneously) once weekly for 26 weeks, in addition to standard cognitive behavioural therapy
outcomes_primary: Reduction in the number of heavy drinking days assessed after 26 weeks of intervention
outcomes_secondary: Multiple secondary alcohol-related and somatic outcomes (not further specified in abstract)
extraction_notes: Secondary outcomes not explicitly defined in abstract. Obesity criteria (e.g., BMI threshold) not specified.

title: Six-month effects of liraglutide and dapagliflozin on lipid profile, cardiovascular risk, and NT-proBNP levels in patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease.
population: Adult patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease
intervention: Liraglutide titrated to 1.8 milligrams daily or dapagliflozin 10 milligrams daily, combined with Mediterranean diet and moderate physical activity, for six months
comparison: Control group receiving lifestyle intervention only (Mediterranean diet and moderate physical activity)
outcomes_primary: Lipid profile (total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, triglycerides, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol); cardiovascular risk assessed using five validated scales (Globorisk, Framingham Risk Score, American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease Risk Calculator, Prospective Cardiovascular Munster Score, World Health Organization cardiovascular risk charts)
outcomes_secondary: N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels
extraction_notes: Study design: prospective, randomized, parallel-group. Three treatment arms described but extraction focuses on the two active interventions versus control.

title: Plasma enteroglucagon after jejunoileal bypass with 3:1 or 1:3 jejunoileal ratio.
population: Morbidly obese patients (24 total)
intervention: Jejunoileal bypass with 1:3 jejunoileal ratio of the functioning segment
comparison: Jejunoileal bypass with 3:1 jejunoileal ratio of the functioning segment; unoperated morbidly obese patients
outcomes_primary: Plasma enteroglucagon concentration in peripheral blood (fasting values and postprandial integrated increments after a test meal)
extraction_notes: This appears to be an observational/mechanistic study rather than a randomized controlled trial. The abstract does not specify primary vs secondary outcomes; all outcomes listed under primary. No information on randomization, blinding, or study duration provided.

title: The effect of pirenzepine on meal-stimulated gastrointestinal hormones.
population: Healthy subjects (n=6)
intervention: Pirenzepine 10 mg in 2 ml solvent, given intravenously 30 min before a standard normal breakfast (2220 kJ)
comparison: 2 ml saline (0.15 mol/l) given intravenously 30 min before a standard normal breakfast
outcomes_secondary: Plasma concentrations of gut hormones in fasting and postprandial states: insulin, glucagon, gastric inhibitory peptide (GIP), neurotensin, vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP), somatostatin, pancreatic polypeptide (PP), motilin, enteroglucagon, gastrin
extraction_notes: Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes. Study used crossover design with random order administration on separate days.

title: Gut and pancreatic hormones after jejunoileal bypass with 3:1 or 1:3 jejunoileal ratio.
population: Obese patients, including those waiting for bypass surgery and those who had undergone jejunoileal bypass surgery 3, 9, or 15 months earlier
intervention: Jejunoileal bypass with 3:1 jejunoileal ratio between functioning segments
comparison: Jejunoileal bypass with 1:3 jejunoileal ratio between functioning segments; patients waiting for bypass surgery (pre-operative controls)
outcomes_primary: Plasma levels of gut hormones (gastrin, gastric inhibitory polypeptide, enteroglucagon) and pancreatic hormones (insulin, glucagon, pancreatic polypeptide) and glucose during fasting and after a test meal
extraction_notes: This is a non-randomized comparative study. The abstract does not specify randomization or blinding. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished. Sample size is 34 total patients (5 pre-operative, 29 post-operative) but distribution between 3:1 and 1:3 ratio groups not specified.

title: Pharmacokinetic, insulinotropic, and glucagonostatic properties of GLP-1 [7-36 amide] after subcutaneous injection in healthy volunteers. Dose-response-relationships.
population: Healthy volunteers, fasting state
intervention: GLP-1 [7-36 amide] subcutaneous injection at doses of 0.15, 0.5, 1.5, or 4.5 nmol/kg body weight (volume 1 ml or 2 ml at highest dose)
comparison: Placebo (0.9% NaCl with 1% human serum albumin) subcutaneous injection
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucose concentrations, insulin concentrations, C-peptide concentrations, GLP-1 [7-36 amide] concentrations, glucagon concentrations, kG-values (glucose disappearance rate), reactive hypoglycaemia
extraction_notes: Primary outcomes not explicitly distinguished from secondary outcomes. Small sample size (n=8). Study design is dose-response with randomized crossover (five occasions in randomized order). Intravenous glucose bolus (0.33 g/kg) administered 30 min after subcutaneous injection as part of study protocol.

title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 7-36 amide and peptide YY from the L-cell of the ileal mucosa are potent inhibitors of vagally induced gastric acid secretion in man.
population: Healthy volunteers
intervention: Intravenous infusion of GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1 7-36 amide) at 41 pmol/kg/h, or Peptide YY (PYY) at 50 pmol/kg/h
comparison: Intravenous infusion of saline
outcomes_primary: Integrated gastric acid output during vagally induced (sham feeding) acid secretion
outcomes_secondary: Plasma concentrations of GLP-1 and PYY; serum gastrin concentrations; plasma somatostatin concentrations
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=6). Crossover design implied by 'randomly assigned' to receive each infusion. Duration of infusion not specified. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; assumed based on study aim.

title: Fat-induced ileal brake in humans: a dose-dependent phenomenon correlated to the plasma levels of peptide YY.
population: Patients in the defunctionalized stage of total colectomy
intervention: Ileal pouch infusion of 20% oleic acid solution
comparison: 0.9% saline infusion, 2% oleic acid infusion
outcomes_primary: Gastric emptying rate
outcomes_secondary: Plasma concentrations of peptide YY (PYY), enteroglucagon, neurotensin, and motilin
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=7). Crossover design with each patient studied on three separate occasions. Infusions administered 30 minutes after labeled meal consumption. This appears to be a mechanistic/physiological study rather than a therapeutic intervention trial.

title: Voglibose (AO-128) is an efficient alpha-glucosidase inhibitor and mobilizes the endogenous GLP-1 reserve.
population: Healthy volunteers
intervention: Voglibose (AO-128) at doses of 0.5 mg, 1.0 mg, 2.0 mg, or 5.0 mg administered three times daily for 7 days
comparison: Placebo (two parallel groups)
extraction_notes: Primary and secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished in abstract. Outcomes measured included blood glucose, insulin, C peptide, gastric inhibitory polypeptide, and glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) levels at regular intervals up to 180 minutes after standardized breakfast. Study conducted in healthy volunteers rather than the target population of non-insulin-dependent diabetics mentioned in the drug design description.

title: Gastric emptying, glucose responses, and insulin secretion after a liquid test meal: effects of exogenous glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1)-(7-36) amide in type 2 (noninsulin-dependent) diabetic patients.
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
population: Type 2 (non-insulin-dependent) diabetic patients with poor glycemic control, studied in fasting state
intervention: GLP-1-(7-36) amide 1.2 pmol/kg.min intravenous infusion from -30 to 240 min
comparison: Placebo (0.9% NaCl with 1% human serum albumin) infusion
outcomes_primary: Gastric emptying (gastric volume determined by dye dilution technique using phenol red)
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucose, insulin, C-peptide, GLP-1-(7-36) amide, and glucagon concentrations
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=8). Randomized crossover design implied but not explicitly stated. Baseline characteristics provided (age 58±6 yr, BMI 30.0±5.2 kg/m2, HbA1c 10.5±1.2%) but unclear if these are inclusion criteria or descriptive statistics.

title: Glucagonostatic actions and reduction of fasting hyperglycemia by exogenous glucagon-like peptide I(7-36) amide in type I diabetic patients.
population: Type I diabetic patients with fasting hyperglycemia provoked by halving usual evening NPH insulin dose; HbA1c 9.1 ± 2.1% (normal 4.2-6.3%)
intervention: Glucagon-like peptide I(7-36) amide (GLP-1) 1.2 pmol/kg/min intravenous infusion
comparison: Placebo intravenous infusion
outcomes_primary: Plasma glucose concentration, plasma glucagon concentration
outcomes_secondary: C-peptide, insulin, nonesterified fatty acids, triglycerides, cholesterol, cortisol, growth hormone
extraction_notes: Crossover design with random order on two occasions; n=11 patients; primary outcomes not explicitly labeled as such - inferred from study objectives

title: Potential therapeutic levels of glucagon-like peptide I achieved in humans by a buccal tablet.
population: Healthy volunteers, fasting conditions
intervention: Mucoadhesive buccal GLP-I (glucagon-like peptide I(7-36) amide) tablet containing 119 nmol, single dose, transmucosal absorption
comparison: Placebo (buccal tablet)
outcomes_primary: Plasma GLP-I concentration (total GLP-I immunoreactivity measured using COOH-terminal radioimmunoassay and NH2-terminal radioimmunoassay for active nondegraded peptide)
outcomes_secondary: Time to peak GLP-I concentration, area under curve, relative bioavailability versus intravenous and subcutaneous injection, half-life of peptide activity, insulin concentrations, glucose concentrations, glucagon concentrations
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=8). Study conducted in healthy volunteers rather than NIDDM patients. Primary outcome not explicitly designated; inferred from study objectives.

title: The antidiabetogenic effect of GLP-1 is maintained during a 7-day treatment period and improves diabetic dyslipoproteinemia in NIDDM patients.
population: Patients with NIDDM (non-insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus)
intervention: GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide 1) given subcutaneously at meals together with regular insulin (days 8-12), then GLP-1 only at meals (days 13-14), with NPH insulin at bedtime throughout
comparison: Control group continuing with intensive insulin treatment only
outcomes_primary: Blood glucose control, antidiabetogenic effect of GLP-1
outcomes_secondary: VLDL triglycerides, LDL cholesterol, HDL cholesterol, LDL particle diameter, plasma insulin levels, lipoprotein lipase activity, hepatic lipase activity, development of tolerance to GLP-1
extraction_notes: Small sample size with unequal randomization (8 to GLP-1 group, 4 to control group). Primary outcome not explicitly designated; inferred from study objectives. All 12 patients received intensive insulin treatment during week 1 before randomization on day 8.

title: Effects of glucagon-like peptide 1 (7-36 amide) on whole-body protein metabolism in healthy man.
population: Healthy volunteers
intervention: Synthetic GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide 1, 7-36 amide) infusion for 180 minutes during hyperglycaemic clamping, with or without pancreatic clamping (somatostatin infusion)
comparison: Placebo (saline) infusion
outcomes_primary: Whole-body protein metabolism assessed by [1-13C]-leucine kinetics (leucine flux and leucine oxidation rate as parameters of whole-body protein breakdown)
outcomes_secondary: Energy expenditure and CO2 production measured by indirect calorimetry; plasma insulin levels
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=13). Study used crossover design with two conditions (intact pancreatic secretion vs. pancreatic clamping) to differentiate insulin-mediated vs. direct GLP-1 effects. Exact GLP-1 dose not specified in abstract.

title: Subcutaneous glucagon-like peptide I combined with insulin normalizes postcibal glycemic excursions in IDDM.
population: Patients with insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus (IDDM)
intervention: Subcutaneous glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) combined with insulin
comparison: Not explicitly stated
outcomes_primary: Postprandial (postcibal) glycemic excursions
outcomes_secondary: Not explicitly stated
extraction_notes: No abstract text available; extraction based solely on title. Comparator group not specified in title. Dose, route, frequency, and duration of GLP-1 and insulin not available. Primary and secondary outcome distinction not explicitly stated in title.

title: Acute incretin response to oral glucose is associated with stimulation of gastric inhibitory polypeptide, not glucagon-like peptide in young subjects.
population: Young nonobese subjects
intervention: Hyperglycemic clamp with superimposed ingestion of oral glucose (30 g) at 120 min; glucose acutely raised by 12.5 mg/dL above fasting values by i.v. glucose infusion and maintained at this level for 180 min with glucose infusion adjusted to maintain plasma glucose plateau after oral glucose
comparison: Hyperglycemic clamp without oral glucose ingestion; glucose acutely raised by 12.5 mg/dL above fasting values by i.v. glucose infusion and maintained at this level for 180 min
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=8). This is a physiological mechanistic study rather than a traditional clinical trial. Primary and secondary outcomes were not explicitly designated; measured outcomes included plasma insulin responses, C-peptide levels, plasma gastric inhibitory polypeptide (GIP) levels, and plasma glucagon-like peptide-1 (7-37) levels.

title: Combined use of guar and acarbose in reduction of postprandial glycaemia.
population: 8 healthy volunteers
intervention: 50 mg acarbose together with 14.5 g guar gum added to a breakfast test meal
comparison: acarbose alone; implied control/test meal alone
outcomes_primary: peak rise in blood-glucose at 30 min
outcomes_secondary: areas under the insulin response curve; areas under the gastrointestinal-polypeptide response curve; carbohydrate malabsorption assessed by measurement of breath hydrogen; symptoms associated with carbohydrate malabsorption
extraction_notes: Crossover or within-subject design implied but not explicitly stated. No explicit primary/secondary outcome designation; categorization based on emphasis in abstract. Comparator conditions not fully explicit - baseline/control meal condition implied.

title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 7-36 amide and peptide YY have additive inhibitory effect on gastric acid secretion in man.
population: Healthy volunteers
intervention: Intravenous infusion of GLP-1 (Glucagon-like peptide-1 7-36 amide) and PYY (peptide YY) in combination, at two different rates: 0.25 pmol/kg/min (low rate) and 0.5 pmol/kg/min (high rate)
comparison: Intravenous infusion of GLP-1 alone at 0.25 pmol/kg/min and 0.5 pmol/kg/min; Intravenous infusion of PYY alone at 0.25 pmol/kg/min and 0.5 pmol/kg/min
outcomes_primary: Pentagastrin-induced gastric acid secretion
extraction_notes: Small sample size (n=8). Study design not explicitly stated but appears to be a crossover design. Primary vs secondary outcomes not explicitly distinguished.

title: No apparent benefit of liquid formula diet in NIDDM.
journal: Experimental and clinical endocrinology & diabetes : official journal, German Society of Endocrinology [and] German Diabetes Association
population: Type II non-insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus (NIDDM) patients under oral treatment regimen with diet plus glibenclamide
intervention: Liquid formula diets administered as 500 ml single dose after overnight fast: standard liquid diet (Biosorb Sonde), fibre containing diet (Biosorb Plus Sonde), or carbohydrate modified fructose containing diabetes diet (Fresubin Diabetes); each containing approximately 60 g carbohydrate; tests performed in randomized order with 10 day intervals
comparison: Crossover comparison between the three liquid formula diets (standard vs fibre containing vs carbohydrate modified fructose containing diabetes diet)
outcomes_primary: Plasma glucose area under the curve over 180 minutes
outcomes_secondary: IR-insulin, IR-C-peptide, IR-glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), IR-glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) in plasma over 180 minutes
extraction_notes: Crossover design with randomized order. Primary outcome not explicitly labeled but glucose AUC appears to be main focus. Sample size is 10 patients (7 men, 3 women). This is a tolerance test study rather than a treatment intervention trial.

title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1): a trial of treatment in non-insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus.
population: Patients with poorly controlled non-insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus (NIDDM)
intervention: Subcutaneous GLP-1 (Glucagon-like peptide-1 (7-36) amide) 40 nmol, given three times a day immediately before meals, for three weeks
comparison: Subcutaneous saline, given three times a day immediately before meals, for three weeks
outcomes_primary: Plasma glucose area under the curve (AUC) following standardized test meal
outcomes_secondary: Plasma glucagon levels postprandially; postprandial insulin levels
extraction_notes: Crossover design with six-week total duration (three weeks per treatment period). Small sample size (n=5). Primary outcome not explicitly labeled as such; determined based on emphasis in abstract.

title: A liquid mixed meal or exogenous glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) do not alter plasma leptin concentrations in healthy volunteers.
population: Healthy volunteers
intervention: Intravenous infusion of GLP-1 [7-36 amide] at 0.4 pmol/kg/min or 0.8 pmol/kg/min from -30 to 240 min, with liquid test meal (50 g sucrose in 400 ml 8% amino acid solution, total amino acids 80 g/l) administered via nasogastric tube at 0 min
comparison: Placebo infusion with liquid test meal
